questions.stem: A researcher studying the origin of blood cancers explains that leukemias, lymphomas, and multiple myeloma all trace back to a single population of cells that also produces normal red blood cells, white blood cells, and platelets. From which of the following cells do hematopoietic neoplasms arise?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Endothelial cells lining the lymphatic vessels

choices.label: B
choices.text: Epithelial stem cells of the thymic cortex

choices.label: C
choices.text: Hematopoietic stem cells in the bone marrow

choices.label: D
choices.text: Mature plasma cells circulating in the blood

explanation.summary: Hematopoietic neoplasms arise from the primordial hematopoietic stem cells (HSCs) of the bone marrow.
explanation.whyCorrect: Hematopoietic neoplasms arise from the primordial hematopoietic stem cells (HSCs) found in the bone marrow. These same stem cells also give rise to normal blood cells such as red blood cells, white blood cells, and platelets, but under influences like genetic mutations, toxins, radiation, and medications they can develop into neoplasms.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Lymphatic endothelial cells are structural vessel cells and do not give rise to hematopoietic neoplasms.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Thymic epithelial stem cells give rise to the thymic stroma, not to the hematopoietic neoplasms described here.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Mature plasma cells are a downstream derivative of the lymphoid line; the neoplasms as a group arise from the upstream hematopoietic stem cell.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Reticuloendothelial cells of the spleen are not the source of hematopoietic neoplasms, which originate from marrow stem cells.

questions.stem: A pathologist is applying the current World Health Organization (WHO) classification to a newly diagnosed hematopoietic neoplasm. According to this system, which of the following is used as the main framework for categorizing these tumors?

choices.label: A
choices.text: The cell of origin, either myeloid or lymphoid

choices.label: B
choices.text: The presence or absence of lymphadenopathy

choices.label: C
choices.text: The response of the tumor to chemotherapy

choices.label: D
choices.text: Whether the disease is acute or chronic

choices.label: E
choices.text: Whether the patient is a child or an adult

explanation.summary: The WHO classification uses the cell of origin (myeloid vs lymphoid) as the primary framework.
explanation.whyCorrect: The brick emphasizes the current WHO classification, which uses the cell of origin as the main framework, dividing hematopoietic neoplasms into those derived from the myeloid cell line and those derived from the lymphoid cell line.

whyWrongByChoice.B: Lymphadenopathy helps distinguish lymphomas from leukemias clinically but is not the organizing principle of the WHO system.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Treatment response is not the basis of the WHO classification.
whyWrongByChoice.D: The acute versus chronic distinction applies within leukemias but is not the primary myeloid-versus-lymphoid framework.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Age is a helpful clinical clue (myeloid neoplasms are more common in adults) but is not the main WHO framework.

questions.stem: A 62-year-old man is being evaluated for a hematopoietic malignancy. His physician notes that distinguishing a leukemia from a lymphoma can be difficult but that certain features help. Which of the following findings is most characteristic of a leukemia rather than a lymphoma?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Alterations in peripheral blood cell counts

choices.label: C
choices.text: Origin restricted to the lymphoid cell line

explanation.summary: Because of their bone marrow origin, leukemias typically alter blood cell counts, whereas lymphomas typically cause lymphadenopathy.
explanation.whyCorrect: Due to their bone marrow origin, leukemias typically have alterations in blood cell counts, which is less common in lymphomas (although it can occur in lymphomas that involve the bone). Lymphomas, by contrast, typically present with lymphadenopathy.

whyWrongByChoice.B: Fever is a nonspecific symptom seen in both leukemias and lymphomas.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Only lymphomas are restricted to the lymphoid line; leukemias can arise from either the myeloid or lymphoid cell line.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Lymphadenopathy is characteristic of lymphomas, not leukemias.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Weight loss is a generalized symptom that can be seen in both leukemias and lymphomas.

questions.stem: A 30-year-old woman is diagnosed with an acute leukemia. Compared with a chronic leukemia, which of the following best characterizes the cells responsible for her disease and its expected course if untreated?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Cells arrested at a single intermediate stage with an indolent course

choices.label: B
choices.text: Dysplastic precursors that never enter the peripheral blood

choices.label: C
choices.text: Fully mature lymphocytes confined to peripheral lymph nodes

choices.label: D
choices.text: Mature, well-differentiated cells with survival measured in years

choices.label: E
choices.text: Very immature precursor cells with short survival of weeks to months

explanation.summary: Acute leukemias are caused by very immature precursor cells and, if untreated, carry short survival of weeks to months.
explanation.whyCorrect: Acute leukemias are caused by very immature precursor hematopoietic cells and have a more abrupt, rapid presentation. Because of the rapid proliferation that takes over the bone marrow, patients exhibit short survival (weeks to months) if not treated. Chronic leukemias, by contrast, are caused by more mature cells at an advanced stage of development and have longer survival (years).

whyWrongByChoice.A: An indolent course reflects chronic disease; acute leukemia is rapidly progressive.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Dysplastic precursors that fail to mature describe myelodysplastic neoplasms rather than the immature precursors of acute leukemia.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Confinement of mature lymphocytes to lymph nodes describes a lymphoma pattern, not acute leukemia.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Mature cells with survival in years describe chronic, not acute, leukemia.

questions.stem: A 55-year-old man is found to have a myeloproliferative neoplasm in which the marrow shows a striking overproduction of red blood cells and his hematocrit is markedly elevated. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

explanation.summary: Among myeloproliferative neoplasms, red blood cell dominance defines polycythemia vera.
explanation.whyCorrect: In myeloproliferative neoplasms, the disorders are separated based on which cell line becomes dominant. Polycythemia vera is characterized by red blood cell (RBC) dominance, matching the overproduction of red cells and elevated hematocrit described here.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Chronic myeloid leukemia is characterized by granulocyte dominance.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Essential thrombocythemia is defined by platelet dominance, not red cell overproduction.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Myelodysplastic neoplasm causes marrow failure with low blood counts, not an overproduction of red cells.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Primary myelofibrosis features expansion of all precursor lines with eventual marrow fibrosis rather than isolated red cell dominance.

questions.stem: A 70-year-old man has a myeloid neoplasm in which the bone marrow is replaced by abnormal, dysplastic precursor cells that have not differentiated into mature blood cells, resulting in low peripheral blood counts. Approximately what proportion of patients with this disorder progress to acute myeloid leukemia?

explanation.summary: In myelodysplastic neoplasms, transformation to AML occurs in about 30% of patients.
explanation.whyCorrect: In myelodysplastic neoplasms, the marrow is replaced by dysplastic cells derived from progenitor myeloid stem cells that have not differentiated into mature blood cells, causing bone marrow failure with low counts. Transformation to AML occurs in 30% of patients.

whyWrongByChoice.A: 5% understates the risk; the brick specifies transformation in 30% of patients.
whyWrongByChoice.C: 50% is higher than the figure given for progression to AML.
whyWrongByChoice.D: 75% overstates the risk of transformation in myelodysplastic neoplasms.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Not all patients progress; the stated proportion is 30%, not 100%.

questions.stem: A 68-year-old woman presents with fatigue and recurrent infections. Her bone marrow is filled with malignant myeloid cells, and a complete blood count shows pancytopenia. This represents a true malignant transformation of myeloid cells. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

explanation.summary: AML is a true malignant transformation of myeloid cells that fills the marrow, causing pancytopenia and frequent infections.
explanation.whyCorrect: In acute myeloid leukemia (AML), there is true malignant transformation of myeloid cells. The malignant cells fill the bone marrow and can extend locally or metastasize, often causing bone marrow failure and pancytopenia. Infections are common because of the reduced number and function of circulating white blood cells.

whyWrongByChoice.B: Essential thrombocythemia shows platelet dominance rather than marrow-filling malignant transformation with pancytopenia.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Follicular lymphoma is a mature B-cell (lymphoid) neoplasm, not a myeloid malignancy.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Multiple myeloma is a plasma cell neoplasm of lymphoid origin, distinct from a malignant transformation of myeloid cells.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Polycythemia vera is a myeloproliferative neoplasm with red cell overproduction, not pancytopenia from malignant transformation.

questions.stem: A 6-year-old boy is diagnosed with a precursor T-cell neoplasm. His disease predominantly involves the blood and bone marrow, so it is called T-cell acute lymphoblastic leukemia (T-ALL); a closely related presentation predominantly involving tissue such as lymph nodes and thymus is called T-lymphoblastic lymphoma (T-LBL). Which of the following best describes the relationship between T-ALL and T-LBL?

choices.label: A
choices.text: T-ALL is a myeloid neoplasm and T-LBL is a lymphoid neoplasm

choices.label: B
choices.text: T-LBL is a mature neoplasm while T-ALL is a plasma cell neoplasm

choices.label: C
choices.text: They are the same disease, distinguished mainly by the predominant site of involvement

choices.label: D
choices.text: They are unrelated diseases that share only a name

choices.label: E
choices.text: They differ because one expresses B-cell markers and the other expresses T-cell markers

explanation.summary: T-ALL and T-LBL are the same precursor T-cell disease, separated by whether the blood/marrow or tissue is predominantly involved.
explanation.whyCorrect: A precursor T-cell neoplasm that occurs predominantly in the blood and bone marrow is called T-ALL, whereas one predominantly in tissue (lymph nodes, thymus) is called T-LBL. They are the same disease, and because the overall site of involvement may not be known at presentation, the neoplasm is usually named T-lymphoblastic leukemia/lymphoma.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Both are precursor T-cell (lymphoid) neoplasms; neither is myeloid.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Both are precursor neoplasms, and neither is a plasma cell neoplasm.
whyWrongByChoice.D: They are not unrelated; the brick states explicitly that they are the same disease.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Both arise from T cells; the distinction is site of involvement, not B-cell versus T-cell marker expression.

questions.stem: A 60-year-old man has a years-long history of slowly progressive skin patches that have evolved into skin tumors and a near-full-body desquamating rash. Biopsy shows a mature T-cell neoplasm. He is told there is no cure but that his life expectancy is generally normal. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

explanation.summary: Mycosis fungoides/Sezary syndrome is a mature T-cell neoplasm with slow-growing skin lesions and generally normal life expectancy.
explanation.whyCorrect: Mycosis fungoides/Sezary syndrome is the emphasized mature peripheral T-cell neoplasm. Patients have slow-growing skin lesions that can later develop into skin tumors or a near-full-body desquamating rash. There is no cure, but because it is slow-growing, patients generally have a normal life expectancy.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Burkitt lymphoma is a high-grade B-cell non-Hodgkin lymphoma that grows explosively, not a chronic skin disorder.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Hodgkin lymphoma is defined by Reed-Sternberg cells and presents with lymphadenopathy, not desquamating skin lesions.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Multiple myeloma is a plasma cell neoplasm affecting marrow, bone, and kidney, not the skin.
whyWrongByChoice.E: T-ALL/LBL is a precursor T-cell neoplasm seen mostly in children, not an indolent adult skin disease.

questions.stem: A 66-year-old woman presents with bone pain, anemia, recurrent infections, and acute kidney injury. Workup reveals massive proliferation of plasma cells in the bone marrow, precipitation of immunoglobulins in the kidney, and an elevated serum calcium. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

explanation.summary: Multiple myeloma is a plasma cell neoplasm causing marrow failure, immunoglobulin-related kidney failure, bone lesions, and hypercalcemia.
explanation.whyCorrect: Plasma cell neoplasms derive from plasma cells, the B-cell derivative responsible for antibody secretion. The most common is multiple myeloma, with massive proliferation of plasma cells in the bone marrow. Consequences include bone marrow failure (infections, anemia), precipitation of immunoglobulins in the kidney causing kidney failure, and bone lesions with fractures and secondary hypercalcemia.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Acute myeloid leukemia is a myeloid malignancy filling the marrow, not a plasma cell neoplasm.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Chronic lymphocytic leukemia is a mature B-cell neoplasm that does not classically cause immunoglobulin precipitation in the kidney and hypercalcemia from bone destruction.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Hodgkin lymphoma is defined by Reed-Sternberg cells and lymphadenopathy, not plasma cell proliferation.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Mycosis fungoides/Sezary syndrome is a mature T-cell skin neoplasm, unrelated to this plasma cell picture.

questions.stem: A 22-year-old man presents with painless cervical lymphadenopathy, fevers, and night sweats. A lymph node biopsy shows gigantic cells with at least two large nuclei, each containing a single nucleolus, producing an "owl's-eye" appearance. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

explanation.summary: Hodgkin lymphoma is defined by neoplastic Reed-Sternberg cells, which are gigantic and have an owl's-eye appearance.
explanation.whyCorrect: Hodgkin lymphoma usually occurs in young adults ages 15 to 34 years and is defined by the presence of neoplastic Reed-Sternberg cells. These cells have a distinct morphology: they are gigantic and often have at least two big nuclei with single nucleoli, giving the cell an owl's-eye appearance.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Chronic myeloid leukemia is a myeloproliferative neoplasm with granulocyte dominance, not a Reed-Sternberg cell lymphoma.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Diffuse large B-cell lymphoma is a high-grade non-Hodgkin lymphoma and is not defined by Reed-Sternberg cells.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Follicular lymphoma is a low-grade non-Hodgkin lymphoma without owl's-eye Reed-Sternberg cells.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Multiple myeloma involves plasma cells in the marrow, not Reed-Sternberg cells in a lymph node.

questions.stem: A young patient presents to the emergency department with fatigue and bone pain. An initial complete blood count identifies an abundance of blasts, confirming a diagnosis of acute leukemia. Which of the following laboratory methods would be most useful to confirm the lineage (cell type/origin) of the leukemia?

explanation.summary: Flow cytometry classifies leukemia lineage by reading surface antigens on the blasts, distinguishing lymphoid (ALL) from myeloid (AML).
explanation.whyCorrect: By analyzing the antigens on the cell surface of the blasts, flow cytometry can confirm the lineage (cell type/origin) of the leukemia. The way a leukemia is identified as lymphoid (ALL) or myeloid (AML) is primarily by flow cytometry, and it works well on peripheral blood.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Conventional cytogenetics detects abnormalities in chromosome number and structure, not the surface-antigen lineage of the cells.
whyWrongByChoice.C: FISH evaluates select chromosomes with specific probes and does not establish cell lineage.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Molecular analysis detects specific mutations of the leukemia but not the lineage of the cells.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Routine histology requires tissue and cannot be performed on peripheral blood, so it is not the method to confirm lineage here.

questions.stem: A first-year student is reviewing the diagram of normal blood cell development from the hematopoietic stem cell. She is asked to name the one listed cell that belongs to the lymphoid series rather than the myeloid series. Which of the following cells is correctly identified as lymphoid in origin?

explanation.summary: The lymphoid stem cell line develops into lymphocytes, and the plasma cell is the B-cell derivative of that line.
explanation.whyCorrect: Two lines of healthy cells derive from hematopoietic stem cells: the myeloid stem cell line develops into erythrocytes, monocytes, granulocytes, and platelets, while the lymphoid stem cell line develops into lymphocytes. The plasma cell is derived from the B cell and is therefore lymphoid.

whyWrongByChoice.A: The basophil is one of the granulocytes produced by the myeloid line.
whyWrongByChoice.B: The erythrocyte is the red cell product of the myeloid line.
whyWrongByChoice.C: The megakaryocyte is a myeloid cell and is the precursor that produces platelets.
whyWrongByChoice.D: The monocyte arises from the myeloid line and matures into the macrophage.

questions.stem: A 58-year-old man asks his hematologist why his blood-forming stem cells could have turned into a cancer. The physician explains that several different influences can drive hematopoietic stem cells to develop into neoplasms. Which of the following exposures is among those influences?

explanation.summary: Familial genetic mutations, toxins, radiation, and medications can all drive hematopoietic stem cells to become neoplastic.
explanation.whyCorrect: Hematopoietic stem cells normally give rise to red cells, white cells, and platelets, but for many different reasons, including familial genetic mutations, toxins, radiation, and even medications, they can instead develop into neoplasms, sometimes with deadly results. Radiation exposure is one of the listed influences.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Dietary iron overload is not listed among the influences that transform hematopoietic stem cells into neoplasms.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Vitamin B12 deficiency causes a nutritional anemia and is not one of the cited neoplastic influences.
whyWrongByChoice.D: High-altitude residence raises red cell mass physiologically and is not a neoplastic influence.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Common viral respiratory infections are not among the exposures named as causes of hematopoietic neoplasms.

questions.stem: A hematopathology service reviews its annual case mix and compares the age distribution of patients whose neoplasms derive from the myeloid line with those whose neoplasms derive from the lymphoid line. Which of the following statements correctly describes these two groups?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Lymphoid neoplasms occur only in children, and myeloid neoplasms occur at any age

choices.label: B
choices.text: Myeloid and lymphoid neoplasms are both essentially limited to adults older than 60 years

choices.label: C
choices.text: Myeloid neoplasms are most common in adults, and lymphoid neoplasms are seen at any age

choices.label: D
choices.text: Myeloid neoplasms are most common in children, and lymphoid neoplasms are confined to adults

choices.label: E
choices.text: Myeloid neoplasms occur at any age, and lymphoid neoplasms are limited to older adults

explanation.summary: Myeloid neoplasms are most common in adults, whereas lymphoid neoplasms are seen across all ages.
explanation.whyCorrect: In the myeloid-versus-lymphoid framework, the myeloid neoplasms are described as most common in adults and give rise to three sets of disorders, while the lymphoid neoplasms are seen in any age group and are divided into T-cell neoplasms, B-cell neoplasms, and Hodgkin lymphoma.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Lymphoid neoplasms are not restricted to children; they occur at any age.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Lymphoid neoplasms occur at any age, including childhood, so neither group is limited to patients older than 60 years.
whyWrongByChoice.D: This reverses the pattern; myeloid neoplasms predominate in adults rather than children.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Lymphoid neoplasms are not limited to older adults, and myeloid neoplasms are specifically most common in adults.

questions.stem: A 58-year-old man has fatigue and early satiety. His white blood cell count is markedly elevated with granulocytes at all stages of maturation, and the bone marrow is replaced by neoplastic cells with clear granulocyte dominance. Which of the following myeloproliferative neoplasms best fits these findings?

explanation.summary: Among the myeloproliferative neoplasms, granulocyte dominance defines chronic myeloid leukemia.
explanation.whyCorrect: Myeloproliferative neoplasms replace the normal bone marrow with neoplastic cells, and they are most easily separated by which cell line becomes dominant. Chronic myeloid leukemia is the one characterized by granulocyte dominance.

whyWrongByChoice.B: Essential thrombocythemia is defined by platelet dominance.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Myelodysplastic neoplasm replaces the marrow with dysplastic precursors and lowers peripheral counts.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Polycythemia vera is defined by red blood cell dominance rather than granulocyte dominance.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Primary myelofibrosis expands all precursor lines and eventually fills the marrow with fibrosis.

questions.stem: A 64-year-old woman is referred after several complete blood counts show a platelet count above 900,000/microliter with normal hemoglobin and white cell count. Marrow examination confirms a myeloproliferative neoplasm in which the platelet line is the dominant, clinically significant line. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

explanation.summary: Platelet dominance within a myeloproliferative neoplasm identifies essential thrombocythemia.
explanation.whyCorrect: In myeloproliferative neoplasms one or more myelocytic lines increase, and the disorders are separated by which line becomes most dominant or clinically significant. Essential thrombocythemia is the entity characterized by platelet dominance.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Acute myeloid leukemia is a true malignant transformation that fills the marrow and typically causes pancytopenia.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Myelodysplastic neoplasm produces dysplastic precursors and low peripheral counts rather than a high platelet count.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Polycythemia vera is defined by red blood cell dominance with an elevated red cell mass.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Primary myelofibrosis involves expansion of all precursor lines with eventual marrow fibrosis, not isolated platelet dominance.

questions.stem: A 71-year-old man is diagnosed with primary myelofibrosis. Which of the following best describes what happens in the bone marrow in this disorder?

choices.label: A
choices.text: All precursor lines expand, and the marrow eventually becomes fibrotic

choices.label: B
choices.text: Dysplastic precursors fail to mature, producing low peripheral blood counts

choices.label: C
choices.text: Malignant blasts fill the marrow after true malignant transformation

choices.label: D
choices.text: The erythroid line alone expands, producing an elevated hematocrit

choices.label: E
choices.text: The granulocytic line alone expands, producing a very high white cell count

explanation.summary: Primary myelofibrosis expands all precursor lines and ends with a fibrotic marrow.
explanation.whyCorrect: Primary myelofibrosis is listed among the main myeloproliferative neoplasms and is distinguished by expansion of all the precursor lines, with the marrow eventually filled with fibrosis rather than by dominance of a single line.

whyWrongByChoice.B: Dysplastic precursors that never mature, with resulting low counts, describe myelodysplastic neoplasms.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Malignant blasts filling the marrow after true malignant transformation describes acute myeloid leukemia.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Isolated red cell dominance with a high hematocrit describes polycythemia vera.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Isolated granulocyte dominance describes chronic myeloid leukemia.

questions.stem: A pathology resident is asked where leukemias and lymphomas typically begin. Which of the following statements correctly contrasts the usual site of origin of these two groups of disorders?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Both leukemias and lymphomas originate exclusively within peripheral lymph nodes

choices.label: B
choices.text: Both leukemias and lymphomas originate exclusively within the bone marrow

choices.label: C
choices.text: Leukemias generally begin in peripheral lymph nodes; lymphomas only in the bone marrow

choices.label: D
choices.text: Leukemias generally begin in the marrow; lymphomas in marrow or peripheral nodes

choices.label: E
choices.text: Leukemias generally originate in the spleen; lymphomas begin within the thymus

explanation.summary: Leukemias generally start in the bone marrow, while lymphomas can start either in the marrow or in peripheral lymph nodes.
explanation.whyCorrect: Among the general tips separating the two groups, leukemias generally originate in the bone marrow, while lymphomas can originate either in the marrow or in the peripheral lymph nodes. As either disease progresses, leukemias may spill into the blood and involve nodes and lymphomas may infiltrate marrow or blood.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Leukemias are marrow-derived disorders, so neither group is restricted to peripheral lymph nodes.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Lymphomas are not restricted to the marrow; they may begin in peripheral lymph nodes.
whyWrongByChoice.C: This reverses the pattern; it is the leukemias that generally begin in the marrow.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Neither group is described as originating in the spleen or the thymus as its usual site.

questions.stem: The B- and T-cell lymphoid neoplasms are subdivided into precursor (immature) and mature groups. Which of the following statements correctly characterizes the mature group?

choices.label: A
choices.text: They arise from circulating mature lymphocytes and are confined to the spleen

choices.label: B
choices.text: They arise from more mature lymphoid cells in marrow, nodes, or skin

choices.label: C
choices.text: They arise from plasma cells in the marrow and characteristically spare lymph nodes

choices.label: D
choices.text: They arise from primitive lymphoid precursors restricted to the bone marrow

choices.label: E
choices.text: They arise only within the thymus and never involve lymph nodes

explanation.summary: Mature lymphoid neoplasms derive from more mature lymphoid cells and can arise in marrow, lymph nodes, or other organs such as skin.
explanation.whyCorrect: Precursor neoplasms derive from primitive lymphoid precursor cells in the bone marrow, whereas mature neoplasms derive from more mature lymphoid cells and can arise either in the bone marrow, lymph nodes, or even other organs like the skin.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Mature lymphoid neoplasms are not confined to the spleen; they involve marrow, nodes, and other organs.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Plasma cell neoplasms are only one subset of mature B-cell disease, and this does not define the group.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Origin from primitive lymphoid precursors in the bone marrow defines the precursor group, not the mature group.
whyWrongByChoice.E: The thymus is a site of precursor T-cell disease, and mature neoplasms commonly involve lymph nodes.

questions.stem: A 5-year-old boy is diagnosed with B-cell acute lymphoblastic leukemia/lymphoma. His parents have read about the T-cell form of the same disease and ask how his son's disease compares. Which of the following is the most accurate response?

choices.label: A
choices.text: It arises from mature B cells and occurs mainly in older adults

choices.label: B
choices.text: It has a better prognosis than the T-cell form and is given different treatment

choices.label: C
choices.text: It has a worse prognosis than the T-cell form and is given identical treatment

choices.label: D
choices.text: It is a myeloid neoplasm and is treated with the same regimen as acute myeloid leukemia

choices.label: E
choices.text: It is defined by Reed-Sternberg cells and is cured in nearly all children

explanation.summary: B-cell acute lymphoblastic leukemia/lymphoma also occurs mostly in children but has a better prognosis and different treatment than the T-cell variant.
explanation.whyCorrect: B-cell acute lymphoblastic leukemia/lymphoma is the main precursor B-cell disorder. Like its T-cell cousin it occurs mostly in children, and these precursor lymphoblastic leukemias/lymphomas are in fact the most common childhood cancers overall, but the B-cell form has a better prognosis than the T-cell variant and different treatments.

whyWrongByChoice.A: This is a precursor neoplasm arising from immature B cells, and it occurs mostly in children.
whyWrongByChoice.C: The B-cell form has the better, not the worse, prognosis, and its treatment differs from the T-cell form.
whyWrongByChoice.D: It is a lymphoid, not a myeloid, neoplasm.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Reed-Sternberg cells define Hodgkin lymphoma, not precursor B-cell disease.

questions.stem: Which of the following mature B-cell disorders is classified as a low-grade non-Hodgkin lymphoma with a good prognosis?

explanation.summary: Hairy cell leukemia is listed among the slow-growing, low-grade non-Hodgkin lymphomas, which carry a good prognosis.
explanation.whyCorrect: The non-Hodgkin lymphomas that grow slowly are termed low-grade and have a good prognosis; the examples given are chronic lymphocytic leukemia/small lymphocytic lymphoma, follicular lymphoma, mucosa-associated lymphatic tissue (MALT) lymphoma, and hairy cell leukemia.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Burkitt lymphoma is a high-grade non-Hodgkin lymphoma that grows explosively.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Diffuse large B-cell lymphoma is grouped with the high-grade non-Hodgkin lymphomas.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Hodgkin lymphoma is a separate category and is not a non-Hodgkin lymphoma.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Multiple myeloma is a plasma cell neoplasm rather than a low-grade non-Hodgkin lymphoma.

questions.stem: A 9-year-old boy living in equatorial Africa develops a tumor mass that has enlarged dramatically over 3 weeks. Biopsy shows a high-grade B-cell non-Hodgkin lymphoma with a high mortality rate if untreated. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

explanation.summary: Burkitt lymphoma is a high-grade non-Hodgkin lymphoma that grows explosively and is common in Africa.
explanation.whyCorrect: High-grade non-Hodgkin lymphomas grow in an explosive fashion and have a high mortality rate; the two given examples are Burkitt lymphoma, which is common in Africa, and diffuse large B-cell lymphoma. The African setting and the rapid growth point to Burkitt lymphoma.

whyWrongByChoice.B: Chronic lymphocytic leukemia/small lymphocytic lymphoma is low grade and indolent rather than explosive.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Follicular lymphoma is a slow-growing low-grade non-Hodgkin lymphoma with a good prognosis.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Hairy cell leukemia is another low-grade disorder and does not produce an explosively growing mass.
whyWrongByChoice.E: MALT lymphoma is also grouped among the low-grade, slow-growing non-Hodgkin lymphomas.

questions.stem: A 20-year-old college student reports 2 weeks of worsening fatigue that he first blamed on poor sleep. He has had no fevers and no sore throat. On examination you palpate enlarged lymph nodes under his jaw and in both axillae. Which of the following is the most appropriate next step in management?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Begin empiric combination chemotherapy for presumed lymphoma

choices.label: B
choices.text: Obtain a bone marrow aspirate now and submit the sample for flow cytometry

choices.label: C
choices.text: Obtain a complete blood count and a monospot test for Epstein-Barr virus

choices.label: D
choices.text: Reassure him and arrange routine follow-up in 1 year without any testing

choices.label: E
choices.text: Schedule an excisional biopsy of an enlarged axillary node now

explanation.summary: Enlarged nodes in a young person are most often infectious, so the first step is a blood count and a monospot test for Epstein-Barr virus.
explanation.whyCorrect: Lymph node enlargement in a young person is more likely a viral infection such as mononucleosis, although pharyngitis and fever can be absent. The only way to really know is to do a blood count and check the monospot test for Epstein-Barr virus; if it is negative a lymph node biopsy may be needed later.

whyWrongByChoice.A: No diagnosis of lymphoma has been established, so chemotherapy is not appropriate.
whyWrongByChoice.B: A marrow aspirate with flow cytometry is an invasive step that comes after initial blood testing suggests a neoplasm.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Deferring all testing for a year ignores the possibility of a serious disorder such as lymphoma.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Biopsy would be premature at this point, since lymphoma is not yet likely and the initial blood work has not been done.

questions.stem: A patient with newly diagnosed Hodgkin lymphoma asks how her disease compares with non-Hodgkin lymphoma. Which of the following statements is most accurate?

choices.label: A
choices.text: It arises from myeloid precursors and is treated like acute myeloid leukemia

choices.label: B
choices.text: It occurs almost exclusively in infants and is uniformly fatal

choices.label: C
choices.text: It produces symptoms entirely unlike those of non-Hodgkin lymphoma

choices.label: D
choices.text: It usually occurs in adults older than 65 years of age and carries a worse prognosis

choices.label: E
choices.text: It usually occurs in young adults 15 to 34 years of age and carries a better prognosis

explanation.summary: Hodgkin lymphoma typically affects young adults aged 15 to 34 years and has a better prognosis than non-Hodgkin lymphoma.
explanation.whyCorrect: Hodgkin lymphoma usually occurs in young adults ages 15 to 34 years. Its symptoms are similar to those of non-Hodgkin lymphoma, but the disease progression and treatments differ and the prognosis is better than that of non-Hodgkin lymphoma.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Hodgkin lymphoma is a lymphoid neoplasm whose cells originate from mature B cells, not from myeloid precursors.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Hodgkin lymphoma is not an infantile disease and is not uniformly fatal.
whyWrongByChoice.C: The symptoms are actually similar to those of non-Hodgkin lymphoma; the progression and treatment differ.
whyWrongByChoice.D: The peak age is young adulthood, and the prognosis is better rather than worse than non-Hodgkin lymphoma.

questions.stem: In the classification of lymphoid neoplasms, Hodgkin lymphoma is given its own category rather than being grouped with the B-cell neoplasms. Which of the following best explains this decision?

choices.label: A
choices.text: The neoplastic cells arise from mature T cells that have acquired B-cell markers

choices.label: B
choices.text: The neoplastic cells come from mature B cells but lost B-cell gene expression

choices.label: C
choices.text: The neoplastic cells derive from plasma cells that no longer secrete immunoglobulin

choices.label: D
choices.text: The neoplastic cells originate from follicular dendritic cells within the lymph node

choices.label: E
choices.text: The neoplastic cells originate from myeloid rather than lymphoid precursors

explanation.summary: Reed-Sternberg cells come from mature B cells but have mostly lost the B-cell gene expression pattern, so Hodgkin lymphoma is kept separate from the B-cell neoplasms.
explanation.whyCorrect: The abnormal cells of Hodgkin lymphoma largely originate from mature B cells. However, because they have mostly lost their characteristic B-cell gene expression pattern and do not express B-cell markers, Hodgkin lymphoma is not included among the B-cell neoplasms.

whyWrongByChoice.A: The cells arise from mature B cells, not from T cells that acquired B-cell markers.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Plasma cell derivation defines plasma cell neoplasms such as multiple myeloma, not Hodgkin lymphoma.
whyWrongByChoice.D: The neoplastic cells are of B-cell origin rather than follicular dendritic cell origin.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Hodgkin lymphoma is a lymphoid neoplasm; its cells do not originate from myeloid precursors.

questions.stem: A patient with circulating blasts has had only a peripheral blood specimen collected. The team asks whether routine histology can be used to evaluate the process. Which of the following is the relevant limitation of routine histology here?

choices.label: A
choices.text: It cannot detect translocations in dividing cells

choices.label: B
choices.text: It detects mutations that are also present in healthy individuals

choices.label: C
choices.text: It loses tissue architecture when cells are analyzed single file

choices.label: D
choices.text: It requires acquisition of tissue and cannot be done on blood

choices.label: E
choices.text: It requires fresh tissue placed in saline or RPMI solution

explanation.summary: Routine histology requires tissue and cannot be performed on samples such as peripheral blood.
explanation.whyCorrect: Routine histology processes tissue obtained by biopsy, excision, or resection into formalin-fixed paraffin embedded blocks that are sectioned and stained with hematoxylin and eosin. Its drawback is that it requires acquisition of tissue and cannot be done with certain samples such as peripheral blood.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Detecting translocations is the province of cytogenetics; that is not the stated drawback of routine histology.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Detection of mutations that also occur in normal individuals is a drawback of molecular analysis.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Loss of architecture from breaking tissue into a single cell file is a disadvantage of flow cytometry.
whyWrongByChoice.E: The requirement for fresh tissue in saline or RPMI applies to flow cytometry, not to routine histology.

questions.stem: Molecular testing on a child newly diagnosed with B-lymphoblastic leukemia detects a BCR::ABL1 rearrangement. This result is most useful for which of the following purposes?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Confirming a diagnosis of hairy cell leukemia

choices.label: B
choices.text: Establishing that the blasts are of B-cell rather than T-cell lineage

choices.label: C
choices.text: Excluding involvement of the bone marrow by the leukemia

choices.label: D
choices.text: Indicating that the patient has a worse prognosis

choices.label: E
choices.text: Selecting a FLT3 inhibitor such as midostaurin

explanation.summary: Detection of BCR::ABL1 in B-lymphoblastic leukemia is a prognostic finding associated with worse outcome.
explanation.whyCorrect: Molecular results are used for diagnosis, prognosis, and treatment selection. Among the prognostic examples, detection of a BCR::ABL1 rearrangement in patients with B-lymphoblastic leukemia is associated with a worse prognosis.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Hairy cell leukemia is confirmed by demonstrating the BRAF V600E mutation.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Lineage is established by flow cytometry through the antigens on the cell surface, not by this rearrangement.
whyWrongByChoice.C: A molecular rearrangement says nothing about whether the marrow is involved.
whyWrongByChoice.E: FLT3 inhibitors such as midostaurin are guided by detection of a FLT3 mutation in acute myeloid leukemia.

questions.stem: In a flow cytometer, cells pass single file through a series of finely focused lasers and scatter light as they interrupt the beam. The side scatter (SSC) signal provides information about which of the following properties of the cell?

choices.label: B
choices.text: Number of chromosomes in the nucleus

choices.label: D
choices.text: Sequence of mutations carried by the cell

choices.label: E
choices.text: Viability of the cell in RPMI solution

explanation.summary: Side scatter reports cytoplasmic complexity (granularity), while forward scatter reports cell size.
explanation.whyCorrect: As a cell interrupts the last laser beam it scatters light based on its size (forward scatter, FSC), its cytoplasmic complexity (side scatter, SSC), and the antigens on its surface. SSC is therefore the measure of cytoplasmic complexity or granularity.

whyWrongByChoice.B: Chromosome number is assessed by conventional cytogenetics or FISH, not by scatter properties.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Cell size is reported by forward scatter (FSC), not side scatter.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Mutation sequences are determined by molecular methods such as PCR and next generation sequencing.
whyWrongByChoice.E: RPMI preserves cell viability for the assay but is not what the scatter signal measures.

questions.stem: A lymph node excised from a patient with suspected lymphoma is placed directly into formalin in the operating room. The following morning the clinical team requests flow cytometry on the specimen. Which of the following is the most accurate response?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Flow cytometry can proceed once the paraffin block is sectioned at 3 micrometers

choices.label: B
choices.text: Flow cytometry can proceed, because formalin preserves the surface antigens

choices.label: C
choices.text: Flow cytometry cannot be done, because lymph node is not an accepted sample type

choices.label: D
choices.text: Flow cytometry cannot be done, because the specimen contains too few cells

choices.label: E
choices.text: Flow cytometry cannot be done, because the specimen was not kept fresh

explanation.summary: Flow cytometry requires fresh tissue in saline or RPMI; a specimen placed in formalin cannot be analyzed.
explanation.whyCorrect: Flow cytometry requires fresh tissue, usually placed in saline or RPMI solution. If the specimen is placed in formalin, flow cytometry cannot be performed. RPMI is a nutritive liquid used to preserve cell viability in samples submitted for flow cytometry studies.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Sectioning a paraffin block supports routine histology and immunohistochemistry, not flow cytometry.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Formalin fixation prevents the assay rather than preserving the cells for it.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Lymph node is explicitly an appropriate sample for flow cytometry when submitted fresh.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Flow cytometry can be performed with a minimal number of cells, so cell number is not the problem here.

questions.stem: A 45-year-old man has a persistently elevated white blood cell count in which the predominant circulating cell is the neutrophil. The team is deciding which laboratory study will give the most useful information about this finding. Which of the following should be relied on?

choices.label: B
choices.text: Conventional karyotype of the peripheral blood

choices.label: C
choices.text: Excisional lymph node biopsy for routine histology

choices.label: E
choices.text: Flow cytometry of the peripheral blood

explanation.summary: Flow cytometry is not useful when the predominant blood cell is a neutrophil; the complete blood count with differential gives the best information.
explanation.whyCorrect: Flow cytometry is not useful in every indication. In cases where the predominant cell type in the blood is a neutrophil, the complete blood count and differential provide the best information.

whyWrongByChoice.B: Conventional karyotype is time-consuming and technically demanding and is not the best first source of information here.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Routine histology requires tissue and would not address a peripheral blood neutrophilia.
whyWrongByChoice.D: FISH interrogates only the chromosomes targeted by the chosen probes and does not characterize a neutrophilia.
whyWrongByChoice.E: This is precisely the setting in which flow cytometry is stated not to be useful.

questions.stem: Flow cytometry performed on a patient's B-cell lymphoma shows that the tumor cells are positive for CD20. Which of the following is the most important consequence of this result?

choices.label: A
choices.text: It confirms the presence of Reed-Sternberg cells in the specimen

choices.label: B
choices.text: It demonstrates a BRAF V600E mutation in the tumor cells

choices.label: C
choices.text: It determines the number of chromosomes within the tumor cells

choices.label: D
choices.text: It establishes that the marrow has been replaced by fibrosis

choices.label: E
choices.text: It identifies a target for antibody-based therapy with rituximab

explanation.summary: Identifying surface antigens by flow cytometry can reveal therapeutic targets, such as CD20 for rituximab.
explanation.whyCorrect: One of the listed uses of flow cytometry is identification of therapeutic targets: tumors that are positive for a certain antigen can be treated with antibody-based therapies. The given example is that CD20-positive tumors can be treated with rituximab, an antibody against CD20.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Reed-Sternberg cells are identified by their morphology on routine histology.
whyWrongByChoice.B: BRAF V600E is detected by molecular analysis of nucleic acid, not by flow cytometry.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Chromosome number is evaluated by conventional cytogenetics or FISH.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Marrow fibrosis is assessed on marrow histology, not by a surface antigen result.

questions.stem: A bone marrow sample from a patient with suspected chronic myeloid leukemia is sent for conventional cytogenetics to look for t(9;22). Which of the following must the specimen provide for this study to yield a result?

choices.label: A
choices.text: A probe directed at the chromosomes of interest

choices.label: B
choices.text: At least one million cells suspended in RPMI solution

choices.label: D
choices.text: Nucleic acid amplified by polymerase chain reaction

choices.label: E
choices.text: Viable, dividing cells examined in metaphase

explanation.summary: Conventional karyotyping studies metaphase chromosomes and therefore requires viable, dividing cells.
explanation.whyCorrect: Conventional cytogenetics (karyotype) is based on the study of metaphase chromosomes obtained from viable, dividing cells from bone marrow, peripheral blood, or tissue. It evaluates all chromosomes at once and can confirm a diagnosis of chronic myeloid leukemia with t(9;22), but the requirement for dividing cells is one reason the process is technically demanding.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Specific probes are what FISH uses, which is why FISH analyzes only selected chromosomes.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Karyotype is limited by the need for dividing cells rather than by a fixed minimum cell number in RPMI.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Paraffin blocks are the substrate for routine histology, not for metaphase karyotyping.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Amplification of nucleic acid by PCR belongs to molecular pathology.

questions.stem: A 60-year-old woman is newly diagnosed with acute myeloid leukemia, and molecular testing of the marrow detects a FLT3 mutation. This result most directly guides which of the following?

choices.label: B
choices.text: Prediction of hyperdiploidy on the karyotype

choices.label: C
choices.text: Reclassification of the leukemia as lymphoid

choices.label: D
choices.text: Selection of rituximab as antibody-based therapy

choices.label: E
choices.text: Treatment with an inhibitor such as midostaurin

explanation.summary: A FLT3 mutation in acute myeloid leukemia is a treatment-directing result that supports use of a FLT3 inhibitor.
explanation.whyCorrect: Molecular findings are used for diagnosis, prognosis, and treatment. The treatment example given is that detection of a FLT3 mutation in acute myeloid leukemia guides treatment with FLT3 inhibitors such as midostaurin.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Lymphoplasmacytic lymphoma is diagnosed by detecting the MYD88 L265P mutation, seen in more than 90% of cases.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Hyperdiploidy is a karyotype finding with prognostic value in acute lymphoblastic leukemia and is unrelated to FLT3.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Lineage is assigned by flow cytometry based on surface antigens, not by a FLT3 result.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Rituximab is directed at CD20-positive tumors identified by flow cytometry.

questions.stem: A sensitive next generation sequencing panel run on blood from an 80-year-old man reports a low-level mutation, yet the morphologic findings are unremarkable. Which of the following best explains why this molecular result must be correlated with the routine histology?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Molecular methods cannot be performed on peripheral blood samples

choices.label: B
choices.text: Molecular testing is less sensitive than a conventional karyotype

choices.label: C
choices.text: Nucleic acid extraction degrades the mutation in older patients

choices.label: D
choices.text: Polymerase chain reaction cannot distinguish DNA from RNA in a specimen

choices.label: E
choices.text: Some detected mutations also occur in normal individuals

explanation.summary: The high sensitivity of molecular testing means some mutations are found in normal people, with frequency increasing with age, so histologic correlation is essential.
explanation.whyCorrect: Because molecular techniques use nucleic acids, they are generally more sensitive than other methods. That robust sensitivity creates one of the major drawbacks of molecular analysis: some detected mutations can be seen in a percentage of normal individuals, increasing with age. Correlation of results with routine histology therefore remains essential.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Molecular analysis can be done on blood, marrow, tissue, body fluids, and fine needle aspirates.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Molecular methods are more sensitive than conventional cytogenetic analysis, not less.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Extraction does not destroy mutations in older patients; the issue is that such mutations may be nonneoplastic.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Nucleic acid extraction and amplification handle both DNA and RNA; this is not a stated limitation.

questions.stem: FISH performed on a patient with chronic lymphocytic leukemia uses a chromosome 12 probe and shows three copies of the signal, confirming trisomy 12. Compared with a conventional karyotype, which of the following is a limitation of this technique?

choices.label: A
choices.text: It can be performed only on formalin-fixed tissue

choices.label: B
choices.text: It cannot detect changes in chromosome number

choices.label: C
choices.text: It evaluates only the chromosomes selected in advance

choices.label: D
choices.text: It requires that the cells be actively dividing in metaphase

choices.label: E
choices.text: It takes substantially longer to produce a result

explanation.summary: FISH uses specific probes, so it interrogates only a selected component of the genome, unlike a karyotype that evaluates all chromosomes.
explanation.whyCorrect: FISH hybridizes fluorescently labeled probes to interphase nuclei or metaphase spreads. Because it uses only specific probes, FISH can analyze just a component of the genome, and you must know in advance which chromosomes you want to evaluate. The summary table lists its advantage as speed and its disadvantage as analyzing only select chromosomes.

whyWrongByChoice.A: FISH is not restricted to formalin-fixed tissue; it is applied to the preparations used for cytogenetic analysis.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Detecting three copies of chromosome 12 in this case shows that FISH does detect changes in chromosome number.
whyWrongByChoice.D: FISH can be applied to interphase nuclei, so it does not depend on obtaining dividing cells in metaphase.
whyWrongByChoice.E: FISH is listed as a fast method, whereas conventional karyotype is the time-consuming one.

questions.stem: A 56-year-old man with diffuse large B-cell lymphoma completes two cycles of combination chemotherapy. Imaging shows a dramatic reduction in tumor size, but disease is still detectable. He asks why he cannot simply stop, since the chemotherapy is clearly working. Which principle best explains why several additional cycles are still required?

choices.label: A
choices.text: A single adequate dose eradicates all malignant cells if given at maximum tolerated dose

choices.label: B
choices.text: Chemotherapy only becomes effective after the immune system is fully suppressed

choices.label: C
choices.text: Each dose eliminates a fixed number of tumor cells regardless of tumor size

choices.label: D
choices.text: Each dose kills a constant proportion of the remaining tumor cells

choices.label: E
choices.text: The tumor has already developed complete resistance to the regimen

explanation.summary: The log-cell kill hypothesis states chemotherapy kills a constant fraction, not a constant number, of cancer cells per dose.
explanation.whyCorrect: By the log-cell kill hypothesis, a given dose kills a constant proportion of tumor cells, reflecting first-order kinetics. Because each cycle removes only a fraction (e.g., 90-95%) of the cells that remain, a few cells persist after every dose, so multiple cycles are needed to drive the burden down to a clinically insignificant level.

whyWrongByChoice.A: The article emphasizes that a single treatment rarely eradicates all cells, which is why cycles are required.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Cytotoxic chemotherapy does not require immunosuppression to work; that is not the mechanism described.
whyWrongByChoice.C: The hypothesis specifically states a constant proportion, not a constant number, is killed per dose.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Persistent detectable disease after a good response reflects fractional killing kinetics, not established resistance.

questions.stem: A 60-year-old woman with a large but resectable breast tumor is given chemotherapy before her planned mastectomy in order to shrink the primary mass and address distant micro-metastases, making surgery easier. This treatment strategy is best described as which of the following?

explanation.summary: Neoadjuvant therapy is given before the primary treatment to shrink the tumor and micro-metastases.
explanation.whyCorrect: Neoadjuvant therapy is administered before the primary treatment (such as surgery) to shrink both the primary cancer, making it easier to resect, and distant micro-metastases. This matches the timing and intent described in the vignette.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Adjuvant therapy is given after the primary treatment to improve outcomes.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Induction therapy is the first-line treatment aimed at killing as many cancer cells as possible, not specifically pre-surgical shrinkage.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Maintenance therapy is not the strategy described; the timing here is clearly before surgery.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Salvage therapy is used only after preferred therapies have failed to produce remission.

questions.stem: A 48-year-old man undergoes complete surgical resection of a colon cancer. To reduce the risk of recurrence from residual microscopic disease, he then receives a course of chemotherapy. This post-operative chemotherapy is best classified as which of the following?

explanation.summary: Adjuvant therapy is given after the primary treatment to improve outcomes.
explanation.whyCorrect: Adjuvant therapy is defined as treatment given after the primary treatment to improve outcomes. Chemotherapy given after surgical resection to eliminate residual microscopic disease fits this definition.

whyWrongByChoice.B: Endocrine therapy is a mechanism-based class for hormone-responsive cancers, not a timing category.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Induction therapy is the first-line treatment to kill as many cancer cells as possible, not post-operative therapy.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Neoadjuvant therapy is given before, not after, the primary treatment.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Salvage therapy is reserved for cases where preferred therapies have already failed.

questions.stem: A 34-year-old man with Hodgkin lymphoma has relapsed after first-line and second-line regimens, both of which failed to produce remission. His oncologist now selects a chemotherapy regimen used specifically because all preferred therapies have been exhausted. This regimen is best described as which of the following?

explanation.summary: Salvage therapy is used when all preferred therapies have been tried and failed to produce remission.
explanation.whyCorrect: Salvage therapy is defined as treatment used when all preferred therapies have been tried and have failed to produce cancer remission. The refractory, multiply-relapsed scenario matches this definition.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Adjuvant therapy follows a primary treatment to improve outcomes, not after multiple failures.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Consolidation therapy is not the category defined by the article for this refractory setting.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Induction is the initial, first-line treatment, not the option chosen after failures.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Neoadjuvant therapy precedes a primary treatment such as surgery.

questions.stem: A patient's tumor initially responds to chemotherapy but later progresses. Laboratory analysis of the resistant tumor cells shows that they now rapidly extrude the drug via an upregulated membrane transporter, an effect promoted by tumor-derived interleukin-6. Which of the following resistance mechanisms is most consistent with these findings?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Altered DNA methylation of promoters reducing drug sensitivity

choices.label: B
choices.text: Decreased drug uptake from loss of an inward membrane transport protein

choices.label: C
choices.text: Increased efflux through the multiple drug-resistance transporter

choices.label: D
choices.text: Increased intracellular glutathione that chemically inactivates the drug

choices.label: E
choices.text: Upregulation of DNA-repair enzymes that reverse drug-induced breaks

explanation.summary: The MDR transporter pumps drug out of the cell and can be induced by cytokines such as IL-6.
explanation.whyCorrect: Cancer cells may pump the drug out as fast as it enters using the multiple drug-resistance (MDR) protein, a membrane transporter that shuttles drugs out of the cell. This efflux can arise from a direct mutation or be induced by cytokines like interleukin-6 produced by the tumor cells, matching the findings described.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Altered methylation changes gene expression and sensitivity but is not a membrane efflux mechanism.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Decreased uptake involves failure of the inward transport protein, not active efflux driven by IL-6.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Glutathione reacts with and inactivates the drug intracellularly rather than pumping it out.
whyWrongByChoice.E: DNA-repair enzyme upregulation corrects drug-induced breaks; it does not extrude the drug.

questions.stem: An oncologist explains to a trainee that a single cytotoxic drug often fails because the original tumor is not a uniform population; it contains many genetic variants, and the subset that happens to resist the drug survives and proliferates. Combination chemotherapy is used to counter this problem. Which concept does this scenario best illustrate?

explanation.summary: Tumors contain many genetic variants, and pre-existing resistant subclones can survive and expand.
explanation.whyCorrect: Cancers are not usually a uniform population but harbor many genetic variants, some of which resist a given drug and proliferate. This heterogeneity is a key reason combination chemotherapy is preferred, since a second drug may kill cells resistant to the first.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Log-cell kill describes the fractional killing per dose, not the genetic diversity of the tumor.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Myelosuppression is an adverse effect, unrelated to why monotherapy fails.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Neoadjuvant sequencing refers to timing of therapy, not tumor cell diversity.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Progression-free survival is an outcome measure, not a mechanism of resistance.

questions.stem: A 62-year-old woman receives an anthracycline as part of her chemotherapy regimen. Her care team schedules serial cardiac function monitoring because this agent is best known for which of the following characteristic adverse effects?

explanation.summary: Doxorubicin (an anthracycline) is classically associated with cardiotoxicity.
explanation.whyCorrect: The ChemoMan adverse-effect map links doxorubicin (anthracyclines) with cardiotoxicity, which is why cardiac monitoring is warranted with these agents.

whyWrongByChoice.B: Hemorrhagic cystitis is associated with cyclophosphamide.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Ototoxicity is linked to cisplatin and carboplatin.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Peripheral neuropathy is associated with the vinca alkaloids.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Pulmonary fibrosis is characteristic of bleomycin and busulfan, not anthracyclines.

questions.stem: A 27-year-old man treated for testicular cancer develops progressive dyspnea and a dry cough. Pulmonary function testing shows a restrictive pattern with reduced diffusing capacity, and imaging suggests interstitial fibrosis. Which chemotherapeutic agent in his regimen most likely caused this finding?

explanation.summary: Bleomycin characteristically causes pulmonary fibrosis.
explanation.whyCorrect: The ChemoMan map associates bleomycin (along with busulfan) with pulmonary fibrosis, which fits the restrictive lung disease and interstitial fibrosis described.

whyWrongByChoice.B: Cyclophosphamide is linked to hemorrhagic cystitis.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Cytarabine is associated with keratitis and conjunctivitis.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Doxorubicin is associated with cardiotoxicity, not pulmonary fibrosis.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Vincristine causes peripheral neuropathy.

questions.stem: A 55-year-old man receiving cisplatin-based chemotherapy develops a rising serum creatinine along with new high-frequency hearing loss and tinnitus. These adverse effects are most characteristic of which drug class?

explanation.summary: Platinum agents such as cisplatin and carboplatin cause nephrotoxicity and ototoxicity.
explanation.whyCorrect: The ChemoMan map links cisplatin/carboplatin (platinum agents) to both nephrotoxicity and ototoxicity, matching the rising creatinine and hearing loss with tinnitus described.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Alkylating agents such as cyclophosphamide cause hemorrhagic cystitis.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Anthracyclines such as doxorubicin cause cardiotoxicity.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Antimetabolites such as cytarabine cause keratitis/conjunctivitis and methotrexate causes myelosuppression.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Vinca alkaloids cause peripheral neuropathy.

questions.stem: A 40-year-old woman receiving chemotherapy develops gross hematuria and suprapubic pain, and cystoscopy shows diffuse bladder mucosal inflammation and bleeding. This adverse effect is most characteristic of which agent?

explanation.summary: Cyclophosphamide is classically associated with hemorrhagic cystitis.
explanation.whyCorrect: The ChemoMan map links cyclophosphamide to hemorrhagic cystitis, which matches the hematuria, suprapubic pain, and inflamed bleeding bladder mucosa described.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Bleomycin is associated with pulmonary fibrosis.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Doxorubicin is associated with cardiotoxicity.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Irinotecan is associated with severe acute and delayed diarrhea.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Methotrexate is associated with myelosuppression.

questions.stem: A 58-year-old man being treated with a vinca alkaloid develops distal numbness, tingling, and diminished ankle reflexes. Consistent with this agent's mechanism, vinca alkaloids exert their cytotoxic effect primarily by acting on which of the following?

choices.label: A
choices.text: DNA cross-linking at guanine independent of the cell cycle

choices.label: B
choices.text: Estrogen receptor signaling in hormone-responsive tissue

choices.label: C
choices.text: Microtubules of the mitotic spindle during M phase

choices.label: D
choices.text: Nucleotide synthesis by folate-dependent enzymes during S phase

explanation.summary: Vinca alkaloids are microtubule inhibitors that act during mitosis and cause peripheral neuropathy.
explanation.whyCorrect: The cell-cycle diagram places vinca alkaloids (with taxanes) among microtubule inhibitors that act at mitosis (M phase), interfering with the spindle. Clinically, vinca alkaloids are also linked to peripheral neuropathy, matching the sensory symptoms described.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Cell cycle-independent DNA cross-linking describes alkylating and platinum agents.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Estrogen receptor signaling is the target of endocrine therapy such as tamoxifen.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Targeting S-phase nucleotide synthesis is the mechanism of antimetabolites such as cytarabine and methotrexate.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Topoisomerase inhibition is the mechanism of irinotecan.

questions.stem: A 61-year-old woman with an estrogen receptor-positive breast cancer is started on tamoxifen. This drug is an example of which category of cancer therapy?

explanation.summary: Endocrine therapy treats hormone-responsive cancers by blocking or modulating hormones; tamoxifen is the example for ER-positive breast cancer.
explanation.whyCorrect: Endocrine therapy treats specific hormone-responsive cancers by blocking or modulating certain hormones. The article gives tamoxifen used for estrogen receptor-positive breast cancer as the prototypical example.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Alkylating chemotherapy is a cytotoxic subtype that cross-links DNA, not a hormone-modulating therapy.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Cytotoxic chemotherapy uses cellular poisons to prevent growth and replication; methotrexate is its example.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Immunotherapy helps the immune system attack cancer, exemplified by pembrolizumab.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Molecularly targeted therapy hits specific receptors/pathways, exemplified by imatinib in CML.

questions.stem: A 62-year-old man is newly diagnosed with acute myeloid leukemia. He is started on the regimen considered first-line, or best, for his disease, given with the aim of killing as many cancer cells as possible. This treatment is best described as which of the following?

explanation.summary: Induction therapy is the first-line, or best, treatment for a particular cancer, given to kill as many cancer cells as possible.
explanation.whyCorrect: Chemotherapy is classified by timing, and induction therapy is defined as the first-line (best) treatment for a particular cancer, intended to kill as many cancer cells as possible. That is exactly the intent described for this newly diagnosed patient.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Adjuvant therapy is given after the primary treatment to improve outcomes.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Maintenance therapy is not the first-line regimen used at diagnosis to maximize cell kill.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Neoadjuvant therapy is given before a primary treatment to shrink the primary cancer and distant micro-metastases.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Salvage therapy is used only after all preferred therapies have been tried and failed to produce remission.

questions.stem: A trial of a new anticancer agent reports the period after treatment during which the patients' disease did not get worse. Which term best describes this outcome measure?

explanation.summary: Progression-free survival is the period after treatment in which a patient's disease does not get worse.
explanation.whyCorrect: Progression-free survival is defined as the period after the treatment in which a patient's disease does not get worse. It is explicitly distinguished from overall survival, which measures how long the patient lives after treatment.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Log-cell kill describes the fractional killing of tumor cells per dose.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Overall survival refers to the length of time after treatment that the patient lives, not the time without worsening.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Growth fraction describes the proportion of dividing cells in a tumor, not a treatment outcome measure.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Tumor-doubling time describes how fast a tumor grows, not the interval free of progression.

questions.stem: A 45-year-old woman with chronic myelogenous leukemia is started on imatinib, a drug chosen because it acts on a specific cellular receptor and signaling pathway in her tumor. This agent is an example of which category of cancer therapy?

explanation.summary: Molecularly targeted therapy acts on specific cellular receptors and molecular pathways; imatinib in chronic myelogenous leukemia is the example.
explanation.whyCorrect: Molecularly targeted therapy targets specific cellular receptors and molecular pathways and includes signal transduction inhibitors. Imatinib used for chronic myelogenous leukemia is given as the prototypical example of this category.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Alkylating chemotherapy is a cytotoxic subtype acting on DNA, not a receptor-directed agent.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Immunotherapy helps the immune system attack cancer cells, as with pembrolizumab.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Cytotoxic chemotherapy uses cellular poisons to prevent cell growth and replication; methotrexate is its example.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Endocrine therapy blocks or modulates hormones in hormone-responsive cancers, as with tamoxifen.

questions.stem: A 58-year-old man with advanced melanoma begins pembrolizumab. Which of the following best describes how this drug produces its antitumor effect?

choices.label: A
choices.text: It blocks estrogen receptor signaling in hormone-responsive tissue

choices.label: B
choices.text: It blocks the cancer cells' protective mechanism against immune cells

choices.label: C
choices.text: It cross-links tumor cell DNA regardless of the cell cycle phase

choices.label: D
choices.text: It disrupts the microtubules of the mitotic spindle during mitosis

choices.label: E
choices.text: It inhibits an abnormal signaling kinase produced by the tumor cells

explanation.summary: Immunotherapy such as pembrolizumab helps the immune system attack cancer by blocking the protective mechanism of cancer cells.
explanation.whyCorrect: Immunotherapy helps the immune system attack cancer cells, including by blocking the protective mechanism of cancer cells so that immune cells can destroy the cancer. Pembrolizumab is the example given, used for many advanced cancers including melanoma and cervical cancer.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Blocking estrogen receptor signaling describes endocrine therapy such as tamoxifen.
whyWrongByChoice.C: DNA cross-linking independent of the cell cycle describes alkylating and platinum agents.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Microtubule disruption describes the taxanes and vinca alkaloids.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Kinase inhibition in the tumor describes molecularly targeted therapy such as imatinib.

questions.stem: A 49-year-old woman has taken methotrexate for rheumatoid arthritis. Her oncologist explains that the same drug is used in some cancers because it acts as a cellular poison that prevents cell growth and replication. Methotrexate is the prototype of which category of cancer therapy?

explanation.summary: Cytotoxic chemotherapy uses cellular poisons to prevent cell growth and replication; methotrexate is the listed example.
explanation.whyCorrect: Cytotoxic chemotherapy is defined as therapy that uses cellular poisons to prevent cell growth and replication, and methotrexate, used for rheumatoid arthritis and some cancers, is given as the example of this class.

whyWrongByChoice.B: Endocrine therapy blocks or modulates hormones in hormone-responsive cancers, exemplified by tamoxifen.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Immunotherapy enables immune cells to destroy the cancer, exemplified by pembrolizumab.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Molecularly targeted therapy acts on specific cellular receptors and pathways, exemplified by imatinib.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Signal transduction inhibition is a form of molecularly targeted therapy, not a cellular poison.

questions.stem: A new regimen lengthens the period after treatment during which patients' disease does not worsen, but the length of time patients live after treatment is no different from the comparator regimen. The measure that was unchanged is best described as which of the following?

explanation.summary: Overall survival is the length of time after treatment that the patient lives, and it is not the same as progression-free survival.
explanation.whyCorrect: Overall survival refers to the length of time after treatment that the patient lives. Progression-free survival, the time without worsening disease, improved here, but these are explicitly not the same measure, so the unchanged endpoint is overall survival.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Growth fraction refers to the proportion of proliferating tumor cells.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Log-cell kill describes the constant fraction of cells killed per dose.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Progression-free survival is the measure that improved in this trial, not the one that was unchanged.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Tumor burden is the number of tumor cells present, not a survival endpoint.

questions.stem: A tumor is estimated to contain approximately 10^12 cells. A cycle of chemotherapy produces a 3-log kill. Approximately how many tumor cells remain after this cycle?

explanation.summary: A 3-log kill reduces the tumor cell number by three orders of magnitude, from 10^12 to 10^9.
explanation.whyCorrect: Because cell kill follows first-order kinetics, the magnitude of tumor cell reduction is logarithmic. A tumor of 10^12 cells subjected to a 3-log kill is reduced to 10^9 cells, the specific example used to illustrate the log-cell kill hypothesis.

whyWrongByChoice.A: 10^11 would represent only a 1-log reduction, not the 3-log kill described.
whyWrongByChoice.B: 10^3 would represent a 9-log reduction, far more than a 3-log kill.
whyWrongByChoice.C: 10^6 would require a 6-log kill from a starting burden of 10^12 cells.
whyWrongByChoice.E: A single treatment rarely eradicates all cells, which is precisely why multiple cycles are required.

questions.stem: A small tumor is estimated to contain about 1,000 cells, and each dose of the chosen drug eliminates about 95% of the cells present at the time it is given. Approximately how many tumor cells remain after the second dose?

explanation.summary: Fractional killing of 95% per dose leaves about 50 cells after the first dose and about two after the second.
explanation.whyCorrect: Each dose kills a constant proportion of the cells remaining at that moment. Starting from 1,000 cells, a 95% kill leaves about 50 cells; a second dose kills 95% of those 50, leaving about two cells.

whyWrongByChoice.A: About 100 cells would require a much smaller fractional kill per dose.
whyWrongByChoice.C: About 50 cells is the number remaining after the first dose, not the second.
whyWrongByChoice.D: About 500 would correspond to a 50% kill after a single dose, not two doses at 95%.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Even after repeated doses a few cells persist, which is why multiple cycles are needed.

questions.stem: A fellow is asked in which clinical setting the log-cell kill hypothesis most closely predicts the response to cytotoxic chemotherapy. Which of the following is the most appropriate answer?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Hormone-responsive cancers managed with endocrine therapy

choices.label: B
choices.text: Large solid tumors whose growth has slowed as they enlarged

choices.label: C
choices.text: Rapidly dividing malignancies such as acute leukemias

choices.label: D
choices.text: Tumors that already express the multiple drug-resistance protein

choices.label: E
choices.text: Tumors whose expansion is restricted by a limited blood supply

explanation.summary: The log-cell kill principle is most applicable to rapidly dividing malignancies such as acute leukemias and aggressive lymphomas.
explanation.whyCorrect: The fractional-kill principle is most applicable to rapidly dividing malignancies such as acute leukemias and aggressive lymphomas, where a high proportion of cells are cycling and each dose removes a predictable fraction.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Endocrine therapy for hormone-responsive cancer is a separate treatment category, not the setting this kinetic model describes.
whyWrongByChoice.B: In solid tumors growth rates slow as the tumor enlarges, so treatment responses are more variable.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Expression of the multiple drug-resistance protein produces drug efflux and treatment failure rather than predictable fractional kill.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Limitations in blood supply are precisely what slow solid tumor growth and make responses less predictable.

questions.stem: A bulky solid tumor responds less predictably to cytotoxic chemotherapy than an aggressive lymphoma of comparable size. Which of the following best explains why the growth rate of the enlarging solid tumor has slowed?

choices.label: A
choices.text: A shift of the drugs toward cell cycle-independent action

choices.label: B
choices.text: Killing of a constant number rather than a constant fraction of cells

choices.label: C
choices.text: Limitations in blood supply as the tumor mass enlarges

choices.label: D
choices.text: Loss of the protein that transports drug into the cell

choices.label: E
choices.text: Upregulation of DNA-repair enzymes within tumor cells

explanation.summary: Solid tumor growth rates slow with increasing size because of limitations in blood supply, making treatment responses more variable.
explanation.whyCorrect: In solid tumors, growth rates slow as tumors enlarge due to limitations in blood supply. Because fewer cells are actively dividing, responses to cytotoxic chemotherapy are more variable than in rapidly dividing leukemias and aggressive lymphomas.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Cell cycle independence is a property of certain drug classes, not an explanation for the tumor's growth rate.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Chemotherapy kills a constant proportion of cells; constant-number killing is not the model described.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Loss of the inward transport protein is a resistance mechanism affecting drug entry, not growth kinetics.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Upregulated DNA repair is a mechanism of acquired drug resistance, not of slowed tumor growth.

questions.stem: A chemotherapy regimen is written as an intensive drug dose followed by a defined recovery period before the next cycle begins. What is the primary purpose of the recovery period between cycles?

choices.label: A
choices.text: To allow resistant subclones to be identified before re-dosing

choices.label: B
choices.text: To allow the patient's rapidly dividing normal tissues to regenerate

choices.label: C
choices.text: To let the drug reach steady-state concentrations in the tumor

choices.label: D
choices.text: To let the tumor become responsive to hormonal blockade

choices.label: E
