whyWrongByChoice.E: The total WBC count alone does not reveal which specific cell line is increased or decreased.

questions.stem: A 3-day-old male newborn is evaluated before discharge. He is afebrile, feeding well, and his physical examination is normal. A complete blood count shows a white blood cell count of 21,000/mm3 with a normal differential and normal-appearing cells on the smear. Which of the following best characterizes this white blood cell count?

choices.label: A
choices.text: A count within the normal range for his age

choices.label: C
choices.text: Leukemoid reaction to an occult infection

choices.label: E
choices.text: Neoplastic leukocytosis of the bone marrow

explanation.summary: The normal WBC range varies with age, and newborns have a much wider and higher normal range (9000-30,000 cells/mm3) than adults.
explanation.whyCorrect: The WBC count is the total number of WBCs per mm3 of blood, and the normal range varies according to age. Newborns have a normal range of 9000 to 30,000 cells/mm3, children under age 2 have a range of 6200 to 17,000 cells/mm3, and adults and children over age 2 have a range of 4000 to 11,000 cells/mm3. A count of 21,000/mm3 in a 3-day-old is therefore normal; the same count would be distinctly high in an adult.

whyWrongByChoice.B: Demargination raises the mature neutrophil count above the age-specific normal range in settings such as stress or steroid use, neither of which applies here.
whyWrongByChoice.C: A leukemoid reaction includes neutrophil precursors on the smear and follows infection or inflammation; this infant is afebrile with a normal differential.
whyWrongByChoice.D: A leukoerythroblastic reaction requires both immature neutrophils and nucleated red blood cells on the smear.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Neoplastic leukocytosis is caused by a bone marrow neoplasm and is often associated with counts of 100,000/mm3 or more.

questions.stem: An automated hematology analyzer reports a white blood cell count on an EDTA specimen without any slide being examined by a technologist. Which of the following sets of parameters does the instrument use to separate white blood cells from red blood cells and platelets?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Cell size, internal complexity, and DNA/RNA content

choices.label: B
choices.text: Hemoglobin content, cell shape, and membrane charge

choices.label: C
choices.text: Nuclear lobe count, granule color, and cell diameter

choices.label: D
choices.text: Sedimentation rate, cell density, and staining intensity

choices.label: E
choices.text: Surface immunoglobulin, cytoplasmic pH, and cell volume

explanation.summary: Automated analyzers separate WBCs from other cells using cell size, internal complexity, and DNA/RNA content rather than visual inspection.
explanation.whyCorrect: The machine cannot see the cells the way a technologist does on a smear. It uses parameters such as cell size, internal complexity, and DNA/RNA content to determine which cells are which. WBCs are much larger than RBCs and platelets and are also much more complex because they have nuclei and granules, so the automated count is usually very accurate and more reliable than an estimate from a smear.

whyWrongByChoice.B: Hemoglobin content is measured as a separate red cell index and is not how the instrument classifies leukocytes.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Nuclear lobe count and granule color are morphologic features assessed by manual smear review, not by the analyzer.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Sedimentation rate and staining intensity are separate laboratory measurements and are not used to classify cells on the analyzer.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Surface immunoglobulin and cytoplasmic pH are not parameters used by the automated counter.

questions.stem: A hospitalized patient's automated differential reports only neutrophils, lymphocytes, monocytes, eosinophils, and basophils. A pathologist who later reviews the flagged slide reports numerous metamyelocytes and myelocytes. Which of the following best explains why these cells were not reported by the instrument?

choices.label: A
choices.text: The instrument converts all values to percentages and discards them

choices.label: B
choices.text: The instrument is capable of only a 5-part differential

choices.label: C
choices.text: The instrument measures only the total count, not cell types

choices.label: D
choices.text: The instrument reports lymphocyte subsets in place of granulocytes

choices.label: E
choices.text: The instrument reports red cell morphology in place of cell types

explanation.summary: Automated instruments perform only a 5-part differential, so abnormal or precursor cells trigger a flag for technologist or pathologist slide review.
explanation.whyCorrect: The caveat of automated counting is that the instrument is only capable of doing a 5-part differential: neutrophils, lymphocytes, monocytes, eosinophils, and basophils. If abnormal cells are present or the WBC count or differential is abnormal, the instrument flags the specimen so a slide is made for technologist or pathologist review, which is how precursor cells such as metamyelocytes and myelocytes are identified.

whyWrongByChoice.A: The differential is reported both as percentages and as absolute numbers for each of the five types.
whyWrongByChoice.C: The instrument reports both a total WBC count and an automated differential of the five mature cell types.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Lymphocyte subset analysis is a different test and is not part of the automated differential.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Red blood cell indices are reported separately and do not replace the white cell differential.

questions.stem: A normal adult differential count is being reviewed. Which of the following white blood cell types normally makes up the largest percentage of the total white blood cell count?

explanation.summary: Neutrophils comprise the largest share of the normal adult differential, at 57% to 67% of the total WBC count.
explanation.whyCorrect: In the normal adult differential, neutrophils account for 57% to 67% of the total WBC count (an absolute count of 2500 to 7400/mm3), more than any other cell type. Lymphocytes are the second most numerous cell type.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Basophils are the least numerous, at less than 1% and under 110/mm3.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Eosinophils make up only 1% to 3% of the differential, or 45 to 330/mm3.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Lymphocytes are second most abundant at 25% to 33%, or 1125 to 3630/mm3.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Monocytes make up only 3% to 7% of the differential, or 135 to 770/mm3.

questions.stem: A 25-year-old man has a white blood cell count of 10,000/mm3. His differential shows 56% neutrophils, 32% lymphocytes, 5% monocytes, 6% eosinophils, and 1% basophils, and all cells appear normal on the smear. Which of the following abnormalities is present?

explanation.summary: Absolute counts are obtained by multiplying the total WBC count by each percentage; here only the eosinophil count exceeds its threshold (>500/mm3).
explanation.whyCorrect: Multiplying the total WBC count by each percentage gives 5600 neutrophils, 3200 lymphocytes, 500 monocytes, 600 eosinophils, and 100 basophils per mm3. Eosinophilia is defined as an eosinophil count above 500/mm3, so only the eosinophil line is abnormal despite a normal total WBC count.

whyWrongByChoice.A: The absolute basophil count of 100/mm3 is far below the 300/mm3 threshold for basophilia.
whyWrongByChoice.C: The absolute lymphocyte count of 3200/mm3 is below the 4000/mm3 threshold for lymphocytosis.
whyWrongByChoice.D: The absolute monocyte count of 500/mm3 is below the 800/mm3 threshold for monocytosis.
whyWrongByChoice.E: The absolute neutrophil count of 5600/mm3 is below the 7700/mm3 threshold for neutrophilia.

questions.stem: A 58-year-old woman with rheumatoid arthritis has a white blood cell count of 12,000/mm3 with 75% neutrophils. The smear shows only normally segmented mature neutrophils without toxic changes, and no nucleated red blood cells are seen. Which of the following best describes her findings?

explanation.summary: Benign neutrophilia is a neutrophil count above 7700/mm3 not caused by a hematopoietic neoplasm, and it is mature when all circulating neutrophils are normal segmented forms.
explanation.whyCorrect: Her absolute neutrophil count is 9000/mm3 (12,000 x 0.75), which exceeds the 7700/mm3 threshold for neutrophilia. Because all of the cells are normal mature neutrophils with normal nuclear segmentation and there is no neoplasm, this is benign mature neutrophilia, which commonly occurs in response to inflammation such as her rheumatoid arthritis.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Immature neutrophilia requires precursor cells such as myelocytes or metamyelocytes on the smear, which are absent here.
whyWrongByChoice.C: A leukoerythroblastic reaction requires both immature neutrophils and nucleated red blood cells in the blood.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Neoplastic leukocytosis is caused by a bone marrow neoplasm and is often associated with counts of 100,000/mm3 or more.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Reactive lymphocytosis involves an increased proportion of abnormal-appearing lymphocytes, not neutrophils.

questions.stem: A 62-year-old man has a white blood cell count of 1800/mm3, and the differential shows decreased absolute counts of neutrophils, lymphocytes, and monocytes. Which of the following causes of leukopenia best accounts for depletion of all of these subsets?

explanation.summary: Depletion of all WBC subsets points to bone marrow failure, whereas most other causes of cytopenia affect a single line.
explanation.whyCorrect: Depletion of one or more types of WBCs carries the suffix -penia. It can be due to infection (which may cause neutropenia and/or lymphopenia), bone marrow failure, or immune diseases. Bone marrow failure is the cause that produces depletion of all subsets, because the marrow can no longer produce any of the lines; it may result from malignancy, toxins, or other unknown causes.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Allergic reactions raise the eosinophil count rather than depleting leukocytes.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Helminthic infections are a classic cause of eosinophilia, not of generalized leukopenia.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Immune diseases typically cause lymphopenia rather than depletion of every subset.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Stress raises the neutrophil count through demargination and can cause a transient lymphocytosis, not a pancytopenia.

questions.stem: A 6-year-old boy with fatigue and easy bruising has a white blood cell count of 75,000/mm3 composed largely of lymphoblasts, and his absolute neutrophil count is 300/mm3. Which of the following best explains the dangerously low number of normal white blood cells despite the very high total count?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Demargination has emptied the marginated neutrophil pool

choices.label: B
choices.text: Marrow fibrosis is releasing nucleated red blood cells early

choices.label: C
choices.text: Normal neutrophils were consumed destroying circulating pathogens

choices.label: D
choices.text: The analyzer has miscategorized mature cells as blast forms

choices.label: E
choices.text: The malignant blasts have crowded out normal precursors

explanation.summary: In acute lymphoblastic leukemia, malignant lymphoblasts crowd out normal hematopoietic precursors, so the total WBC count skyrockets while normal WBCs fall dangerously low.
explanation.whyCorrect: In acute lymphoblastic leukemia, malignant lymphoblasts proliferate in the bone marrow and crowd out normal hematopoietic precursors. As the malignant cells pour into the blood, the WBC count skyrockets, but the normal WBCs drop to a dangerously low level, which is why his absolute neutrophil count is only 300/mm3.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Demargination moves mature neutrophils into the circulating pool and raises, rather than lowers, the neutrophil count.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Marrow fibrosis produces a leukoerythroblastic picture with nucleated red cells and immature neutrophils, not circulating lymphoblasts.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Consumption of neutrophils in pathogen destruction produces toxic changes such as vacuolization, not a blast-filled blood picture.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Miscategorization by the analyzer is corrected on smear review and would not explain a genuinely low absolute neutrophil count.

questions.stem: A 7-year-old girl has a 3-day history of fever, rhinorrhea, and nonproductive cough consistent with a viral upper respiratory infection. Which of the following differential findings is most expected?

explanation.summary: Looking at the differential gives clues to the type of infection: viral infections raise the lymphocyte count.
explanation.whyCorrect: Infection is among the most common causes of leukocytosis, and the differential points toward the type of organism. Viral infections raise the lymphocyte count, bacterial infections increase both mature and immature neutrophils, and parasitic infections raise the eosinophil count.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Basophilia is the least common form of benign leukocytosis and is associated with allergies, hypothyroidism, and certain infections such as influenza and tuberculosis.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Eosinophils rise with parasitic infections, allergies, asthma, and drug reactions rather than with common viral illnesses.
whyWrongByChoice.D: An increase in both mature and immature neutrophils is the typical pattern of bacterial infection.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Nucleated red blood cells appear in a leukoerythroblastic reaction, not in a routine viral illness.

questions.stem: A 47-year-old man recovering from pneumonia has a monocyte count of 1100/mm3 along with a mildly elevated neutrophil count. Which of the following best characterizes his elevated monocyte count?

choices.label: A
choices.text: It indicates an allergic or toxic reaction to a drug

choices.label: B
choices.text: It is a nonspecific finding that parallels neutrophilia

choices.label: C
choices.text: It is specific for an underlying myeloproliferative neoplasm

choices.label: D
choices.text: It points to an underlying helminthic worm infection

choices.label: E
choices.text: It signals depletion of the marrow granulocyte reserve

explanation.summary: Monocytosis (>800/mm3) is a fairly nonspecific finding because the conditions that raise neutrophils also raise monocytes.
explanation.whyCorrect: Monocytosis is an elevated monocyte count above 800/mm3. It is a fairly nonspecific finding because many conditions that cause neutrophilia also affect monocytes: monocytes can increase in any of the conditions in which neutrophils increase, including infection, inflammation, and medications.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Toxic or allergic drug reactions characteristically produce eosinophilia.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Basophilia, not monocytosis, is the finding classically associated with myeloproliferative disorders such as chronic myeloid leukemia.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Helminthic worm infections characteristically raise the eosinophil count.
whyWrongByChoice.E: A rise in monocytes does not indicate marrow depletion; depletion of a cell line is designated by the suffix -penia.

questions.stem: A 44-year-old woman reports fatigue, cold intolerance, weight gain, and constipation. Her white blood cell count is 9000/mm3 with an absolute basophil count of 420/mm3. She has no allergic symptoms and no recent infection. Which of the following is the most likely cause of her basophilia?

explanation.summary: Basophilia (>300/mm3) has a short benign differential: allergies, hypothyroidism, and certain infections such as influenza and tuberculosis.
explanation.whyCorrect: Basophilia is an elevated basophil count above 300/mm3 and is the least common type of benign leukocytosis. Its common benign causes are allergies, hypothyroidism, and certain infections such as influenza and tuberculosis. Her cold intolerance, weight gain, fatigue, and constipation point to hypothyroidism as the explanation.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Corticosteroids produce a mature neutrophilia through demargination, not an isolated basophilia.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Epstein-Barr virus infection causes a reactive lymphocytosis with Downey cells.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Helminthic infection is a classic cause of eosinophilia rather than basophilia.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Tobacco smoking is listed among the causes of benign mature neutrophilia, not basophilia.

questions.stem: A healthy 35-year-old man is evaluated for a mildly elevated neutrophil count on a specimen drawn at 4 PM. A repeat specimen drawn the following day at 7 AM shows a lower neutrophil count. He is asymptomatic and takes no medications. Which of the following best explains the difference between the two specimens?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Counts are normally lowest in the morning and highest in late afternoon

choices.label: B
choices.text: Counts are reported as percentages that shift with the lymphocyte count

choices.label: C
choices.text: Counts fall during an overnight fast and rise after meals

choices.label: D
choices.text: Counts rise overnight as circulating cells return to the vessel wall

choices.label: E
choices.text: Counts vary with the interval since the most recent medication dose

explanation.summary: The neutrophil count varies with the time of day, being lowest in the morning and highest in the late afternoon.
explanation.whyCorrect: Benign mature neutrophilia has several causes besides bacterial infection and inflammation, including stress, smoking tobacco, medications such as corticosteroids and G-CSF, and even the time of day: the neutrophil count is lowest in the morning and highest in the late afternoon. The two specimens are consistent with this normal diurnal variation.

whyWrongByChoice.B: Both specimens report an absolute neutrophil count, and absolute counts rather than percentages are most important in diagnosis.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Fasting and meals are not among the listed influences on the neutrophil count.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Cells returning to the marginated pool would be described as the reverse of demargination, and the variation described here is a normal daily pattern rather than an overnight shift.
whyWrongByChoice.E: He takes no medications, so drug timing cannot explain the difference.

questions.stem: Which of the following is a recognized benign cause of an increased mature neutrophil count?

explanation.summary: Benign mature neutrophilia is usually a response to bacterial infection or inflammation, but stress, tobacco smoking, medications, and time of day also raise the count.
explanation.whyCorrect: Benign mature neutrophilia usually occurs in response to bacterial infection or inflammation. Other recognized causes include stress, smoking tobacco, medications such as corticosteroids and granulocyte colony stimulating factor, and the time of day.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Enteroviruses such as coxsackievirus cause infectious lymphocytosis in children.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Epstein-Barr virus infection produces a reactive lymphocytosis with Downey type II cells.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Helminthic infections raise the eosinophil count rather than the neutrophil count.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Hypothyroidism is a common cause of basophilia.

questions.stem: A 60-year-old woman receiving granulocyte colony stimulating factor after chemotherapy has a rising white blood cell count, and her smear shows bands and metamyelocytes without toxic granulation or vacuolization. She is afebrile with no localizing signs of infection, and no nucleated red blood cells are present. Which of the following best explains the immature neutrophils on her smear?

explanation.summary: Besides infection, a left shift can be produced by inflammatory disease and by certain chemotherapy drugs such as G-CSF.
explanation.whyCorrect: A left shift refers to the presence of immature neutrophils such as bands, metamyelocytes, and promyelocytes in the blood. The most common reason is infection, but it is also seen in inflammatory disease such as systemic lupus erythematosus and rheumatoid arthritis and with the use of certain chemotherapy drugs, notably G-CSF, which is exactly the setting here.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Demargination moves mature neutrophils into the circulation and does not release precursor forms.
whyWrongByChoice.B: A leukoerythroblastic reaction requires nucleated red blood cells in addition to immature neutrophils, and none are present.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Reactive lymphocytosis involves enlarged abnormal-appearing lymphocytes, not neutrophil precursors.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Sepsis would be expected to produce toxic changes such as cytoplasmic vacuolization along with fever, neither of which is present.

questions.stem: A blood smear from a patient with benign mature neutrophilia is reviewed. Which of the following nuclear findings is expected in the increased neutrophils?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Bilobed nuclei with abundant basophilic cytoplasm

explanation.summary: In mature neutrophilia the neutrophil count is increased but every cell is a normal mature neutrophil with 2 to 5 nuclear lobes.
explanation.whyCorrect: In benign mature neutrophilia, the neutrophil count is increased and the cells are all normal mature neutrophils with normal nuclear segmentation of 2 to 5 lobes. The presence of precursor forms would instead indicate immature neutrophilia.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Bilobed nuclei with abundant basophilic cytoplasm describe reactive lymphocytes.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Myelocytes and metamyelocytes are precursor cells and are the hallmark of benign immature neutrophilia.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Round nuclei with prominent nucleoli describe blast cells, which are seen in acute leukemia.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Band forms are unsegmented precursors and indicate a left shift, which defines immature rather than mature neutrophilia.

questions.stem: A 55-year-old man with pyelonephritis has a white blood cell count of 45,000/mm3, and his smear shows bands, metamyelocytes, and myelocytes together with mature neutrophils. Which of the following is most likely to occur after his infection is treated?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Nucleated red blood cells will appear on the smear

choices.label: B
choices.text: Reactive lymphocytes will come to predominate

choices.label: D
choices.text: The count will fall to leukopenic levels

choices.label: E
choices.text: The count will return to normal

explanation.summary: A leukemoid reaction is a benign increase in neutrophils and their precursors driven by infection or another non-cancerous disease, and the count normalizes once that disease is treated.
explanation.whyCorrect: A leukemoid reaction describes an increase in neutrophils that occurs because of an infection or a disease other than cancer. Unlike mature neutrophilia, the increment includes both neutrophils and their precursors such as bands, metamyelocytes, and myelocytes. The WBC count generally returns to normal following treatment of the infection or disease.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Nucleated red blood cells define a leukoerythroblastic reaction, which is a different pattern of immature neutrophilia.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Reactive lymphocytes are seen in viral infections and drug reactions rather than after treatment of a bacterial infection.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Counts of 100,000/mm3 or more characterize neoplastic leukocytosis such as chronic myeloid leukemia, not a treated leukemoid reaction.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Leukopenia follows bone marrow failure or certain infections, not resolution of a leukemoid reaction.

questions.stem: A 68-year-old man has immature neutrophils and nucleated red blood cells on his peripheral smear, and a bone marrow biopsy shows widespread fibrosis. Which of the following best explains the presence of these immature cells in his blood?

choices.label: A
choices.text: A viral infection has stimulated reactive cell production

choices.label: B
choices.text: Lysosomal degranulation has released precursors from the marrow

choices.label: C
choices.text: Scar tissue fills the marrow space, so cells leave before maturing

choices.label: D
choices.text: Stress has driven marginated neutrophils into the circulation

choices.label: E
choices.text: The analyzer has miscategorized mature cells as precursor forms

explanation.summary: A leukoerythroblastic reaction can be ominous: a neoplasm or widespread fibrosis fills the marrow space, so immature cells leave home early.
explanation.whyCorrect: A leukoerythroblastic reaction, sometimes called a myelophthisic process, can represent a normal marrow response in severe anemia, but it can also have more ominous implications. A neoplasm or widespread fibrosis can fill up the bone marrow space, leaving little room for normal cells to mature, so they leave home early and can be seen in the peripheral blood.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Viral infection produces lymphocytosis with reactive lymphocytes rather than a leukoerythroblastic picture.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Lysosomal degranulation within neutrophils causes cytoplasmic vacuolization, a toxic change, not release of precursors.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Demargination releases mature neutrophils already in the vasculature and does not produce nucleated red blood cells.
whyWrongByChoice.E: The immature cells were confirmed on the smear and on marrow biopsy, so they are not an analyzer artifact.

questions.stem: Two hospitalized patients each have immature neutrophils on the peripheral smear. One has a leukemoid reaction and the other has a leukoerythroblastic reaction. Which of the following findings is most characteristic of the patient with the leukoerythroblastic reaction?

explanation.summary: Leukemoid reactions present with signs of the underlying infection or inflammation, while leukoerythroblastic reactions present with signs and symptoms of anemia.
explanation.whyCorrect: Patients with leukoerythroblastic reactions most often present with signs and symptoms of anemia, including pallor, an unhealthy paleness of the skin, and symptoms such as fatigue. This fits the fact that the reaction frequently accompanies severe anemia or a marrow filled by tumor or fibrosis.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Cloudy urine suggests a urinary source of infection and belongs to the leukemoid presentation.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Fever and cough are underlying signs of infection or inflammation seen with a leukemoid reaction.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Joint pain reflects underlying inflammatory disease and is listed with the leukemoid presentation.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Tender cervical lymphadenopathy suggests an infection such as infectious mononucleosis rather than a leukoerythroblastic reaction.

questions.stem: A blood smear from a febrile patient with a bacterial infection shows neutrophils whose cytoplasm is filled with prominent dark granules that stain the same color as the nucleus. Which of the following best describes the basis of this finding?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Azurophilic granules within enlarged reactive lymphocytes

choices.label: B
choices.text: Blue-gray inclusions of ribosomes at the cell periphery

choices.label: C
choices.text: Increased primary granules containing peroxidases and hydrolases

choices.label: D
choices.text: Membrane-bound clear vesicles from lysosomal degranulation

choices.label: E
choices.text: Retained nuclear material from incomplete segmentation

explanation.summary: Toxic granulation reflects increased numbers of primary granules, which contain peroxidases and hydrolases and stain the same color as the nucleus.
explanation.whyCorrect: Toxic granulation is one of the three toxic changes in neutrophils, along with cytoplasmic vacuolization and Dohle bodies. Neutrophils with toxic granulation show increased numbers of primary granules in the cytoplasm; these granules contain peroxidases and hydrolases and stain the same color as the nucleus.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Azurophilic granules in enlarged cells are a feature of reactive lymphocytes, not of neutrophils with toxic change.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Blue-gray peripheral inclusions of ribosomes and rough endoplasmic reticulum are Dohle bodies, a different toxic change.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Clear membrane-bound vesicles from lysosomal degranulation describe cytoplasmic vacuolization, typically seen in sepsis.
whyWrongByChoice.E: The dark granules are cytoplasmic, and incomplete nuclear segmentation describes band forms in a left shift.

questions.stem: A 29-year-old woman at 32 weeks gestation has a routine complete blood count. She is afebrile with no symptoms of infection, and her smear shows occasional neutrophils containing small blue-gray inclusions at the periphery of the cytoplasm. Which of the following best explains this finding?

choices.label: A
choices.text: These inclusions are also associated with pregnancy

choices.label: B
choices.text: These inclusions are an artifact of the automated slidemaker

choices.label: C
choices.text: These inclusions are azurophilic granules of lymphocytes

choices.label: D
choices.text: These inclusions indicate a myeloproliferative neoplasm

choices.label: E
choices.text: These inclusions occur only in bacterial sepsis

explanation.summary: Dohle bodies are associated with infection but also with burns, trauma, pregnancy, neoplastic disease, and exposure to cytotoxic agents.
explanation.whyCorrect: The described inclusions are Dohle bodies, small circular or oval blue-gray cytoplasmic inclusions usually located at the periphery of the neutrophil. Although they are often a manifestation of increased protein production in neutrophils responding to bacterial infection, they are also associated with burns, trauma, pregnancy, neoplastic diseases, and exposure to cytotoxic agents, so their presence in an afebrile pregnant patient is expected.

whyWrongByChoice.B: Dohle bodies are a genuine morphologic finding confirmed on manual review, not a slidemaker artifact.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Azurophilic granules are a feature of reactive lymphocytes, whereas these inclusions are in neutrophils.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Myeloproliferative disorders are classically associated with basophilia rather than with Dohle bodies.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Dohle bodies are not limited to sepsis; several non-infectious conditions are recognized associations.

questions.stem: Which of the following causes of benign lymphocytosis characteristically produces the most extreme elevations of the lymphocyte count, up to 100,000/mm3?

explanation.summary: Of the causes of lymphocytosis with normal-appearing lymphocytes, infectious lymphocytosis produces the most extreme counts, up to 100,000/mm3.
explanation.whyCorrect: Lymphocytosis composed of normal-appearing lymphocytes has three main causes: infectious lymphocytosis, Bordetella pertussis infection, and transient stress. Of these, infectious lymphocytosis, a viral illness of children usually due to enteroviruses such as coxsackievirus or echovirus, can produce the most extreme elevations of the lymphocyte count, with counts up to 100,000/mm3.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Bordetella pertussis causes lymphocytosis with normal-appearing cells but is not the cause listed as producing the most extreme counts.
whyWrongByChoice.B: A drug reaction with eosinophilia and systemic symptoms produces a reactive lymphocytosis with fever and rash.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Epstein-Barr virus produces a reactive lymphocytosis with Downey cells rather than these extreme counts.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Transient stress, such as after cardiac arrest in adults, causes a much more modest lymphocytosis.

questions.stem: An unvaccinated 4-month-old infant has 2 weeks of paroxysmal coughing spells followed by an inspiratory whoop and post-tussive vomiting. Her white blood cell count is elevated with a marked lymphocytosis, and the lymphocytes appear normal on the smear. Which of the following is the most likely cause?

explanation.summary: Bordetella pertussis, the cause of whooping cough, is a bacterial cause of lymphocytosis with normal-appearing lymphocytes.
explanation.whyCorrect: Lymphocytosis composed of normal-appearing lymphocytes has three main causes, one of which is Bordetella pertussis bacterial infection, known as whooping cough. The paroxysmal cough with an inspiratory whoop in an unvaccinated infant, together with a marked lymphocytosis of normal-appearing cells, fits this diagnosis.

whyWrongByChoice.B: Coxsackievirus causes infectious lymphocytosis in children but does not produce the paroxysmal whooping illness described.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Cytomegalovirus is listed among the viruses producing reactive-appearing lymphocytes rather than normal-appearing ones.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Epstein-Barr virus causes infectious mononucleosis with reactive-appearing lymphocytes, including Downey type II cells.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Mycobacterium tuberculosis is a bacterial cause of reactive lymphocytosis and presents as a chronic pulmonary illness.

questions.stem: A 66-year-old man is resuscitated after an out-of-hospital cardiac arrest. Several hours later his white blood cell count is elevated with an absolute lymphocyte count of 6000/mm3, and the lymphocytes appear normal on the smear. He is afebrile with no evidence of infection. Which of the following best explains his lymphocytosis?

choices.label: A
choices.text: A drug reaction with eosinophilia and systemic symptoms

choices.label: B
choices.text: A lymphocytosis due to an underlying neoplasia

choices.label: E
choices.text: Reactive lymphocytosis from an acute viral infection

explanation.summary: Transient stress, as in adults after cardiac arrest, is one of the three causes of lymphocytosis with normal-appearing lymphocytes.
explanation.whyCorrect: Benign lymphocytosis is an abnormally high lymphocyte count above 4000/mm3 that is not due to neoplasia. Among the causes of lymphocytosis with normal-appearing lymphocytes is transient stress, for example in adults after cardiac arrest, which is precisely this patient's setting.

whyWrongByChoice.A: A drug reaction with eosinophilia and systemic symptoms is characterized by fever, rash, and eosinophilia, none of which is present.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Benign lymphocytosis is by definition not due to neoplasia, and the cells here are normal-appearing.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Infectious lymphocytosis is a viral illness that typically occurs in children, not in a 66-year-old man.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Reactive lymphocytosis from a viral infection would show enlarged abnormal-appearing lymphocytes on the smear.

questions.stem: A 38-year-old man who started carbamazepine 3 weeks ago now has fever, a diffuse rash, and eosinophilia, and his blood smear shows an increased proportion of reactive-appearing lymphocytes. Which of the following best explains his findings?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Bordetella pertussis infection of the airway

choices.label: B
choices.text: Drug reaction with eosinophilia and systemic symptoms

explanation.summary: DRESS syndrome is a drug reaction characterized by fever, rash, and eosinophilia that also produces a reactive lymphocytosis; anticonvulsants such as carbamazepine are common causes.
explanation.whyCorrect: Reactive lymphocytosis may also be caused by drug reactions, as in the drug reaction with eosinophilia and systemic symptoms (DRESS). DRESS syndrome is characterized by fever, rash, and eosinophilia, and the most common causes are drugs used to treat seizures such as carbamazepine, phenytoin, and lamotrigine, along with allopurinol, sulfa antibiotics, and vancomycin.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Bordetella pertussis causes lymphocytosis with normal-appearing lymphocytes and a paroxysmal cough.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Helminthic infection causes eosinophilia but is not a cause of reactive lymphocytosis with fever and rash after starting a drug.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Infectious mononucleosis causes reactive lymphocytosis but presents with sore throat and lymphadenopathy rather than a drug-associated rash with eosinophilia.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Myeloproliferative disorders classically show basophilia and are neoplastic rather than drug-induced.

questions.stem: A 24-year-old woman is evaluated for a neck mass. On examination, several enlarged cervical lymph nodes are palpated. Which of the following physical findings would most strongly suggest a benign, rather than neoplastic, cause of her lymphadenopathy?

choices.label: B
choices.text: Nodes that are firm and rubbery-hard

choices.label: C
choices.text: Nodes that are fixed to the underlying tissue

choices.label: D
choices.text: Nodes that are immobile on palpation

choices.label: E
choices.text: Nodes that are soft, freely movable, and tender

explanation.summary: Benign lymphadenopathy typically produces nodes that are soft, smooth, freely movable, and often tender.
explanation.whyCorrect: In benign lymphadenopathy, nodes are generally soft, smooth, freely moveable, and often tender because the enlargement results from reactive hyperplasia rather than infiltrative growth. Neoplastic nodes, by contrast, tend to be firm, immobile, fixed to the underlying tissue, and painless.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Painless nodes are typical of malignancy; benign reactive nodes are often tender.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Firm, hard nodes are characteristic of neoplastic rather than benign lymphadenopathy.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Fixation to underlying tissue is a feature that favors a neoplastic process, not a benign one.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Immobility suggests infiltration by tumor and points away from a benign cause.

questions.stem: A 58-year-old man is found to have an enlarged, firm lymph node just above the left clavicle. It is nontender and fixed. Enlargement of this particular node should most prompt a search for a malignancy in which of the following locations?

explanation.summary: The left supraclavicular (Virchow) node drains the abdomen and its enlargement suggests abdominal, especially gastric, cancer.
explanation.whyCorrect: The left supraclavicular node, also called the Virchow node, receives abdominal lymphatics that drain into the thoracic duct and then into the left supraclavicular node. An enlarged node here should prompt a search for an abdominal cancer, particularly gastric cancer.

whyWrongByChoice.B: Breast cancer classically involves axillary nodes rather than the left supraclavicular node.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Chest malignancy such as lung cancer is suggested by an enlarged right supraclavicular node, not the left.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Oral and pharyngeal disease points to submandibular or submental nodes, not the supraclavicular region.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Upper extremity infection drains to axillary nodes, not to the supraclavicular area.

questions.stem: A 35-year-old woman has a dry cough and mild fatigue. A chest radiograph shows symmetric bilateral hilar lymphadenopathy. Which of the following conditions is most consistent with this pattern of adenopathy?

explanation.summary: Hilar lymphadenopathy classically points to lung infection, lung cancer, or the granulomatous condition sarcoidosis.
explanation.whyCorrect: Hilar lymphadenopathy most often indicates a lung infection, lung cancer, or sarcoidosis, and sarcoidosis classically presents with bilateral hilar adenopathy. This granulomatous disease is a well-recognized benign cause of adenopathy in this location.

whyWrongByChoice.A: A dental abscess causes submandibular or submental adenopathy, not hilar enlargement.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Gastric carcinoma would be suggested by a left supraclavicular (Virchow) node rather than bilateral hilar nodes.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Toxoplasmosis typically causes generalized or head-and-neck adenopathy, not an isolated bilateral hilar pattern.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Typhoid fever produces mesenteric adenopathy rather than hilar lymphadenopathy.

questions.stem: A 40-year-old woman develops diffuse lymph node enlargement two weeks after starting a new medication for a seizure disorder. She also has a low-grade fever and joint aches resembling serum sickness. Which type of hypersensitivity reaction most likely underlies this drug-induced generalized adenopathy?

explanation.summary: Many drugs cause generalized adenopathy through a serum-sickness-like, type 3 hypersensitivity reaction.
explanation.whyCorrect: The article notes that drugs most commonly cause generalized adenopathy via a serum-sickness-like hypersensitivity reaction, which is a type 3 (immune complex) hypersensitivity. Antiseizure medications such as carbamazepine, lamotrigine, and primidone are among the drugs implicated.

whyWrongByChoice.A: IgA-mediated mucosal reactions are not the mechanism of drug-induced generalized lymphadenopathy.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Type 1 hypersensitivity mediates anaphylaxis and allergic reactions, not serum-sickness-like generalized adenopathy.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Type 2 hypersensitivity involves antibody-mediated cell destruction, which is not the mechanism described here.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Type 4 hypersensitivity is delayed and T-cell mediated, whereas the serum-sickness-like drug reaction is immune complex driven.

questions.stem: A lymph node biopsy from a patient with a chronic infection shows enlarged follicles containing prominent germinal centers with tingible body macrophages. This pattern of benign follicular hyperplasia is driven predominantly by proliferation of which of the following cell types?

explanation.summary: Benign follicular hyperplasia reflects B-cell proliferation within lymph node follicles.
explanation.whyCorrect: Benign follicular hyperplasia is caused by B-cell proliferation in the lymph node follicles in response to an immune stimulus. The stimulus converts small primary follicles into enlarged secondary follicles that develop germinal centers containing proliferating lymphocytes and tingible body macrophages.

whyWrongByChoice.B: Fibroblasts contribute to fibrosis, not to the reactive follicular hyperplasia of an immune response.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Neutrophils are agents of acute suppurative inflammation and are not the basis of follicular hyperplasia.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Plasma cells may be present but are not the proliferating population that defines follicular hyperplasia.
whyWrongByChoice.E: T-cell proliferation drives interfollicular/paracortical hyperplasia, not follicular hyperplasia.

questions.stem: A 22-year-old man with a recent viral illness has a lymph node biopsy showing diffuse expansion of the paracortex and the areas between the follicles. A predominant proliferation of which of the following cell types best explains this reactive pattern?

explanation.summary: Benign interfollicular/paracortical hyperplasia represents a predominant T-cell response.
explanation.whyCorrect: Benign interfollicular/paracortical hyperplasia represents a predominant T-cell (not B-cell) response to an immune stimulus, and the lymph node shows expansion of the paracortex and the areas between follicles. Causes of this paracortical pattern include viral infection, vaccination, reaction to a nearby malignancy, and autoimmune disease.

whyWrongByChoice.A: B-cell proliferation produces follicular hyperplasia with germinal centers, not paracortical expansion.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Endothelial cells line vessels and are not the proliferating population in this reactive pattern.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Mast cells mediate allergic responses and do not drive paracortical hyperplasia.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Osteoclasts are bone-resorbing cells and have no role in lymph node paracortical hyperplasia.

questions.stem: A 30-year-old man develops an infected laceration on his right hand after a gardening injury. Over the next few days he notices tender swelling in the ipsilateral armpit. Enlargement of which group of lymph nodes best explains this finding?

explanation.summary: The axillary nodes drain the upper extremity and enlarge with an arm or hand infection.
explanation.whyCorrect: Axillary nodes drain the upper extremities, so an infection of the hand or arm produces regional axillary adenopathy. A localized infection often presents with related regional lymphadenopathy in the nodes that drain the affected site.

whyWrongByChoice.B: Hilar nodes drain the lungs and are unrelated to a hand infection.
whyWrongByChoice.C: The left supraclavicular node drains the abdomen and would not enlarge from a hand infection.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Mesenteric nodes drain intra-abdominal structures and are seen with conditions such as typhoid fever.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Submental nodes drain the floor of the mouth and chin, not the upper extremity.

questions.stem: A 62-year-old man is evaluated for enlarged cervical lymph nodes that appeared shortly after he began atenolol for newly diagnosed hypertension. He has no fever, no weight loss, and no other findings; examination and laboratory studies show no evidence of infection or malignancy. Which of the following is the most appropriate management?

choices.label: D
choices.text: Perform excisional biopsy of a cervical node now

choices.label: E
choices.text: Start anti-inflammatory therapy for an autoimmune disease

explanation.summary: Management of benign lymphadenopathy is tailored to the cause; drug-induced adenopathy resolves after stopping the offending drug.
explanation.whyCorrect: Management is tailored to the underlying cause, and treatment is based on eliminating infections, stopping offending drugs, and addressing inflammatory conditions. When the clinical picture points to a drug such as atenolol as the cause, stopping the offending drug will likely lead to resolution of the lymphadenopathy.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Antibiotics treat adenopathy secondary to infection, but no infection is identified in this case.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Systemic corticosteroids are not the initial step; removing the offending drug is the appropriate action.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Excisional biopsy is reserved for adenopathy that does not resolve with initial measures or that raises concern for malignancy.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Anti-inflammatory therapy addresses an underlying inflammatory disorder, which is not present here.

questions.stem: A 66-year-old woman presents with a single, 1.5 cm, movable, rubbery lymph node in her right axilla. She has not felt any lump herself, and the rest of the examination is normal. Which of the following is the most appropriate next step in evaluation?

explanation.summary: A single enlarged axillary node in a woman warrants breast evaluation to exclude breast cancer.
explanation.whyCorrect: A single enlarged axillary node suggests pathology in the arm or chest wall, and in women breast cancer is an obvious consideration because the axillary nodes drain the breast. A thorough breast exam and mammography are the appropriate next steps so that malignancy can be excluded, with biopsy reserved for later if these are unrevealing.

whyWrongByChoice.B: Stopping medications is used for drug-induced adenopathy, which typically causes diffuse rather than single-node enlargement.
whyWrongByChoice.C: HIV testing is appropriate for unexplained generalized adenopathy, not for a single localized axillary node.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Lymph node biopsy would only be done after routine testing such as mammography, not as the immediate first step.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Reassurance without workup is inappropriate because a solitary axillary node in a woman requires exclusion of breast cancer.

questions.stem: A 55-year-old man has enlarged cervical lymph nodes together with a 6 kg unintentional weight loss and drenching night sweats over the past two months. On examination, a firm node is fixed to underlying tissue. Which of the following is the most appropriate step on initial workup?

choices.label: E
choices.text: Prescribe a course of oral antibiotics

explanation.summary: Signs or symptoms of cancer, such as weight loss and a fixed node, warrant lymph node biopsy on initial workup.
explanation.whyCorrect: A lymph node biopsy is indicated on initial workup if the patient has underlying signs or symptoms of cancer, such as weight loss, fever, or a palpable tumor outside the nodes. The goal is to exclude neoplastic causes of the lymphadenopathy, which this patient's weight loss and fixed, firm node raise concern for.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Stopping medications addresses drug-induced adenopathy and does not fit a patient with weight loss and a fixed node.
whyWrongByChoice.C: A four-week period of observation is appropriate for unexplained local adenopathy without worrisome features, not for adenopathy with cancer warning signs.
whyWrongByChoice.D: A heterophile test evaluates for mononucleosis and would not address the concern for malignancy raised by his systemic symptoms.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Empiric antibiotics would only be reasonable if infection were suspected, not when malignancy is the concern.

questions.stem: A 28-year-old man has enlargement of noncontiguous cervical, axillary, and inguinal lymph nodes without an obvious localizing source. History and physical examination do not reveal the cause. Which of the following sets of tests is the most appropriate initial evaluation for this generalized adenopathy?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Bone marrow aspiration and biopsy as the first step

choices.label: B
choices.text: Complete blood count, HIV test, and chest x-ray

choices.label: D
choices.text: Serum ferritin, iron, and total iron-binding capacity

explanation.summary: Generalized adenopathy is initially evaluated with tests such as a CBC, HIV test, and chest x-ray.
explanation.whyCorrect: For generalized adenopathy, testing may include a CBC, HIV test, and chest x-ray, with testing for tuberculosis and EBV also conducted. If all of these are negative, a biopsy may then be done on an easily reached node in the neck or supraclavicular area.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Bone marrow biopsy is not the routine first step; initial testing screens for infection and systemic disease first.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Mammography targets a single axillary node in a woman with possible breast cancer, not diffuse generalized adenopathy in a young man.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Iron studies evaluate anemia and are unrelated to the workup of generalized lymphadenopathy.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Upper endoscopy pursues gastric disease suggested by a Virchow node, not undifferentiated generalized adenopathy.

questions.stem: A histopathologist examines a reactive lymph node and points out large phagocytic cells within the germinal center that contain engulfed cellular debris, described as tingible body macrophages. In which region of the lymph node are these cells and their surrounding germinal center normally located?

choices.label: B
choices.text: Within the hilum near the efferent vessel

choices.label: D
choices.text: Within the paracortex among the T cells

explanation.summary: Germinal centers with tingible body macrophages reside in secondary follicles of the follicular (B-cell) region.
explanation.whyCorrect: The follicular region contains B cells arranged in follicles, and secondary follicles contain a germinal center that has been antigenically stimulated. The germinal center holds proliferating lymphocytes along with tingible body macrophages that are busy cleaning up cellular debris.

whyWrongByChoice.B: The hilum is where vessels enter and leave the node and does not contain germinal centers.
whyWrongByChoice.C: The medullary cords are deep cords rich in plasma cells, not the location of germinal-center macrophages.
whyWrongByChoice.D: The paracortex is the T-cell zone that surrounds the follicles and does not house germinal centers.
whyWrongByChoice.E: The subcapsular sinus is a lymphatic channel beneath the capsule, not the site of germinal centers.

questions.stem: A 19-year-old man is examined because he felt a lump in his neck. The physician explains that a lymph node is considered abnormally enlarged once its diameter exceeds a particular size. Enlargement beyond which of the following measurements is generally used to define lymphadenopathy?

explanation.summary: Lymphadenopathy means one or more lymph nodes are enlarged, usually greater than 1 cm in diameter.
explanation.whyCorrect: Patients with lymph node disorders present with lymphadenopathy, meaning that one or more lymph nodes are enlarged, usually more than 1 cm in diameter. Nodes that exceed this size are considered abnormal and prompt a search for an underlying infectious, inflammatory, or neoplastic cause.

whyWrongByChoice.A: A node of 0.5 cm falls below the size used to define enlargement and would be considered normal.
whyWrongByChoice.C: A 2-cm node is clearly abnormal, but adenopathy is already recognized at a smaller diameter.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Requiring 3 cm would miss the many enlarged nodes that measure between 1 and 3 cm.
whyWrongByChoice.E: A 5-cm threshold is far above the size at which a node is considered enlarged.

questions.stem: A 26-year-old woman is found on examination to have enlarged cervical nodes and enlarged inguinal nodes, with no enlarged node groups between these two sites. Which of the following best characterizes her pattern of lymphadenopathy?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Generalized adenopathy, because noncontiguous node groups are enlarged

choices.label: B
choices.text: Hilar adenopathy, because intrathoracic node groups are enlarged

choices.label: C
choices.text: Localized adenopathy, because a single drainage basin is enlarged

choices.label: D
choices.text: Mesenteric adenopathy, because intra-abdominal node groups are enlarged

choices.label: E
choices.text: Regional adenopathy, because contiguous node groups are enlarged

explanation.summary: Generalized lymphadenopathy means two or more noncontiguous lymph node groups are enlarged at a given time.
explanation.whyCorrect: Lymphadenopathy is generalized when two or more noncontiguous lymph nodes are enlarged at a given time; enlarged cervical and inguinal nodes are the classic example of this pattern. Localized adenopathy, by contrast, involves only one region such as the cervical nodes alone.

whyWrongByChoice.B: Hilar adenopathy involves nodes at the lung hila, which are not the sites enlarged in this patient.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Localized adenopathy involves a single region, whereas two separated regions are enlarged here.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Mesenteric adenopathy involves intra-abdominal nodes, which are not described as enlarged here.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Regional adenopathy refers to nodes draining one anatomic area, and the cervical and inguinal groups are not contiguous.

questions.stem: A 66-year-old man with a 40 pack-year smoking history is found to have a spiculated mass in the right upper lobe on chest CT. Enlargement of which of the following nodes would be most consistent with a malignancy arising in the chest cavity?

explanation.summary: An enlarged right supraclavicular node points to malignancy in the chest cavity, such as lung cancer.
explanation.whyCorrect: The right supraclavicular node drains the thorax, so an enlarged node in this location may indicate malignancy in the chest cavity such as lung cancer. This differs from the left supraclavicular node, which receives abdominal lymphatic drainage.

whyWrongByChoice.A: The left supraclavicular (Virchow) node receives abdominal lymphatics through the thoracic duct and suggests abdominal cancer such as gastric cancer.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Mesenteric nodes drain intra-abdominal structures and enlarge in conditions such as typhoid fever.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Submental nodes drain the chin and floor of the mouth, not intrathoracic structures.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Inguinal nodes drain the lower extremity and genital region rather than the thorax.

questions.stem: A 34-year-old man has several days of throbbing pain at the root of a lower molar, and an abscess is found at that tooth. He now notices tender swelling beneath the jaw. Enlargement of which of the following node groups best accounts for this finding?

explanation.summary: A localized infection produces regional adenopathy, and dental abscess or pharyngitis enlarges the submandibular and submental nodes.
explanation.whyCorrect: A localized infection often presents with related regional lymphadenopathy in the nodes that drain the infected site. Submandibular and submental lymph nodes enlarge with infections such as pharyngitis or a dental abscess.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Axillary nodes drain the upper extremities and would enlarge with a hand or arm infection.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Hilar nodes drain the lungs and enlarge with lung infection, lung cancer, or sarcoidosis.
whyWrongByChoice.C: The left supraclavicular node reflects abdominal drainage and would not respond to a dental abscess.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Mesenteric nodes drain intra-abdominal structures and are not related to a dental infection.

questions.stem: A 6-year-old boy has fever and painful swelling over the angle of the jaw in the region of the parotid gland. Which of the following viral infections characteristically produces enlargement in this particular location?

explanation.summary: Among viral causes of lymphadenopathy, mumps characteristically involves the parotid region.
explanation.whyCorrect: Viral infections have distinctive distributions: HIV and cytomegalovirus cause generalized adenopathy, Epstein-Barr virus and measles cause cervical adenopathy, and mumps involves the parotid region. The parotid location in this child therefore points to mumps.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Cytomegalovirus, like HIV, is associated with a generalized pattern of node enlargement.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Epstein-Barr virus causes cervical adenopathy as part of infectious mononucleosis.
whyWrongByChoice.C: HIV produces generalized adenopathy rather than isolated parotid enlargement.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Measles is associated with cervical adenopathy rather than parotid involvement.

questions.stem: A 28-year-old man returns from international travel with two weeks of sustained fever and abdominal pain. Abdominal CT shows several enlarged mesenteric lymph nodes. Which of the following infections is most consistent with this distribution of adenopathy?

explanation.summary: Among bacterial causes of adenopathy, typhoid fever characteristically produces mesenteric lymphadenopathy.
explanation.whyCorrect: Bacterial causes of lymphadenopathy have distinctive patterns: tuberculosis may be generalized or regional in the lung, typhoid fever is mesenteric, and brucellosis is generalized. Enlarged mesenteric nodes in a febrile traveler fit typhoid fever.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Brucellosis is a bacterial cause that produces generalized rather than mesenteric adenopathy.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Histoplasmosis is a fungal infection associated with hilar and mediastinal adenopathy.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Measles is associated with cervical adenopathy, not with enlarged mesenteric nodes.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Toxoplasmosis is a parasitic cause producing generalized or head and neck adenopathy.

questions.stem: A 45-year-old man has several weeks of cough and fatigue, and chest CT shows hilar and mediastinal lymphadenopathy. Cultures of respiratory specimens grow a fungus. Which of the following infections best accounts for his adenopathy?

explanation.summary: Histoplasmosis is the fungal infection classically associated with hilar and mediastinal lymphadenopathy.
explanation.whyCorrect: Among infectious causes of lymphadenopathy, histoplasmosis is the fungal organism, and it characteristically produces hilar and mediastinal adenopathy. Both the fungal culture and the intrathoracic nodal distribution point to this diagnosis.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Brucellosis is bacterial and causes generalized adenopathy rather than a hilar pattern.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Toxoplasmosis is parasitic and causes generalized or head and neck adenopathy.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Tuberculosis is a bacterial infection that may be generalized or regional in the lung, and it is not a fungus.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Typhoid fever is bacterial and produces mesenteric rather than hilar adenopathy.

questions.stem: A 27-year-old woman comes to the emergency department in tears because of severe pain with urination. Her temperature is 38 C (100.4 F), and there are clusters of small blisters filled with clear fluid on the external genitalia and around the urethra. Several tender, freely movable inguinal nodes measuring 1 to 2 cm are palpated. Which of the following best explains her inguinal findings?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Drug reaction producing a serum-sickness-like adenopathy

choices.label: B
choices.text: Lymphoma presenting as painless generalized adenopathy

choices.label: C
choices.text: Metastatic spread of an occult vulvar carcinoma to the nodes

choices.label: D
choices.text: Noncaseating granulomas of sarcoidosis within the nodes

choices.label: E
choices.text: Reactive node enlargement caused by the herpesvirus infection

explanation.summary: Tender, freely movable regional nodes accompanying genital vesicles represent reactive enlargement from herpesvirus infection.
explanation.whyCorrect: The clustered clear vesicles with painful urination indicate genital herpes, and the inguinal nodes have become enlarged because of the herpesvirus infection. These reactive nodes are soft, freely movable, and tender, and they diminish in size as the infection subsides; antiviral medication reduces symptoms and decreases the likelihood of transmission.

whyWrongByChoice.A: A drug-related serum-sickness-like reaction produces generalized adenopathy and would not explain the genital vesicles.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Lymphoma produces firm, painless nodes and does not account for the vesicular genital lesions.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Metastatic nodes are typically firm, fixed, and painless rather than tender and freely movable.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Sarcoidosis classically presents with hilar adenopathy, not tender inguinal nodes with genital vesicles.

questions.stem: A 31-year-old man has enlarged cervical, axillary, and inguinal nodes with no localizing source of infection, and a viral cause is suspected. Which of the following pairs of viral infections characteristically produces this generalized pattern of adenopathy?

explanation.summary: HIV and cytomegalovirus are the viral infections that characteristically cause generalized lymphadenopathy.
explanation.whyCorrect: Among viral causes, HIV and cytomegalovirus produce generalized adenopathy, whereas Epstein-Barr virus and measles cause cervical adenopathy and mumps affects the parotid region. Only the HIV and cytomegalovirus pair matches this patient's noncontiguous, multiregional enlargement.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Both Epstein-Barr virus and measles are associated with cervical adenopathy rather than a generalized pattern.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Epstein-Barr virus causes cervical adenopathy and mumps affects the parotid, so neither member of this pair is generalized.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Measles causes cervical adenopathy and mumps affects the parotid region rather than multiple distant regions.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Cytomegalovirus is generalized, but mumps involves the parotid, so this pair does not fit the pattern.

questions.stem: A 40-year-old man has generalized lymphadenopathy of unclear cause. His complete blood count is normal, an HIV test is negative, and a chest x-ray is unremarkable. Which of the following is the most appropriate next step in his evaluation?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Bone marrow aspiration and biopsy to look for leukemia

choices.label: B
choices.text: Empiric corticosteroid therapy to shrink the enlarged nodes

choices.label: C
choices.text: Mammography to look for an occult primary breast cancer

choices.label: D
choices.text: Testing for tuberculosis and a heterophile test for EBV

choices.label: E
choices.text: Upper endoscopy to look for an occult gastric carcinoma

explanation.summary: Workup of generalized adenopathy proceeds from CBC, HIV testing, and chest x-ray to testing for tuberculosis and EBV.
explanation.whyCorrect: For generalized adenopathy, testing may include a CBC, HIV test, and chest x-ray, and testing for tuberculosis and EBV with a heterophile test may also be conducted. Only if all of these are negative is a biopsy then performed on an easily reached node.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Bone marrow examination is not part of the routine sequence for evaluating generalized adenopathy.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Corticosteroids treat an identified inflammatory disorder and would obscure the diagnosis if given empirically.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Mammography is directed at axillary adenopathy in a woman, not at generalized node enlargement in this patient.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Endoscopy pursues gastric cancer suggested by a Virchow node, not undifferentiated generalized adenopathy.

questions.stem: A 44-year-old woman has generalized adenopathy with a normal CBC, a negative HIV test, an unremarkable chest x-ray, and negative tuberculosis and heterophile testing. A lymph node biopsy is now planned. Which of the following nodes is the most appropriate to sample?

choices.label: A
choices.text: A hilar node sampled by mediastinoscopy in the operating room

choices.label: B
choices.text: A mesenteric node sampled at exploratory laparotomy

choices.label: C
choices.text: A retroperitoneal node sampled under CT guidance

choices.label: D
choices.text: An easily reached node in the neck or supraclavicular area

choices.label: E
choices.text: An intraparotid node sampled by open surgical dissection

explanation.summary: When initial testing for generalized adenopathy is negative, biopsy is performed on an easily reached node in the neck or supraclavicular area.
explanation.whyCorrect: If the CBC, HIV test, chest x-ray, and tuberculosis and EBV testing are all negative, a biopsy may be done on an easily reached node in the neck or supraclavicular area. Because the adenopathy is generalized, any involved node is representative, so the most accessible site is chosen.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Mediastinoscopy is reserved for intrathoracic disease when superficial nodes are not available.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Laparotomy is a far more invasive route to tissue that accessible superficial nodes can provide.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Retroperitoneal sampling is unnecessary when enlarged superficial nodes can be biopsied directly.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Intraparotid nodes are a technically difficult site and are not the preferred sampling location.

questions.stem: A 25-year-old woman has a single 1.5-cm soft, mildly tender cervical lymph node. She has no fever, no weight loss, and no mass outside the nodes, and a careful history and physical examination do not identify a cause. Which of the following is the most appropriate management?

choices.label: A
choices.text: A course of antituberculous therapy started now

choices.label: B
choices.text: Bone marrow aspiration and biopsy performed today

choices.label: C
choices.text: CT of the chest, abdomen, and pelvis performed today

choices.label: D
choices.text: Excisional biopsy of the node within the week

choices.label: E
choices.text: Observation for 4 weeks with biopsy if it persists

explanation.summary: Local adenopathy whose cause is not identified by history and physical may be observed for 4 weeks, with biopsy if it persists.
explanation.whyCorrect: For local adenopathy in which the cause cannot be identified by the history and physical, the patient can be observed for 4 weeks and a biopsy done if the adenopathy is still present at that time. This patient has soft, tender, localized adenopathy without signs or symptoms of cancer, so immediate biopsy is not required.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Antituberculous therapy is not started without evidence of tuberculosis, and no such testing has been pursued.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Bone marrow examination is not part of the evaluation of an isolated, soft, tender node.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Imaging is driven by the organ system of concern, and she has no symptoms directing a body-wide scan.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Biopsy on initial workup is reserved for patients with signs or symptoms of cancer, which she does not have.

questions.stem: A 36-year-old woman with persistent cervical adenopathy undergoes needle biopsy of an enlarged node. The specimen shows reactive changes with no evidence of malignancy. Which of the following best describes what this biopsy result has established?

choices.label: A
choices.text: It confirms a drug reaction as the cause of the adenopathy

choices.label: B
choices.text: It establishes an autoimmune disorder as the cause of the adenopathy

choices.label: C
choices.text: It excludes a neoplastic cause but not the specific benign cause

choices.label: D
choices.text: It identifies the specific organism responsible for the adenopathy

choices.label: E
choices.text: It proves the adenopathy will resolve without any treatment

explanation.summary: Lymph node biopsy excludes neoplastic causes of lymphadenopathy but usually cannot determine the underlying cause of benign adenopathy.
explanation.whyCorrect: Lymph node biopsy is used to exclude neoplastic causes of lymphadenopathy, but it cannot usually determine the underlying cause of benign adenopathy. A reactive biopsy therefore reassures against malignancy while leaving the specific benign etiology to be established by the history, physical examination, and laboratory testing.

whyWrongByChoice.A: A reactive pattern does not distinguish a drug reaction from infectious or autoimmune causes.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Autoimmune disease cannot be diagnosed from a reactive node; serologic and clinical findings are required.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Biopsy of a reactive node does not identify the particular organism causing the adenopathy.
whyWrongByChoice.E: A benign biopsy says nothing about whether the adenopathy will resolve on its own.

questions.stem: A lymph node has been excised from a patient with unexplained adenopathy, and routine histologic sections are equivocal for a lymphoid neoplasm. Which of the following groups of additional studies would most appropriately be performed on the sampled node?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Blood cultures, urinalysis, and acid-fast smear of the sputum

choices.label: B
choices.text: Chest radiography, CT scanning, and mammography of the breast

choices.label: C
choices.text: Flow cytometry, immunohistochemical stains, and FISH

choices.label: D
choices.text: Heterophile antibody test, antinuclear antibody, and complete blood count

choices.label: E
choices.text: Protein electrophoresis, sedimentation rate, and C-reactive protein

explanation.summary: Additional studies performed on a sampled lymph node include flow cytometry, immunohistochemical stains, and FISH.
explanation.whyCorrect: Additional studies may need to be performed on the sampled lymph node itself, such as flow cytometry, immunohistochemical stains, and FISH. These tissue-based techniques characterize the lymphoid population and help distinguish a reactive process from a neoplastic one when routine sections are equivocal.

whyWrongByChoice.A: These culture and smear studies sample blood, urine, and sputum rather than the excised node.
whyWrongByChoice.B: These are imaging studies that define the extent of adenopathy rather than characterize the tissue.
whyWrongByChoice.D: These are blood-based tests used in the clinical workup, not studies applied to the node itself.
whyWrongByChoice.E: These are serum inflammatory studies and are not performed on the biopsy specimen.

questions.stem: A 52-year-old man reports a sensation of fullness in the neck and upper chest, but physical examination cannot establish whether lymph nodes are truly enlarged. Which of the following studies would best determine whether adenopathy is present and define its extent?

explanation.summary: CT is helpful when the diagnosis of adenopathy is not clear on physical examination and can define the extent of enlarged nodes.
explanation.whyCorrect: A CT scan may be helpful if the diagnosis of adenopathy is not clear by physical exam, and the scan may define the extent of the enlarged nodes. Imaging is otherwise driven by the organ system of concern, such as chest radiography or CT for a patient with pulmonary symptoms.

whyWrongByChoice.A: An antinuclear antibody titer supports a diagnosis of SLE and does not image the nodes.
whyWrongByChoice.B: A complete blood count may suggest leukemia but cannot establish the presence or extent of adenopathy.
whyWrongByChoice.D: A heterophile test screens for EBV infection and does not demonstrate whether nodes are enlarged.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Mammography is appropriate for a patient with axillary adenopathy, not for defining deep nodal disease in the neck and chest.

questions.stem: A 30-year-old woman has generalized lymphadenopathy together with a rash across her cheeks and pain in several joints. Which of the following laboratory findings would best support the suspected underlying cause of her adenopathy?

choices.label: D
choices.text: Blast cells on the peripheral blood smear

choices.label: E
choices.text: Growth of a fungus on sputum culture

explanation.summary: A positive antinuclear antibody supports systemic lupus erythematosus as the autoimmune cause of diffuse adenopathy.
explanation.whyCorrect: Laboratory tests can provide clues to the disease underlying lymphadenopathy, and a positive ANA suggests SLE. Autoimmune diseases such as rheumatoid arthritis, SLE, and Sjogren syndrome may cause diffuse adenopathy, and skin rashes and arthritis are seen in these inflammatory conditions.

whyWrongByChoice.B: A positive heterophile test indicates EBV mononucleosis, which does not explain a malar rash and arthritis.
whyWrongByChoice.C: An elevated alkaline phosphatase is nonspecific and does not support an autoimmune cause of adenopathy.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Blast cells on the CBC point to leukemia, a neoplastic rather than autoimmune cause of adenopathy.
whyWrongByChoice.E: A positive fungal culture would suggest histoplasmosis with hilar and mediastinal adenopathy.

questions.stem: A 63-year-old man is evaluated for generalized lymphadenopathy. His complete blood count shows marked leukocytosis with circulating blast cells. This laboratory finding most strongly suggests which of the following underlying causes of his adenopathy?

explanation.summary: Leukocytosis with blast cells on the complete blood count suggests leukemia as the cause of lymphadenopathy.
explanation.whyCorrect: Laboratory clues help identify the disease underlying lymphadenopathy, and leukocytosis or blast cells on the complete blood count suggests leukemia. Leukemia is a neoplastic cause of lymph node disease that must be excluded before a benign explanation is accepted.

whyWrongByChoice.A: A drug reaction causes generalized adenopathy without blast cells in the peripheral blood.
whyWrongByChoice.B: EBV infection is supported by a positive heterophile test and does not generate circulating blasts.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Sarcoidosis classically presents with hilar adenopathy and does not produce circulating blasts.
whyWrongByChoice.E: SLE is suggested by a positive antinuclear antibody rather than by blast cells on the smear.

questions.stem: A physician is taking a history from a patient who has lymphadenopathy of unclear cause. Which of the following historical features would most strongly suggest an underlying cancer or tuberculosis?

choices.label: A
choices.text: A sore throat during the preceding week

choices.label: B
choices.text: Free mobility of the nodes on palpation

choices.label: C
choices.text: Soft, smooth consistency of the nodes

explanation.summary: Weight loss in a patient with lymphadenopathy suggests an underlying cancer or tuberculosis.
explanation.whyCorrect: Key history questions in a patient with lymphadenopathy include whether there has been weight loss, which suggests underlying cancer or tuberculosis. Weight loss is also one of the signs that makes lymph node biopsy appropriate on the initial workup.

whyWrongByChoice.A: A recent sore throat points toward a localized infection such as viral pharyngitis.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Freely movable nodes are a feature of benign lymphadenopathy, not of malignant infiltration.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Soft, smooth nodes are typical of benign disease rather than of a neoplastic process.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Tenderness is characteristic of benign reactive nodes rather than of cancer or tuberculosis.

questions.stem: A pathologist examining a lymph node describes small, closely packed collections of mature B cells in the cortex that contain no germinal centers. Which of the following best describes these structures?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Medullary cords containing antibody-secreting plasma cells

choices.label: B
choices.text: Paracortical zones composed predominantly of T cells

choices.label: C
choices.text: Primary follicles that have not been antigenically stimulated

choices.label: D
choices.text: Secondary follicles that have been antigenically stimulated

choices.label: E
choices.text: Subcapsular sinuses receiving afferent lymphatic flow

explanation.summary: Primary follicles are small, closely packed collections of mature B cells that have not been antigenically stimulated.
explanation.whyCorrect: The follicular region contains B cells arranged in two types of follicles. Primary follicles are small, closely packed collections of mature B cells that have not been antigenically stimulated, while secondary follicles contain a germinal center and have been antigenically stimulated.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Medullary cords lie in the medulla and are not the cortical B-cell collections described here.
whyWrongByChoice.B: The paracortex lies in the deepest part of the cortex and contains mostly T cells, not packed B cells.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Secondary follicles are defined by the presence of a germinal center, which these structures lack.
whyWrongByChoice.E: The subcapsular sinus is a lymphatic channel beneath the capsule rather than a collection of B cells.

questions.stem: A lymph node removed from a patient with a recent viral illness shows expansion of the paracortex and of the areas between the follicles. Which of the following combinations of cells is typically found within these expanded areas?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Lymphocytes, macrophages, plasma cells, and eosinophils

choices.label: C
choices.text: Neutrophils, fibroblasts, and multinucleated giant cells

choices.label: D
choices.text: Osteoclasts, mast cells, and endothelial precursor cells

choices.label: E
choices.text: Squamous cells, glandular cells, and stromal fibroblasts

explanation.summary: Interfollicular/paracortical hyperplasia contains a mixture of lymphocytes, macrophages, plasma cells, and eosinophils.
explanation.whyCorrect: In benign interfollicular/paracortical hyperplasia, the lymph node shows expansion of the paracortex and the areas between follicles, and a variety of cells are typically present: lymphocytes, macrophages, plasma cells, and eosinophils. This mixed population reflects a predominantly T-cell response to an immune stimulus such as viral infection.

whyWrongByChoice.B: These are hematopoietic marrow elements and are not the populations expanding the paracortex.
whyWrongByChoice.C: This combination describes acute suppurative and granulomatous inflammation rather than paracortical hyperplasia.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Osteoclasts and endothelial precursors are not constituents of the reactive interfollicular areas.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Squamous and glandular cells within a node would indicate metastatic carcinoma, not reactive hyperplasia.
