whyWrongByChoice.A: Iron chelation by macrophages would limit rather than amplify radical injury.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Absence of topoisomerase II in pneumocytes is not described and is not the basis of bleomycin lung.
whyWrongByChoice.D: SN-38 is the metabolite of irinotecan that damages intestinal mucosa, not a bleomycin metabolite.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Tubulin turnover pertains to microtubule inhibitors and is not how bleomycin injures lung.

questions.topicName: Topoisomerase Inhibitors, Microtubule Inhibitors, and Antitumor Antibiotics

questions.stem: A 68-year-old man three months into a bleomycin-containing regimen reports a nonproductive cough and dyspnea on exertion. Examination reveals dry inspiratory crackles, and chest x-ray shows bilateral infiltrates. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

explanation.summary: Bleomycin pulmonary toxicity presents as pneumonitis with cough, dyspnea, dry crackles, and infiltrates.
explanation.whyCorrect: Pulmonary toxicity is dose-limiting for bleomycin and usually presents as pneumonitis with cough, dyspnea, dry inspiratory crackles on physical examination, and infiltrates on chest x-ray. This patient's presentation matches that syndrome, often called bleomycin lung, which can progress to fibrosis.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Cardiogenic edema would accompany signs of volume overload and a failing ventricle, seen with anthracyclines instead.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Community-acquired pneumonia typically produces fever and focal consolidation rather than diffuse dry crackles on therapy.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Pneumocystis pneumonia is an opportunistic infection and is not the described toxicity of this drug.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Pulmonary embolism causes abrupt dyspnea and pleuritic pain without bilateral infiltrates and crackles.

questions.topicName: Topoisomerase Inhibitors, Microtubule Inhibitors, and Antitumor Antibiotics

questions.stem: An oncology team reviews which patients are at greatest risk of pulmonary toxicity before starting bleomycin. Which of the following most increases the incidence of this toxicity?

explanation.summary: The incidence of bleomycin pulmonary toxicity is increased in patients older than 70 years.
explanation.whyCorrect: Pulmonary toxicity occurs in about 6 to 10 percent of patients on bleomycin therapy, and the incidence of this toxicity is increased in patients older than 70 years of age. Age is therefore the risk factor that most changes the calculus before starting therapy.

whyWrongByChoice.B: Anemia is not described as a determinant of bleomycin pulmonary toxicity.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Atropine is used for irinotecan-induced cholinergic symptoms and does not alter pulmonary risk.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Sex is not identified as a factor that raises the risk of bleomycin lung.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Vincristine causes neuropathy and constipation and is not linked to this pulmonary risk.

questions.topicName: Topoisomerase Inhibitors, Microtubule Inhibitors, and Antitumor Antibiotics

questions.stem: Bleomycin is frequently added to combination regimens for lymphoma. Apart from its broad antitumor activity, which property makes it especially useful alongside other cytotoxic drugs?

choices.label: A
choices.text: It carries no risk of organ toxicity at any dose

choices.label: C
choices.text: It chelates iron and protects cardiac tissue

choices.label: D
choices.text: It kills resting cells because it is cell cycle-independent

choices.label: E
choices.text: It shortens the neutropenia caused by other agents

explanation.summary: Bleomycin is unusual among chemotherapy drugs because myelosuppression is rare.
explanation.whyCorrect: Bleomycin is used to treat several types of cancers, including lymphomas, because of its broad activity and low myelotoxicity. It is unusual among chemotherapeutic agents in that myelosuppression is rare, which makes it easier to combine with marrow-suppressing drugs.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Bleomycin has a prominent organ toxicity: dose-limiting pulmonary toxicity that can be fatal and irreversible.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Iron chelation with cardiac protection describes dexrazoxane, used against anthracyclines.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Bleomycin is cell-cycle specific in G2 and M, not cell cycle-independent.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Bleomycin does not accelerate recovery of neutrophil counts after other agents.

questions.topicName: Topoisomerase Inhibitors, Microtubule Inhibitors, and Antitumor Antibiotics

questions.stem: In bleomycin-treated lungs, repeated oxidative injury to epithelial and endothelial cells triggers an inflammatory response. Which of the following processes most directly produces the resulting fibrosis?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Clonal proliferation of type II pneumocytes lining the alveoli

choices.label: B
choices.text: Deposition of immune complexes within alveolar capillaries

choices.label: C
choices.text: Eosinophil degranulation causing remodeling of bronchial walls

choices.label: D
choices.text: Macrophage release of profibrotic mediators that activate fibroblasts

choices.label: E
choices.text: Neutrophil elastase digestion of alveolar septa and elastic tissue

explanation.summary: Recruited macrophages release profibrotic mediators that activate fibroblasts and drive extracellular matrix deposition.
explanation.whyCorrect: Repeated bleomycin injury triggers an inflammatory response dominated by innate immune mechanisms, including recruitment of tissue-derived and monocyte-derived macrophages. These macrophages release profibrotic mediators that promote fibroblast activation and extracellular matrix deposition, which is the fibrosis itself.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Pneumocyte clonal proliferation is not what drives matrix deposition here; the cells are injured, not clonally expanded.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Immune complex deposition is not the described mechanism of bleomycin-induced fibrosis.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Eosinophil-driven bronchial remodeling describes asthma rather than this drug toxicity.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Elastase digestion of septa produces emphysematous destruction, the opposite of fibrotic matrix deposition.

questions.topicName: Topoisomerase Inhibitors, Microtubule Inhibitors, and Antitumor Antibiotics

questions.stem: Chemotherapeutic agents can be grouped by whether their activity depends on the phase of the cell cycle. Which of the following agents acts independently of cell-cycle phase?

explanation.summary: Platinum agents such as cisplatin are cell cycle-independent, unlike topoisomerase and microtubule inhibitors.
explanation.whyCorrect: The cell cycle-independent drugs include the platinum agents such as cisplatin, the alkylating agents, and the anthracyclines. By contrast, topoisomerase inhibitors and microtubule inhibitors are cell-cycle specific, acting at defined points in the cycle.

whyWrongByChoice.B: Etoposide is a topoisomerase II inhibitor that acts in S or early G2 phase.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Paclitaxel is a microtubule inhibitor that acts at mitosis.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Topotecan is a topoisomerase I inhibitor and is cell-cycle specific.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Vincristine is a microtubule inhibitor that arrests cells in metaphase.

questions.topicName: Topoisomerase Inhibitors, Microtubule Inhibitors, and Antitumor Antibiotics

questions.stem: Topoisomerases relieve the tension created by supercoiling of the DNA double helix. This release of tension is important for which of the following sets of cellular processes?

choices.label: B
choices.text: Oxidative phosphorylation, glycolysis, and fatty acid oxidation

choices.label: C
choices.text: Receptor signaling, second messenger release, and exocytosis

choices.label: D
choices.text: Ribosome assembly, translation, and protein folding

choices.label: E
choices.text: Vesicle transport, spindle formation, and cytokinesis

explanation.summary: Relieving supercoiling tension is required for DNA replication, transcription, and repair.
explanation.whyCorrect: Topoisomerase inhibitors kill cancer cells by interfering with topoisomerases, the enzymes that release the tension caused by supercoiling in the DNA double helix. That release of tension is important in DNA replication, transcription, and repair, so blocking it is lethal to dividing cells.

whyWrongByChoice.B: Energy metabolism pathways are unrelated to relief of DNA supercoiling.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Receptor signaling and exocytosis are membrane events with no dependence on topoisomerase activity.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Ribosome assembly and translation are downstream of transcription and are not what topoisomerases enable directly.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Vesicle transport, spindle formation, and cytokinesis depend on microtubules rather than on topoisomerases.

questions.topicName: Topoisomerase Inhibitors, Microtubule Inhibitors, and Antitumor Antibiotics

questions.stem: A 56-year-old woman being evaluated as a living kidney donor is found on a routine complete blood count to have a white blood cell count of 21.6 x 10^9/L with 60% lymphocytes; her hemoglobin and platelet counts are low-normal. She is asymptomatic with no palpable lymphadenopathy. A peripheral smear shows numerous mature-appearing small lymphocytes with condensed chromatin and scattered smudge cells. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

explanation.summary: An incidental absolute lymphocytosis of mature B cells with smudge cells on smear is the classic presentation of CLL/SLL.
explanation.whyCorrect: CLL/SLL is the most common low-grade non-Hodgkin lymphoma and the most common leukemia in Western adults. It is usually discovered incidentally when a blood count reveals high numbers of mature-appearing lymphocytes (lymphocytosis), and smudge cells are a frequent smear finding.

whyWrongByChoice.B: Diffuse large B-cell lymphoma is an aggressive lymphoma with a rapidly enlarging mass and B-symptoms, not an asymptomatic incidental lymphocytosis.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Follicular lymphoma presents with slowly progressive lymphadenopathy and the t(14;18) translocation, not an isolated incidental blood lymphocytosis with smudge cells.
whyWrongByChoice.D: MALT lymphoma is an extranodal disease that presents with gastric symptoms such as reflux and GI bleeding, not a peripheral lymphocytosis.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Hairy cell leukemia causes pancytopenia and splenomegaly rather than lymphocytosis, and its cells show hairy projections, not smudging.

questions.stem: A peripheral blood smear from a 68-year-old man with newly diagnosed chronic lymphocytic leukemia shows numerous mature lymphocytes plus several ruptured, smeared cellular remnants. Which of the following best explains these smudge cells?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Apoptotic neutrophils undergoing programmed cell death

choices.label: C
choices.text: Fragments of megakaryocytes in the peripheral blood

choices.label: D
choices.text: Nucleated red blood cell precursors released from marrow

choices.label: E
choices.text: Reactive plasma cells responding to infection

explanation.summary: Smudge cells are preparation artifacts formed when fragile CLL lymphocytes are crushed during smear creation.
explanation.whyCorrect: The brick describes smudge cells as a frequent histologic feature of CLL that arise as artifacts from fragile lymphocytes being crushed during slide preparation. They are not specific for CLL and can be seen in other lymphoproliferative disorders with leukocytes in the blood.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Smudge cells derive from the fragile malignant lymphocytes of CLL, not from apoptotic neutrophils.
whyWrongByChoice.C: They are not megakaryocyte fragments (which would relate to platelets), but crushed lymphocytes.
whyWrongByChoice.D: They are not nucleated red cell precursors; they represent disrupted lymphocytes.
whyWrongByChoice.E: They are not reactive plasma cells; they are a mechanical artifact of smear preparation.

questions.stem: Flow cytometry on the malignant cells of a patient with chronic lymphocytic leukemia demonstrates expression of CD19, CD20, and CD22 with dim light chain restriction, along with CD23 and CD200. Which additional marker, typically considered a T-cell antigen, is characteristically expressed by these cells?

explanation.summary: CLL cells aberrantly express CD5, a marker normally associated with T cells.
explanation.whyCorrect: The brick states that CLL cells express B-cell markers (CD19, CD20, CD22) with light chain restriction and also express CD5, which is typically a T-cell marker, along with CD23 and CD200.

whyWrongByChoice.A: CD3 is a pan-T-cell marker and is not expressed on the malignant B cells of CLL.
whyWrongByChoice.C: CD10 marks germinal-center cells and is characteristic of follicular lymphoma, not CLL.
whyWrongByChoice.D: CD30 is associated with Hodgkin and anaplastic lymphomas, not CLL.
whyWrongByChoice.E: CD103 is among the markers used to identify hairy cell leukemia, not CLL.

questions.stem: A patient with a several-year history of chronic lymphocytic leukemia/small lymphocytic lymphoma suddenly develops weakness, fevers, and widespread bulky lymphadenopathy. A lymph node biopsy shows sheets of transformed cells several times the size of a normal lymphocyte. This transformation is most consistent with which of the following, and what is the approximate prognosis?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Burkitt lymphoma; highly curable with intensive multi-agent chemotherapy

choices.label: B
choices.text: Diffuse large B-cell lymphoma; average life expectancy about 8 months

choices.label: C
choices.text: Follicular lymphoma; indolent with median survival beyond 10 years

choices.label: D
choices.text: Hodgkin lymphoma; usually cured, with average survival about 10 years

choices.label: E
choices.text: MALT lymphoma; cured with antibiotic eradication of Helicobacter pylori

explanation.summary: Richter transformation is the feared conversion of CLL into aggressive diffuse large B-cell lymphoma, with a poor prognosis.
explanation.whyCorrect: The brick describes Richter transformation, in which CLL transforms into the high-grade aggressive NHL diffuse large B-cell lymphoma. It occurs in about 2% to 9% of cases, presents with sudden deterioration and B-symptoms, and carries an average life expectancy of only 8 months.

whyWrongByChoice.A: The transformation is to diffuse large B-cell lymphoma, not Burkitt lymphoma.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Follicular lymphoma is not the product of Richter transformation, and the sudden aggressive course described is not indolent.
whyWrongByChoice.D: CLL does not transform into Hodgkin lymphoma in this scenario; the transformed disease is diffuse large B-cell lymphoma with a much shorter survival.
whyWrongByChoice.E: MALT lymphoma is unrelated to Richter transformation and is treated by H. pylori eradication, not relevant here.

questions.stem: A 45-year-old asymptomatic man has flow cytometry performed after a mildly elevated lymphocyte count is noted. It reveals a small clonal B-cell population with an immunophenotype similar to CLL, quantified at 3,000 clonal lymphocytes/microliter. Which of the following is the most appropriate diagnosis?

explanation.summary: A CLL-like monoclonal B-cell population below 5,000/microliter defines monoclonal B-cell lymphocytosis, a precursor state.
explanation.whyCorrect: The brick defines monoclonal B-cell lymphocytosis (MBL) as a small monoclonal B-cell population with a phenotype similar to CLL but in lower quantities (<5,000 clonal lymphocytes/microliter; >5,000 is CLL). It is considered a precursor state to CLL that may never transform and usually requires no treatment.

whyWrongByChoice.A: A diagnosis of CLL requires >5,000 clonal lymphocytes/microliter, which this patient does not meet.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Reactive lymphocytosis is polyclonal, whereas this population is monoclonal.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Richter transformation is an aggressive conversion of established CLL, not an asymptomatic low-level clone.
whyWrongByChoice.E: SLL presents predominantly with lymphadenopathy rather than a small circulating monoclonal population.

questions.stem: A 65-year-old woman has slowly progressive painless cervical and axillary lymphadenopathy. A lymph node biopsy shows a nodular pattern of CD10-positive cells, and cytogenetics reveal a t(14;18) translocation. Which of the following best explains the pathogenesis of this lymphoma?

choices.label: A
choices.text: A BCR-ABL fusion producing a constitutively active tyrosine kinase

choices.label: B
choices.text: A BRAF mutation activating a serine/threonine kinase

choices.label: C
choices.text: Isolated loss of TP53 as the sole driver mutation

choices.label: D
choices.text: Overexpression of MYC driving uncontrolled cellular proliferation

choices.label: E
choices.text: Placement of BCL-2 under the IGH regulatory region

explanation.summary: Follicular lymphoma is driven by t(14;18), which places BCL-2 under IGH control so it is constitutively expressed and blocks apoptosis.
explanation.whyCorrect: In the t(14;18) translocation the BCL-2 gene on chromosome 18 ends up within the regulatory region of the IGH gene on chromosome 14, so BCL-2 becomes constantly expressed. Because BCL-2 normally blocks apoptosis, the cells become immortal and develop into lymphoma.

whyWrongByChoice.A: The BCR-ABL fusion is the driver of chronic myeloid leukemia, not follicular lymphoma.
whyWrongByChoice.B: BRAF mutation is the characteristic lesion of hairy cell leukemia, not follicular lymphoma.
whyWrongByChoice.C: The described disease is defined by the t(14;18)/BCL-2 mechanism, not by isolated TP53 loss.
whyWrongByChoice.D: MYC overexpression is characteristic of Burkitt lymphoma, not follicular lymphoma.

questions.stem: A pathologist must distinguish the neoplastic follicles of follicular lymphoma from the reactive follicular hyperplasia of a benign lymph node responding to infection. Which of the following histologic features favors follicular lymphoma?

choices.label: B
choices.text: Polytypic (mixed kappa and lambda) light chain expression

choices.label: C
choices.text: Preserved nodal architecture with open patent sinuses

choices.label: D
choices.text: Prominent mantle zones with numerous tingible-body macrophages

choices.label: E
choices.text: Scattered sheets of binucleate Reed-Sternberg cells

explanation.summary: Follicular lymphoma follicles lack the mantle zones seen in reactive nodes and are more uniform and crowded together.
explanation.whyCorrect: The brick teaches that the follicles in follicular lymphoma lack the mantle zones (dark blue collars of small mature lymphocytes) that normally surround germinal centers in nonneoplastic lymph nodes, and that FL follicles are more uniform in shape and closer together.

whyWrongByChoice.B: Polytypic light chain expression indicates a reactive polyclonal population; lymphoma shows light chain restriction.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Preserved nodal architecture points to a benign process; lymphoma tends to efface architecture.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Prominent mantle zones and tingible-body macrophages are features of a reactive/benign follicle, not follicular lymphoma.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Reed-Sternberg cells are a feature of Hodgkin lymphoma, not follicular lymphoma.

questions.stem: A patient with stage III follicular lymphoma is started on the R-CVP regimen. The monoclonal antibody component of this regimen exerts its effect by targeting which of the following?

explanation.summary: Rituximab, the R in R-CVP, is a monoclonal antibody directed against the CD20 antigen.
explanation.whyCorrect: The brick states that rituximab is a monoclonal antibody against the CD20 antigen that activates B-cell cytotoxicity; common reactions include fever, upper respiratory tract infections, infusion reactions, and asthenia.

whyWrongByChoice.A: BTK is inhibited by ibrutinib, which is used in CLL, not by rituximab.
whyWrongByChoice.C: CD5 is a marker used to identify CLL cells but is not the target of rituximab.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Microtubule function is inhibited by vincristine, another component of R-CVP, not by the antibody.
whyWrongByChoice.E: BCL-2 is the target of venetoclax, a BH3 mimetic, not of rituximab.

questions.stem: A patient receiving the R-CVP regimen for follicular lymphoma is counseled about a risk of hemorrhagic cystitis, which is mitigated by co-administration of Mesna. Which component of the regimen carries this risk?

explanation.summary: Cyclophosphamide, an alkylating agent, can cause hemorrhagic cystitis, whose risk is reduced with Mesna.
explanation.whyCorrect: The brick lists cyclophosphamide as an alkylating agent that interferes with DNA/RNA replication, with myelosuppression, SIADH, and hemorrhagic cystitis (risk reduced with Mesna) as common adverse effects.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Cladribine is a purine analog used for hairy cell leukemia and is not part of the R-CVP regimen.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Prednisolone causes steroid effects such as fractures, osteonecrosis, and mood changes.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Rituximab characteristically causes fever, infusion reactions, and asthenia, not hemorrhagic cystitis.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Vincristine causes dose-related peripheral neuropathy, not hemorrhagic cystitis.

questions.stem: A 58-year-old man has epigastric pain, reflux, and intermittent GI bleeding. Upper endoscopy with biopsy reveals a low-grade B-cell lymphoma with lymphoepithelial lesions that is CD5-negative and CD10-negative; Helicobacter pylori is identified on biopsy. Which of the following is the most appropriate first-line treatment?

explanation.summary: Gastric MALT lymphoma is tied to H. pylori, so first-line therapy is antibiotic eradication of the organism.
explanation.whyCorrect: The brick explains that gastric MALT lymphoma's main association is with H. pylori, so first-line treatment is eradication of H. pylori with antibiotics; the regimen includes a proton pump inhibitor, tetracycline, metronidazole, and bismuth subsalicylate, and can cure the disease if caught early.

whyWrongByChoice.B: Cladribine is the purine analog used for hairy cell leukemia, not MALT lymphoma.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Ibrutinib is a BTK inhibitor used in CLL, not first-line for gastric MALT lymphoma.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Chemotherapy (along with radiation and surgery) is reserved for cases where eradication therapy fails, not as first-line.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Splenectomy is not a treatment for gastric MALT lymphoma.

questions.stem: A 55-year-old man presents with fatigue and abdominal fullness. Examination shows marked splenomegaly but no lymphadenopathy. Laboratory studies reveal pancytopenia, and the peripheral smear shows rare mononuclear cells with abundant fluffy cytoplasm and fine, indistinct cytoplasmic projections; molecular testing detects a BRAF mutation. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

explanation.summary: Pancytopenia and splenomegaly without lymphadenopathy, plus hairy cells and a BRAF mutation, define hairy cell leukemia.
explanation.whyCorrect: The brick describes HCL as an NHL that, unlike others, does not present with enlarged lymph nodes; marrow invasion causes pancytopenia and splenomegaly. It arises from memory B cells with a BRAF mutation (seen in >90% of cases), and the smear shows hairy cells with fluffy cytoplasm and characteristic projections.

whyWrongByChoice.A: CLL/SLL produces lymphocytosis and lymphadenopathy with CD5-positive cells, not pancytopenia with hairy cells.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Diffuse large B-cell lymphoma is an aggressive nodal/mass lesion, not this indolent hairy-cell presentation.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Follicular lymphoma presents with lymphadenopathy and a t(14;18) translocation, not this marrow-failure picture.
whyWrongByChoice.E: MALT lymphoma is an extranodal gastric disease, not a cause of pancytopenia with splenomegaly.

questions.stem: A 57-year-old man with hairy cell leukemia now has symptomatic pancytopenia and splenomegaly. Which of the following is the preferred first-line treatment?

explanation.summary: Symptomatic hairy cell leukemia is treated first-line with a purine analog such as cladribine or pentostatin.
explanation.whyCorrect: The brick states that in symptomatic HCL, purine analogs like cladribine or pentostatin are the preferred initial treatment. These are adenosine analogs that are incorporated into DNA, causing strand breaks and inhibition of DNA synthesis.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Antibiotic H. pylori eradication is first-line for gastric MALT lymphoma, not hairy cell leukemia.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Observation is appropriate only for asymptomatic HCL; this patient is symptomatic and warrants treatment.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Ibrutinib is a BTK inhibitor used for CLL, not first-line for hairy cell leukemia.
whyWrongByChoice.E: R-CVP is used for follicular lymphoma, not hairy cell leukemia.

questions.stem: A hematology lecture compares the burden of B-cell non-Hodgkin lymphomas with that of Hodgkin lymphoma. Which of the following best describes the epidemiology of B-cell non-Hodgkin lymphomas?

choices.label: A
choices.text: New cases are outnumbered by Hodgkin lymphoma by about 2 to 1 and occur in an older population

choices.label: B
choices.text: New cases are outnumbered by Hodgkin lymphoma by about 8 to 1 and occur in a younger population

choices.label: C
choices.text: New cases outnumber Hodgkin lymphoma by about 2 to 1 and occur in a younger population

choices.label: D
choices.text: New cases outnumber Hodgkin lymphoma by about 8 to 1 and occur in an older population

choices.label: E
choices.text: New cases roughly equal those of Hodgkin lymphoma and occur at a similar age

explanation.summary: B-cell non-Hodgkin lymphomas are far more common than Hodgkin lymphoma and affect an older population.
explanation.whyCorrect: Non-Hodgkin B-cell lymphomas account for 2% to 3% of all malignancies. Annual new cases outnumber Hodgkin lymphoma by about 8 to 1, and the affected population skews older than that of Hodgkin lymphoma. Of the subtypes, CLL/SLL is the most common.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Non-Hodgkin lymphomas are not outnumbered by Hodgkin lymphoma at any ratio.
whyWrongByChoice.B: The ratio runs the other direction: non-Hodgkin lymphomas are the more numerous group.
whyWrongByChoice.C: The excess over Hodgkin lymphoma is roughly 8-fold rather than 2-fold, and the population is older rather than younger.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Non-Hodgkin lymphoma cases far exceed Hodgkin lymphoma cases and affect an older age group, so neither the number nor the age distribution is equal.

questions.stem: A 63-year-old man is evaluated for a 6-month history of painless enlargement of cervical and axillary lymph nodes. A node biopsy shows sheets of monotonous, mature-appearing lymphocytes no larger than a normal lymphocyte that are CD5 positive and CD23 positive. His complete blood count is normal, with no circulating lymphocytosis. Which of the following terms best describes his disease?

explanation.summary: CLL and SLL are the same disease; the SLL label is used when the presentation is predominantly nodal rather than in blood and marrow.
explanation.whyCorrect: The cells of CLL and SLL look the same (small and mature) and carry the same immunophenotype. The distinction is one of presentation: patients with CLL present with large numbers of malignant white blood cells in the blood and bone marrow, while patients with SLL present mostly with lymphadenopathy, as here.

whyWrongByChoice.A: The CLL designation applies when malignant lymphocytes dominate the blood and marrow, and this patient's blood count is normal.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Follicular lymphoma forms nodules of CD10-positive germinal center cells, not sheets of CD5-positive small lymphocytes.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Hairy cell leukemia characteristically spares the lymph nodes and presents with pancytopenia and splenomegaly.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Monoclonal B-cell lymphocytosis requires a small circulating monoclonal population, not bulky nodal disease.

questions.stem: A 68-year-old woman has a white blood cell count of 5.2 x 10^9/L with 65% lymphocytes, giving an absolute lymphocyte count of 3.4 x 10^9/L. Another patient in the same clinic has a white blood cell count of 24 x 10^9/L with 65% lymphocytes. Which of the following best characterizes the first patient's finding?

choices.label: A
choices.text: A relative lymphocytosis, derived by multiplying the lymphocyte percentage by the white blood cell count

choices.label: B
choices.text: A relative lymphocytosis, which may appear when other white blood cell lines are decreased

choices.label: C
choices.text: An absolute lymphocytosis, derived by dividing the lymphocyte percentage by the white blood cell count

choices.label: D
choices.text: An absolute lymphocytosis, which carries the same significance as a relative lymphocytosis

choices.label: E
choices.text: Both an absolute and a relative lymphocytosis, because the percentage exceeds 50%

explanation.summary: A high lymphocyte percentage with a normal absolute count is a relative lymphocytosis, which often reflects a fall in the other white cell lines.
explanation.whyCorrect: On a CBC the white blood cells are reported as a percentage and as an absolute number, the absolute number being the percentage multiplied by the total WBC. Here the absolute lymphocyte count is normal, so the elevated percentage is a relative lymphocytosis, which may simply reflect a decrease in the proportion of other white blood cells such as neutrophils. The absolute lymphocytosis of the second patient is the more clinically significant finding.

whyWrongByChoice.A: The multiplication step yields the absolute count; a relative lymphocytosis is read off the percentage alone.
whyWrongByChoice.C: The absolute count is obtained by multiplying, not dividing, and this patient's absolute count is not elevated.
whyWrongByChoice.D: An absolute lymphocytosis is more clinically significant than a relative lymphocytosis, so the two are not equivalent.
whyWrongByChoice.E: A percentage above 50% does not by itself establish an absolute lymphocytosis, which depends on the total WBC.

questions.stem: A 74-year-old man has had chronic lymphocytic leukemia for 9 years. He has required several hospital admissions for pneumonia and has neutropenia in addition to his lymphocytosis. Which of the following is by far the most common cause of death in this disease?

explanation.summary: Infection is by far the most common cause of death in CLL.
explanation.whyCorrect: Cytopenias of the other mature cell lines (granulocytes, platelets, red cells) develop in CLL and may lead to anemia and bleeding, but infections are by far the most common cause of death. These lymphomas also produce cytokines that suppress the normal immune system and infiltrate the marrow, further reducing normal white blood cell production.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Autoimmune hemolysis develops in a minority of patients and is not the most common cause of death.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Bleeding from low platelets occurs in CLL but is not the leading cause of death.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Anemia is a recognized consequence of the cytopenias but is not the usual terminal event.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Transformation in CLL is to diffuse large B-cell lymphoma (Richter transformation), not to acute myeloid leukemia.

questions.stem: A 66-year-old woman with newly diagnosed chronic lymphocytic leukemia has flow cytometry performed. In addition to the markers used to establish the diagnosis, the panel reports CD38 and CD49d. Which of the following best describes the role of these two markers?

choices.label: A
choices.text: They confirm the B-cell lineage of the malignant clone

choices.label: B
choices.text: They demonstrate the light chain restriction required for diagnosis

choices.label: C
choices.text: They distinguish chronic lymphocytic leukemia from small lymphocytic lymphoma

choices.label: D
choices.text: They establish that Richter transformation has occurred

choices.label: E
choices.text: They provide prognostic information about the disease course

explanation.summary: CD38 and CD49d are cell surface markers used for prognostication in CLL rather than for diagnosis.
explanation.whyCorrect: The diagnosis of CLL rests on the immunophenotype of B-cell markers (CD19, CD20, CD22) with light chain restriction plus CD5, CD23, and CD200. Some cell surface markers, such as CD38 and CD49d, have been used to establish prognosis.

whyWrongByChoice.A: B-cell lineage is established by CD19, CD20, and CD22, not by CD38 or CD49d.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Light chain restriction is demonstrated by dim kappa or lambda expression, not by these two markers.
whyWrongByChoice.C: CLL and SLL share an identical immunophenotype; they are separated by clinical presentation, not by surface markers.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Richter transformation is established by biopsy showing high-grade diffuse large B-cell lymphoma, not by a flow marker.

questions.stem: A high-power view of a lymph node involved by small lymphocytic lymphoma shows that the majority of the tumor cells are small round lymphocytes. Scattered among them is a larger cell with a centrally placed nucleolus. This larger cell is best identified as which of the following?

explanation.summary: The larger cell with a centrally placed nucleolus seen among the small lymphocytes of SLL is a prolymphocyte.
explanation.whyCorrect: In SLL involving a lymph node, low power shows effacement of nodal architecture and high power shows that most tumor cells are small round lymphocytes. A prolymphocyte, a larger cell with a centrally placed nucleolus, is also present in such fields.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Centroblasts are the large cells with vesicular chromatin found within follicular lymphoma nodules.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Hairy cells are the fluffy-cytoplasm cells of hairy cell leukemia, a disease that does not involve lymph nodes.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Reed-Sternberg cells belong to Hodgkin lymphoma, which is pathologically distinct from the non-Hodgkin lymphomas.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Tingible-body macrophages are a feature of reactive germinal centers, not of SLL infiltrates.

questions.stem: A 70-year-old man with a 4-year history of chronic lymphocytic leukemia develops fatigue and scleral icterus. Hemoglobin is 7.8 g/dL, the reticulocyte count is elevated, indirect bilirubin is elevated, and the direct antiglobulin test is positive. Which of the following best explains his anemia?

choices.label: B
choices.text: Autoantibody-mediated destruction of red blood cells

choices.label: C
choices.text: Iron deficiency from occult gastrointestinal blood loss

choices.label: D
choices.text: Marrow replacement by lymphoma cells suppressing erythropoiesis

choices.label: E
choices.text: Transformation to diffuse large B-cell lymphoma

explanation.summary: About a quarter of CLL patients develop autoantibodies, and those against red cells produce autoimmune hemolytic anemia.
explanation.whyCorrect: Beyond the cytopenia caused by bone marrow failure, approximately 25% of patients with CLL develop autoantibodies through complex interactions of malignant and normal B cells. These can react against normal blood cells, causing autoimmune hemolytic anemia, pure red cell aplasia, autoimmune granulocytopenia, and immune thrombocytopenia. The elevated reticulocyte count, elevated indirect bilirubin, and positive antiglobulin test point to immune hemolysis.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Antiplatelet autoantibodies cause immune thrombocytopenia and bleeding, which would not produce this hemolytic picture.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Iron deficiency causes a hypoproliferative microcytic anemia without hemolytic markers or a positive antiglobulin test.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Marrow replacement produces a hypoproliferative anemia with a low reticulocyte count, not the brisk reticulocytosis seen here.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Richter transformation presents with sudden deterioration, B-symptoms, and bulky lymphadenopathy rather than isolated hemolysis.

questions.stem: A 62-year-old woman is found to have early-stage chronic lymphocytic leukemia. She is asymptomatic, has no lymphadenopathy, and has normal hemoglobin and platelet counts, though flow cytometry reports expression of CD38. Which of the following is the most appropriate next step in management?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Begin R-CVP combination chemotherapy every three weeks

choices.label: B
choices.text: Begin treatment with ibrutinib immediately and continue it indefinitely

choices.label: C
choices.text: Begin venetoclax combined with rituximab now after a dose ramp-up

choices.label: D
choices.text: Observation with blood counts about every three months

choices.label: E
choices.text: Refer for allogeneic stem cell transplantation from a sibling donor

explanation.summary: Early-stage CLL is observed with periodic blood counts regardless of risk markers.
explanation.whyCorrect: For all patients in the early stages of CLL, irrespective of risk factors, the standard of care is observation. During this period blood counts are obtained every three months, though the interval can be lengthened in patients with clinically stable disease. Treatment is reserved for active disease.

whyWrongByChoice.A: R-CVP is the systemic regimen used in follicular lymphoma of stage II and above, not in early-stage CLL.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Ibrutinib is one of the agents used once the disease is active, not for early-stage asymptomatic disease.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Venetoclax with rituximab is a treatment option for active CLL and is not indicated during the observation period.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Transplantation is not the described management approach for early-stage disease.

questions.stem: A 71-year-old man with active chronic lymphocytic leukemia is started on ibrutinib. Which of the following adverse effects is most characteristic of this agent and should be discussed with him before therapy?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Atrial fibrillation along with bruising and hemorrhage

choices.label: B
choices.text: Dose-related peripheral neuropathy with loss of reflexes

choices.label: C
choices.text: Hemorrhagic cystitis requiring Mesna for prophylaxis

choices.label: D
choices.text: Osteonecrosis and fragility fractures with long-term use

choices.label: E
choices.text: Pyrexia in over 30% of patients along with headache

explanation.summary: Ibrutinib, a BTK inhibitor, characteristically causes bleeding and atrial fibrillation.
explanation.whyCorrect: Ibrutinib inhibits Bruton tyrosine kinase, an integral component of the B-cell receptor and cytokine receptor pathways. Its adverse effects include bruising and hemorrhage, atrial fibrillation, rash, gastrointestinal disturbances such as diarrhea and nausea, infections, and cytopenias.

whyWrongByChoice.B: Dose-related peripheral neuropathy with areflexia is characteristic of vincristine.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Hemorrhagic cystitis is the alkylating-agent toxicity of cyclophosphamide, mitigated with Mesna.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Osteonecrosis and fractures are long-term glucocorticoid effects, as with prednisolone.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Pyrexia in more than 30% of patients along with headache describes the purine analogs cladribine and pentostatin.

questions.stem: A 69-year-old man with relapsed chronic lymphocytic leukemia is started on venetoclax. The protein this drug targets is overexpressed in CLL, allowing the malignant cells to evade apoptosis and develop resistance to chemotherapeutic agents. Which of the following best describes how venetoclax works?

choices.label: A
choices.text: It inhibits Bruton tyrosine kinase within the B-cell receptor pathway

choices.label: B
choices.text: It is a BH3 mimetic that binds and inhibits BCL-2, restoring programmed cell death

choices.label: C
choices.text: It is a monoclonal antibody that activates cytotoxicity against CD20

choices.label: D
choices.text: It is an adenosine analog incorporated into DNA, causing strand breaks

choices.label: E
choices.text: It is an alkylating agent that interferes with DNA and RNA replication

explanation.summary: Venetoclax is an orally bioavailable BH3 mimetic that selectively inhibits BCL-2 and restores apoptosis in CLL cells.
explanation.whyCorrect: The BCL-2 protein family regulates mitochondrial outer membrane permeabilization and apoptosis, and proapoptotic members require a BH3 domain to dimerize with other family members and initiate apoptosis. Venetoclax mimics that domain, binding and inhibiting the overexpressed BCL-2 so that BCL-2-mediated survival signaling is blocked and apoptosis resumes. Common adverse effects include neutropenia, diarrhea, nausea, anemia, thrombocytopenia, fatigue, and upper respiratory infections, and it may cause fetal harm.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Bruton tyrosine kinase inhibition describes ibrutinib and the related agents acalabrutinib and zanubrutinib.
whyWrongByChoice.C: The anti-CD20 monoclonal antibody that activates B-cell cytotoxicity is rituximab.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Adenosine analogs incorporated into DNA are cladribine and pentostatin, used in hairy cell leukemia.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Alkylating activity against DNA and RNA replication describes cyclophosphamide.

questions.stem: A hematologist is choosing a Bruton tyrosine kinase inhibitor for a 68-year-old man with active chronic lymphocytic leukemia and selects acalabrutinib rather than ibrutinib. Which of the following best explains this preference?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Acalabrutinib acts as a BH3 mimetic, whereas ibrutinib does not

choices.label: B
choices.text: Acalabrutinib is given as a single dose, whereas ibrutinib requires infusion

choices.label: C
choices.text: Acalabrutinib is the only agent effective after Richter transformation

choices.label: D
choices.text: Acalabrutinib offers better efficacy and progression-free survival

choices.label: E
choices.text: Acalabrutinib removes the need for periodic monitoring of blood counts

explanation.summary: Newer BTK inhibitors such as acalabrutinib and zanubrutinib are increasingly favored over ibrutinib for better efficacy and progression-free survival.
explanation.whyCorrect: Other BTK inhibitors, such as acalabrutinib or zanubrutinib, are becoming more preferred over ibrutinib because of better efficacy and progression-free survival. Another treatment option in CLL is venetoclax combined with rituximab.

whyWrongByChoice.A: The BH3 mimetic used in CLL is venetoclax; acalabrutinib acts on Bruton tyrosine kinase.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Both agents are BTK inhibitors given as oral therapy, and the preference is not based on a single infused dose.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Richter transformation converts the disease into aggressive diffuse large B-cell lymphoma with a poor prognosis; no BTK inhibitor is described as the sole effective agent for it.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Cytopenias remain a concern with BTK inhibitors, so monitoring of blood counts is still required.

questions.stem: A 66-year-old woman with newly diagnosed follicular lymphoma undergoes staging evaluation. Imaging shows enlarged lymph nodes in the left axilla and in the retroperitoneum, with no involvement of any organ. Which of the following best describes her stage?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Stage I, because disease is limited to a single lymph node region

choices.label: B
choices.text: Stage II, because a single organ plus one adjacent nodal region is involved

choices.label: C
choices.text: Stage II, because two or more nodal regions on the same side are involved

choices.label: D
choices.text: Stage III, because nodal disease lies on both sides of the diaphragm

choices.label: E
choices.text: Stage IV, because the disease is widespread through multiple organs

explanation.summary: Nodal disease above and below the diaphragm without organ involvement is stage III.
explanation.whyCorrect: Staging evaluation assesses the extent of disease: stage I is localized disease in a single lymph node region or single organ, stage II is two or more lymph node regions on the same side of the diaphragm, stage III is two or more lymph node regions above and below the diaphragm, and stage IV is widespread disease in multiple organs. Localized disease (stage I-II) has a better prognosis than advanced disease (stage III-IV), and most patients with follicular lymphoma present with high-stage disease despite its indolent growth.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Two separate nodal regions are involved, which exceeds the single region or single organ of stage I.
whyWrongByChoice.B: No organ is involved, so this does not fit the described stage II pattern.
whyWrongByChoice.C: The axilla and retroperitoneum lie on opposite sides of the diaphragm, so the disease is not confined to one side.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Stage IV requires widespread disease involving multiple organs, and no organ is involved here.

questions.stem: A high-power view of a nodule within a lymph node involved by follicular lymphoma shows small dark cells with condensed chromatin and cleaved nuclear outlines admixed with a population of larger cells with vesicular chromatin and nucleoli. These two neoplastic populations are termed which of the following?

explanation.summary: Follicular lymphoma nodules contain small cleaved centrocytes mixed with larger centroblasts.
explanation.whyCorrect: At high power the individual neoplastic cells of follicular lymphoma are termed centrocytes, the small dark cells with condensed chromatin and cleaved nuclear outlines, and centroblasts, the larger cells with vesicular chromatin and nucleoli. Both are found within the nodules the lymphoma cells form.

whyWrongByChoice.B: Hairy cells are the malignant cells of hairy cell leukemia and are not found in follicular lymphoma.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Mantle zones are precisely what the neoplastic follicles of follicular lymphoma lack, and tingible-body macrophages belong to reactive follicles.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Plasma cells and immunoblasts do not describe the two cell populations within follicular lymphoma nodules.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Prolymphocytes and smudge cells belong to the pathology of CLL/SLL, not to follicular lymphoma nodules.

questions.stem: A 64-year-old woman has follicular lymphoma confined to a single cervical nodal region on staging evaluation. She has no B-symptoms and normal blood counts. Which of the following is the most appropriate initial treatment?

choices.label: B
choices.text: Eradication of Helicobacter pylori with antibiotics

explanation.summary: Early-stage follicular lymphoma is treated initially with radiation therapy; systemic chemotherapy is reserved for stage II and above.
explanation.whyCorrect: Based on the pathologic evaluation of the patient, initial treatment of follicular lymphoma may involve radiation therapy, particularly at early stages. Radiation therapy uses ionizing radiation to kill abnormal cells and control their growth. Systemic therapy with R-CVP is reserved for patients in stages II and above.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Cladribine is a purine analog used for symptomatic hairy cell leukemia.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Antibiotic eradication of H. pylori is the first-line treatment for gastric MALT lymphoma, not follicular lymphoma.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Ibrutinib is a BTK inhibitor used in active CLL rather than in follicular lymphoma.
whyWrongByChoice.D: R-CVP is systemic therapy reserved for stage II and above, not for disease limited to one nodal region.

questions.stem: A 60-year-old man receiving R-CVP for follicular lymphoma develops paresthesias of the hands and feet, loss of deep tendon reflexes, weakness, and hoarseness attributed to vocal cord paralysis. Which component of the regimen is most likely responsible?

explanation.summary: Vincristine causes a dose-related peripheral neuropathy that can extend to autonomic paralysis, including vocal cord paralysis.
explanation.whyCorrect: Vincristine works by inhibition of microtubule function. Dose-related peripheral neuropathy is associated with its use and can cause paresthesia, loss of reflexes, weakness, and autonomic paralysis, including vocal cord paralysis.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Cyclophosphamide causes myelosuppression, SIADH, and hemorrhagic cystitis.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Mesna is given to reduce the risk of hemorrhagic cystitis and is not a cause of neuropathy.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Prednisolone produces long-term steroid effects such as fractures, osteonecrosis, infections, and mood or behavior problems.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Rituximab characteristically causes fever, upper respiratory tract infections, infusion reactions, and asthenia.

questions.stem: A patient treated with the R-CVP regimen for several cycles is counseled about the long-term risks of its glucocorticoid component. Which of the following adverse effects is most characteristic of that component?

explanation.summary: Prednisolone, the glucocorticoid in R-CVP, causes steroid-associated fractures, osteonecrosis, infections, and mood changes.
explanation.whyCorrect: Prednisolone is a glucocorticoid that can cause long-term steroid-associated adverse drug reactions such as fractures, osteonecrosis, infections, and mood or behavior problems.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Atrial fibrillation is associated with the BTK inhibitor ibrutinib, which is not part of R-CVP.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Hemorrhagic cystitis belongs to cyclophosphamide, the alkylating agent in the regimen.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Infusion reactions and asthenia are common reactions to rituximab.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Peripheral neuropathy is the dose-related toxicity of vincristine.

questions.stem: Although follicular lymphoma typically behaves as a low-grade disease, it can progress to a higher-grade lymphoma. Progression is most likely to be to which of the following?

choices.label: C
choices.text: Gastric MALT lymphoma from H. pylori

choices.label: D
choices.text: Hairy cell leukemia with BRAF mutation

explanation.summary: Follicular lymphoma can progress to higher-grade disease, particularly diffuse large B-cell lymphoma.
explanation.whyCorrect: Though follicular lymphoma typically presents as a low-grade disease, it can progress to higher-grade disease, particularly diffuse large B-cell lymphoma, which is one of the aggressive B-cell neoplasms contrasted with the low-grade lymphomas.

whyWrongByChoice.A: CLL/SLL is itself a low-grade lymphoma and is not the product of follicular lymphoma progression.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Gastric MALT lymphoma is a low-grade extranodal lymphoma tied to chronic inflammation, not a higher-grade transformation.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Hairy cell leukemia is a separate low-grade entity arising from memory B cells with a BRAF mutation.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Hodgkin lymphoma is pathologically distinct from the non-Hodgkin lymphomas and is not the result of this progression.

questions.stem: A 52-year-old woman with a long history of Sjögren syndrome develops painless enlargement of a parotid gland. Biopsy shows a low-grade B-cell lymphoma of marginal zone type arising within the gland. Which of the following best explains the development of this lymphoma?

choices.label: A
choices.text: A BRAF mutation arising within a memory B cell

choices.label: B
choices.text: A t(14;18) translocation placing BCL-2 under IGH control

choices.label: C
choices.text: Aberrant expression of CD5 by the malignant B cells

choices.label: D
choices.text: Chronic inflammation at an extranodal mucosal site

choices.label: E
choices.text: Overexpression of MYC driving uncontrolled proliferation

explanation.summary: MALT lymphoma arises at extranodal mucosal sites in states of chronic inflammation, including autoimmune disease.
explanation.whyCorrect: MALT lymphoma is a low-grade, indolent B-cell lymphoma of extranodal mucosal sites typically associated with states of chronic inflammation, which is why it is linked to certain microorganisms and autoimmune diseases. Besides H. pylori, associations include Chlamydia and Campylobacter infections and autoimmune diseases such as Sjogren syndrome, Hashimoto thyroiditis, and lupus. MALT tissue lies beneath mucosal surfaces, including the salivary glands, Peyer patches, and the bronchial tree.

whyWrongByChoice.A: A BRAF mutation in a memory B cell underlies hairy cell leukemia, which presents with pancytopenia and splenomegaly.
whyWrongByChoice.B: The t(14;18) translocation with constitutive BCL-2 expression drives follicular lymphoma.
whyWrongByChoice.C: CD5 expression characterizes CLL/SLL; MALT lymphoma cells are typically CD5 negative and CD10 negative.
whyWrongByChoice.E: MYC overexpression is characteristic of Burkitt lymphoma, an aggressive B-cell neoplasm.

questions.stem: A gastric biopsy from a patient with MALT lymphoma shows neoplastic marginal zone B cells invading and disrupting the glandular epithelial structures. This histologic finding is termed which of the following?

explanation.summary: MALT cells invading the glands produce the lymphoepithelial lesion.
explanation.whyCorrect: Histologically, MALT lymphoma shows lymphoid cells invading the surrounding glandular epithelial structures. When the MALT cells invade the glands, the finding is called a lymphoepithelial lesion. The lymphoma cells typically demonstrate a CD5-negative and CD10-negative immunophenotype.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Nodules are the round organized structures formed by follicular lymphoma cells within lymph nodes.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Germinal centers are normal follicular structures of the lymph node, not gland invasion by lymphoma.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Smudge cells are peripheral smear artifacts from fragile lymphocytes, most often noted in CLL.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Tingible-body macrophages are seen in reactive follicles, not within invaded gastric glands.

questions.stem: A 60-year-old man with gastric MALT lymphoma has Helicobacter pylori identified on biopsy and is to begin eradication therapy. Besides a proton pump inhibitor for acid suppression, the regimen should include which of the following?

explanation.summary: H. pylori eradication for gastric MALT lymphoma combines a proton pump inhibitor with tetracycline, metronidazole, and bismuth subsalicylate.
explanation.whyCorrect: Because gastric MALT is mainly associated with H. pylori, first-line treatment is eradication of the organism with antibiotics. The regimen includes a proton pump inhibitor for acid suppression, tetracycline, metronidazole, and bismuth subsalicylate. If eradication therapy fails, radiation, chemotherapy, and surgery are options.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Cladribine and pentostatin are the purine analogs used for symptomatic hairy cell leukemia.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Chemotherapy and radiation are reserved for MALT lymphoma only after eradication therapy fails.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Ibrutinib, venetoclax, and rituximab are agents used for active CLL, not for eradicating H. pylori.
whyWrongByChoice.E: These are the cytotoxic components of R-CVP, the systemic regimen used in follicular lymphoma of stage II and above.

questions.stem: Which of the following demographic patterns is characteristic of hairy cell leukemia?

choices.label: A
choices.text: A 4:1 female predominance with a median age at diagnosis of 55 years

choices.label: B
choices.text: A 4:1 male predominance with a median age at diagnosis of 25 years

choices.label: C
choices.text: A 4:1 male predominance with a median age at diagnosis of 55 years

choices.label: D
choices.text: A slight female predominance with a median age at diagnosis of 40 years

choices.label: E
choices.text: An equal sex distribution with a median age at diagnosis of 70 years

explanation.summary: Hairy cell leukemia shows a strong male predilection with a 4:1 male-to-female ratio and a median age at diagnosis of 55 years.
explanation.whyCorrect: Hairy cell leukemia has a predilection for males, with a 4:1 male-to-female ratio, and the median age at diagnosis is 55 years.

whyWrongByChoice.A: The 4:1 ratio favors males, not females.
whyWrongByChoice.B: The median age at diagnosis is 55 years, well above the mid-20s.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Hairy cell leukemia is strongly male predominant, and the median age is 55 years.
whyWrongByChoice.E: A median age of 70 years with near-equal sex distribution describes CLL, which has only a slight male predominance.

questions.stem: A 56-year-old man with pancytopenia, splenomegaly, and no lymphadenopathy undergoes bone marrow aspiration and biopsy, the test most useful in his suspected diagnosis. Which of the following marrow findings would be most characteristic of hairy cell leukemia?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Diffuse marrow infiltration with associated fibrosis

choices.label: B
choices.text: Effacement by nodules that lack mantle zones

choices.label: D
choices.text: Normal to high cellularity from increased B lymphocytes

choices.label: E
choices.text: Sheets of large transformed cells with prominent nucleoli

explanation.summary: In hairy cell leukemia the marrow is filled with hairy cells and the fibrosis they induce, and marrow sampling is the most useful diagnostic test.
explanation.whyCorrect: Bone marrow aspirate and biopsy are most useful in hairy cell leukemia, in which the bone marrow is the primary site of involvement and lymph nodes are spared. The marrow is filled with hairy cells and with the fibrosis that they induce, similar to what is seen in some myeloproliferative neoplasms.

whyWrongByChoice.B: Nodules lacking mantle zones are the nodal pathology of follicular lymphoma, which does involve lymph nodes.
whyWrongByChoice.C: The marrow in hairy cell leukemia is infiltrated rather than hypocellular and fatty, even though the blood counts are low.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Normal to high cellularity from increased B lymphocyte proliferation describes the marrow of CLL/SLL.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Sheets of large transformed cells describe diffuse large B-cell lymphoma, as arises in Richter transformation.

questions.stem: Flow cytometry on the marrow of a patient with suspected hairy cell leukemia shows light chain restriction with expression of CD19, CD20, and CD22. Expression of which additional set of markers would best support the diagnosis?

choices.label: A
choices.text: CD3, CD4, and CD8 with T-cell receptor beta

choices.label: B
choices.text: CD5, CD23, CD200, and CD38 with dim CD20

choices.label: C
choices.text: CD10 with overexpression of BCL-2 and BCL-6

choices.label: D
choices.text: CD11c, CD25, CD103, and annexin A1

choices.label: E
choices.text: CD30 and CD15 with weak PAX5 staining

explanation.summary: Hairy cells carry B-cell markers plus the distinctive combination of CD11c, CD25, CD103, CD123, and annexin A1.
explanation.whyCorrect: The typical immunophenotype of the malignant hairy cells demonstrates light chain restriction and expression of B-cell markers (CD19, CD20, CD22), along with additional markers including CD11c, CD25, CD103, CD123, and annexin A1.

whyWrongByChoice.A: CD3, CD4, and CD8 are T-cell markers and would not be expressed by this mature B-cell neoplasm.
whyWrongByChoice.B: CD5, CD23, and CD200 with CD38 describe the phenotype and prognostic markers of CLL/SLL.
whyWrongByChoice.C: CD10 positivity with BCL-2 overexpression reflects the germinal center origin and t(14;18) of follicular lymphoma.
whyWrongByChoice.E: CD30 and CD15 are not the markers used to identify hairy cells.

questions.stem: A 58-year-old man with symptomatic hairy cell leukemia begins cladribine. Which of the following adverse effects occurs in more than 30% of patients treated with this agent?

explanation.summary: Pyrexia occurs in more than 30% of patients receiving the purine analogs cladribine and pentostatin.
explanation.whyCorrect: Cladribine and pentostatin are adenosine analogs incorporated into DNA, causing strand breaks and inhibition of DNA synthesis. Their adverse effects include pyrexia in more than 30% of patients, fatigue in about 31%, nausea, and headache.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Atrial fibrillation is associated with the BTK inhibitor ibrutinib.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Hemorrhagic cystitis is a toxicity of cyclophosphamide, reduced in risk by Mesna.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Osteonecrosis is a long-term adverse effect of glucocorticoids such as prednisolone.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Vocal cord paralysis falls under the autonomic neuropathy caused by vincristine.

questions.stem: A 63-year-old man with a 4-year history of stable, asymptomatic chronic lymphocytic leukemia/small lymphocytic lymphoma (CLL/SLL) develops the sudden onset of fevers, abdominal pain, and rapidly progressive lymphadenopathy over several weeks. Examination shows new hepatosplenomegaly, and a lymph node biopsy reveals sheets of neoplastic B cells several times the size of a small lymphocyte. Which of the following best explains this patient's new diagnosis?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Development of mantle cell lymphoma from the mantle zone

choices.label: B
choices.text: Evolution of CLL/SLL into Burkitt lymphoma

choices.label: C
choices.text: Progression of CLL/SLL into acute lymphoblastic leukemia

choices.label: E
choices.text: Transformation of CLL/SLL into diffuse large B-cell lymphoma

explanation.summary: A subset of CLL/SLL patients transform into aggressive DLBCL, known as Richter transformation.
explanation.whyCorrect: Around 2% to 9% of patients with CLL/SLL develop diffuse large B-cell lymphoma in what is termed Richter transformation. A previously chronic, smoldering lymphoma suddenly becomes much more symptomatic, with fevers, abdominal pain, and progressive lymphadenopathy and hepatosplenomegaly, and biopsy shows a diffuse proliferation of large neoplastic B cells.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Mantle cell lymphoma is a distinct entity defined by t(11;14); it does not arise as a transformation of CLL/SLL.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Burkitt lymphoma is a separate MYC-driven lymphoma of medium-sized cells and is not the transformation product of CLL/SLL.
whyWrongByChoice.C: CLL/SLL is not described as transforming into acute lymphoblastic leukemia; the biopsy shows large mature-appearing neoplastic B cells, not lymphoblasts.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Chronic myeloid leukemia is a myeloid neoplasm with the t(9;22) Philadelphia chromosome and is unrelated to CLL/SLL transformation.

questions.stem: A 70-year-old woman presents with a rapidly enlarging neck mass and drenching night sweats. Excisional biopsy of a cervical lymph node shows sheets of neoplastic cells that are at least twice the size of normal lymphocytes, with vesicular nuclei and a single prominent nucleolus. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Burkitt lymphoma with a starry-sky pattern

choices.label: C
choices.text: Follicular lymphoma with a nodular pattern

choices.label: D
choices.text: Mantle cell lymphoma of small cells

choices.label: E
choices.text: Small lymphocytic lymphoma of mature cells

explanation.summary: DLBCL is composed of large neoplastic B cells at least twice the size of normal lymphocytes.
explanation.whyCorrect: DLBCL is composed of a diffuse proliferation of large neoplastic B cells that are typically at least twice the size of normal lymphocytes. These cells have large nuclei, often with a single prominent nucleolus (or multiple small nucleoli), matching this biopsy in an older adult with a rapidly enlarging mass and B symptoms.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Burkitt lymphoma is a diffuse proliferation of uniform medium-sized cells with a starry-sky pattern, not large cells twice the size of normal lymphocytes.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Follicular lymphoma has a nodular (follicular) growth pattern rather than a diffuse sheet of large cells.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Mantle cell lymphoma shows small-to-intermediate sized cells, not large cells with prominent nucleoli.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Small lymphocytic lymphoma is composed of small mature lymphocytes, the opposite of large neoplastic cells.

questions.stem: A pathologist is working up a case of diffuse large B-cell lymphoma and orders fluorescence in situ hybridization (FISH) for three genes. Rearrangements in two or three of these genes would indicate a so-called double-hit or triple-hit lymphoma with a more aggressive clinical course. Which set of genes is routinely tested in this panel?

explanation.summary: DLBCL is routinely evaluated by FISH for MYC, BCL2, and BCL6.
explanation.whyCorrect: In diagnosing DLBCL, it is routine to run a panel for MYC, BCL2, and BCL6 expression using fluorescence in situ hybridization. Mutations in two (double hit) or three (triple hit) of these genes typically suggest a more aggressive clinical course.

whyWrongByChoice.A: BCR-ABL1 and JAK2 are markers of myeloproliferative neoplasms and leukemias, not the DLBCL FISH panel.
whyWrongByChoice.B: CCND1-IGH defines mantle cell lymphoma and CD5 is an immunophenotype marker, not the DLBCL double-hit panel.
whyWrongByChoice.C: RB1, TP53, and MDM2 are cell-cycle and tumor-suppressor genes not used as the routine DLBCL panel.
whyWrongByChoice.E: FLT3, NPM1, and CEBPA are prognostic mutations in acute myeloid leukemia, not DLBCL.

questions.stem: A 68-year-old man is diagnosed with diffuse large B-cell lymphoma and is scheduled to begin systemic therapy. Which of the following is the typical first-line chemoimmunotherapy regimen for this disease?

explanation.summary: R-CHOP is the standard combination regimen for DLBCL.
explanation.whyCorrect: For patients with DLBCL, systemic therapy uses a combination of chemotherapy agents; a typical regimen is R-CHOP (rituximab, cyclophosphamide, doxorubicin, vincristine, and prednisone). Usually 3-5 cycles are given, followed by response assessment.

whyWrongByChoice.A: CODOX-M (cyclophosphamide, doxorubicin, methotrexate) is used to treat Burkitt lymphoma, not DLBCL.
whyWrongByChoice.B: High-dose cytarabine is used with rituximab for mantle cell lymphoma, not as first-line DLBCL therapy.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Rituximab plus bendamustine (R-B) is a preferred regimen for mantle cell lymphoma.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Single-agent methotrexate is not the standard treatment for DLBCL, which requires multidrug chemoimmunotherapy.

questions.stem: A 72-year-old man with stage IV diffuse large B-cell lymphoma is started on R-pola-CHP, which includes polatuzumab vedotin. This agent is an antibody-drug conjugate whose monoclonal antibody component binds a specific B-cell surface protein, triggering internalization and release of an anti-mitotic agent. Which surface protein does polatuzumab vedotin target?

explanation.summary: Polatuzumab vedotin is a CD79b-directed antibody-drug conjugate used in advanced DLBCL.
explanation.whyCorrect: Polatuzumab vedotin is a CD79b-directed antibody-drug conjugate consisting of a humanized IgG1 monoclonal antibody specific for CD79b, a small-molecule anti-mitotic agent, and a protease linker. Binding to CD79b-expressing B cells causes internalization of the complex and release of the anti-mitotic agent, inhibiting cell division and inducing apoptosis. It is added in advanced DLBCL as R-pola-CHP.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Cyclin D1 is an intracellular protein overexpressed in mantle cell lymphoma and cannot be targeted by a surface-binding antibody conjugate.
whyWrongByChoice.B: CD5 is a marker of mantle cell lymphoma and CLL/SLL, not the target of polatuzumab vedotin.
whyWrongByChoice.C: CD10 is a B-cell marker that may be expressed by DLBCL and Burkitt lymphoma but is not the polatuzumab target.
whyWrongByChoice.D: CD20 is the target of rituximab, not the antibody component of polatuzumab vedotin.

questions.stem: A 7-year-old boy who recently emigrated from equatorial Africa presents with rapidly enlarging firm masses of the jaw and facial bones. Biopsy confirms a high-grade B-cell lymphoma. Infection with which of the following organisms is most strongly associated with this form of the disease?

explanation.summary: Endemic Burkitt lymphoma of the jaw in African children is strongly linked to Epstein-Barr virus.
explanation.whyCorrect: Endemic Burkitt lymphoma occurs primarily in children in equatorial Africa and has a strong association with Epstein-Barr virus infection. In more than half of patients it presents with rapidly growing tumors of the jaw and facial bones; there may also be a co-factor link with malaria.

whyWrongByChoice.B: Helicobacter pylori is linked to MALT lymphoma and gastric ulcers, not Burkitt lymphoma.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Human herpesvirus 8 causes Kaposi sarcoma in HIV-positive patients, not Burkitt lymphoma.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Human papillomavirus (especially HPV16/18) is linked to cervical and oropharyngeal cancers, not Burkitt lymphoma.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Human T-lymphotropic virus 1 is associated with adult T-cell leukemia/lymphoma, not B-cell Burkitt lymphoma.

questions.stem: A 12-year-old boy presents with rapidly growing mandibular masses. A lymph node biopsy shows a diffuse proliferation of uniform medium-sized lymphocytes with numerous pale macrophages scattered against a background of darker malignant cells, producing a "starry-sky" appearance. These pale macrophages are best described as which of the following?

explanation.summary: The starry-sky pattern of Burkitt lymphoma is produced by tingible-body macrophages.
explanation.whyCorrect: With its short doubling time and high turnover, Burkitt lymphoma creates abundant tumor cell debris, which macrophages come in to clean up. These are called tingible-body macrophages because they contain visible, stainable (tingible) debris; they appear as pale spots against a background of darker malignant lymphoma cells, the characteristic starry-sky pattern.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Foam cells are lipid-laden macrophages seen in atherosclerosis and storage disorders, not the starry-sky pattern.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Langhans giant cells are multinucleated macrophages found in granulomas, such as in tuberculosis.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Reed-Sternberg cells are the hallmark of Hodgkin lymphoma, not the pale macrophages of Burkitt lymphoma.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Sezary cells are malignant T cells seen in cutaneous T-cell lymphoma, not benign macrophages.

questions.stem: A 10-year-old boy is diagnosed with Burkitt lymphoma. Genetic testing reveals a translocation that repositions the MYC gene next to the immunoglobulin heavy chain locus, causing marked MYC overexpression. Which of the following translocations is most likely responsible?

explanation.summary: Burkitt lymphoma is defined by t(8;14), which drives MYC overexpression.
explanation.whyCorrect: In Burkitt lymphoma, a t(8;14) translocation repositions the MYC gene from chromosome 8 next to the immunoglobulin heavy chain genes on chromosome 14, causing marked overexpression of MYC and excessive MYC protein that drives uncontrolled proliferation.

whyWrongByChoice.B: t(9;22) is the Philadelphia chromosome of chronic myeloid leukemia and some acute lymphoblastic leukemia.
whyWrongByChoice.C: t(11;14) fuses CCND1 with IGH and characterizes mantle cell lymphoma, not Burkitt lymphoma.
whyWrongByChoice.D: t(11;22) is associated with Ewing sarcoma, not Burkitt lymphoma.
whyWrongByChoice.E: t(14;18) drives BCL2 overexpression and is classically associated with follicular lymphoma and some DLBCL.

questions.stem: A 15-year-old boy in the United States presents with several weeks of abdominal pain, distension, and ascites. Imaging reveals a large mass centered on the ileocecal region causing partial intestinal obstruction, and the initial concern was appendicitis. Biopsy shows a high-grade B-cell lymphoma with a starry-sky pattern. Which of the following best describes this presentation?

explanation.summary: Sporadic Burkitt lymphoma is the most common form in the US and presents with an ileocecal abdominal mass.
explanation.whyCorrect: Sporadic Burkitt lymphoma is the most common form of BL in the United States and usually presents with abdominal symptoms. The tumor often involves the ileocecum (leading to intestinal obstruction), mesentery, kidneys, and ovaries, can mimic appendicitis, and is commonly associated with ascites and abdominal pain. The starry-sky pattern confirms Burkitt lymphoma.

whyWrongByChoice.A: DLBCL presents with large cells and rapidly enlarging lymphadenopathy or an extranodal mass, not the medium-sized starry-sky pattern described.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Endemic Burkitt lymphoma occurs in African children and classically presents with jaw and facial bone tumors, not an ileocecal mass in a US patient.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Follicular lymphoma is an indolent nodular lymphoma and would not present as a rapidly growing starry-sky abdominal mass.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Mantle cell lymphoma affects older adults with lymphadenopathy and hepatosplenomegaly, not a teenage ileocecal Burkitt presentation.

questions.stem: A 61-year-old man presents with generalized lymphadenopathy, hepatosplenomegaly, and bone marrow involvement. A lymph node biopsy shows a proliferation of small-to-intermediate sized lymphocytes, and immunohistochemistry demonstrates strong nuclear cyclin D1 positivity. Which translocation underlies this finding?

explanation.summary: Mantle cell lymphoma is defined by t(11;14), which overexpresses cyclin D1.
explanation.whyCorrect: Mantle cell lymphoma is characterized by the prototypical translocation t(11;14) between CCND1 (cyclin D1) on chromosome 11 and the IGH gene on chromosome 14. This causes increased expression of cyclin D1 and increased cell cycle progression; cyclin D1 immunohistochemistry serves as a surrogate for the translocation.

whyWrongByChoice.A: t(8;14) drives MYC overexpression in Burkitt lymphoma, not cyclin D1 positivity.
whyWrongByChoice.B: t(9;22) is the Philadelphia chromosome of chronic myeloid leukemia, unrelated to cyclin D1.
whyWrongByChoice.D: t(14;18) causes BCL2 overexpression in follicular lymphoma and some DLBCL, not cyclin D1.
whyWrongByChoice.E: t(15;17) defines acute promyelocytic leukemia, a myeloid neoplasm, not mantle cell lymphoma.

questions.stem: A 64-year-old man presents with lymphadenopathy and an axillary lymph node biopsy showing a diffuse proliferation of small-to-intermediate sized lymphocytes. Flow cytometry reveals kappa light chain-restricted B cells expressing CD19, CD20, and CD5. Which additional immunophenotype finding would best distinguish mantle cell lymphoma from CLL/SLL?

explanation.summary: Mantle cell lymphoma is CD5 positive but, unlike CLL/SLL, is usually CD23 negative.
explanation.whyCorrect: The immunophenotype of mantle cell lymphoma demonstrates light chain restriction, expression of B-cell markers (CD19, CD20, CD22, CD79a), and expression of CD5. In contrast to CLL/SLL, CD23 is usually negative in mantle cell lymphoma, which helps distinguish the two CD5-positive B-cell neoplasms.

whyWrongByChoice.A: CD19 is a B-cell marker expressed by mantle cell lymphoma and is already positive in this case.
whyWrongByChoice.B: CD20 is a pan-B-cell marker expressed by mantle cell lymphoma, so it is not absent.
whyWrongByChoice.D: CD23 positivity is characteristic of CLL/SLL, so it would not distinguish mantle cell lymphoma; MCL is typically CD23 negative.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Mantle cell lymphoma shows light chain restriction; its loss is not a feature and would not distinguish it from CLL/SLL.

questions.stem: A 66-year-old woman receiving R-CHOP for diffuse large B-cell lymphoma is monitored with serial echocardiograms during treatment. Which component of the regimen most directly accounts for the need for this cardiac monitoring?

explanation.summary: Doxorubicin causes cumulative dose-related cardiomyopathy, prompting cardiac monitoring.
explanation.whyCorrect: Doxorubicin inhibits DNA/RNA synthesis and can cause cumulative dose-related cardiomyopathy, which can progress to heart failure. Because cardiotoxicity is dose-dependent, cardiac function is monitored during doxorubicin-containing regimens such as R-CHOP.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Cyclophosphamide is an alkylating agent whose characteristic toxicities are hemorrhagic cystitis and SIADH, not cardiotoxicity.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Prednisone is a corticosteroid and is not the component responsible for the cardiac monitoring in this regimen.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Rituximab is an anti-CD20 monoclonal antibody associated with infusion reactions, not cumulative cardiomyopathy.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Vincristine causes dose-related peripheral neuropathy and autonomic (including vocal cord) paralysis, not cardiomyopathy.

questions.stem: A hematopathology laboratory tabulates its newly diagnosed non-Hodgkin lymphomas in the United States over one year. One subtype accounts for approximately 30% to 40% of all cases, making it the single most common. Which of the following is that subtype?

explanation.summary: DLBCL is the most common subtype of non-Hodgkin lymphoma in the United States, at roughly 30% to 40% of cases.
explanation.whyCorrect: Diffuse large B-cell lymphoma is the most common subtype of non-Hodgkin lymphoma in the US, accounting for about 30% to 40% of cases. It is usually a neoplasm of older patients, although it can occur in children, and it typically presents with rapidly enlarging lymphadenopathy or an extranodal mass with B symptoms.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Burkitt lymphoma is described as less common than DLBCL and is a hyper-aggressive rather than a numerically dominant lymphoma.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Follicular lymphoma is a common indolent lymphoma but is not the subtype accounting for 30% to 40% of US non-Hodgkin lymphoma cases.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Mantle cell lymphoma accounts for only 3% to 10% of non-Hodgkin lymphoma cases.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Small lymphocytic lymphoma is the tissue counterpart of CLL and is not the most common non-Hodgkin lymphoma subtype.

questions.stem: Among patients with HIV/AIDS and other immunosuppressed states, one B-cell lymphoma is the most common cause of primary B-cell lymphoma. Which of the following is that lymphoma?

choices.label: E
choices.text: Mantle cell lymphoma of older adults

explanation.summary: DLBCL is the most common cause of primary B-cell lymphoma in immunosuppressed patients such as those with HIV/AIDS.
explanation.whyCorrect: In addition to being the most common non-Hodgkin lymphoma subtype overall, diffuse large B-cell lymphoma is specifically the most common cause of primary B-cell lymphoma in immunosuppressed patients, including those with HIV/AIDS.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Burkitt lymphoma does have an immunodeficiency-associated form seen in AIDS, but it is not the most common primary B-cell lymphoma in these patients.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Follicular lymphoma is an indolent nodular lymphoma without a described predilection for immunosuppressed hosts.
whyWrongByChoice.D: MALT lymphoma is associated with chronic antigenic stimulation such as Helicobacter pylori infection, not with HIV/AIDS.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Mantle cell lymphoma is a disease of middle-aged to older adults and is not linked to immunosuppression.

questions.stem: A 67-year-old woman newly diagnosed with diffuse large B-cell lymphoma asks about her long-term prognosis. Which of the following best approximates the 5-year overall survival rate for this disease?

explanation.summary: Diffuse large B-cell lymphoma carries a 5-year overall survival rate of about 30% to 50%.
explanation.whyCorrect: Although DLBCL displays a rapid, aggressive clinical course that is fatal if untreated, aggressive chemotherapy produces complete remission in 60% to 80% of patients and cures 40% to 50%. Its 5-year overall survival rate is 30% to 50%.

whyWrongByChoice.A: A 5% to 15% figure understates DLBCL survival, which is substantially better with modern chemoimmunotherapy.
