whyWrongByChoice.B: A 15% to 25% figure is well below the stated 5-year overall survival for DLBCL.
whyWrongByChoice.C: A 20% to 30% figure falls below the survival range reported for DLBCL.
whyWrongByChoice.E: A 70% to 90% figure corresponds to survival in pediatric Burkitt lymphoma, not to DLBCL.

questions.stem: Flow cytometry is performed on a lymph node from a 70-year-old man whose biopsy shows a diffuse proliferation of large neoplastic B cells. The cells demonstrate lambda light chain restriction and express CD19, CD20, CD22, and CD79a. Which of the following additional markers may also be expressed by this neoplasm?

explanation.summary: The DLBCL immunophenotype includes light chain restriction, pan-B-cell markers, and possible CD10 expression.
explanation.whyCorrect: The immunophenotype of DLBCL demonstrates light chain restriction, expression of B-cell markers such as CD19, CD20, CD22, and CD79a, and possible expression of CD10. CD10 is therefore the marker that may additionally be seen in this large B-cell neoplasm.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Cyclin D1 positivity is the immunohistochemical surrogate for t(11;14) in mantle cell lymphoma.
whyWrongByChoice.B: CD3 is a T-cell marker and would not be expressed by a B-cell lymphoma with light chain restriction.
whyWrongByChoice.C: CD5 expression characterizes mantle cell lymphoma and CLL/SLL rather than DLBCL.
whyWrongByChoice.E: CD23 positivity is a feature of CLL/SLL and is not part of the DLBCL immunophenotype.

questions.stem: Genetic studies of a lymph node involved by diffuse large B-cell lymphoma show overexpression of BCL2, an abnormality also connected to the t(14;18) translocation seen in other lymphomas. Overexpression of BCL2 most directly dysregulates which of the following cellular processes?

explanation.summary: BCL2 regulates apoptosis, and its overexpression is one of the common genetic abnormalities of DLBCL.
explanation.whyCorrect: Most cases of DLBCL carry genetic abnormalities, often multiple. One of the most common is overexpression of BCL2, a gene that regulates apoptosis; this abnormality is also connected to the t(14;18) translocation seen in other lymphomas. Loss of normal apoptotic control allows neoplastic B cells to accumulate.

whyWrongByChoice.B: Light chain secretion relates to plasma cell function and is not controlled by BCL2.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Microtubule assembly is the target of vincristine and of the anti-mitotic agent in polatuzumab vedotin, not of BCL2.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Nucleotide excision repair is not the process regulated by BCL2 in these lymphomas.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Ribosomal translation is not the process that BCL2 governs; the MYC protein, not BCL2, drives the synthetic machinery for growth.

questions.stem: Fluorescence in situ hybridization on a lymphoma specimen demonstrates overexpression of the MYC oncogene, leading to uncontrolled cell proliferation. The MYC gene encodes a transcriptional regulator with which of the following specific functions?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Blocks programmed cell death in germinal center B cells

choices.label: B
choices.text: Drives progression from G1 into S phase of the cell cycle

choices.label: C
choices.text: Encodes a constitutively active tyrosine kinase that drives proliferation

choices.label: D
choices.text: Increases expression of genes making the building blocks for growth and division

choices.label: E
choices.text: Transmits antigen receptor signals from the B-cell surface into the cytoplasm

explanation.summary: MYC encodes a transcriptional regulator that turns up the genes making the building blocks required for cell growth and division.
explanation.whyCorrect: MYC encodes a transcriptional regulator with a very specific function: it increases the expression of genes that synthesize all the building blocks needed for cell growth and division. Overexpression, whether in DLBCL or via the t(8;14) translocation in Burkitt lymphoma, therefore leads to uncontrolled cell division.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Blocking programmed cell death describes BCL2, which regulates apoptosis, rather than the transcriptional function of MYC.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Driving G1-to-S cell cycle progression describes cyclin D1, the product of CCND1 overexpressed in mantle cell lymphoma.
whyWrongByChoice.C: A constitutively active tyrosine kinase describes BCR-ABL1 in chronic myeloid leukemia, not the MYC protein.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Transmitting B-cell receptor signals from the cell surface describes CD79b, the target of polatuzumab vedotin.

questions.stem: A diffuse large B-cell lymphoma is evaluated for the genetic abnormalities that are commonly present in this disease. In addition to abnormalities of MYC and BCL2, which of the following BCL6 abnormalities is characteristically found?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Amplification of BCL6 with markedly increased protein levels

choices.label: B
choices.text: Deletion of BCL6 together with loss of the MYC locus

choices.label: D
choices.text: Fusion of BCL6 to ABL1 producing a chimeric kinase

choices.label: E
choices.text: Point mutation of BCL6 causing constitutive kinase activity

explanation.summary: Among the common genetic abnormalities of DLBCL is down-regulation of BCL6.
explanation.whyCorrect: The most common genetic abnormalities in DLBCL are overexpression of BCL2, down-regulation of BCL6, and overexpression of MYC. BCL6 prevents apoptosis and causes T cells to become T helper cells, and it is one of the three genes routinely assessed by FISH in these tumors.

whyWrongByChoice.A: BCL6 amplification with increased protein is not the described abnormality; BCL6 is down-regulated in DLBCL.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Deletion of BCL6 with loss of MYC is the opposite of the MYC overexpression that characterizes these tumors.
whyWrongByChoice.D: A BCL6-ABL1 fusion kinase is not a feature of DLBCL; fusion kinases such as BCR-ABL1 characterize myeloid neoplasms.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Constitutive kinase activation is not how BCL6 contributes to DLBCL, which involves altered expression rather than kinase activity.

questions.stem: A 66-year-old man with newly diagnosed diffuse large B-cell lymphoma starts R-CHOP. After how many cycles is response to therapy typically assessed?

explanation.summary: Usually 3 to 5 cycles of R-CHOP are given before response is assessed.
explanation.whyCorrect: For patients with DLBCL, systemic therapy uses combination chemotherapy, typically R-CHOP (rituximab, cyclophosphamide, doxorubicin, vincristine, and prednisone). Usually 3 to 5 cycles of R-CHOP are given, and these are followed by response assessment.

whyWrongByChoice.A: A single cycle is too early for the response assessment point described for R-CHOP.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Two cycles falls short of the usual number of cycles given before reassessment.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Eight to 10 cycles exceeds the number of cycles typically administered before response assessment.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Twelve cycles is far more than the standard course given before reassessing response.

questions.stem: A 71-year-old man with stage IV diffuse large B-cell lymphoma is treated with R-pola-CHP instead of standard R-CHOP. Compared with R-CHOP, which of the following agents is absent from the R-pola-CHP regimen?

explanation.summary: R-pola-CHP substitutes polatuzumab vedotin for the vincristine of R-CHOP in advanced DLBCL.
explanation.whyCorrect: In advanced-stage DLBCL (stages III or IV), polatuzumab vedotin is added to the regimen, which is then called R-pola-CHP: rituximab, polatuzumab vedotin, cyclophosphamide, doxorubicin, and prednisone. Vincristine, the O of CHOP, is not part of this regimen.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Cyclophosphamide is the C of R-pola-CHP and is retained.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Doxorubicin is the H of R-pola-CHP and is retained.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Prednisone is the P of R-pola-CHP and is retained.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Rituximab is the R of R-pola-CHP and remains part of the regimen.

questions.stem: A 69-year-old woman with stage IV diffuse large B-cell lymphoma begins R-pola-CHP and is scheduled for frequent blood counts. Which adverse effect of polatuzumab vedotin occurs in more than 60% of treated patients?

explanation.summary: Neutropenia is the most frequent adverse effect of polatuzumab vedotin, occurring in more than 60% of patients.
explanation.whyCorrect: Polatuzumab vedotin can cause neutropenia in more than 60% of patients, along with thrombocytopenia in 32% to 49% and peripheral neuropathy in 40% to 55%. Infusion-related reactions can occur within 24 hours of infusion, and infectious complications such as sepsis and pneumonia may follow the neutropenia.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Cardiomyopathy is the cumulative dose-related toxicity of doxorubicin rather than of polatuzumab vedotin.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Hemorrhagic cystitis is a toxicity of alkylating agents such as cyclophosphamide and bendamustine, not of polatuzumab vedotin.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Peripheral neuropathy occurs in 40% to 55% of patients treated with polatuzumab vedotin, less often than neutropenia.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Thrombocytopenia occurs with polatuzumab vedotin but at a rate of 32% to 49%, below the threshold asked about.

questions.stem: Polatuzumab vedotin binds CD79b on a neoplastic B cell, and the antibody-drug conjugate complex is internalized. Which of the following events then directly releases the small-molecule anti-mitotic agent inside the cell?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Cleavage of the protease linker joining drug to antibody

choices.label: B
choices.text: Complement-mediated lysis of the neoplastic cell membrane

choices.label: C
choices.text: Glycosylation of the humanized IgG1 antibody backbone

choices.label: D
choices.text: Phosphorylation of the CD79b cytoplasmic tail by a kinase

choices.label: E
choices.text: Reduction of an interchain disulfide bond by glutathione

explanation.summary: After internalization, protease cleavage of the linker frees the anti-mitotic payload of polatuzumab vedotin.
explanation.whyCorrect: Polatuzumab vedotin is an antibody-drug conjugate with three parts: a humanized IgG1 monoclonal antibody specific for human CD79b, a small-molecule anti-mitotic agent, and a protease linker that covalently attaches the drug to the antibody. Binding to CD79b-expressing B cells causes internalization of the ADC-CD79b complex, and the anti-mitotic agent is released via protease linker cleavage, inhibiting cell division and inducing apoptosis in rapidly dividing cells.

whyWrongByChoice.B: Complement-mediated lysis is an antibody effector mechanism, not the intracellular release step of this conjugate.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Glycosylation of the antibody backbone is not the step that liberates the payload of this conjugate.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Phosphorylation of CD79b relates to receptor signaling and does not release the attached drug.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Disulfide reduction is not the described release mechanism; this conjugate uses a protease-cleavable linker.

questions.stem: A 9-year-old boy has a lymphoma mass that is visibly larger from one day to the next. Burkitt lymphoma is unique among malignancies for which of the following characteristics?

choices.label: A
choices.text: The highest lifetime incidence of any childhood cancer

choices.label: B
choices.text: The highest rate of spontaneous regression without therapy

choices.label: C
choices.text: The longest median doubling time of the B-cell lymphomas

choices.label: D
choices.text: The lowest cure rate among the pediatric lymphomas

choices.label: E
choices.text: The shortest doubling time of all human cancers

explanation.summary: Burkitt lymphoma has the shortest doubling time of all human cancers.
explanation.whyCorrect: Burkitt lymphoma is a hyper-aggressive lymphoma that is unique for several reasons, foremost among them that it has the shortest doubling time of all human cancers. This explosive turnover also generates the tumor cell debris that tingible-body macrophages clear, producing the starry-sky pattern.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Burkitt lymphoma is less common than DLBCL and is not the most frequent childhood cancer.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Spontaneous regression is not a described feature of this hyper-aggressive lymphoma, which is fatal without treatment.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Its doubling time is the shortest, not the longest, among malignancies.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Cure rates in children with Burkitt lymphoma are excellent at 80% to 90%, not the lowest among pediatric lymphomas.

questions.stem: A 62-year-old man with mantle cell lymphoma is treated with rituximab plus high-dose cytarabine (HiDAc). Cytarabine exerts its antineoplastic effect by which of the following mechanisms?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Acting as a pyrimidine analog that inhibits DNA polymerase

choices.label: B
choices.text: Alkylating DNA and interfering with DNA/RNA replication

choices.label: C
choices.text: Binding CD20 and triggering immune-mediated cell killing

choices.label: E
choices.text: Inhibiting microtubule function required for mitosis

explanation.summary: Cytarabine is a pyrimidine analog that inhibits DNA polymerase.
explanation.whyCorrect: Cytarabine is a pyrimidine analog that inhibits DNA polymerase. In mantle cell lymphoma it is given at high dose (HiDAc) with rituximab as one of the preferred regimens; its adverse effects include myelosuppression and megaloblastic anemia.

whyWrongByChoice.B: Alkylation with interference in DNA/RNA replication describes bendamustine and cyclophosphamide, not cytarabine.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Binding CD20 describes rituximab, the monoclonal antibody given alongside cytarabine, not cytarabine itself.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Competitive inhibition of dihydrofolate reductase is the mechanism of methotrexate.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Inhibition of microtubule function is the mechanism of vincristine.

questions.stem: A pediatric oncologist notes that endemic Burkitt lymphoma clusters geographically in equatorial Africa. Beyond Epstein-Barr virus, a connection has been proposed with which of the following infections that is common in the same region?

explanation.summary: Endemic Burkitt lymphoma arises where malaria is common, and a connection between the two is proposed.
explanation.whyCorrect: Endemic Burkitt lymphoma occurs primarily in children in equatorial Africa and has a strong association with Epstein-Barr virus. There may also be a connection between Burkitt lymphoma and malarial infection, which would explain why endemic Burkitt lymphoma arises in the same area where malaria is common.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Hepatitis B is associated with hepatocellular carcinoma rather than with Burkitt lymphoma.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Schistosoma haematobium chronically irritates bladder epithelium and is linked to squamous cell carcinoma of the bladder.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Trypanosomiasis is endemic in parts of Africa but is not the infection connected with Burkitt lymphoma.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Tuberculosis causes granulomatous disease with Langhans giant cells and is not linked to endemic Burkitt lymphoma.

questions.stem: A 6-year-old girl in equatorial Africa is diagnosed with endemic Burkitt lymphoma after presenting with rapidly growing jaw and facial bone masses. Staging is undertaken because of the risk of extranodal spread. Which of the following groups of sites is most characteristically involved?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Lungs, pleura, pericardium, and mediastinal fat

choices.label: B
choices.text: Ovaries, kidneys, breasts, and central nervous system

choices.label: C
choices.text: Prostate, bladder, urethra, and seminal vesicles

choices.label: D
choices.text: Skin, joints, synovium, and subcutaneous tissue

choices.label: E
choices.text: Thyroid, parathyroid, adrenal, and pituitary glands

explanation.summary: Endemic Burkitt lymphoma spreads extranodally to the ovaries, kidneys, breasts, and CNS.
explanation.whyCorrect: In more than half of patients, endemic Burkitt lymphoma presents with rapidly growing tumors of the jaw and facial bones. Extranodal spread to the ovaries, kidneys, breasts, and central nervous system may also occur, so these sites are assessed at staging.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Pulmonary and pleural spread is not the group of extranodal sites described for endemic Burkitt lymphoma.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Male genitourinary organs are not the characteristic extranodal sites; the kidneys and ovaries are the urogenital sites involved.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Skin and joint involvement is not the described pattern of extranodal spread in endemic Burkitt lymphoma.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Endocrine gland involvement is not a characteristic site of spread for this lymphoma.

questions.stem: A 38-year-old man with AIDS is diagnosed with immunodeficiency-associated Burkitt lymphoma and undergoes staging, including lumbar puncture. Approximately what proportion of patients with this form of Burkitt lymphoma present with central nervous system involvement?

explanation.summary: Immunodeficiency-associated Burkitt lymphoma involves the CNS in about 15% of patients at presentation.
explanation.whyCorrect: Immunodeficiency-associated Burkitt lymphoma is most common in people with HIV/AIDS but is seen with any congenital or acquired immunodeficiency. It most often involves the lymph nodes, but about 15% present with CNS involvement and 20% to 30% of tumors have spread to the bone marrow at diagnosis. Like the endemic form, it has a strong association with EBV.

whyWrongByChoice.A: About 2% markedly understates the frequency of CNS involvement in this form of Burkitt lymphoma.
whyWrongByChoice.C: About 25% falls within the 20% to 30% range for bone marrow spread, not for CNS involvement.
whyWrongByChoice.D: About 35% is higher than the CNS involvement rate reported at presentation.
whyWrongByChoice.E: About 50% overstates CNS involvement; roughly half is the proportion of endemic cases presenting with jaw tumors.

questions.stem: A 14-year-old girl undergoes biopsy of a rapidly enlarging abdominal mass. Histopathology shows a diffuse proliferation of uniform medium-sized lymphocytes with a high nuclear-to-cytoplasmic ratio and round nuclei containing fine chromatin and visible nucleoli. Which additional cytologic finding is characteristic of this neoplasm?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Abundant pale cytoplasm with a prominent perinuclear clear zone

choices.label: B
choices.text: Clumped clock-face chromatin with eccentric paranuclear clearing

choices.label: C
choices.text: Coarse cytoplasmic granules that stain with myeloperoxidase

choices.label: D
choices.text: Deeply basophilic cytoplasm with sharply demarcated punched-out vacuoles

choices.label: E
choices.text: Scant cytoplasm containing needle-shaped azurophilic inclusions

explanation.summary: Burkitt lymphoma cells have deeply basophilic cytoplasm containing sharply demarcated, punched-out vacuoles.
explanation.whyCorrect: Burkitt lymphoma histopathology shows a diffuse proliferation of uniform medium-sized lymphocytes with a high nuclear-to-cytoplasmic ratio. The nuclei are round with fine chromatin and visible nucleoli, and they are surrounded by deeply basophilic cytoplasm with sharply demarcated, punched-out vacuoles.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Abundant pale cytoplasm with a perinuclear clear zone is not a feature of these medium-sized, high N:C ratio cells.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Clock-face chromatin with paranuclear clearing describes plasma cells, not the fine-chromatin nuclei described here.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Myeloperoxidase-positive granules indicate myeloid differentiation rather than a B-cell lymphoma.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Needle-shaped azurophilic inclusions correspond to Auer rods of myeloid blasts, not to Burkitt lymphoma cells.

questions.stem: A 63-year-old man is diagnosed with mantle cell lymphoma after a node biopsy performed for an incidentally noted small cervical node. He has no B symptoms, no cytopenias, and no organ compromise, and he feels entirely well. Which of the following is the most appropriate next step in management?

explanation.summary: Mantle cell lymphoma requires treatment when symptomatic; selected asymptomatic patients may be observed.
explanation.whyCorrect: Treatment of mantle cell lymphoma is required for symptomatic disease; however, in some cases patients may benefit from observation. An entirely asymptomatic patient with low-volume disease is therefore reasonably followed rather than treated immediately.

whyWrongByChoice.A: High-dose cytarabine with rituximab is a preferred regimen for mantle cell lymphoma, but it is reserved for patients who need treatment.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Intrathecal methotrexate is used for central nervous system treatment and is not indicated for asymptomatic nodal disease.
whyWrongByChoice.C: R-CHOP is the standard regimen for DLBCL, and immediate chemoimmunotherapy is not required for this asymptomatic patient.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Single-agent vincristine is not a standardized regimen for mantle cell lymphoma, all of which include rituximab.

questions.stem: A 17-year-old boy with Burkitt lymphoma is treated with CODOX-M. One component of this regimen acts as a competitive inhibitor of dihydrofolate reductase, thereby inhibiting DNA synthesis, repair, and replication. Which agent is this?

explanation.summary: Methotrexate competitively inhibits dihydrofolate reductase, blocking DNA synthesis, repair, and replication.
explanation.whyCorrect: Methotrexate is a competitive inhibitor of dihydrofolate reductase that inhibits DNA synthesis, repair, and replication; high-dose methotrexate is used in adults with Burkitt lymphoma. Its adverse effects include myelosuppression, nephrotoxicity, hepatotoxicity, and mucositis, and it may also be delivered intrathecally into the CSF for CNS treatment.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Cyclophosphamide is an alkylating agent that interferes with DNA/RNA replication rather than inhibiting dihydrofolate reductase.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Doxorubicin inhibits DNA/RNA synthesis and is notable for cumulative dose-related cardiomyopathy.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Rituximab is an anti-CD20 monoclonal antibody and is not an enzyme inhibitor.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Vincristine inhibits microtubule function and has no antifolate activity.

questions.stem: A 15-year-old boy receiving multi-agent chemotherapy for Burkitt lymphoma develops gross hematuria and suprapubic pain. His oncology team notes that mesna is given with one component of his regimen specifically to reduce the risk of this complication. Which agent is responsible?

explanation.summary: Cyclophosphamide causes hemorrhagic cystitis, and mesna is given to reduce that risk.
explanation.whyCorrect: Cyclophosphamide is an alkylating agent that interferes with DNA/RNA replication. Myelosuppression, SIADH, and hemorrhagic cystitis are its common adverse effects, and the risk of hemorrhagic cystitis is reduced with mesna.

whyWrongByChoice.B: Doxorubicin causes cumulative dose-related cardiomyopathy that can progress to heart failure, not hemorrhagic cystitis.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Methotrexate causes myelosuppression, nephrotoxicity, hepatotoxicity, and mucositis, and mesna is not given with it.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Rituximab is a monoclonal antibody whose adverse effects do not include hemorrhagic cystitis.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Vincristine causes dose-related peripheral neuropathy and autonomic paralysis rather than bladder toxicity.

questions.stem: A 58-year-old man receiving cyclophosphamide-containing chemotherapy for lymphoma is found to have a serum sodium of 124 mEq/L. He is euvolemic on examination. Which of the following best explains this abnormality?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Adrenal insufficiency with deficient aldosterone-mediated sodium retention

choices.label: B
choices.text: Excess antidiuretic hormone causing water retention that dilutes serum sodium

choices.label: C
choices.text: Gastrointestinal sodium losses from chemotherapy-induced mucositis

choices.label: D
choices.text: Osmotic diuresis produced by marked hyperglycemia and glycosuria

choices.label: E
choices.text: Renal tubular injury leading to inappropriate urinary salt wasting

explanation.summary: Cyclophosphamide can cause SIADH, in which excess ADH retains water and dilutes serum sodium.
explanation.whyCorrect: SIADH is a condition in which the body produces too much antidiuretic hormone, also known as vasopressin. This leads to retention of too much water, which dilutes the blood and lowers sodium levels, producing hyponatremia. SIADH is among the listed adverse effects of cyclophosphamide, along with myelosuppression and hemorrhagic cystitis.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Aldosterone deficiency from adrenal insufficiency is not an adverse effect attributed to cyclophosphamide.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Mucositis is a toxicity of methotrexate, and gastrointestinal sodium loss is not the mechanism of SIADH.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Osmotic diuresis from hyperglycemia is unrelated to the adverse effect profile of this alkylating agent.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Salt wasting from tubular injury is not the described mechanism of cyclophosphamide-associated hyponatremia.

questions.stem: A 20-year-old woman being treated for Burkitt lymphoma develops progressive hoarseness. Laryngoscopy demonstrates vocal cord paralysis. She also reports paresthesias in her feet, and examination shows absent ankle reflexes and distal weakness. Which chemotherapeutic agent most likely caused these findings?

explanation.summary: Vincristine causes dose-related peripheral neuropathy and autonomic paralysis, including vocal cord paralysis.
explanation.whyCorrect: Vincristine inhibits microtubule function. Dose-related peripheral neuropathy is associated with its use and can cause paresthesia, loss of reflexes, weakness, and autonomic paralysis, including vocal cord paralysis. This combination of hoarseness with a distal sensorimotor neuropathy points to vincristine.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Bendamustine causes myelosuppression, SIADH, and hemorrhagic cystitis, and is used in mantle cell lymphoma rather than Burkitt lymphoma.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Cytarabine causes myelosuppression and megaloblastic anemia, not autonomic and peripheral neuropathy.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Methotrexate toxicity consists of myelosuppression, nephrotoxicity, hepatotoxicity, and mucositis rather than neuropathy with vocal cord paralysis.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Prednisone is a corticosteroid and does not produce this dose-related neuropathy.

questions.stem: A 16-year-old boy with a bulky Burkitt lymphoma is about to start multi-agent chemotherapy. Rituximab is added to the regimen, as is often done in this disease, especially to minimize which of the following complications?

explanation.summary: In Burkitt lymphoma, rituximab is often added to the regimen especially to minimize tumor lysis syndrome.
explanation.whyCorrect: Patients with Burkitt lymphoma require frequent multi-agent chemotherapy, commonly CODOX-M. In many cases rituximab is added to the regimen, especially to minimize tumor lysis syndrome, a particular hazard given the disease's very short doubling time and high cell turnover.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Cumulative cardiomyopathy is a dose-related doxorubicin toxicity and is not reduced by adding rituximab.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Hemorrhagic cystitis from cyclophosphamide is mitigated with mesna, not with rituximab.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Mucositis is an adverse effect of methotrexate and is not the reason rituximab is added.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Peripheral neuropathy from vincristine is dose-related and is not prevented by rituximab.

questions.stem: A 60-year-old man is diagnosed with mantle cell lymphoma. Approximately what proportion of all non-Hodgkin lymphoma cases does this subtype represent?

explanation.summary: Mantle cell lymphoma accounts for 3% to 10% of non-Hodgkin lymphoma cases.
explanation.whyCorrect: Mantle cell lymphoma accounts for 3% to 10% of non-Hodgkin lymphoma cases. It typically occurs in middle-aged to older adults, with a median age of 60 years and a male predominance, and most patients present at high-stage disease with lymphadenopathy, hepatosplenomegaly, and bone marrow involvement.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Less than 1% understates its frequency; mantle cell lymphoma is uncommon but not that rare.
whyWrongByChoice.C: A 15% to 20% share overstates the frequency of mantle cell lymphoma among non-Hodgkin lymphomas.
whyWrongByChoice.D: The 30% to 40% share corresponds to diffuse large B-cell lymphoma, the most common subtype in the US.
whyWrongByChoice.E: A 45% to 55% share would make mantle cell lymphoma the majority of non-Hodgkin lymphomas, which it is not.

questions.stem: A 58-year-old man is evaluated for scaly, itchy skin patches on his trunk and limbs that have slowly enlarged over several years despite treatment for presumed eczema. A skin biopsy reveals a neoplastic infiltrate of lymphocytes with markedly convoluted nuclei. Immunophenotyping shows the malignant cells are derived from helper T cells. Which of the following surface markers is most characteristic of the cell of origin in this disorder?

explanation.summary: The neoplastic cells of mycosis fungoides derive from CD4+ (helper) T cells.
explanation.whyCorrect: The brick states that the neoplastic lymphoma cells in mycosis fungoides are thought to derive from CD4+ (helper) T cells, and cytokine production from these cells likely drives tumor development. CD4 positivity therefore identifies the cell of origin.

whyWrongByChoice.B: CD8 marks cytotoxic T cells, not the helper T cells from which mycosis fungoides arises.
whyWrongByChoice.C: CD15 is associated with Reed-Sternberg cells of Hodgkin lymphoma, not mycosis fungoides.
whyWrongByChoice.D: CD19 is a B-cell marker; mycosis fungoides is a T-cell neoplasm.
whyWrongByChoice.E: CD20 is a B-cell marker and is not expressed by these malignant T cells.

questions.stem: A dermatopathologist examines a skin biopsy from a patient with suspected cutaneous T-cell lymphoma and notes malignant lymphocytes whose nuclei are extremely convoluted, with indentations resembling the sulci and gyri of the brain. This nuclear morphology is described by which of the following terms, which is used almost exclusively for this lymphoma?

explanation.summary: The convoluted nuclei of mycosis fungoides cells are termed cerebriform nuclei.
explanation.whyCorrect: The brick explains that the unique feature of mycosis fungoides lymphoma cells is their extremely convoluted nuclear contours, which resemble the sulci and gyri of the brain, giving rise to the term cerebriform nuclei used almost exclusively with this lymphoma.

whyWrongByChoice.B: A fried-egg appearance describes oligodendroglioma cells, unrelated to this disorder.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Notched or buttock-shaped nuclei describe Burkitt or follicular lymphoma cells, not the cerebriform contour described.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Owl-eye inclusions describe cytomegalovirus-infected cells, not this lymphoma.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Smudge cells are seen in chronic lymphocytic leukemia, not mycosis fungoides.

questions.stem: A skin biopsy from a patient with advancing mycosis fungoides shows small clusters of atypical lymphocytes collected within the epidermis. The pathologist notes that the historical name for these collections is misleading. Which of the following best describes these clusters?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Aggregates of binucleate Reed-Sternberg cells in the dermis

choices.label: B
choices.text: Clusters of malignant lymphoma cells within the epidermis

choices.label: C
choices.text: Collections of neutrophils within the epidermis responding to a bacterial infection

choices.label: D
choices.text: Deposits of degranulating eosinophils in the dermis

choices.label: E
choices.text: Granulomas of epithelioid macrophages with lymphocytes

explanation.summary: Pautrier microabscesses are intraepidermal clusters of lymphoma cells, not neutrophils.
explanation.whyCorrect: The brick describes these clusters, poorly named Pautrier microabscesses, as a unique feature of mycosis fungoides. The name is misleading because true abscesses are collections of neutrophils, whereas these clusters are instead made up of lymphoma cells.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Reed-Sternberg cells are the hallmark of Hodgkin lymphoma, not these epidermal clusters.
whyWrongByChoice.C: This is precisely why the name is misleading; the clusters are lymphoma cells, not neutrophils.
whyWrongByChoice.D: The clusters are malignant lymphocytes, not eosinophil deposits.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Granulomas of epithelioid macrophages are seen in granulomatous disease, not mycosis fungoides.

questions.stem: A 63-year-old man with a long history of mycosis fungoides now presents with a red, itchy, peeling rash covering more than 80% of his body surface, along with diffuse lymphadenopathy. A peripheral blood smear reveals circulating malignant T cells with cerebriform nuclei. Which of the following terms best describes this advanced clinical presentation?

explanation.summary: Sezary syndrome is the erythrodermic, leukemic-phase evolution of mycosis fungoides.
explanation.whyCorrect: The brick defines Sezary syndrome as the triad of erythroderma, generalized lymphadenopathy, and clonally related T cells with cerebriform nuclei in the skin, lymph nodes, and peripheral blood. Erythroderma over 80% of the body with circulating Sezary cells matches this advanced form of the disease.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Adult T-cell leukemia/lymphoma is HTLV-1 associated with flower-shaped nuclei and hypercalcemia, not this evolution of mycosis fungoides.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Hodgkin lymphoma is a B-cell-derived lymphoma with Reed-Sternberg cells, not cerebriform T cells.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Patch-stage disease is the early, localized form and lacks erythroderma and circulating malignant cells.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Peripheral T-cell lymphoma, NOS is a separate mature T-cell subtype and does not describe this cutaneous erythrodermic picture.

questions.stem: A 54-year-old woman is newly diagnosed with mycosis fungoides limited to a few scaly cutaneous plaques, without lymphadenopathy or systemic symptoms. She asks about her long-term outlook. Which of the following is the most accurate statement about her prognosis?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Although incurable, she is likely to have a normal life expectancy

choices.label: B
choices.text: Median survival is less than one year regardless of treatment

choices.label: C
choices.text: Rapid progression to acute leukemia is expected within weeks

choices.label: D
choices.text: The condition invariably transforms into Hodgkin lymphoma

choices.label: E
choices.text: The disease is readily curable with a single course of systemic chemotherapy

explanation.summary: Mycosis fungoides is incurable but indolent; limited cutaneous disease carries a normal life expectancy.
explanation.whyCorrect: The brick states that although mycosis fungoides is incurable, most patients can keep the disease under control for years, and most people with limited cutaneous involvement have a normal life expectancy.

whyWrongByChoice.B: Limited cutaneous disease carries a normal life expectancy, not survival under one year.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Progression is slow and measured in years; rapid leukemic transformation within weeks is not typical of limited disease.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Mycosis fungoides may evolve to a leukemic (Sezary) phase but does not transform into Hodgkin lymphoma.
whyWrongByChoice.E: The brick specifically describes the disease as incurable, though controllable, not cured by a single chemotherapy course.

questions.stem: A 50-year-old man is diagnosed with early-stage (Stage I) mycosis fungoides consisting of a few scaly patches. His dermatologist plans skin-directed therapy. Which of the following is the most appropriate first-line treatment for his early-stage disease?

choices.label: E
choices.text: Wide surgical excision of all lesions

explanation.summary: Early-stage mycosis fungoides is treated first with skin-directed therapy such as topical corticosteroids.
explanation.whyCorrect: The brick lists several skin-directed options for Stage I/II disease, beginning with topical corticosteroids such as betamethasone and clobetasol, which are used for their anti-inflammatory properties in early-stage MF.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Bone marrow transplant is not the described first-line therapy for early cutaneous disease.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Systemic chemotherapy is reserved for advanced disease, given along with topical therapy, not for a few early patches.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Radiation is used for localized disease or combined with systemic therapy in advanced disease, not as the first-line skin-directed choice here.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Surgical excision is not described as a primary treatment for mycosis fungoides.

questions.stem: A patient with mycosis fungoides is prescribed a topical alkylating agent as skin-directed therapy. The pharmacist explains that this drug forms inter- and intra-strand DNA cross-links, resulting in inhibition of DNA synthesis. Which of the following agents is being described?

explanation.summary: Topical mechlorethamine is an alkylating agent that cross-links DNA and inhibits DNA synthesis.
explanation.whyCorrect: The brick states that topical mechlorethamine is an alkylating agent used as a topical formulation that forms inter- and intra-strand DNA cross-links, resulting in inhibition of DNA synthesis, exactly matching the description.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Betamethasone is a topical corticosteroid that works by anti-inflammatory action, not DNA cross-linking.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Bexarotene is a retinoid used in early cutaneous disease, not a DNA-cross-linking alkylating agent.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Brentuximab is a systemic agent used in advanced disease and does not act by DNA cross-linking.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Interferon alpha is a systemic immune therapy, not a topical alkylating agent.

questions.stem: A 45-year-old man who emigrated from southwestern Japan presents with markedly elevated white blood cell count, a rash, generalized lymphadenopathy, and hypercalcemia with lytic bone lesions. A peripheral blood smear shows malignant T cells with multi-lobated, flower-shaped nuclei. Infection with which of the following organisms is most strongly associated with his condition?

explanation.summary: Adult T-cell leukemia/lymphoma is pathogenetically linked to HTLV-1.
explanation.whyCorrect: The brick states that ATLL is a mature T-cell neoplasm pathogenetically linked to HTLV-1 and is more common in endemic regions including southwestern Japan, the Caribbean, parts of central Africa, and Iran. The acute presentation with high WBC, hypercalcemia, and flower-shaped nuclei is classic.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Cytomegalovirus is related to systemic infections, not ATLL.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Epstein-Barr virus is associated with certain B-cell lymphomas, not ATLL.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Human herpesvirus 8 is associated with Kaposi sarcoma and primary effusion lymphoma, not ATLL.
whyWrongByChoice.D: HIV can cause immunosuppression but is not directly linked to ATLL.

questions.stem: A 47-year-old woman from the Caribbean presents with hypercalcemia, lymphadenopathy, and hepatosplenomegaly. Adult T-cell leukemia/lymphoma is suspected, and tissue is sampled to verify the immunophenotype and clonality of the atypical cells. Which of the following immunophenotypes is most characteristic of the malignant cells in this disorder?

explanation.summary: ATLL cells are characteristically CD3+, CD4+, CD25+, and CD7-.
explanation.whyCorrect: The brick states that ATLL malignant T cells have a relatively specific immunophenotype that aids in diagnosis: the T cells are CD3+, CD4+, CD25+, and CD7-.

whyWrongByChoice.B: ATLL cells are CD4+, CD25+, and CD7-, not CD8+/CD25-/CD7+.
whyWrongByChoice.C: This is a B-cell profile; ATLL is a mature T-cell neoplasm.
whyWrongByChoice.D: CD15+/CD30+ describes Reed-Sternberg cells of Hodgkin lymphoma, not ATLL.
whyWrongByChoice.E: CD34+/TdT+ marks immature precursor (lymphoblastic) cells, whereas ATLL is a mature T-cell neoplasm.

questions.stem: A patient is diagnosed with the most common clinical form of adult T-cell leukemia/lymphoma, characterized by a leukemic phase. Beyond the markedly elevated white blood cell count and lymphadenopathy, which of the following metabolic abnormalities is most characteristically associated with this acute form?

explanation.summary: The acute form of ATLL is characteristically associated with hypercalcemia.
explanation.whyCorrect: The brick states that the acute form is the most common, characterized by a leukemic phase with markedly elevated WBC, rash, and generalized lymphadenopathy, and that hypercalcemia, with or without lytic bone lesions, is common.

whyWrongByChoice.B: Hyperkalemia from tumor lysis is not the metabolic hallmark the brick emphasizes for this form.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Hypernatremia is not an associated finding described for acute ATLL.
whyWrongByChoice.D: The brick describes hypercalcemia, not hypocalcemia, as characteristic of acute ATLL.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Hypoglycemia is not described as a feature of acute ATLL.

questions.stem: A 52-year-old man with adult T-cell leukemia/lymphoma is started on a regimen that adds a recombinant humanized monoclonal antibody to chemotherapy. The antibody targets a chemokine receptor expressed on normal and malignant T cells; binding increases antibody-dependent cytotoxicity and reduces the number of these T cells. Which receptor does this antibody target?

explanation.summary: Mogamulizumab is an anti-CCR4 monoclonal antibody used in ATLL.
explanation.whyCorrect: The brick states that mogamulizumab is a recombinant humanized anti-CCR4 monoclonal antibody, that CCR4 is a chemokine receptor expressed on normal and malignant T cells including ATLL, and that binding increases antibody-dependent cytotoxicity, decreasing CCR4-expressing T cells.

whyWrongByChoice.A: PD-1 is targeted by checkpoint inhibitors such as pembrolizumab, not the agent described.
whyWrongByChoice.C: CD20 is targeted by rituximab in B-cell lymphomas, not by the anti-CCR4 antibody described.
whyWrongByChoice.D: CD30 is targeted by brentuximab; mogamulizumab targets CCR4.
whyWrongByChoice.E: CD52 is targeted by alemtuzumab, not by mogamulizumab.

questions.stem: A 60-year-old man reports that scaly patches first appeared years ago in his groin and on his buttocks, areas usually covered by clothing, and were repeatedly treated as eczema and psoriasis before a biopsy confirmed a cutaneous T-cell lymphoma. Which of the following best explains why mycosis fungoides is frequently misdiagnosed in its early stages?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Early lesions closely resemble common skin diseases

choices.label: B
choices.text: It always produces erythroderma before any patches appear

choices.label: C
choices.text: It causes a diagnostic peripheral blood leukocytosis from the outset

choices.label: D
choices.text: It is defined by pathognomonic Reed-Sternberg cells on first biopsy

choices.label: E
choices.text: It presents abruptly with high fever and rapidly enlarging nodes

explanation.summary: Early mycosis fungoides mimics benign skin conditions like eczema and psoriasis, delaying diagnosis.
explanation.whyCorrect: The brick states that mycosis fungoides usually presents as a slow-growing skin lesion that goes through multiple phases and may take years to diagnose, with the first stage looking very much like common skin diseases such as eczema and psoriasis, so patients may be misdiagnosed until further symptoms arise.

whyWrongByChoice.B: Erythroderma is a late (Sezary) finding, not an early presentation preceding patches.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Blood studies are usually not helpful and the WBC count is typically normal early on, since malignant T cells are confined to the skin.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Reed-Sternberg cells define Hodgkin lymphoma; mycosis fungoides shows cerebriform T cells.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Mycosis fungoides is slow-growing rather than abrupt with high fever and rapidly enlarging nodes.

questions.stem: A hematopathologist is teaching about mature T-cell neoplasms and notes that, although this brick focuses on a few classic subtypes, one entity accounts for the largest share of mature T-cell lymphomas overall. Which of the following is the most common subtype of mature T-cell lymphoma?

choices.label: B
choices.text: Mycosis fungoides, a cutaneous T-cell lymphoma

choices.label: C
choices.text: Peripheral T-cell lymphoma, not otherwise specified

choices.label: D
choices.text: Primary cutaneous anaplastic large cell lymphoma, CD30-positive

choices.label: E
choices.text: Sezary syndrome with erythroderma and circulating cells

explanation.summary: Peripheral T-cell lymphoma, not otherwise specified (PTCL-NOS) is the most common mature T-cell lymphoma.
explanation.whyCorrect: Mature T-cell lymphomas are a heterogeneous group of neoplasms, and the most common subtype is peripheral T-cell lymphoma, not otherwise specified. The other subtypes discussed here are singled out because they are unique and frequently tested, not because they are the most frequent.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Adult T-cell leukemia/lymphoma is a unique HTLV-1-linked neoplasm concentrated in endemic regions, not the most common subtype.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Mycosis fungoides is the most common cutaneous T-cell lymphoma but is uncommon overall, accounting for about 1% of hematopoietic neoplasms.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Primary cutaneous anaplastic large cell lymphoma is an aggressive cutaneous T-cell lymphoma, but it is not the most common subtype.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Sezary syndrome is the advanced, erythrodermic form of mycosis fungoides rather than the most common mature T-cell lymphoma.

questions.stem: A medical student is comparing lymphoma categories before an examination. Compared with B-cell lymphomas, which of the following best characterizes mature T-cell lymphomas as a group?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Equal in frequency and comparable in aggressiveness

choices.label: B
choices.text: Less common and more aggressive than B-cell lymphomas

choices.label: C
choices.text: Less common and more indolent than B-cell lymphomas

choices.label: D
choices.text: More common and more aggressive than B-cell lymphomas

choices.label: E
choices.text: More common and more indolent than B-cell lymphomas

explanation.summary: Mature T-cell lymphomas are less common than B-cell lymphomas but tend to behave more aggressively.
explanation.whyCorrect: Mature T-cell lymphomas are a heterogeneous group that is much less common than B-cell lymphomas and tends to be more aggressive. This frequency-versus-behavior contrast is the framing used to introduce the T-cell subtypes covered here.

whyWrongByChoice.A: The two groups differ in both frequency and clinical behavior rather than being equivalent.
whyWrongByChoice.C: The frequency is correct, but T-cell lymphomas tend to be more aggressive rather than more indolent.
whyWrongByChoice.D: The aggressiveness is correct, but T-cell lymphomas are less common, not more common, than B-cell lymphomas.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Both halves are reversed: T-cell lymphomas are the less common group and are not more indolent.

questions.stem: Mycosis fungoides and Sezary syndrome were originally regarded as two separate diseases on the basis of their clinical presentation and histopathology. Once precise immunophenotypic and genotypic studies became available, which of the following was demonstrated about the relationship between them?

choices.label: A
choices.text: They are distinct neoplasms driven by unrelated somatic mutations

choices.label: B
choices.text: They are genetically and histologically identical, differing only clinically

choices.label: C
choices.text: They arise from different lineages, one B-cell and one T-cell

choices.label: D
choices.text: They differ in histology but follow an identical clinical course

choices.label: E
choices.text: They share a clinical picture but differ markedly in genetic profile

explanation.summary: Mycosis fungoides and Sezary syndrome proved identical genetically and histologically, differing only in clinical presentation.
explanation.whyCorrect: The two disorders were first thought to be distinct because of their clinical presentation and histopathology. More precise immunophenotypic and genotypic studies showed them to be genetically and histologically identical in every way, differing only in the clinical presentation, which is why the compound name is used.

whyWrongByChoice.A: The studies showed them to be the same disease process, not two unrelated neoplasms.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Both disorders arise from mature T cells; neither is of B-cell lineage.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Their histology is identical, and their clinical courses differ, so this reverses both findings.
whyWrongByChoice.E: The opposite is true: the genetics are identical and it is the clinical presentation that differs.

questions.stem: A dermatology clinic is compiling a profile of patients newly diagnosed with mycosis fungoides. At approximately what age does the peak incidence of this disease occur?

explanation.summary: Mycosis fungoides peaks in incidence at 55 to 60 years of age.
explanation.whyCorrect: Mycosis fungoides is uncommon, representing about 1% of hematopoietic neoplasms, with roughly 2000 new cases per year in the United States compared with 8000 to 10,000 per year for Hodgkin lymphoma. Its peak incidence is at 55 to 60 years.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Adolescence is well before the peak; this is not a disease of the teenage years.
whyWrongByChoice.B: The third decade is earlier than the described peak incidence.
whyWrongByChoice.C: The early forties precede the stated peak of 55 to 60 years.
whyWrongByChoice.E: The peak occurs about fifteen years earlier than this range.

questions.stem: A 57-year-old man is evaluated for scaly, red skin lesions that have been present for two years. His dermatologist notes that the early lesions of mycosis fungoides tend to appear in a characteristic pattern often called a "bathing suit distribution." Which of the following areas is most consistent with this pattern?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Buttocks and genitalia, in areas protected from the sun

choices.label: B
choices.text: Extensor surfaces of the elbows and knees

choices.label: C
choices.text: Flexural creases of the neck and antecubital fossae

choices.label: D
choices.text: Palms and soles exclusively, with sparing of the trunk

choices.label: E
choices.text: Sun-exposed skin of the face and forearms

explanation.summary: Early mycosis fungoides lesions favor sun-protected sites such as the buttocks and genitalia.
explanation.whyCorrect: The scaly, red lesions of mycosis fungoides are often initially limited to parts of the body protected from the sun, such as the buttocks and genitalia, a pattern described as a bathing suit distribution. As the disease progresses, other areas including the extremities, soles, and palms can become involved.

whyWrongByChoice.B: Extensor elbows and knees are the classic distribution of psoriasis rather than the sun-protected pattern described.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Flexural involvement is characteristic of atopic dermatitis, not the bathing suit pattern.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Palms and soles can be involved as the disease progresses, but they are not the early, sun-protected pattern.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Sun-exposed sites are the opposite of the sun-protected areas involved early in this disease.

questions.stem: A student is puzzled that a T-cell lymphoma carries a name suggesting a fungal disease. Which of the following features of this disorder gave rise to the name "mycosis fungoides"?

choices.label: A
choices.text: A dermatophyte organism cultured from the skin lesions

choices.label: B
choices.text: A mold-like odor produced by the ulcerated skin lesions

choices.label: C
choices.text: Branching fungal hyphae seen within the biopsy specimen

choices.label: D
choices.text: Nodular, mushroom-like tumors seen in advanced stages

choices.label: E
choices.text: Ring-shaped scaly plaques closely resembling tinea corporis

explanation.summary: The name comes from the nodular, mushroom-like tumors of advanced disease, not from any fungal cause.
explanation.whyCorrect: The disease name might make one think of the word fungi, but the nodular, mushroom-like tumors that appear in advanced stages of mycosis fungoides are the feature that led to the name. The disorder is a neoplasm of mature T cells, not an infection.

whyWrongByChoice.A: No fungal organism is responsible; the lesions are infiltrates of neoplastic T lymphocytes.
whyWrongByChoice.B: The name derives from the gross shape of the advanced tumors, not from any odor.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Biopsies show neoplastic lymphocytes with convoluted nuclei, not fungal hyphae.
whyWrongByChoice.E: The early lesions resemble eczema and psoriasis rather than a ringed dermatophyte infection.

questions.stem: A 68-year-old man with long-standing mycosis fungoides has progressed to erythroderma with generalized lymphadenopathy and tumor invasion of the lungs and liver. His oncologist counsels the family about the most likely cause of death in this advanced stage. Which of the following should she describe?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Acute leukemic transformation with a blast crisis

choices.label: B
choices.text: Fatal arrhythmia precipitated by severe hypercalcemia

choices.label: C
choices.text: Infection, because these patients often become immunosuppressed

choices.label: D
choices.text: Massive gastrointestinal hemorrhage from tumor invasion

choices.label: E
choices.text: Progressive renal failure from light-chain deposition

explanation.summary: In advanced mycosis fungoides/Sezary syndrome, patients become immunosuppressed and death from infection is common.
explanation.whyCorrect: In the advanced stage there may be lymphadenopathy and tumor invasion of the lungs, liver, or spleen. Patients often become immunosuppressed, and death from infection is common.

whyWrongByChoice.A: The disease may evolve to a leukemic phase with circulating Sezary cells, but a blast crisis is not the described mode of death.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Hypercalcemia is a feature of adult T-cell leukemia/lymphoma, not of advanced mycosis fungoides.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Tumor invasion involves the lungs, liver, and spleen; gastrointestinal hemorrhage is not the described cause of death.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Light-chain deposition is a complication of plasma cell disorders, not of this T-cell neoplasm.

questions.stem: A 49-year-old woman newly diagnosed with mycosis fungoides asks whether her children are at risk and whether an exposure at work could have caused her disease. Which of the following statements best describes the genetic and environmental basis of this disorder?

choices.label: A
choices.text: It follows an autosomal dominant pattern with high penetrance

choices.label: B
choices.text: It has no hereditary link but is associated with acquired mutations

choices.label: C
choices.text: It is caused by a retrovirus usually acquired early in life

choices.label: D
choices.text: It is caused by a well-defined occupational chemical exposure

choices.label: E
choices.text: It results from a germline mutation in a DNA repair gene

explanation.summary: Mycosis fungoides has no hereditary link and is associated with a variety of acquired gene mutations.
explanation.whyCorrect: Mycosis fungoides has no hereditary link but is associated with a variety of acquired gene mutations, and no clear environmental risks have been identified. Her children are therefore not at inherited risk, and no specific exposure can be implicated.

whyWrongByChoice.A: There is no hereditary link, so no Mendelian inheritance pattern applies.
whyWrongByChoice.C: A retrovirus acquired early in life describes HTLV-1 and adult T-cell leukemia/lymphoma, not mycosis fungoides.
whyWrongByChoice.D: No clear environmental risks, occupational or otherwise, have been identified.
whyWrongByChoice.E: The mutations associated with this disease are acquired rather than germline.

questions.stem: A skin biopsy is taken from an early patch lesion in a patient with newly diagnosed mycosis fungoides. Which of the following best describes the location of the malignant lymphomatous cells at this stage of disease?

choices.label: A
choices.text: In the deep reticular dermis without epidermal involvement

choices.label: B
choices.text: In the subcutaneous fat with extension into skeletal muscle

choices.label: C
choices.text: In the upper dermis with extension into the epidermis

choices.label: D
choices.text: Inside lymph node germinal centers and mantle zones

choices.label: E
choices.text: Within bone marrow sinusoids and medullary cords

explanation.summary: Early mycosis fungoides cells infiltrate the upper dermis and extend into the epidermis.
explanation.whyCorrect: In the early stages of mycosis fungoides, the malignant lymphomatous cells infiltrate the upper dermis, extend into the epidermis, and are often seen in the blood. Sometimes the cells invade the epidermis in small clusters known as Pautrier microabscesses.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Epidermal involvement is a defining early feature, so sparing of the epidermis is incorrect.
whyWrongByChoice.B: The infiltrate is superficial, centered on the upper dermis, rather than in subcutaneous fat and muscle.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Lymph node involvement occurs in more advanced disease, not in early patch-stage lesions.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Bone marrow spread is an uncommon, late event rather than the early pattern of involvement.

questions.stem: A 64-year-old woman with advancing mycosis fungoides has developed diffuse lymphadenopathy, and an enlarged node is biopsied. Which of the following best describes the range of findings that may be encountered in the node?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Either reactive activated lymphocytes or lymphomatous Sezary cells

choices.label: B
choices.text: Granulomatous inflammation from an opportunistic mycobacterium

choices.label: C
choices.text: Lymphomatous infiltration only, because nodes are always involved

choices.label: D
choices.text: Metastatic epidermal carcinoma seeded from the skin lesions

choices.label: E
choices.text: Reactive change only, because this disease never involves nodes

explanation.summary: Lymphadenopathy in mycosis fungoides may be reactive or may represent true lymphomatous involvement by Sezary cells.
explanation.whyCorrect: The lymphadenopathy seen in mycosis fungoides is usually diffuse and can be either reactive, consisting of normal activated lymphocytes, or involve the lymphomatous Sezary cells. These cells can less commonly spread to the bone marrow and peripheral organs such as the liver and spleen.

whyWrongByChoice.B: Granulomatous inflammation is not among the described nodal findings in this disease.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Enlarged nodes are often simply reactive, so lymphomatous involvement is not invariable.
whyWrongByChoice.D: The neoplastic cells are T lymphocytes; the skin lesions are not carcinomas and do not metastasize as such.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Nodes can be genuinely infiltrated by lymphomatous Sezary cells, so reactive change is not the only possibility.

questions.stem: A 60-year-old man has scaly, erythematous plaques suspicious for cutaneous T-cell lymphoma. A skin biopsy is performed, but the histologic findings are equivocal and do not permit a confident diagnosis. Which of the following is the most appropriate next step?

choices.label: A
choices.text: An empiric course of systemic combination chemotherapy

choices.label: B
choices.text: Bone marrow aspiration and biopsy to establish the stage

choices.label: C
choices.text: Immunophenotyping and genetic analysis of the biopsy specimen

choices.label: D
choices.text: Repeat complete blood count with review of the blood smear

choices.label: E
choices.text: Serologic testing for antibodies directed against HTLV-1

explanation.summary: When the histology of a skin biopsy is uncertain, immunophenotyping and genetic analysis are used to confirm the diagnosis.
explanation.whyCorrect: Definitive diagnosis is made by skin biopsy, both to rule out benign skin conditions and to confirm a cutaneous T-cell lymphoma. If the histology is uncertain, immunophenotyping and genetic analysis can be done on the specimen.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Treatment should not be started before the diagnosis is established, and systemic chemotherapy is reserved for advanced disease.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Bone marrow spread is uncommon in this disease, and marrow sampling does not resolve an equivocal skin biopsy.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Blood studies are not usually helpful because the malignant T cells are typically confined to the skin.
whyWrongByChoice.E: HTLV-1 serology is confirmatory for adult T-cell leukemia/lymphoma, a different disease from the one suspected here.

questions.stem: A 51-year-old woman with early-stage cutaneous T-cell lymphoma is prescribed topical bexarotene, a retinoid. Which of the following adverse effects should she be counseled to expect from this agent?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Dermatitis, pruritus, and generalized skin inflammation

choices.label: B
choices.text: Hemorrhagic cystitis with hematuria and dysuria

choices.label: C
choices.text: Hypercalcemia with lytic lesions of the long bones

choices.label: D
choices.text: Infusion-related reactions, fatigue, and watery diarrhea

choices.label: E
choices.text: Peripheral neuropathy, constipation, and jaw pain

explanation.summary: Topical bexarotene causes dermatitis, pruritus, and skin inflammation.
explanation.whyCorrect: Bexarotene is a retinoid used in the early stages of cutaneous T-cell lymphoma, and its adverse effects include dermatitis, pruritus, and skin inflammation. These are local cutaneous reactions at the site of application.

whyWrongByChoice.B: Hemorrhagic cystitis is associated with cyclophosphamide, not with topical bexarotene.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Hypercalcemia with lytic bone lesions is a feature of adult T-cell leukemia/lymphoma, not a drug effect of bexarotene.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Infusion reactions, fatigue, and diarrhea are adverse effects of mogamulizumab, a systemic monoclonal antibody.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Neuropathy, constipation, and jaw pain are typical of vinca alkaloids rather than a topical retinoid.

questions.stem: A dermatologist plans phototherapy for a patient with mycosis fungoides, noting that this modality can be used in either early or advanced disease. Which of the following forms of light is used?

explanation.summary: Narrowband ultraviolet B phototherapy is used in both early and advanced mycosis fungoides.
explanation.whyCorrect: Among the skin-directed options for mycosis fungoides, UV phototherapy with narrowband ultraviolet B is used in the treatment of early or advanced disease.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Blue light therapy is used for other dermatologic indications, not for cutaneous T-cell lymphoma here.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Infrared light is not among the treatment modalities described for mycosis fungoides.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Narrowband ultraviolet A is not the phototherapy specified for this disease.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Pulsed-dye laser targets vascular lesions and is not the phototherapy described.

questions.stem: An oncologist is reviewing the place of radiotherapy in the management of mycosis fungoides. Which of the following statements best describes how radiation therapy is used in this disease?

choices.label: A
choices.text: It is contraindicated because the malignant T cells are radioresistant

choices.label: B
choices.text: It is reserved exclusively for hepatic and splenic tumor involvement

choices.label: C
choices.text: It is the first-line therapy for every stage of the disease

choices.label: D
choices.text: It is used for localized disease and combined with systemic drugs when advanced

choices.label: E
choices.text: It is used only after allogeneic stem cell transplantation fails

explanation.summary: Radiotherapy treats localized mycosis fungoides and is combined with systemic pharmacologic therapy in advanced disease.
explanation.whyCorrect: In some cases of localized disease radiotherapy can be used, and in advanced disease radiotherapy is combined with systemic pharmacological treatment. Treatment overall depends on the severity of disease, and most patients receive a combination of treatments.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Radiotherapy is an accepted treatment option, so radioresistance is not a reason to withhold it.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Radiotherapy is used for localized skin disease, not restricted to visceral organ involvement.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Topical corticosteroids and other skin-directed options are first-line for early Stage I/II disease.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Transplantation is not described as a prerequisite for the use of radiotherapy in this disease.

questions.stem: A 66-year-old man with advanced mycosis fungoides is to receive systemic therapy in addition to his topical treatment. Which of the following agents is a systemic option used in this setting?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Brentuximab given as an intravenous infusion

choices.label: E
choices.text: Topical mechlorethamine applied to involved plaques

explanation.summary: Brentuximab is one of the systemic agents added to topical therapy in advanced mycosis fungoides.
explanation.whyCorrect: In advanced disease, systemic chemotherapy or immune therapy is used along with topical therapy. The agents named for this purpose are oral bexarotene, brentuximab, and interferon alpha.

whyWrongByChoice.B: Clobetasol is likewise a topical corticosteroid and is not a systemic agent.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Narrowband ultraviolet B is a skin-directed phototherapy, not a systemic drug.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Betamethasone is a topical corticosteroid used for early-stage skin-directed treatment.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Mechlorethamine here is a topical alkylating formulation, a skin-directed rather than systemic therapy.

questions.stem: A 55-year-old man is found to have adult T-cell leukemia/lymphoma. He has prominent generalized lymphadenopathy, hepatosplenomegaly, and an elevated lactate dehydrogenase, but his white blood cell count is normal and no neoplastic cells are identified in the peripheral blood. Which clinical form of this disease does he have?

explanation.summary: The lymphomatous form of ATLL features prominent lymphadenopathy without peripheral blood involvement.
explanation.whyCorrect: The lymphomatous form is characterized by prominent lymphadenopathy without peripheral blood involvement. Patients may have systemic disease with hepatosplenomegaly and elevated lactate dehydrogenase, exactly as described here.

whyWrongByChoice.A: The acute form is defined by a leukemic phase with a markedly elevated white blood cell count, which he lacks.
whyWrongByChoice.B: The chronic form is associated with skin lesions, most often an exfoliative rash, which is not described.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Leukemic-phase evolution refers to mycosis fungoides progressing to Sezary syndrome, a different disease.
whyWrongByChoice.E: In the smoldering form lymphadenopathy is usually absent, whereas his lymphadenopathy is prominent.

questions.stem: A 58-year-old woman from an HTLV-1 endemic region is found to have adult T-cell leukemia/lymphoma. Her white blood cell count is normal, fewer than 5% of circulating cells are neoplastic, and she has several skin lesions and a pulmonary nodule. Serum calcium is normal and no lymphadenopathy is present. Which clinical form of this disease does she have?

explanation.summary: The smoldering form of ATLL has a normal white blood cell count with fewer than 5% circulating neoplastic cells and lacks hypercalcemia and lymphadenopathy.
explanation.whyCorrect: In the smoldering form the white blood cell count is normal, with fewer than 5% circulating neoplastic cells. Patients frequently have skin or pulmonary lesions, but hypercalcemia and lymphadenopathy are usually absent, which matches this presentation precisely.

whyWrongByChoice.A: The acute form has a markedly elevated white blood cell count with rash, generalized lymphadenopathy, and common hypercalcemia.
whyWrongByChoice.B: The chronic form is characterized by skin lesions that are most often an exfoliative rash, rather than the low circulating burden defined here.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Erythroderma is the hallmark of Sezary syndrome and is not one of the clinical forms of this disease.
whyWrongByChoice.D: The lymphomatous form is defined by prominent lymphadenopathy, which she does not have.

questions.stem: Adult T-cell leukemia/lymphoma is divided into several clinical forms. The form associated with skin lesions, most often an exfoliative rash, is best designated as which of the following?

explanation.summary: The chronic form of ATLL is the one associated with skin lesions, most often an exfoliative rash.
explanation.whyCorrect: Among the clinical forms of adult T-cell leukemia/lymphoma, the chronic form is described as being associated with skin lesions, most often an exfoliative rash.

whyWrongByChoice.A: The acute form is dominated by a leukemic phase with markedly elevated white blood cell count, generalized lymphadenopathy, and hypercalcemia.
whyWrongByChoice.B: An aleukemic form is not one of the recognized clinical forms of this disease.
whyWrongByChoice.D: The lymphomatous form features prominent lymphadenopathy without peripheral blood involvement.
whyWrongByChoice.E: The smoldering form has a normal white blood cell count with fewer than 5% circulating neoplastic cells and skin or pulmonary lesions.

questions.stem: A public health worker in an HTLV-1 endemic region is designing a program to interrupt transmission of the virus responsible for adult T-cell leukemia/lymphoma. Given that most patients are exposed to the virus early in life, which of the following routes should the program target?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Bite of an infected arthropod vector

choices.label: B
choices.text: Direct contact with contaminated soil through broken skin

choices.label: C
choices.text: Fecal-oral spread through contaminated drinking water

choices.label: E
choices.text: Mother-to-infant spread, chiefly via breast milk

explanation.summary: HTLV-1 is transmitted mother-to-infant mainly through breast milk, which accounts for early-life exposure.
explanation.whyCorrect: The HTLV-1 virus has a long latency and most patients are exposed early in life. The three major routes of infection are mother-to-infant transmission, mainly through breast milk, sexual transmission, and transmission through blood and blood products. Only the first of these explains exposure in infancy.

whyWrongByChoice.A: No arthropod vector is involved in the transmission of this virus.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Soil contact is not a recognized route; transmission occurs via breast milk, sexual contact, and blood products.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Fecal-oral spread is not a described route of HTLV-1 infection.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Respiratory droplet spread is not among the routes of transmission for this retrovirus.

questions.stem: A 52-year-old man has hypercalcemia, generalized lymphadenopathy, and circulating T cells with multi-lobated nuclei. Tissue sampling shows a CD3+, CD4+, CD25+, CD7- clonal T-cell population, and adult T-cell leukemia/lymphoma is suspected. Which of the following studies would be confirmatory?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Bone marrow biopsy demonstrating more than 20% blasts in the aspirate

choices.label: B
choices.text: Flow cytometry for CD15 and CD30 co-expression on large cells

choices.label: C
choices.text: In situ hybridization for Epstein-Barr virus RNA on the node

choices.label: D
choices.text: Serologic antibody testing or polymerase chain reaction for HTLV-1

choices.label: E
choices.text: Serum protein electrophoresis with immunofixation of light chains

explanation.summary: Serologic studies for antibodies to HTLV-1, or PCR for HTLV-1, confirm the diagnosis of ATLL.
explanation.whyCorrect: Once adult T-cell leukemia/lymphoma is suspected, the diagnosis is made by sampling affected tissue to verify the immunophenotype and clonality of the atypical cells. Serologic studies for antibodies to HTLV-1 or PCR for HTLV-1 can then be confirmatory.

whyWrongByChoice.A: A blast count threshold defines acute leukemia; this is a mature T-cell neoplasm.
whyWrongByChoice.B: CD15 and CD30 co-expression characterizes Reed-Sternberg cells of Hodgkin lymphoma, not this neoplasm.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Epstein-Barr virus is linked to certain B-cell lymphomas; the viral association here is with HTLV-1.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Protein electrophoresis is used to evaluate plasma cell disorders rather than T-cell lymphomas.

questions.stem: A 58-year-old man with adult T-cell leukemia/lymphoma begins the VCAP-AMP-VECP regimen. One component, vindesine, is a semisynthetic agent derived from vinblastine. Which of the following best describes its mechanism of action?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Cross-linking of DNA strands by an alkylating metabolite

choices.label: B
choices.text: Formation of platinum-DNA adducts that block replication

choices.label: C
choices.text: Inhibition of microtubule assembly and function

choices.label: D
choices.text: Inhibition of topoisomerase II causing DNA strand breaks

choices.label: E
choices.text: Intercalation into DNA with generation of free radicals

explanation.summary: Vindesine is a vinca alkaloid derived from vinblastine and acts as a microtubule inhibitor.
explanation.whyCorrect: Within the VCAP-AMP-VECP regimen, vindesine is specifically noted to be a microtubule inhibitor and a semisynthetic vinca alkaloid derived from vinblastine. Vinca alkaloids act on microtubules rather than directly on DNA.

whyWrongByChoice.A: DNA cross-linking by an alkylating metabolite describes cyclophosphamide and mechlorethamine, not vindesine.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Platinum-DNA adduct formation describes carboplatin, a different component of VECP.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Topoisomerase II inhibition describes etoposide, another component of the VECP portion of the regimen.
whyWrongByChoice.E: DNA intercalation with free radical generation describes doxorubicin, the anthracycline in the regimen.

questions.stem: A 57-year-old woman with adult T-cell leukemia/lymphoma has mogamulizumab added to her chemotherapy regimen. Which of the following adverse effect profiles is most commonly associated with this agent?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Dermatitis, pruritus, and generalized skin inflammation

choices.label: B
choices.text: Hemorrhagic cystitis, hematuria, and bladder fibrosis

choices.label: C
choices.text: Infusion reactions, fatigue, diarrhea, and upper respiratory infection

choices.label: D
choices.text: Photosensitivity, corneal deposits, and blue-gray skin discoloration

choices.label: E
choices.text: Pulmonary fibrosis, digital gangrene, and Raynaud phenomenon

explanation.summary: Mogamulizumab commonly causes infusion-related reactions, fatigue, diarrhea, and upper respiratory tract infection.
explanation.whyCorrect: Mogamulizumab is a recombinant humanized anti-CCR4 monoclonal antibody added to the chemotherapy regimen for this disease. Infusion-related reactions, fatigue, diarrhea, and upper respiratory tract infection are the common adverse effects associated with it.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Dermatitis, pruritus, and skin inflammation are the adverse effects of topical bexarotene.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Hemorrhagic cystitis is characteristic of cyclophosphamide rather than a monoclonal antibody.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Corneal deposits and skin discoloration are not among the described effects of this antibody.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Pulmonary fibrosis and digital vascular events are not the described adverse effect profile here.

questions.stem: A 74-year-old man is diagnosed with adult T-cell leukemia/lymphoma. His oncologist notes that his age influences the choice of chemotherapy backbone. Which of the following regimens is generally used for patients in his age group?

explanation.summary: Patients 70 years and older with ATLL are generally treated with CHOP, with mogamulizumab often added.
explanation.whyCorrect: For patients 70 years of age and older, treatment is generally with CHOP, consisting of cyclophosphamide, doxorubicin, vincristine, and prednisone. Adding mogamulizumab to the CHOP regimen has shown benefits in this group.

whyWrongByChoice.B: Phototherapy is used for cutaneous T-cell lymphoma and is not a chemotherapy backbone here.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Interferon alpha is listed among systemic agents for advanced mycosis fungoides, not as this regimen.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Topical mechlorethamine is a skin-directed therapy for mycosis fungoides, not a regimen for this disease.
whyWrongByChoice.E: VCAP-AMP-VECP is the widely adopted regimen, but CHOP is preferred in patients of this age.

questions.stem: A 59-year-old woman with biopsy-proven mycosis fungoides confined to several cutaneous plaques has a complete blood count performed. Her white blood cell count is normal. Which of the following best explains this finding?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Circulating tumor cells are destroyed by anti-CCR4 antibodies

choices.label: B
choices.text: The bone marrow compensates by increasing granulopoiesis

choices.label: C
choices.text: The malignant cells lack the markers detected by the analyzer

choices.label: D
choices.text: The malignant T cells are rapidly cleared by the spleen

choices.label: E
choices.text: The malignant T cells usually remain within the skin

explanation.summary: The white blood cell count is normal in mycosis fungoides because the malignant T cells are usually confined to the skin.
explanation.whyCorrect: Blood studies are not usually helpful in this disease. On a complete blood count, the white blood cell count is normal because the malignant T cells are usually confined to the skin. Uncommonly, circulating Sezary cells may be seen on the peripheral blood smear.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Anti-CCR4 antibody therapy is a treatment used in adult T-cell leukemia/lymphoma, not an explanation for an untreated patient's normal count.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Marrow compensation is not invoked; the count is normal because the tumor is localized to skin.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Automated counts do not miss these cells; the cells are simply not circulating in early disease.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Splenic clearance of malignant cells is not the described reason for the normal count.

questions.stem: A 32-year-old man presents with 3 months of intermittent fever, drenching night sweats, and a 7-kg (15-lb) unintentional weight loss. On examination he has several firm, nontender, enlarged cervical lymph nodes. There is no history of infection or inflammatory disease. Which of the following is the most appropriate next step to establish a definitive diagnosis?

choices.label: E
choices.text: PET/CT scan of the chest, abdomen, and pelvis

explanation.summary: A lymph node biopsy provides the definitive tissue diagnosis of Hodgkin lymphoma.
explanation.whyCorrect: In a patient with lymphadenopathy but no underlying infection or inflammatory disorder, the brick teaches that a lymph node biopsy is the next step and provides a definitive diagnosis of HL using its characteristic histologic features, such as Reed-Sternberg cells.
