choices.text: Transports erythropoietin across the membrane into the nucleus

explanation.summary: JAK2 phosphorylates proteins in the JAK-STAT pathway, which stimulates growth-promoting genes.
explanation.whyCorrect: The brick states that JAK2 codes for a tyrosine kinase that phosphorylates other proteins in the JAK-signal transducer and activator of transcription (JAK-STAT) signaling pathway to stimulate growth-promoting genes. Normally erythropoietin binding activates this cascade; in PV the mutated kinase stays on regardless of erythropoietin.

whyWrongByChoice.A: JAK2 transmits the signal rather than terminating it by cleaving the receptor.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Converting arachidonic acid to prostaglandins is the cyclooxygenase step that aspirin blocks.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Inhibiting ribonucleotide reductase is the mechanism of hydroxyurea, not of JAK2.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Erythropoietin acts at a cell-surface receptor and is not carried into the nucleus by JAK2.

questions.stem: A 60-year-old man with newly diagnosed polycythemia vera has a hemoglobin of 19.2 g/dL and an elevated red blood cell count. Which of the following additional patterns is most likely on his complete blood count?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Decreased white blood cell count and decreased platelet count

choices.label: B
choices.text: Decreased white blood cell count with a normal platelet count

choices.label: C
choices.text: Increased white blood cell count and increased platelet count

choices.label: D
choices.text: Increased white blood cell count with a decreased platelet count

choices.label: E
choices.text: Normal white blood cell count with a decreased platelet count

explanation.summary: Beyond the red cell excess, PV typically produces leukocytosis and thrombocytosis.
explanation.whyCorrect: The brick states that the main finding in the blood of patients with PV is an excess of mature RBCs with increased hemoglobin, hematocrit, and RBC count, and that patients may also have an elevated white blood cell count (leukocytosis) and elevated platelet count (thrombocytosis).

whyWrongByChoice.A: Cytopenias are the opposite of the panmyeloid increase seen in PV.
whyWrongByChoice.B: A low white blood cell count is not characteristic of PV.
whyWrongByChoice.D: The white cell count is correct here, but the platelet count is typically elevated, not decreased.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Thrombocytosis rather than thrombocytopenia is expected in PV.

questions.stem: A peripheral blood smear from a 63-year-old man with polycythemia vera shows a crowded field of red cells interspersed with other blood cells. Which of the following best describes the red cells on this smear?

choices.label: B
choices.text: Increased in number and markedly hypochromic

choices.label: C
choices.text: Increased in number and markedly microcytic

choices.label: D
choices.text: Increased in number and predominantly nucleated

choices.label: E
choices.text: Increased in number but with normal morphology

explanation.summary: In PV the red cells are increased in number but usually have normal morphology.
explanation.whyCorrect: The brick states that a peripheral blood smear in PV will show increased red blood cells, creating a crowded appearance, interspersed with other blood cells, and that though increased in number the red cells usually have normal morphology. The abnormality is quantity, not shape or color.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Red cells are increased, not decreased, and fragmentation is not described.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Hypochromia would suggest a hemoglobinization defect, not the normal-appearing cells of PV.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Microcytosis is not the described smear finding in PV.
whyWrongByChoice.D: The cells that spill into the blood in PV are mature, not nucleated precursors.

questions.stem: A 65-year-old man with polycythemia vera and a platelet count of 900,000/mm3 has recurrent gum bleeding and epistaxis and is now admitted with a gastrointestinal bleed. Major hemorrhage occurs in 5% to 10% of patients with PV. Which of the following best explains bleeding in these patients?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Autoantibodies directed against platelet surface glycoproteins

choices.label: B
choices.text: Consumption of platelets within widespread microthrombi

choices.label: C
choices.text: Deficiency of the vitamin K-dependent clotting factors

choices.label: D
choices.text: High platelet counts combined with impaired platelet function

choices.label: E
choices.text: Marrow fibrosis with a resulting fall in the platelet count

explanation.summary: Most bleeding in PV occurs in patients with high platelet counts and impaired platelet function.
explanation.whyCorrect: The brick states that minor bleeding is very common in PV and that major hemorrhage can occur in 5% to 10% of cases. Most bleeding occurs in patients with high platelet counts and impaired platelet function, similar to the mechanism observed in essential thrombocytosis, another myeloproliferative neoplasm that can overlap with PV in presentation.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Antiplatelet autoantibodies would lower the platelet count rather than raise it.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Platelet consumption in microthrombi is not the described mechanism, and his platelet count is high.
whyWrongByChoice.C: A clotting factor deficiency is not part of the bleeding mechanism the brick describes for PV.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Marrow fibrosis defines the late spent phase; this patient's platelet count is markedly elevated.

questions.stem: A 70-year-old woman has had polycythemia vera for 12 years and asks whether her disease can turn into a more aggressive blood cancer. In roughly 2% of patients, PV transforms into which of the following?

explanation.summary: In rare cases, about 2% of patients, polycythemia vera transforms into acute myeloid leukemia.
explanation.whyCorrect: The brick states that in rare cases, about 2% of patients, PV transforms into acute myeloid leukemia. This is consistent with PV being a neoplasm of the myeloid lineage arising from a single hematopoietic stem cell progenitor.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Transformation is to a myeloid, not a lymphoblastic, leukemia.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Chronic myeloid leukemia is a separate BCR-ABL-driven neoplasm, not the transformation of PV.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Hodgkin lymphoma is a lymphoid malignancy unrelated to PV progression.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Multiple myeloma is a plasma cell neoplasm and is not the described transformation.

questions.stem: A 63-year-old man with polycythemia vera has firm nodular deposits over the helix of one ear and in several finger joints. Which of the following best explains these deposits?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Amyloid derived from a circulating monoclonal protein

choices.label: B
choices.text: Cholesterol deposited in tendons and skin

choices.label: D
choices.text: Iron liberated by repeated therapeutic phlebotomy

choices.label: E
choices.text: Urate deposited because of high circulating uric acid

explanation.summary: Gouty tophi in PV are urate deposits driven by high uric acid from rapid red cell turnover.
explanation.whyCorrect: The brick lists gouty tophi, urate deposits in joints, cartilage, and under the skin, among the physical findings in PV, along with hypertension, an enlarged spleen, and engorged veins in the optic fundus. It explains that the tophi are because of high circulating uric acid levels resulting from rapid RBC turnover.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Amyloid from a monoclonal protein belongs to plasma cell disease, not PV.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Cholesterol deposits reflect lipid disorders and are not attributed to PV in the brick.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Extramedullary hematopoiesis in PV occurs in the spleen and liver during the spent phase.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Phlebotomy removes iron with the blood and does not create nodular tissue deposits.

questions.stem: A 55-year-old man is being evaluated for possible polycythemia vera after an abnormal complete blood count. Which of the following hemoglobin values satisfies the diagnostic criterion for PV in a man?

explanation.summary: The hemoglobin criterion for PV is greater than 16.5 g/dL in men and greater than 16.0 g/dL in women.
explanation.whyCorrect: The brick gives increased hemoglobin and hematocrit as the initial laboratory abnormality in PV, with criteria of Hgb greater than 16.5 g/dL in men and greater than 16.0 g/dL in women. This threshold is one of four listed diagnostic criteria, along with the JAK2 mutation, a hypercellular marrow with trilineage growth, and a serum EPO level below the reference range.

whyWrongByChoice.A: 14.0 g/dL falls within the normal range and is well below the stated threshold.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Greater than 16.0 g/dL is the criterion for women, not men.
whyWrongByChoice.D: 18.5 g/dL is above the stated criterion and would miss qualifying patients.
whyWrongByChoice.E: 20.0 g/dL is far higher than the threshold the criteria use.

questions.stem: A 61-year-old man who has never smoked and lives at sea level has a hematocrit of 57%, gross hematuria, and an oxygen saturation of 98%. CT of the abdomen shows a solid renal mass. Which of the following best explains his increased red cell mass?

choices.label: A
choices.text: A constitutively active JAK2 kinase in red cell precursors

choices.label: B
choices.text: Aberrant erythropoietin production by the tumor

choices.label: E
choices.text: Tissue hypoxia resulting from chronic hypoxemia

explanation.summary: Renal cell cancer causes secondary polycythemia through aberrant erythropoietin production by the tumor cells.
explanation.whyCorrect: The brick states that less commonly, excess EPO in secondary polycythemia is caused by aberrant EPO production or response, such as renal cell cancer in which the tumor cells make too much of the hormone. It adds that renal cell cancer will often show hematuria or a renal mass on CT scanning, both present here.

whyWrongByChoice.A: A constitutively active JAK2 kinase defines PV, which does not produce hematuria or a renal mass.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Relative polycythemia from dehydration would not explain hematuria and a solid renal mass.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Marrow fibrosis with extramedullary hematopoiesis is a late feature of PV, not a cause of tumor-driven erythrocytosis.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Hypoxic secondary polycythemia would be accompanied by a low oxygen saturation and a history such as lung disease, altitude, or smoking.

questions.stem: A 27-year-old competitive cyclist has a hematocrit of 58%. His oxygen saturation is 99%, he lives at sea level, he does not smoke, and he has no lung disease. Serum erythropoietin is elevated and testing for the JAK2 mutation is negative. Which of the following is the most likely cause of his polycythemia?

choices.label: C
choices.text: High-altitude living with a physiologic rise in erythropoietin

choices.label: E
choices.text: Polycythemia vera with a suppressed erythropoietin level

explanation.summary: Erythropoietin abuse, or blood doping, raises EPO and red cell mass without hypoxia or a JAK2 mutation.
explanation.whyCorrect: The brick lists erythropoietin abuse (blood doping) along with androgen abuse and renal cell cancer as less common causes of secondary polycythemia from aberrant EPO production or response. A high EPO with a normal oxygen saturation and no JAK2 mutation excludes both PV and the hypoxic causes.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Chronic lung disease drives polycythemia through hypoxemia and he has neither lung disease nor desaturation.
whyWrongByChoice.C: He lives at sea level, so altitude-driven tissue hypoxia does not apply.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Obstructive sleep apnea raises EPO through chronic hypoxemia, which would lower his oxygen saturation.
whyWrongByChoice.E: PV is characterized by a low EPO level and a JAK2 mutation, neither of which is present.

questions.stem: A 54-year-old woman with polycythemia vera is maintained on therapeutic phlebotomy and low-dose aspirin, and her symptoms are controlled. Which of the following features would classify a patient with PV as high risk and prompt the addition of a cytoreductive agent?

choices.label: A
choices.text: A hematocrit above 45% at the time of diagnosis

choices.label: B
choices.text: A palpable spleen tip on physical examination

choices.label: C
choices.text: A serum erythropoietin level below the reference range

choices.label: D
choices.text: Age older than 60 years or a history of thrombosis

choices.label: E
choices.text: Aquagenic pruritus that responds well to aspirin

explanation.summary: High-risk PV means age over 60 years or a history of thrombosis, and these patients may benefit from a cytoreductive agent.
explanation.whyCorrect: The brick states that patients with high-risk PV, defined as older than 60 years OR a history of thrombosis, may also benefit from cytoreductive agents such as hydroxyurea or pegylated interferon alfa. It repeats this definition when it notes that cytoreductive agents may be added if aspirin alone does not control pruritus and erythromelalgia or if the patient is high risk.

whyWrongByChoice.A: A hematocrit above 45% is the threshold phlebotomy is used to correct, not a high-risk definition.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Splenomegaly is a common finding in PV and is not one of the two high-risk criteria.
whyWrongByChoice.C: A low serum EPO is a diagnostic criterion for PV, not a marker of high-risk disease.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Pruritus that responds to aspirin argues against needing cytoreduction rather than for it.

questions.stem: A 59-year-old woman with polycythemia vera undergoes phlebotomy at regular intervals to remove a controlled volume of blood. Phlebotomy should be performed to maintain her hematocrit below which of the following values?

explanation.summary: Phlebotomy in PV targets a hematocrit in the normal range, below 45%.
explanation.whyCorrect: The brick states that phlebotomy at regular intervals removes a controlled volume of the patient's blood to maintain hematocrit in the normal range (less than 45%), which decreases blood viscosity and the risk of developing clots. This may be sufficient therapy for some patients, though medication may be needed in addition.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Reducing the hematocrit to 35% would push the patient into the anemic range rather than the normal range.
whyWrongByChoice.C: 50% remains above the stated target of less than 45%.
whyWrongByChoice.D: 55% is still well above the normal range the brick targets.
whyWrongByChoice.E: A hematocrit of 60% leaves the blood dangerously viscous and thrombosis-prone.

questions.stem: A 68-year-old man with high-risk polycythemia vera has been taking a cytoreductive agent for 6 months. He now has painful oral and lower leg ulcers, loose stools, and numbness of both feet, and his blood counts have fallen. Which of the following medications is most likely responsible?

explanation.summary: Cytopenia, mucocutaneous ulcers, diarrhea, and peripheral neuropathy are the adverse effects of hydroxyurea.
explanation.whyCorrect: The brick states that because hydroxyurea works by inhibiting ribonucleotide reductase and halting the cell cycle at G1/S, its adverse effects include cytopenia, mucocutaneous ulcers, diarrhea, and peripheral neuropathy. This cluster matches the patient's ulcers, loose stools, foot numbness, and falling counts.

whyWrongByChoice.B: Aspirin's antiplatelet action predisposes to bleeding rather than to ulcers with neuropathy and cytopenia.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Interferon alfa causes elevated liver enzymes, neutropenia, mood changes, fatigue, insomnia, and gastrointestinal upset rather than this pattern.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Ruxolitinib is reserved for patients failing hydroxyurea or interferon and is not described with this adverse effect profile.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Warfarin is an anticoagulant used for thrombosis and does not cause mucocutaneous ulcers and neuropathy.

questions.stem: A 66-year-old woman taking hydroxyurea for polycythemia vera plans international travel and asks her physician about immunizations. Which of the following is contraindicated while she remains on this medication?

explanation.summary: Live vaccine administration is a contraindication while a patient is taking hydroxyurea.
explanation.whyCorrect: The brick states explicitly that live vaccine administration is a contraindication while a patient is on hydroxyurea. This follows from the drug's cell cycle mechanism, which suppresses cell proliferation and can cause cytopenia.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Hepatitis B vaccine is not a live vaccine and is not the contraindication described.
whyWrongByChoice.B: An inactivated influenza vaccine contains no replicating organism and is not the contraindicated type.
whyWrongByChoice.D: The pneumococcal polysaccharide vaccine is not a live product.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Tetanus toxoid is not a live preparation.

questions.stem: A 57-year-old man with high-risk polycythemia vera and known cirrhosis cannot take hydroxyurea and is being considered for pegylated interferon alfa. Which of the following is the greatest concern with this agent in this particular patient?

explanation.summary: Interferon alfa can worsen liver function, so a patient with cirrhosis may experience further hepatic decompensation.
explanation.whyCorrect: The brick states that a patient with liver disease such as cirrhosis may experience further hepatic decompensation on interferon alfa, and it lists elevated liver enzymes among the drug's adverse effects along with neutropenia, anxiety, depression, fatigue, insomnia, and gastrointestinal issues. Because it is obtained from human leukocytes it also has a propensity for hypersensitivity reactions.

whyWrongByChoice.B: Inhibition of ribonucleotide reductase is hydroxyurea's mechanism, not an adverse effect of interferon.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Irreversible cyclooxygenase inhibition describes aspirin's action, not interferon's.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Peripheral neuropathy is listed among hydroxyurea's adverse effects rather than interferon's.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Teratogenicity is the concern with hydroxyurea, and interferon alfa is the agent preferred in pregnancy.

questions.stem: A 71-year-old man with polycythemia vera has persistent pruritus and an inadequately controlled hematocrit despite hydroxyurea, and he was unable to tolerate pegylated interferon alfa. Which of the following is the most appropriate next therapy?

explanation.summary: Ruxolitinib, a Janus associated kinase inhibitor, is reserved for PV patients who fail hydroxyurea or interferon alfa.
explanation.whyCorrect: The brick describes ruxolitinib as a newer targeted therapy and a Janus associated kinase inhibitor that can control PV-associated symptoms. Because its long-term effects on PV are uncertain, it is generally reserved for patients who fail to respond adequately to hydroxyurea or interferon alfa, which is this patient's situation.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Bone marrow transplantation is used in some other hematopoietic neoplasms but not for PV.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Cyclophosphamide is a chemotherapy agent that is not used to treat PV.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Corticosteroids are not part of the described management of PV.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Anticoagulants are prescribed for patients with PV who have thrombosis, not to control pruritus and hematocrit.

questions.stem: A 68-year-old woman is referred for new-onset headaches and occasional blurry vision. Her head CT and ophthalmologic exam are normal. She has no relevant medical history and does not smoke or drink. On examination she has splenomegaly, and her complete blood count reveals a markedly elevated platelet count. Secondary causes of thrombocytosis have been excluded. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

explanation.summary: Essential thrombocythemia is a myeloproliferative neoplasm marked by massive platelet production, often presenting with microvascular symptoms and splenomegaly.
explanation.whyCorrect: ET is a hematopoietic neoplasm characterized by overproduction of platelets. When symptomatic, patients have nonspecific vascular symptoms such as headache and visual changes from microthrombi, and 25% to 50% have splenomegaly from extramedullary hematopoiesis. Once secondary causes are excluded, a very high platelet count with these findings points to ET.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Aplastic anemia produces pancytopenia with a hypocellular, fatty marrow, not an elevated platelet count.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Chronic myeloid leukemia is distinguished by the Philadelphia chromosome (BCR::ABL1) and a marked leukocytosis rather than isolated thrombocytosis.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Iron deficiency anemia causes a reactive thrombocytosis but would show microcytic anemia and would be identified as a secondary cause, which has been excluded here.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Recent surgery is a cause of secondary thrombocytosis, but the stem states secondary causes have already been excluded.

questions.stem: A patient is diagnosed with essential thrombocythemia. In the bone marrow, proliferation of which of the following myeloid cell types is most responsible for the elevated platelet count?

explanation.summary: Megakaryocytes are the platelet precursors, and their proliferation drives the thrombocytosis of ET.
explanation.whyCorrect: In ET the megakaryocytes proliferate the most. Megakaryocytes are the precursors of platelets in the bone marrow, which are then released into the blood, producing the massive increase in platelet number seen in the disease.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Erythroid precursor proliferation drives red cell overproduction in polycythemia vera, not the thrombocytosis of ET.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Lymphoblasts are lymphoid cells seen in acute lymphoblastic leukemia and are not the source of platelets.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Neutrophil precursor expansion characterizes chronic myeloid leukemia rather than ET.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Plasma cells produce immunoglobulin and are expanded in multiple myeloma, not in ET.

questions.stem: Genetic testing of a patient with essential thrombocythemia reveals an activating mutation in JAK2. The protein encoded by this gene most directly promotes cell growth through which of the following mechanisms?

choices.label: A
choices.text: A calcium-binding chaperone in the endoplasmic reticulum lumen

choices.label: B
choices.text: A cell-surface receptor for thrombopoietin on megakaryocytes

choices.label: C
choices.text: A fusion protein generated by the Philadelphia chromosome t(9;22)

choices.label: D
choices.text: A transcription factor that blocks apoptosis directly in the nucleus

choices.label: E
choices.text: A tyrosine kinase that phosphorylates JAK/STAT signaling proteins

explanation.summary: JAK2 encodes a tyrosine kinase that activates JAK/STAT signaling to stimulate hematopoietic cell growth.
explanation.whyCorrect: The JAK2 gene codes for a tyrosine kinase that stimulates growth-promoting genes by phosphorylating JAK/signal transducer and activator of transcription (JAK/STAT) proteins. In hematopoietic stem cells this JAK/STAT pathway mediates cell growth, so an activating JAK2 mutation drives the proliferation seen in ET.

whyWrongByChoice.A: A calcium-binding chaperone describes calreticulin (CALR), a different mutation found in JAK2-negative cases.
whyWrongByChoice.B: A receptor for thrombopoietin describes MPL, not JAK2.
whyWrongByChoice.C: The Philadelphia chromosome fusion protein is BCR::ABL1, which defines chronic myeloid leukemia rather than ET.
whyWrongByChoice.D: JAK2 acts as a tyrosine kinase in the JAK/STAT cascade, not as a transcription factor that directly blocks apoptosis.

questions.stem: A patient has clinical and bone marrow findings suspicious for essential thrombocythemia, but testing for the most common associated mutation is negative. Testing for which of the following gene mutations would be most useful next?

explanation.summary: In JAK2-negative ET, calreticulin (CALR) mutations account for about 30% of cases and are the next appropriate test.
explanation.whyCorrect: Approximately 50% of ET cases carry a JAK2 mutation. In JAK2-negative cases there can be other mutations, such as calreticulin (CALR, roughly 30% of cases) or MPL (5% to 10%). Testing CALR is therefore the most useful next step.

whyWrongByChoice.A: BCR::ABL1 mutations are seen in chronic myeloid leukemia, not essential thrombocythemia.
whyWrongByChoice.B: BRCA1 mutations are associated with breast and ovarian cancer and are not linked to myeloproliferative neoplasms.
whyWrongByChoice.D: FLT3 mutations are tested in acute myeloid leukemia and are not associated with ET.
whyWrongByChoice.E: TP53 mutations are also more relevant to acute myeloid leukemia and are not part of the standard ET workup.

questions.stem: A 55-year-old man is being evaluated for marked thrombocytosis with numerous giant platelets on smear and a JAK2 mutation, after secondary causes were excluded. A bone marrow biopsy is performed. Which of the following findings is most likely?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Abundant lymphoblasts completely replacing the normal marrow

choices.label: B
choices.text: Hypocellular marrow with extensive fatty infiltration throughout

choices.label: C
choices.text: Normocellular marrow with dominant megakaryocyte proliferation

choices.label: D
choices.text: Normocellular marrow with numerous lipid-laden atypical macrophages

choices.label: E
choices.text: Sheets of monoclonal plasma cells filling the marrow space

explanation.summary: The marrow in ET is typically normocellular with a striking proliferation of megakaryocytes in large clusters.
explanation.whyCorrect: The bone marrow in ET is typically normocellular, and its unique feature is the massive proliferation of megakaryocytes, which can be seen in large clusters throughout the marrow. Dominant megakaryocyte proliferation suggests ET, though it is not always present.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Abundant lymphoblasts point to an acute leukemia rather than a myeloproliferative neoplasm.
whyWrongByChoice.B: A hypocellular, fatty marrow is characteristic of aplastic anemia, not ET.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Atypical marrow macrophages suggest a storage disorder such as Gaucher disease, not ET.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Sheets of monoclonal plasma cells define multiple myeloma, which does not cause this picture.

questions.stem: A peripheral blood smear is reviewed for a patient with essential thrombocythemia. Which of the following findings is most characteristic?

choices.label: C
choices.text: Numerous teardrop-shaped red blood cells only

choices.label: D
choices.text: Platelets ranging from tiny to gigantic

choices.label: E
choices.text: Rouleaux formation of red blood cells

explanation.summary: The main smear abnormality in ET is a marked increase in platelets that vary widely in size, called platelet anisocytosis.
explanation.whyCorrect: In ET the principal peripheral blood abnormality is the marked increase in platelet number, and the platelets may range in size from tiny to gigantic. This variation in platelet size is termed platelet anisocytosis, while the other blood cells typically appear normal.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Hypersegmented neutrophils indicate megaloblastic anemia from B12 or folate deficiency.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Spherocytosis is seen in hereditary spherocytosis and immune hemolysis, not in ET.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Teardrop red cells suggest marrow fibrosis; they are not the defining smear finding of ET, which centers on platelets.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Rouleaux formation reflects elevated plasma proteins, as in multiple myeloma, not ET.

questions.stem: A 42-year-old woman with newly diagnosed essential thrombocythemia has no history of arterial or venous thrombosis and no other high-risk features. Which of the following is the most appropriate management?

explanation.summary: All ET patients should receive low-dose aspirin, and young patients without thrombosis need nothing more.
explanation.whyCorrect: All patients with ET should receive low-dose aspirin to reduce microvascular complications and thrombotic risk. Young patients with no history of arterial or venous thrombi can be managed with aspirin alone; cytoreductive therapy is reserved for higher-risk patients.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Cyclophosphamide is a chemotherapy drug not used for ET.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Lisinopril is used to control hypertension, not to manage ET.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Metoprolol is also an antihypertensive and has no role in treating ET.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Tissue plasminogen activator is a clot-busting drug used for acute events such as some myocardial infarctions, not for routine ET management.

questions.stem: A 67-year-old man with essential thrombocythemia continues to have microvascular symptoms despite low-dose aspirin, and he has a prior history of deep vein thrombosis. Which of the following is the most appropriate addition to his therapy?

explanation.summary: High-risk ET (age over 60 or prior thrombosis, or inadequate aspirin control) warrants cytoreduction with hydroxyurea.
explanation.whyCorrect: If aspirin alone does not provide adequate control, or if the patient is high-risk (over 60 years old or a history of thrombosis), then cytoreductive therapy with hydroxyurea or pegylated interferon alfa is added. This patient meets both criteria, so hydroxyurea is appropriate.

whyWrongByChoice.B: Iron supplementation would not lower the platelet count and is unrelated to ET management.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Prednisone is a corticosteroid without a defined cytoreductive role in ET.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Splenectomy is not a standard treatment and can itself cause a reactive thrombocytosis.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Vitamin K reverses warfarin and does not treat the platelet overproduction of ET.

questions.stem: A patient with essential thrombocythemia reports episodes of burning pain and redness in the hands and feet. Which of the following best explains this symptom?

choices.label: B
choices.text: Deposition of monosodium urate crystals in joints

choices.label: D
choices.text: Microvascular occlusion in the distal extremities

explanation.summary: Erythromelalgia in ET results from microthrombi and sludging of platelet-rich blood occluding small vessels of the extremities.
explanation.whyCorrect: Some ET patients have episodic burning pain and redness in the distal extremities, a condition called erythromelalgia. It arises from microvascular occlusion caused by the massive number of platelets producing microthrombi and sluggish flow, and it is also seen in polycythemia vera.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Autoimmune nerve destruction describes an inflammatory neuropathy, not the platelet-driven microvascular process of ET.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Urate crystal deposition causes gout, an unrelated cause of extremity pain.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Iron deficiency does not cause the burning erythema of erythromelalgia.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Cold-induced antibody vasospasm describes cryoglobulinemia or Raynaud phenomenon, not erythromelalgia of ET.

questions.stem: A patient with essential thrombocythemia and a very high platelet count presents with mucosal bleeding. Which of the following best explains bleeding despite the elevated platelet number?

choices.label: C
choices.text: Deficiency of vitamin K-dependent clotting factors

explanation.summary: In ET, excess but poorly functioning platelets and reduced von Willebrand factor activity can paradoxically cause bleeding.
explanation.whyCorrect: The least common ET symptoms result from excessive bleeding. Too many platelets can cause increased bleeding because of decreased platelet function, sometimes from diminished function of von Willebrand factor, a platelet-associated protein necessary for forming blood clots.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Antibody-mediated platelet destruction describes immune thrombocytopenia, which lowers the platelet count rather than raising it.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Vitamin K-dependent factor deficiency reflects warfarin effect or liver disease, not the platelet dysfunction of ET.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Disseminated intravascular coagulation involves widespread clotting and factor consumption, a different process from ET.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Factor VIII deficiency is hemophilia A, a hereditary coagulation factor disorder unrelated to ET.

questions.stem: A 34-year-old woman is found to have a platelet count of 620,000/mm3 on a routine complete blood count. She also has a microcytic, hypochromic anemia and reports heavy menstrual periods. Which of the following is the most likely explanation for her elevated platelet count?

explanation.summary: Not all thrombocytosis is ET; secondary (reactive) causes such as iron deficiency anemia are far more common and must be excluded first.
explanation.whyCorrect: When the platelet count is high for reasons other than ET it is termed secondary thrombocytosis, which is much more common than ET. Reactive causes include infection, surgery, malignancy, chronic inflammation, splenectomy, and anemia, especially iron deficiency anemia. Her microcytic anemia and menorrhagia point to iron deficiency as the reactive cause.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Chronic myeloid leukemia would typically show marked leukocytosis and the Philadelphia chromosome, not an isolated iron-deficiency picture.
whyWrongByChoice.B: ET is a diagnosis of exclusion; a clear secondary cause such as iron deficiency must be ruled out before considering ET.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Polycythemia vera is defined by increased red cell mass, the opposite of this patient's anemia.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Primary myelofibrosis produces marrow fibrosis with teardrop cells and a leukoerythroblastic smear, not a simple iron-deficiency anemia.

questions.stem: A hematologist notes that essential thrombocythemia is associated with an activating JAK2 mutation in about half of cases. This association provides the rationale for using which of the following targeted agents?

explanation.summary: Because roughly 50% of ET cases carry a JAK2 mutation, the JAK inhibitor ruxolitinib may be useful.
explanation.whyCorrect: Similar to polycythemia vera, about 50% of ET cases are associated with activating mutations in the JAK2 gene. This means the JAK inhibitor ruxolitinib may be useful in ET patients, since it targets the overactive JAK/STAT signaling pathway.

whyWrongByChoice.A: All-trans retinoic acid is used in acute promyelocytic leukemia, not in ET.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Bortezomib is a proteasome inhibitor used in multiple myeloma.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Imatinib targets the BCR::ABL1 tyrosine kinase of chronic myeloid leukemia, not JAK2.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Rituximab is an anti-CD20 antibody used for B-cell disorders, not for the myeloid proliferation of ET.

questions.stem: A student asks how essential thrombocythemia differs from an acute leukemia. Which of the following best characterizes essential thrombocythemia as a myeloproliferative neoplasm?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Clonal plasma cell expansion with destructive bone lesions

choices.label: B
choices.text: Ineffective hematopoiesis producing cytopenias in all three lines

choices.label: C
choices.text: Loss of hematopoietic precursors with fatty marrow replacement

choices.label: D
choices.text: Marrow replacement by lymphoid blasts with rapid progression

choices.label: E
choices.text: Overproduction of mature myeloid cells with slower, chronic progression

explanation.summary: Myeloproliferative neoplasms such as ET produce large numbers of neoplastic but mature myeloid cells and follow a more chronic course than acute leukemias.
explanation.whyCorrect: ET belongs to the myeloproliferative neoplasms, a cluster of disorders in which the bone marrow produces large numbers of neoplastic, mature myeloid cells that spill out into the blood. Patients usually have a more chronic and slower development of disease than in the acute leukemias.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Clonal plasma cells with bone lesions describes multiple myeloma, a plasma cell rather than myeloid proliferation.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Ineffective hematopoiesis with cytopenias describes a myelodysplastic syndrome rather than the overproduction seen in ET.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Loss of precursors with a fatty marrow describes aplastic anemia, the opposite of a proliferative process.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Replacement of the marrow by blasts with rapid progression describes an acute leukemia, the entity ET is being contrasted with.

questions.stem: Essential thrombocythemia shows a characteristic age and sex distribution. Which of the following best describes it?

choices.label: A
choices.text: All age groups equally, with no sex predominance at any age

choices.label: B
choices.text: Children younger than 5 years, with a second peak in adolescents

choices.label: C
choices.text: Men in their twenties, with a second peak in elderly men

choices.label: D
choices.text: Older adults, with a second smaller peak in younger women

choices.label: E
choices.text: Pregnant women only, with resolution after delivery

explanation.summary: ET is most common in older adults but has a second, smaller peak of incidence in younger women.
explanation.whyCorrect: Essential thrombocythemia occurs most often in older adult patients, and it also has a second, smaller peak of incidence in younger women. Recognizing this bimodal pattern helps explain why a young woman with unexplained thrombocytosis may still be evaluated for ET.

whyWrongByChoice.A: The distribution is not uniform across ages; incidence is clearly concentrated in older adults.
whyWrongByChoice.B: ET is not a childhood disease; the primary peak is in older adults.
whyWrongByChoice.C: There is no described peak in young men; the second peak is in younger women.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Pregnancy does not define the disease, although pregnant patients with ET have added risk.

questions.stem: The annual incidence of essential thrombocythemia is approximately which of the following?

explanation.summary: ET occurs at roughly 1 to 2 cases per 100,000 people per year, similar to the other myeloproliferative neoplasms.
explanation.whyCorrect: The annual incidence of essential thrombocythemia is approximately 1 to 2 cases per 100,000 people, a rate similar to that of the other myeloproliferative neoplasms. This makes ET uncommon compared with the many reactive causes of a high platelet count.

whyWrongByChoice.A: An incidence of 1 to 2 per 1,000 would make ET a common disease, which it is not.
whyWrongByChoice.B: This underestimates the incidence by a factor of about ten.
whyWrongByChoice.D: This is roughly ten times higher than the reported incidence.
whyWrongByChoice.E: This rate is far above that of any myeloproliferative neoplasm.

questions.stem: A 58-year-old man has a complete blood count drawn during a preoperative evaluation and is found to have a platelet count of 780,000/mm3. He feels entirely well and has no bleeding or clotting history. This scenario illustrates which of the following about essential thrombocythemia?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Many patients are asymptomatic and found incidentally on a CBC

choices.label: B
choices.text: Most patients present with circulating blasts and marrow failure

choices.label: C
choices.text: Most patients present with jaundice and dark-colored urine

choices.label: D
choices.text: Most patients present with painful lymphadenopathy and night sweats

choices.label: E
choices.text: Most patients present with sudden pancytopenia requiring transfusion

explanation.summary: ET is frequently asymptomatic and discovered when thrombocytosis turns up on a CBC ordered for another reason.
explanation.whyCorrect: Many patients with essential thrombocythemia are asymptomatic and are diagnosed when thrombocytosis is found on a complete blood count done for other reasons. Symptoms, when they occur, fall into vascular, thrombotic, and bleeding groups.

whyWrongByChoice.B: Circulating blasts with marrow failure describes an acute leukemia, not ET at presentation.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Jaundice and dark urine point to hemolysis or liver disease, not to thrombocytosis.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Lymphadenopathy with night sweats suggests a lymphoma rather than a myeloproliferative neoplasm.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Pancytopenia is not the ET picture; the platelet count is elevated, not reduced.

questions.stem: A 54-year-old woman is being evaluated for essential thrombocythemia. Which of the following complaints would be least consistent with this diagnosis?

choices.label: E
choices.text: Swelling and pain of one calf

explanation.summary: ET produces vascular, thrombotic, and bleeding symptoms, not gastrointestinal complaints such as diarrhea.
explanation.whyCorrect: The symptoms of ET fall into several groups: nonspecific vascular symptoms such as headache, dizziness, syncope, and chest pain; erythromelalgia; large thrombus events such as stroke, deep vein thrombosis, and myocardial infarction; and, least commonly, excessive bleeding. Gastrointestinal symptoms such as diarrhea are not part of this picture.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Gum bleeding can occur because platelet function is decreased despite the high count.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Burning redness of the extremities is erythromelalgia, a recognized ET finding.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Syncope is one of the listed nonspecific vascular symptoms caused by microthrombi and sluggish flow.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Unilateral calf swelling and pain suggests deep vein thrombosis, a recognized thrombotic complication.

questions.stem: A 59-year-old man with untreated essential thrombocythemia and a platelet count of 1,200,000/mm3 develops sudden right-sided weakness and difficulty speaking. Which of the following best accounts for this event?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Hyperviscosity from an increased red cell mass

choices.label: B
choices.text: Immune complex vasculitis of the cerebral arteries

choices.label: D
choices.text: Large thrombus formation from the abundance of platelets

explanation.summary: Beyond microvascular symptoms, ET can cause large-vessel thrombotic events such as stroke, deep vein thrombosis, and myocardial infarction.
explanation.whyCorrect: Less common than the nonspecific vascular symptoms are events caused by large thrombus formation, leading to stroke, deep vein thrombosis, or myocardial infarction, all attributable to the abundance of platelets present. An acute focal neurologic deficit in an untreated ET patient fits this mechanism.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Increased red cell mass and hyperviscosity characterize polycythemia vera; in ET the platelet line dominates.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Immune complex vasculitis is not among the vascular mechanisms described in ET.
whyWrongByChoice.C: The platelet count in ET is markedly elevated, not low, so thrombocytopenic hemorrhage does not apply.
whyWrongByChoice.E: A septic embolus would require an infectious source such as endocarditis, which is not part of ET.

questions.stem: A 31-year-old woman with essential thrombocythemia is planning a pregnancy and asks about risks to the pregnancy. She is at increased risk for which of the following?

choices.label: C
choices.text: Neural tube defects in the fetus

explanation.summary: Pregnant patients with ET carry an increased risk of first trimester fetal loss.
explanation.whyCorrect: Along with the bleeding risk that follows from decreased platelet function, pregnant patients with essential thrombocythemia have an increased risk of first trimester fetal loss. This is an important counseling point for young women, who make up the second peak of ET incidence.

whyWrongByChoice.B: Gestational diabetes relates to placental hormone effects on glucose metabolism, not to platelet overproduction.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Neural tube defects are linked to folate deficiency and certain medications, not to ET.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Postpartum thyroiditis is an autoimmune thyroid disorder with no described link to ET.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Rh alloimmunization results from maternal-fetal blood group incompatibility, an unrelated mechanism.

questions.stem: Among patients with essential thrombocythemia who do have symptoms, which of the following groups of complaints is most common?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Bone pain from expansion of the marrow cavity

choices.label: C
choices.text: Fever, night sweats, and unintentional weight loss

choices.label: D
choices.text: Large-vessel events such as stroke or deep vein thrombosis

choices.label: E
choices.text: Nonspecific vascular symptoms such as headache and dizziness

explanation.summary: Nonspecific vascular symptoms from microthrombi and sludging are the most common symptomatic presentation of ET.
explanation.whyCorrect: When symptoms are present in ET they fall into groups, and the nonspecific vascular symptoms such as headache, dizziness, syncope, and chest pain are the most common. They occur because of microthrombus formation or sludginess of blood resulting from the massive number of platelets.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Bone pain from marrow expansion is not a described feature of ET.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Symptoms from excessive bleeding are described as the least common group in ET.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Fever, night sweats, and weight loss are not among the described symptom groups of ET.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Large thrombus events such as stroke and deep vein thrombosis are explicitly less common than the nonspecific vascular symptoms.

questions.stem: A woman newly diagnosed with essential thrombocythemia asks whether a chemical exposure at her workplace caused her disease. Which of the following is the most accurate response?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Benzene exposure is the established cause in most cases

choices.label: B
choices.text: Cigarette smoking is the principal identified risk factor

choices.label: C
choices.text: It is inherited in a clear pattern from an affected parent

choices.label: D
choices.text: No environmental risk factor is established; gene mutations cause it

choices.label: E
choices.text: Prior therapeutic radiation accounts for the majority of cases

explanation.summary: No environmental risk factors for ET have been clearly identified; the disease is caused by acquired or hereditary gene mutations.
explanation.whyCorrect: No environmental risk factors for ET have been clearly identified. The disease is caused by acquired or hereditary gene mutations, most commonly activating mutations of JAK2 and, in JAK2-negative cases, CALR or MPL.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Benzene is not identified as a risk factor for ET in this discussion of its causes.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Smoking has not been identified as an ET risk factor.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Most cases are sporadic; families with increased incidence exist but are the exception rather than the rule.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Prior radiation is not listed among established causes of ET.

questions.stem: Mutations in the MPL gene are found in 5% to 10% of patients with essential thrombocythemia. MPL encodes which of the following?

choices.label: A
choices.text: A DNA mismatch repair enzyme in dividing cells

choices.label: B
choices.text: A fusion kinase produced by a chromosomal translocation

choices.label: C
choices.text: A tyrosine kinase that phosphorylates JAK/STAT proteins

choices.label: D
choices.text: An erythropoietin receptor on red cell precursors

explanation.summary: MPL codes for the thrombopoietin receptor and is mutated in 5% to 10% of ET cases.
explanation.whyCorrect: In JAK2-negative ET there can be other mutations, including calreticulin (CALR) in about 30% of cases and MPL, the thrombopoietin receptor, in 5% to 10% of cases. Because thrombopoietin drives megakaryocyte and platelet production, an activating receptor mutation produces the same end result of excess platelets.

whyWrongByChoice.A: MPL has no role as a DNA repair enzyme.
whyWrongByChoice.B: A fusion kinase from a translocation describes BCR::ABL1 of chronic myeloid leukemia.
whyWrongByChoice.C: The tyrosine kinase acting through JAK/STAT is the product of JAK2, the mutation found in about half of ET cases.
whyWrongByChoice.D: The erythropoietin receptor drives red cell production and is not the MPL product.

questions.stem: Genetic testing in a patient with essential thrombocythemia who is JAK2 negative reveals a calreticulin mutation. CALR mutations are present in approximately what proportion of essential thrombocythemia cases?

explanation.summary: CALR mutations account for roughly 30% of ET cases, the second most frequent mutation after JAK2.
explanation.whyCorrect: Approximately 50% of ET cases carry an activating JAK2 mutation. Among JAK2-negative cases, other mutations are found, including calreticulin (CALR) in about 30% of cases and MPL in 5% to 10%.

whyWrongByChoice.A: CALR is a common finding in ET, not a rare one.
whyWrongByChoice.B: About 5% to 10% is the proportion attributed to MPL mutations, not CALR.
whyWrongByChoice.D: About 50% is the proportion of cases associated with JAK2 mutations.
whyWrongByChoice.E: No single mutation accounts for three-quarters of ET cases.

questions.stem: A 63-year-old man has a platelet count of 520,000/mm3, and the history does not clearly establish a reactive cause. His mean platelet volume is reported as increased. This finding most supports which of the following?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Aplastic anemia with failure of all marrow lineages

choices.label: B
choices.text: Essential thrombocythemia rather than secondary thrombocytosis

choices.label: C
choices.text: Immune thrombocytopenia with peripheral platelet destruction

choices.label: D
choices.text: Pseudothrombocytosis from red cell fragments in the sample

choices.label: E
choices.text: Reactive thrombocytosis from an occult infection

explanation.summary: An increased mean platelet volume favors ET over secondary thrombocytosis when the history is not definitive.
explanation.whyCorrect: In ET the CBC shows an increased platelet number and often anisocytosis, and increased platelet size can be quantified by ordering a mean platelet volume. Increased volume suggests ET as opposed to secondary thrombocytosis, which can be important in the differential diagnosis when the history is not definitive.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Aplastic anemia causes pancytopenia, not thrombocytosis with large platelets.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Immune thrombocytopenia lowers the platelet count rather than raising it.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Pseudothrombocytosis reflects miscounted particles, and the platelets themselves would not be genuinely enlarged.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Reactive thrombocytosis is the alternative that an increased mean platelet volume argues against.

questions.stem: On the complete blood count of a patient being evaluated for essential thrombocythemia, an increased platelet number is defined as a count greater than which of the following?

explanation.summary: Thrombocytosis is defined by a platelet count above 400,000/mm3.
explanation.whyCorrect: In the peripheral blood of a patient with ET, the CBC shows an increased platelet number, meaning greater than 400,000/mm3, and often anisocytosis of the platelets as well.

whyWrongByChoice.A: A count of 100,000/mm3 is below the normal range and would represent thrombocytopenia.
whyWrongByChoice.B: A count of 250,000/mm3 falls within the normal platelet range.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Counts above 1,000,000/mm3 occur in ET but are far above the threshold that defines thrombocytosis.
whyWrongByChoice.E: A threshold of 2,000,000/mm3 would miss nearly all patients with thrombocytosis.

questions.stem: A 70-year-old woman with thrombocytosis is undergoing evaluation for a myeloproliferative neoplasm. Besides the platelet abnormalities, which of the following additional peripheral blood findings may be seen?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Bite cells, Heinz bodies, and blister cells after oxidant exposure

choices.label: B
choices.text: Hypersegmented neutrophils, macro-ovalocytes, and megaloblastic changes

choices.label: C
choices.text: Normocytic anemia, teardrop red cells, and immature granulocytes

choices.label: D
choices.text: Rouleaux formation, plasmacytoid cells, and a blue-tinged background

choices.label: E
choices.text: Target cells, acanthocytes, and burr cells with normal platelets

explanation.summary: The smear in ET may also carry findings common to the other myeloproliferative neoplasms, such as normocytic anemia, teardrop cells, nucleated red cells, and immature granulocytes.
explanation.whyCorrect: Besides the increased platelet number and anisocytosis, there might also be findings seen in other myeloproliferative neoplasms, such as normocytic anemia, teardrop-shaped red blood cells, nucleated red blood cells, and immature granulocytes. These reflect the shared marrow biology of this group of disorders.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Bite cells and Heinz bodies follow oxidant injury in G6PD deficiency.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Hypersegmented neutrophils and macro-ovalocytes indicate megaloblastic anemia from B12 or folate deficiency.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Rouleaux with a blue-tinged background suggests a paraprotein, as in multiple myeloma.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Target cells and acanthocytes point to liver disease or hemoglobinopathies, and platelets would not be normal in ET.

questions.stem: A patient followed for many years with essential thrombocythemia now has a repeat bone marrow biopsy showing extensive fibrosis. Which of the following best describes this finding?

choices.label: A
choices.text: A finding that excludes a myeloproliferative neoplasm entirely

choices.label: B
choices.text: A late-stage change also seen in other myeloproliferative neoplasms

choices.label: C
choices.text: A marker of imminent transformation to a lymphoid malignancy

choices.label: D
choices.text: An expected consequence of long-term low-dose aspirin therapy

choices.label: E
choices.text: Evidence that the original diagnosis was actually aplastic anemia

explanation.summary: Marrow fibrosis is a recognized end-stage change in ET, paralleling the other myeloproliferative neoplasms.
explanation.whyCorrect: The marrow in ET is typically normocellular with massive megakaryocyte proliferation, but at the end stages of the disease the bone marrow can become fibrotic, similar to findings at the end stages of the other myeloproliferative neoplasms.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Fibrosis is consistent with late myeloproliferative disease rather than excluding it.
whyWrongByChoice.C: ET may evolve into other hematopoietic neoplasms such as acute myeloid leukemia, not a lymphoid malignancy.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Aspirin reduces microvascular and thrombotic complications; it does not cause marrow fibrosis.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Aplastic anemia shows a hypocellular fatty marrow with pancytopenia, not the ET course described.

questions.stem: A patient with essential thrombocythemia asks about the chance that the disease will turn into another blood cancer such as acute myeloid leukemia. Which of the following is the best estimate?

explanation.summary: About 1% to 2% of patients with ET evolve into another hematopoietic neoplasm, including acute myeloid leukemia.
explanation.whyCorrect: In 1% to 2% of patients, ET may evolve into other hematopoietic neoplasms, including acute myeloid leukemia. This transformation is less common in ET than in the other myeloproliferative neoplasms.

whyWrongByChoice.A: This figure would make transformation essentially nonexistent, understating the recognized risk.
whyWrongByChoice.C: A rate of 10% to 15% overstates the transformation risk in ET.
whyWrongByChoice.D: A quarter of patients transforming would far exceed the observed rate.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Transformation in ET is uncommon, not the usual outcome.

questions.stem: A patient with a hemolytic anemia has an automated complete blood count reporting a platelet count of 600,000/mm3. Review of the peripheral smear shows numerous red cell fragments and only a normal number of platelets. Which of the following best explains the reported count?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Essential thrombocythemia with marked platelet anisocytosis

choices.label: B
choices.text: Megakaryocyte proliferation in clusters within the marrow

choices.label: C
choices.text: Platelet clumping in the tube during specimen collection

choices.label: D
choices.text: Pseudothrombocytosis from fragments counted as platelets

choices.label: E
choices.text: Reactive thrombocytosis driven by ongoing red cell fragmentation

explanation.summary: Pseudothrombocytosis is an artifactually elevated platelet count caused by other small particles being counted as platelets.
explanation.whyCorrect: An additional cause of apparent secondary thrombocytosis is pseudothrombocytosis, in which the platelet count is artifactually elevated. This occurs when other cells are counted as platelets, such as WBC fragments in some leukemias, schistocytes in hemolytic anemias, and microspherocytes. The smear showing fragments with normal platelet numbers confirms the artifact.

whyWrongByChoice.A: ET would show a genuine increase in platelets on the smear, ranging from tiny to gigantic, not a normal platelet number.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Marrow megakaryocyte proliferation would produce a real thrombocytosis visible on the smear.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Platelet clumping makes the automated count falsely low, the opposite of the finding here.
whyWrongByChoice.E: A reactive process would raise the true platelet count, which the smear shows is not elevated.

questions.stem: Splenomegaly is found in 25% to 50% of patients with essential thrombocythemia. Which of the following best explains this finding?

choices.label: B
choices.text: Infiltration of the spleen by monoclonal plasma cells

choices.label: C
choices.text: Portal hypertension from hepatic vein thrombosis

choices.label: D
choices.text: Sequestration of antibody-coated platelets in the red pulp

choices.label: E
choices.text: Venous congestion from chronic right heart failure

explanation.summary: Splenic enlargement in ET, as in the other myeloproliferative neoplasms, is due to extramedullary hematopoiesis.
explanation.whyCorrect: On physical exam, and like the other myeloproliferative neoplasms, ET can produce splenomegaly in 25% to 50% of patients, caused by extramedullary hematopoiesis. Skin findings such as livedo reticularis and erythromelalgia may accompany it.

whyWrongByChoice.B: Plasma cell infiltration relates to plasma cell neoplasms rather than a myeloid proliferation.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Hepatic vein thrombosis with portal hypertension is not the mechanism given for splenomegaly in ET.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Splenic sequestration of antibody-coated platelets describes immune thrombocytopenia, in which the count falls.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Congestive splenomegaly from heart failure is unrelated to the marrow biology of ET.

questions.stem: A 66-year-old woman with essential thrombocythemia is noted on examination to have a mottled, net-like purple discoloration of the skin over her thighs. Which of the following best describes this finding?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Cellulitis caused by bacterial infection of the dermis

choices.label: B
choices.text: Erythromelalgia caused by distal microvascular occlusion

choices.label: C
choices.text: Livedo reticularis caused by narrowing of blood vessels

choices.label: D
choices.text: Palpable purpura caused by small-vessel vasculitis

choices.label: E
choices.text: Petechiae caused by a severely reduced platelet count

explanation.summary: Livedo reticularis, a mottled net-like purple rash from blood vessel narrowing, is a skin finding of ET.
explanation.whyCorrect: Skin findings in ET include livedo reticularis, a mottled, net-like purple rash caused by blood vessel narrowing, and erythromelalgia, which is burning and redness in the feet, hands, arms, face, and ears. The reticulated purple pattern described here is livedo reticularis.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Cellulitis produces warm, tender, confluent erythema rather than a reticulated purple discoloration.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Erythromelalgia presents as episodic burning pain and redness of the extremities, not a net-like purple pattern.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Palpable purpura indicates vasculitis, which is not among the described ET skin findings.
whyWrongByChoice.E: The platelet count in ET is markedly elevated, so petechiae from thrombocytopenia do not apply.

questions.stem: A 48-year-old man hospitalized with pneumonia has a platelet count of 560,000/mm3. He has no history of thrombosis or bleeding, and a complete blood count one year ago was normal. Which of the following is the most appropriate next step?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Begin hydroxyurea to lower the platelet count

choices.label: B
choices.text: Obtain a bone marrow biopsy to look for neoplasia

choices.label: C
choices.text: Send JAK2 mutation testing to confirm the diagnosis

choices.label: D
choices.text: Start therapeutic anticoagulation for thrombosis risk

choices.label: E
choices.text: Treat the infection and recheck the platelet count after

explanation.summary: Secondary thrombocytosis from causes such as infection is far more common than ET and must be excluded before any further workup.
explanation.whyCorrect: Not all patients with thrombocytosis have ET. When the platelet count is high for other reasons it is called secondary thrombocytosis, and causes include infections, surgery, malignancies, chronic inflammatory diseases, splenectomy, and anemia. These should be excluded by history, physical, and CBC before genetic testing or a marrow biopsy is considered.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Cytoreduction is reserved for high-risk ET, a diagnosis that has not been established here.
whyWrongByChoice.B: A bone marrow biopsy is pursued only if no secondary cause of thrombocytosis can be identified.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Genetic testing follows exclusion of secondary thrombocytosis, and an active infection explains this count.
whyWrongByChoice.D: There is no thrombosis to treat, and anticoagulation does not address a reactive platelet elevation.

questions.stem: Chronic myeloid leukemia is defined by the Philadelphia chromosome, but essential thrombocythemia has no comparable classic diagnostic feature. Which of the following best describes the practical consequence for diagnosis?

choices.label: A
choices.text: A family history of thrombocytosis is required

choices.label: B
choices.text: A positive JAK2 test alone establishes the diagnosis

choices.label: C
choices.text: ET is largely a diagnosis of exclusion

choices.label: D
choices.text: Marrow megakaryocyte clusters alone confirm the diagnosis

choices.label: E
choices.text: Only counts above 1,000,000/mm3 permit the diagnosis

explanation.summary: Because ET lacks a defining genetic lesion, the diagnosis is made only after secondary and other neoplastic causes are ruled out.
explanation.whyCorrect: Because ET does not have any classic diagnostic features, such as the Philadelphia chromosome in chronic myeloid leukemia, it becomes largely a diagnosis of exclusion. Only when secondary thrombocytosis, the other myeloproliferative neoplasms, and acute hematopoietic malignancies have been ruled out completely can a diagnosis of ET be made.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Most cases are sporadic, so a family history is not part of making the diagnosis.
whyWrongByChoice.B: JAK2 mutations occur in only about half of ET cases and are found in other myeloproliferative neoplasms, so a positive test is not sufficient on its own.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Dominant megakaryocyte proliferation suggests ET but is not always present and is not confirmatory by itself.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Thrombocytosis is defined at a count above 400,000/mm3; no million-level threshold is required.

questions.stem: Before diagnosing essential thrombocythemia, other hematopoietic neoplasms that can themselves cause thrombocytosis must be excluded. Which of the following is such a neoplasm?

explanation.summary: Other myeloid neoplasms, including primary myelofibrosis, polycythemia vera, CML, myelodysplastic syndromes, and AML, can cause thrombocytosis and must be excluded.
explanation.whyCorrect: A number of other hematopoietic neoplasias can cause thrombocytosis. These include the other myeloproliferative neoplasms (polycythemia vera, primary myelofibrosis, chronic myeloid leukemia), myelodysplastic syndromes, and acute myeloid leukemia. Most are identifiable by other CBC or clinical findings.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Hemophilia A is an inherited factor VIII deficiency and does not raise the platelet count.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Hereditary spherocytosis is an inherited red cell membrane disorder, not a hematopoietic neoplasm.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Immune thrombocytopenia is an autoimmune disorder that lowers the platelet count.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Sickle cell disease is a structural hemoglobinopathy rather than a myeloid neoplasm.

questions.stem: A 68-year-old woman with essential thrombocythemia and a prior stroke requires cytoreductive therapy, but she cannot tolerate hydroxyurea. Which of the following is the most appropriate alternative?

explanation.summary: Pegylated interferon alfa is the alternative cytoreductive agent to hydroxyurea in ET.
explanation.whyCorrect: The medications used in polycythemia vera apply in ET as well: aspirin, hydroxyurea, and pegylated interferon alfa. If aspirin alone does not provide adequate control, or the patient is high risk (over 60 years old or a history of thrombosis), cytoreductive therapy with hydroxyurea or pegylated interferon alfa is added.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Prednisone does not reduce the platelet mass in a myeloproliferative neoplasm.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Intravenous immunoglobulin is used to raise counts in immune thrombocytopenia, the opposite goal.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Transfusing platelets would add to an already excessive platelet burden.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Tissue plasminogen activator is a clot-busting drug for acute events, not a cytoreductive therapy.

questions.stem: A 64-year-old man with essential thrombocythemia taking low-dose aspirin and hydroxyurea develops a proximal deep vein thrombosis. Which of the following is the most appropriate addition to his regimen?

choices.label: C
choices.text: Platelet transfusion for the acute event

explanation.summary: Patients on the shared PV/ET regimen who develop thrombosis are prescribed an anticoagulant in addition to their existing therapy.
explanation.whyCorrect: There is no cure for ET, and medications are used to manage symptoms and complications. In patients on this regimen with a history of thrombosis, or those who develop thrombosis, an anticoagulant is prescribed in addition to aspirin and cytoreductive therapy.

whyWrongByChoice.A: All-trans retinoic acid is used in acute promyelocytic leukemia, not in ET.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Platelet transfusion would worsen an already excessive platelet count.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Ruxolitinib targets JAK2-driven signaling but is not the treatment for an acute thrombotic event.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Splenectomy is not a treatment for ET and is itself a cause of secondary thrombocytosis.

questions.stem: A 68-year-old man comes to the clinic with several months of left-sided abdominal heaviness and fatigue. His vital signs are normal, but on examination he has a massively enlarged spleen with the tip reaching the pelvic brim. His complete blood count shows an elevated white blood cell count, and the peripheral smear notes teardrop-shaped cells. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

explanation.summary: Massive splenomegaly with fatigue and teardrop cells on smear in an older patient points to primary myelofibrosis.
explanation.whyCorrect: PMF is a myeloproliferative neoplasm that typically presents in patients in their 60s or older. The spleen can become so large that its tip reaches the pelvis as it performs extramedullary hematopoiesis, and the fibrotic marrow forces red cells into teardrop shapes (dacryocytes) seen on the smear. These findings together are characteristic of PMF.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Hereditary spherocytosis shows spherocytes and hemolysis, not dacryocytes and a leukoerythroblastic picture.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Immune thrombocytopenia causes isolated low platelets and bleeding, not massive splenomegaly with teardrop cells.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Iron deficiency anemia produces microcytic anemia without massive splenomegaly or teardrop cells.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Multiple myeloma is a plasma-cell disorder presenting with bone lesions and rouleaux, not this myeloproliferative picture.

questions.stem: A hematologist explains that primary myelofibrosis differs from the other myeloproliferative neoplasms. Which of the following best describes this distinguishing feature?

choices.label: A
choices.text: No single myeloid cell line proliferates more than the others

choices.label: B
choices.text: Only lymphoid precursors proliferate and replace the marrow

choices.label: C
choices.text: Only the neutrophil series proliferates, driven by the Philadelphia chromosome

choices.label: D
choices.text: Only the red blood cell line proliferates, raising the hematocrit

choices.label: E
choices.text: Plasma cells proliferate and secrete a monoclonal protein

explanation.summary: In PMF all myeloid precursors proliferate at first, and the defining feature is progressive marrow fibrosis rather than one dominant cell line.
explanation.whyCorrect: Unlike the other MPNs, in which one cell line predominates and spills into the blood, PMF has no single myeloid line that proliferates more than the others. All myeloid precursors (erythroid, neutrophilic, and megakaryocytic) proliferate wildly at first, and then, as the name suggests, the marrow becomes fibrotic with collagen fibers.

whyWrongByChoice.B: Lymphoid precursor proliferation describes a lymphoid leukemia, not a myeloproliferative neoplasm.
whyWrongByChoice.C: A dominant neutrophil series driven by the Philadelphia chromosome describes chronic myeloid leukemia.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Predominant red cell proliferation with a high hematocrit describes polycythemia vera.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Monoclonal plasma-cell proliferation describes multiple myeloma.

questions.stem: A 67-year-old man is admitted for a lower-leg deep vein thrombosis treated with intravenous heparin. He reports a year of fatigue, bone pain, early satiety, and exertional dyspnea, and his exam shows marked splenomegaly. His hemoglobin is 10.1 g/dL, and a peripheral smear shows dacryocytes and nucleated red blood cells. Which of the following is the best next step in management?

choices.label: E
choices.text: Transfusion of packed red blood cells

explanation.summary: When splenomegaly, anemia, and dacryocytes suggest PMF, a bone marrow biopsy is needed to confirm the diagnosis.
explanation.whyCorrect: The splenomegaly, anemia, and teardrop cells on smear suggest possible primary myelofibrosis. Because the CBC and smear are suggestive but not diagnostic, a bone marrow biopsy is the next step to confirm the diagnosis by demonstrating fibrosis.

whyWrongByChoice.A: There is no indication for an abdomen and pelvis CT scan in this workup.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Discontinuing heparin is dangerous in the setting of an active deep vein thrombosis.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Myelosuppressive therapy such as ruxolitinib should not be started before a diagnosis is established.
whyWrongByChoice.E: A hemoglobin of 10.1 g/dL does not warrant transfusion of packed red blood cells.

questions.stem: A patient with newly diagnosed primary myelofibrosis undergoes molecular testing. An activating mutation in which of the following genes is most likely to be found?

explanation.summary: Approximately 50% to 60% of PMF cases carry an activating JAK2 mutation, making it the most common molecular finding.
explanation.whyCorrect: About 50% to 60% of PMF cases are associated with activating mutations in the JAK2 (Janus kinase 2) gene. This makes JAK2 the most likely mutation found and provides the rationale for using the JAK inhibitor ruxolitinib. In JAK2-negative cases, CALR (20% to 30%) or MPL (5% to 10%) mutations may be present.

whyWrongByChoice.A: BCR::ABL1 defines chronic myeloid leukemia and is absent in primary myelofibrosis.
whyWrongByChoice.B: BRCA1 mutations are associated with breast and ovarian cancer, not myeloproliferative neoplasms.
whyWrongByChoice.D: FLT3 mutations are tested in acute myeloid leukemia rather than PMF.
whyWrongByChoice.E: TP53 mutations are more relevant to acute myeloid leukemia and are not the common PMF driver.

questions.stem: A patient with primary myelofibrosis has a peripheral blood smear reviewed. Which of the following findings would be most characteristic?

choices.label: C
choices.text: Rouleaux formation of stacked red cells

choices.label: D
choices.text: Sickled red blood cells on the smear

explanation.summary: The PMF smear shows a leukoerythroblastic picture with teardrop cells (dacryocytes) and nucleated red blood cells.
explanation.whyCorrect: In PMF the peripheral smear shows teardrop-shaped RBCs and nucleated RBCs, a picture called a leukoerythroblastic reaction with left-shifted precursors. Teardrop cells form because a fibrotic marrow makes it hard for RBCs to squeeze into the blood, elongating them, and nucleated RBCs are released too early.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Hypersegmented neutrophils indicate megaloblastic anemia from B12 or folate deficiency.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Spherocytes are seen in hereditary spherocytosis and immune hemolysis, not PMF.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Rouleaux formation reflects elevated plasma proteins, as in multiple myeloma.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Sickled cells occur in sickle cell disease, an unrelated hemoglobinopathy.

questions.stem: A physician attempts to aspirate bone marrow from a patient suspected of having primary myelofibrosis, but no marrow can be drawn (a dry tap). A core biopsy is obtained instead. Which of the following findings would most likely be seen in early-stage disease?

choices.label: A
choices.text: A hypocellular, fatty marrow with no reticulin or collagen fibrosis

choices.label: B
choices.text: Absence of reticulin and collagen fibers within the marrow

choices.label: C
choices.text: Clusters of high-grade dysplastic cells replacing the normal marrow

choices.label: D
choices.text: Hypercellular marrow with an increased number of megakaryocytes

choices.label: E
choices.text: Sheets of monoclonal plasma cells replacing the marrow space

explanation.summary: Early PMF shows a hypercellular marrow with proliferation of all myeloid lines and markedly increased, clustered megakaryocytes, accompanied by fibrosis.
explanation.whyCorrect: Initially, PMF is characterized by proliferation of all myeloid cell lines, so the marrow is hypercellular and filled with neoplastic precursors. Megakaryocytes are markedly increased and clustered with atypia, and fibrosis is present. A dry tap occurs because the fibrosis makes the marrow difficult to aspirate, so a core biopsy is more helpful.

whyWrongByChoice.A: A hypocellular, fatty marrow characterizes aplastic anemia; PMF marrow contains extensive fibrosis.
whyWrongByChoice.B: There is an abundance, not an absence, of reticulin and collagen, especially as the disease progresses.
whyWrongByChoice.C: PMF does not cause dysplasia of marrow cells at any point in the disease.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Sheets of monoclonal plasma cells define multiple myeloma, not PMF.

questions.stem: In primary myelofibrosis, the extensive bone marrow fibrosis is thought to be caused by cytokines that stimulate fibroblasts. Which of the following cell types is the primary source of these fibroblast-stimulating cytokines?

explanation.summary: The fibrosis of PMF is driven by fibroblast-stimulating cytokines released by megakaryocytes.
explanation.whyCorrect: Unlike the other myeloproliferative neoplasms, the marrow in PMF develops extensive fibrosis. This fibrosis is thought to be caused by fibroblast-stimulating cytokines released by the markedly increased megakaryocytes, and the marrow eventually becomes nearly completely replaced by fibrosis.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Erythroid precursors give rise to red blood cells and are not the source of the fibrosis-driving cytokines.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Lymphocytes are not the cells responsible for releasing the fibroblast-stimulating cytokines in PMF.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Osteoclasts resorb bone and are not implicated in stimulating the marrow fibroblasts here.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Plasma cells secrete immunoglobulin and are not involved in the marrow fibrosis of PMF.

questions.stem: A patient with primary myelofibrosis develops progressively worsening anemia, recurrent infections, and bleeding episodes as the disease advances. Which of the following best explains this combination of findings?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Acute blood loss from a large gastrointestinal hemorrhage

choices.label: B
choices.text: Autoimmune antibody destruction of circulating blood cells

choices.label: C
choices.text: Bone marrow failure with low production of all blood cell lines

choices.label: D
choices.text: Dietary deficiency of vitamin B12 and folate over time

choices.label: E
choices.text: Sequestration of platelets and white cells by a normal-sized spleen

explanation.summary: As marrow fibrosis worsens, marrow failure lowers all blood counts, causing anemia, infections, and bleeding.
explanation.whyCorrect: As bone marrow fibrosis worsens, bone marrow failure with low blood cell production results. The patient develops anemia-related fatigue and breathlessness, infections from a low WBC count, and bleeding episodes from a low platelet count.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Acute gastrointestinal blood loss would not explain the low WBC count and infections.
whyWrongByChoice.B: The cytopenias of PMF result from marrow failure, not autoimmune destruction of blood cells.
whyWrongByChoice.D: B12 and folate deficiency cause megaloblastic anemia, not the marrow-failure pancytopenia of PMF.
whyWrongByChoice.E: The spleen in PMF is massively enlarged, and the mechanism is marrow failure rather than sequestration by a normal spleen.

questions.stem: A 60-year-old woman with intermediate-risk primary myelofibrosis is otherwise healthy. Her physician recommends a therapy soon after diagnosis, explaining that it is currently the only treatment with curative potential. Which of the following is being recommended?

explanation.summary: Allogeneic hematopoietic stem cell transplantation is the only therapy with curative potential for PMF.
explanation.whyCorrect: In more severe disease with poor prognosis, the nonfunctional marrow can be replaced by allogeneic hematopoietic stem cell transplantation, currently the only therapy with curative potential for PMF. In high- or intermediate-risk patients who are healthy enough, it is recommended soon after diagnosis.

whyWrongByChoice.B: An autologous transplant would reintroduce the patient's own neoplastic cells; a donor (allogeneic) source is used.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Hydroxyurea is a cytoreductive drug that controls counts but is not curative.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Ruxolitinib helps with proliferation and symptoms such as splenomegaly but is not curative.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Splenectomy is not a standard curative therapy for PMF.

questions.stem: A high-risk patient with JAK2-mutated primary myelofibrosis is not eligible for transplantation and is started on ruxolitinib. Which of the following best describes this drug's mechanism of action?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Covalently cross-links DNA strands in dividing cells to trigger apoptosis

choices.label: B
