choices.text: Daunorubicin is a BCL-2 inhibitor and cytarabine is a DNA-alkylating agent

choices.label: D
choices.text: Daunorubicin is an anthracycline and cytarabine is a pyrimidine nucleoside analog

choices.label: E
choices.text: Daunorubicin is an antimetabolite and cytarabine is an anthracycline antibiotic

explanation.summary: In the daunorubicin-cytarabine regimen, daunorubicin is an anthracycline (alkylating agent) and cytarabine is a pyrimidine nucleoside analog (antimetabolite).
explanation.whyCorrect: Daunorubicin-cytarabine is the high-potency regimen often encountered in MDS. Daunorubicin is an anthracycline, that is, an alkylating agent, while cytarabine is a pyrimidine nucleoside analog, that is, an antimetabolite. Such high-potency chemotherapy remains controversial in MDS because patients are frequently older and drug toxicity often outweighs the benefits.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Immune modulation that lowers TNF-alpha describes lenalidomide, not this regimen.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Only cytarabine is a pyrimidine nucleoside analog; daunorubicin is not.
whyWrongByChoice.C: BCL-2 inhibition describes venetoclax, and cytarabine is an antimetabolite rather than an alkylating agent.
whyWrongByChoice.E: The classes are reversed: daunorubicin is the anthracycline and cytarabine the antimetabolite.

questions.stem: An oncologist uses the Revised International Prognostic Scoring System (IPSS-R) to estimate a patient's risk category and median survival with a myelodysplastic neoplasm. Which of the following sets of variables does this system incorporate?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Cytogenetics, blast percentage, hemoglobin, platelet count, and absolute neutrophil count

choices.label: B
choices.text: Patient age, sex, body mass index, smoking history, and ECOG performance status

choices.label: C
choices.text: Prothrombin time, partial thromboplastin time, fibrinogen level, D-dimer, and bleeding time

choices.label: D
choices.text: Serum ferritin, vitamin B12, folate, copper, zinc, and thiamine levels

choices.label: E
choices.text: Spleen size, liver size, lymph node size, fever, night sweats, and weight loss

explanation.summary: The IPSS-R combines cytogenetics, blast percentage, hemoglobin, platelet count, and absolute neutrophil count to determine risk and median survival.
explanation.whyCorrect: The prognosis of MDS varies widely and depends on the bone marrow blast percentage, the specific genetic abnormality present, and peripheral blood cell counts. The Revised International Prognostic Scoring System formalizes this by incorporating cytogenetics, percentage of blasts, hemoglobin level, platelet count, and absolute neutrophil count to determine a patient's risk and median survival.

whyWrongByChoice.B: Demographic and performance variables are not the components of the IPSS-R.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Coagulation studies do not enter the IPSS-R calculation.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Nutritional levels are checked to exclude mimics of MDS, not to score prognosis.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Organ size and constitutional symptoms are staging features of lymphoma, not MDS scoring variables.

questions.stem: A first-year medical student learns that acute myeloid leukemia (AML) is a malignant proliferation of large numbers of abnormal, immature cells that arise from the precursor cells of one specific hematopoietic lineage. From which of the following lineages does AML arise?

explanation.summary: AML arises from the precursor cells of the myeloid lineage.
explanation.whyCorrect: Acute myeloid leukemia specifically arises from the precursor cells of the myeloid lineage. Genetic mutations keep these cells from growing and differentiating normally, leading to an accumulation of immature myeloid cells. Any of the myeloid cell lineages can be affected: neutrophils, platelets, erythrocytes, or monocytes.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Endothelial cells line blood vessels and are not the origin of acute myeloid leukemia.
whyWrongByChoice.B: The lymphoid lineage gives rise to lymphocytes and underlies the lymphoid neoplasms, a separate branch from AML.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Mesenchymal stromal cells give rise to adipocytes and other connective tissue, not to leukemic blasts.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Plasma cells are terminally differentiated B lymphocytes; their neoplasm is multiple myeloma.

questions.stem: A 67-year-old man comes to clinic with several weeks of worsening fatigue and bleeding gums. He appears pale, and his examination is unremarkable except for multiple bruises. A complete blood count shows low white blood cell, red blood cell, and platelet counts, and the peripheral smear shows 33% blasts, some containing needle-like cytoplasmic inclusions. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

explanation.summary: Pancytopenia with 33% blasts containing Auer rods in an older adult is diagnostic of AML.
explanation.whyCorrect: AML presents with symptoms of bone marrow failure such as anemia, bleeding and bruising from thrombocytopenia, and infection risk. A blast count of 20% or more in the marrow or blood establishes the diagnosis, and the needle-like cytoplasmic inclusions are Auer rods, which are most characteristic of AML.

whyWrongByChoice.B: Aplastic anemia produces pancytopenia with a hypocellular marrow and no excess blasts or Auer rods.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Chronic myeloid leukemia presents with a markedly elevated white blood cell count, not the pancytopenia and high blast fraction seen here.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Immune thrombocytopenic purpura causes isolated low platelets, not tri-lineage cytopenia with circulating blasts.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Myelodysplastic neoplasm requires fewer than 20% blasts; this patient has 33%, which crosses into acute leukemia.

questions.stem: A peripheral smear from a patient with acute myeloid leukemia shows blasts containing pink-red, rod-like granular structures within the cytoplasm. Which of the following best describes what these structures are composed of?

choices.label: B
choices.text: Fused lysosomes, primary granules, and enzymes

choices.label: C
choices.text: Nuclear remnants left after splenic filtration

explanation.summary: Auer rods are composed of fused lysosomes, primary granules, and enzymes and are most characteristic of AML.
explanation.whyCorrect: The pink/red rod-like granular cytoplasmic structures are Auer rods. They are composed of fused lysosomes, primary granules, and enzymes. Auer rods are most characteristic of AML, though they can occasionally be seen in some myelodysplastic and myeloproliferative disorders.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Aggregated residual ribosomes produce basophilic stippling, characteristic of lead poisoning.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Nuclear remnants after splenic filtration describe Howell-Jolly bodies, not Auer rods.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Perinuclear iron granules in mitochondria describe ring sideroblasts, a feature of myelodysplasia.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Precipitated denatured hemoglobin describes Heinz bodies, seen in oxidative hemolysis.

questions.stem: A patient is being evaluated for possible acute myeloid leukemia. The hematologist explains that, apart from certain defining genetic abnormalities, the diagnosis requires a minimum percentage of blasts on blood smear or bone marrow biopsy. Which of the following blast percentages is the required threshold to diagnose most forms of AML?

explanation.summary: AML is diagnosed when blasts or blast equivalents make up 20% or more of cells, or when specific genetic abnormalities are present.
explanation.whyCorrect: For AML to be definitively diagnosed, a blood smear or bone marrow biopsy must show either 20% or more blasts (or blast equivalents), or specific genetic abnormalities such as t(15;17), t(8;21), inv(16), or t(16;16), which are classified as AML regardless of blast percentage.

whyWrongByChoice.A: A 5% blast count is within the normal-to-mildly-elevated range and does not meet the AML threshold.
whyWrongByChoice.B: A 10% blast count is below the threshold and is more consistent with myelodysplasia.
whyWrongByChoice.C: A 15% blast count still falls short of the 20% cutoff.
whyWrongByChoice.E: A 50% blast count exceeds the threshold, but 50% is not the minimum required to diagnose AML.

questions.stem: A 40-year-old woman is diagnosed with acute promyelocytic leukemia (APL). Cytogenetic testing reveals the t(15;17) translocation that is present in almost every case. This translocation places the retinoic acid receptor-alpha (RARalpha) gene next to part of which of the following genes, producing a chimeric fusion protein that blocks promyelocyte maturation?

explanation.summary: In APL, the t(15;17) translocation fuses RARalpha on chromosome 17 with PML on chromosome 15 to form the PML-RARalpha fusion protein.
explanation.whyCorrect: The t(15;17) translocation is a balanced translocation in which the RARalpha gene on chromosome 17 is placed next to part of the PML gene on chromosome 15. This creates a fusion gene producing the chimeric PML-RARalpha protein, which makes the cells unresponsive to normal retinoic acid so promyelocytes do not mature, and it also increases neoplastic proliferation.

whyWrongByChoice.A: ABL1 partners with BCR in chronic myeloid leukemia, not with RARalpha.
whyWrongByChoice.B: BCL2 rearrangement, t(14;18), is associated with follicular lymphoma.
whyWrongByChoice.C: BCR fuses with ABL1 in the t(9;22) Philadelphia chromosome of chronic myeloid leukemia, not APL.
whyWrongByChoice.D: MYC translocations, such as t(8;14), are characteristic of Burkitt lymphoma.

questions.stem: A patient with acute promyelocytic leukemia is started on a medication that is a form of vitamin A. The drug binds nuclear receptors and overcomes the signaling block caused by the PML-RARalpha fusion protein, inducing the malignant promyelocytes to mature into normal cells. Which of the following medications is being described?

explanation.summary: All-trans retinoic acid (ATRA), a vitamin A derivative, induces differentiation of APL promyelocytes and overcomes the PML-RARalpha signaling block.
explanation.whyCorrect: APL can be treated with all-trans retinoic acid, a vitamin A derivative that raises trans-retinoic acid to higher-than-normal levels to overcome the signaling block. In APL cells it binds nuclear receptors, decreases proliferation, and induces differentiation, maturing primitive promyelocytes and repopulating the marrow with normal cells.

whyWrongByChoice.B: Hydroxyurea is a cytoreductive agent used for high white counts, not a differentiating agent.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Imatinib is a BCR-ABL tyrosine kinase inhibitor used in chronic myeloid leukemia, not APL.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Methotrexate is an antifolate chemotherapy agent and does not target the PML-RARalpha block.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Rituximab is an anti-CD20 antibody for B-cell disorders and has no role in APL differentiation.

questions.stem: A hospitalized patient with acute myeloid leukemia and profound neutropenia develops a high fever. The team is concerned because this complication is the most common cause of death in AML. Which of the following complications are they most likely concerned about?

explanation.summary: Sepsis, often from atypical bacteria or fungi, is the leading cause of death in AML.
explanation.whyCorrect: The leading cause of death in AML is sepsis, often caused by atypical bacteria or fungi that generally affect immunocompromised patients. This occurs because the circulating blasts lack normal immunologic protective function, leaving the patient with little natural defense against pathogens.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Disseminated intravascular coagulation is a serious complication, especially in APL, but is not the most common cause of death in AML overall.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Hypercholesterolemia is an adverse effect of ATRA therapy, not a leading cause of death in AML.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Leukostasis affects a subset of patients with hyperleukocytosis and is not the most common cause of death.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Tumor lysis syndrome is a metabolic complication that is preventable and is not the leading cause of death.

questions.stem: A patient with acute promyelocytic leukemia develops widespread bleeding and clotting shortly after starting chemotherapy, and laboratory studies confirm disseminated intravascular coagulation (DIC). Which of the following best explains why DIC occurs so frequently in this setting?

choices.label: A
choices.text: An inherited deficiency of factor VIII impairs clotting

choices.label: C
choices.text: Dying blasts release procoagulant granule contents

choices.label: D
choices.text: The spleen sequesters and destroys platelets

choices.label: E
choices.text: Vitamin K deficiency reduces synthesis of clotting factors

explanation.summary: In APL, DIC arises because dying blasts release granule contents and tissue factor that initiate the coagulation cascade and consume clotting factors and platelets.
explanation.whyCorrect: The Auer rods within the blasts contain substances that can easily initiate a coagulation cascade, and the blasts also secrete tissue factor, the primary initiator of the extrinsic clotting pathway. When tumor cells undergo cell death, especially during chemotherapy, they release their granules, consuming clotting factors and platelets and leaving the patient at risk of hemorrhage.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Factor VIII deficiency is the inherited disorder hemophilia A, unrelated to APL.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Antiplatelet autoantibodies cause immune thrombocytopenia, not the consumptive coagulopathy of DIC in APL.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Splenic sequestration causes thrombocytopenia in hypersplenism, not the widespread clotting of DIC.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Vitamin K deficiency impairs factor synthesis but is not the mechanism driving DIC in APL.

questions.stem: A patient with acute myeloid leukemia is about to begin induction chemotherapy. IV hydration and allopurinol are started to prevent tumor lysis syndrome, but the uric acid level is already markedly elevated. A recombinant urate-oxidase enzyme that converts uric acid to allantoin, an inactive and soluble metabolite, is added. Which of the following medications is being described?

explanation.summary: Rasburicase is a recombinant urate-oxidase enzyme that converts existing uric acid to allantoin and is used when uric acid is already elevated in tumor lysis syndrome.
explanation.whyCorrect: IV hydration and allopurinol are used to prevent tumor lysis syndrome, but if the uric acid level is already elevated, rasburicase is administered. Rasburicase is a recombinant urate-oxidase enzyme that converts uric acid to allantoin, an inactive and soluble metabolite of uric acid.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Allopurinol blocks the production of new uric acid but does not eliminate uric acid that is already elevated.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Colchicine treats acute gout flares by inhibiting neutrophil activity and does not lower uric acid.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Febuxostat is a xanthine oxidase inhibitor that, like allopurinol, prevents production rather than degrading existing uric acid.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Probenecid is a uricosuric that increases renal uric acid excretion but does not convert uric acid to allantoin.

questions.stem: Genetic testing on a patient newly diagnosed with acute myeloid leukemia reveals a FLT3 mutation. Which of the following best describes the significance of this finding?

choices.label: A
choices.text: It confers a favorable prognosis and requires no additional therapy

choices.label: B
choices.text: It confers a generally unfavorable prognosis

choices.label: C
choices.text: It defines core binding factor leukemia and carries a favorable prognosis

choices.label: D
choices.text: It is an incidental finding with no prognostic or therapeutic relevance

choices.label: E
choices.text: It is diagnostic of acute promyelocytic leukemia

explanation.summary: FLT3 mutations are common in AML, carry a generally unfavorable prognosis, and can be targeted with FLT3 inhibitors such as midostaurin.
explanation.whyCorrect: FLT3 mutations are common in AML and are associated with a generally unfavorable prognosis. Importantly, patients with this mutation can be given targeted therapy in the form of FLT3 inhibitors, such as midostaurin.

whyWrongByChoice.A: FLT3 mutations are unfavorable, not favorable, and do prompt targeted therapy.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Core binding factor leukemias are defined by t(8;21) or inv(16), not by FLT3 mutations.
whyWrongByChoice.D: FLT3 status is prognostically important and therapeutically actionable, so it is not incidental.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Acute promyelocytic leukemia is defined by the t(15;17) translocation, not by FLT3 mutation.

questions.stem: A 55-year-old man with newly diagnosed acute myeloid leukemia (not the promyelocytic subtype) is started on induction chemotherapy. The regimen consists of a pyrimidine nucleoside analog given as a continuous IV infusion over 7 days plus an anthracycline given for 3 days. Which of the following pairs of drugs constitutes this classic 7+3 regimen?

choices.label: A
choices.text: All-trans retinoic acid and arsenic trioxide

explanation.summary: The 7+3 induction regimen for most AML combines cytarabine (a pyrimidine nucleoside analog) with daunorubicin (an anthracycline).
explanation.whyCorrect: Initial treatment to achieve remission usually includes cytarabine, a pyrimidine nucleoside analog, and daunorubicin, an anthracycline. This is called the 7+3 regimen because cytarabine is given by continuous IV infusion over 7 days while the anthracycline is given as a single daily IV dose for 3 days.

whyWrongByChoice.A: All-trans retinoic acid plus arsenic trioxide is the regimen for acute promyelocytic leukemia, not standard 7+3 induction.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Cyclophosphamide is an alkylating agent and etoposide a topoisomerase inhibitor; these are more often causes of therapy-related AML than the standard induction pair.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Imatinib and dasatinib are tyrosine kinase inhibitors for chronic myeloid leukemia.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Methotrexate and vincristine are used in lymphoid malignancy regimens, not AML induction.

questions.stem: A patient with acute myeloid leukemia has a white blood cell count over 200,000/microL and presents with confusion, gait instability, and dyspnea. The team explains that these clinical findings, thought to result from increased blood viscosity and local hypoxemia caused by the large population of blasts, distinguish this condition from an asymptomatic laboratory finding. Which of the following best describes this clinical condition?

explanation.summary: Leukostasis is the clinical syndrome of neurologic and pulmonary symptoms from increased blood viscosity in a patient with hyperleukocytosis.
explanation.whyCorrect: Leukostasis is a clinical diagnosis defined by symptoms or clinical findings associated with hyperleukocytosis. It is thought to be due to increased blood viscosity from the large population of blasts, with local hypoxemia exacerbated by the high metabolic activity of blasts and excessive cytokine production. Patients predominantly present with neurologic and pulmonary symptoms.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Differentiation syndrome is a cytokine-release reaction to ATRA or arsenic trioxide therapy, not a consequence of blast viscosity.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Disseminated intravascular coagulation is a consumptive coagulopathy, not a syndrome of neurologic and pulmonary symptoms from viscosity.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Hyperleukocytosis is the laboratory-based diagnosis of a WBC count over 100,000/microL, without the clinical symptoms that define leukostasis.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Tumor lysis syndrome is a metabolic complication of cell turnover, not a viscosity-related syndrome.

questions.stem: A hematologist reviewing epidemiologic data notes that acute myeloid leukemia is one of the most common leukemias in adults yet accounts for only about 1% of all cancers, and that it is far more common in adults than in children. Which of the following is the median age of onset of AML?

explanation.summary: AML is rare overall (about 1% of all cancers) and occurs mostly in adults, with a median age of onset of 65 years.
explanation.whyCorrect: AML is one of the most common types of leukemia in adults but is fairly rare overall, accounting for only about 1% of all cancers. It is more common in adults than children, with a median age of onset at 65 years, and its course can be devastating, with more than 11,000 deaths annually.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Onset at 25 years is well below the median; AML in young adults is the exception rather than the rule.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Forty years is younger than the reported median age of onset.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Fifty-five years approaches but still falls short of the stated median.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Eighty years is older than the median, which falls at 65 years.

questions.stem: A hematopathologist explains that the older French-American-British (FAB) system for categorizing acute myeloid leukemia has been replaced because some of the data now used routinely were not available when it was designed. Which of the following is the basis of the current World Health Organization classification of AML?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Cell morphology and cytochemical staining patterns only

choices.label: B
choices.text: Genetics, immunophenotype, morphology, and clinical features

choices.label: C
choices.text: Peripheral blast count and hemoglobin concentration only

choices.label: D
choices.text: Response to induction chemotherapy measured at day 14

choices.label: E
choices.text: Spleen size and the degree of hepatomegaly at diagnosis

explanation.summary: The WHO system classifies AML using genetics, immunophenotype, morphology, and clinical features.
explanation.whyCorrect: The classification of AML is complex. The World Health Organization system classifies AML based on genetics (for example, chromosome translocations), immunophenotype, morphology, and clinical features. These data were not all routinely available in the older French-American-British system, which has now been replaced.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Morphology and cytochemistry reflect the older approach and omit the genetic and immunophenotypic data now used.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Blast count and hemoglobin are part of the diagnostic evaluation but are not the basis of the classification system.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Treatment response informs prognosis and management, not the initial classification of the disease.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Organomegaly may be a physical finding in AML but plays no role in how cases are classified.

questions.stem: A 54-year-old woman who received busulfan as part of treatment for a previous malignancy is now diagnosed with acute myeloid leukemia. Her oncologist notes that this form of therapy-related AML shows a dose-dependent association with the number of chemotherapy cycles received. Which of the following latency periods is most typical between exposure to this class of agents and the onset of AML?

explanation.summary: Alkylating agents such as busulfan, cyclophosphamide, and ifosfamide cause therapy-related AML after a latency of 5 to 7 years, with a dose-dependent relationship to the number of chemotherapy cycles.
explanation.whyCorrect: Most cases of therapy-related AML are caused by alkylating agents and topoisomerase II inhibitors. Alkylating agents such as busulfan, cyclophosphamide, and ifosfamide can lead to AML with a latency period of 5 to 7 years, and there is a dose-dependent association between the number of chemotherapy cycles received and the development of AML.

whyWrongByChoice.A: A 1- to 3-year latency is characteristic of topoisomerase II inhibitors, not alkylating agents.
whyWrongByChoice.C: A latency of under a year is shorter than that described for either class of leukemogenic chemotherapy.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Ten to 15 years is longer than the interval described for alkylating agent exposure.
whyWrongByChoice.E: A latency of two decades is far longer than that reported for therapy-related AML.

questions.stem: A 48-year-old man develops acute myeloid leukemia 2 years after completing etoposide-containing chemotherapy for a germ cell tumor, a latency typical of topoisomerase II inhibitor-related disease. Which of the following best describes the outcome expected for this subset of AML?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Complete remission for more than 5 years in 60% to 80%

choices.label: B
choices.text: Five-year survival of 70% to 98% after treatment

choices.label: C
choices.text: Indefinite remission in about one third of patients

choices.label: D
choices.text: Outcomes equivalent to de novo AML in young adults

explanation.summary: AML arising after topoisomerase II inhibitor therapy is particularly aggressive, with overall survival rates below 10%.
explanation.whyCorrect: Topoisomerase II inhibitors, including epipodophyllotoxins such as etoposide and anthracyclines such as doxorubicin, can lead to AML more rapidly than alkylating agents, with a latency period of 1 to 3 years. This subset of AML carries a poor prognosis, with overall survival rates below 10%.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Sixty to 80% complete remission for more than 5 years describes younger patients with AML in general, not therapy-related disease.
whyWrongByChoice.B: A 5-year survival of 70% to 98% is the figure reported for acute promyelocytic leukemia after treatment.
whyWrongByChoice.C: About one third remaining in remission indefinitely applies to younger patients who achieve complete remission, not to this subset.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Patients with therapy-induced AML have a less successful outcome than those with de novo disease.

questions.stem: The parents of a 2-year-old boy with trisomy 21 ask whether his condition increases his risk of developing leukemia. Compared with children without the disorder, children with Down syndrome have approximately which of the following increases in risk of AML?

explanation.summary: Down syndrome (trisomy 21) is a constitutional chromosomal abnormality that raises the risk of AML 10- to 20-fold in children.
explanation.whyCorrect: Among the constitutional chromosomal abnormalities associated with AML, children with Down syndrome (trisomy 21) have a 10- to 20-fold increased risk of AML compared to children without the disorder.

whyWrongByChoice.B: A 100- to 200-fold increase overstates the reported risk.
whyWrongByChoice.C: A 2- to 3-fold increase understates the magnitude of the association with trisomy 21.
whyWrongByChoice.D: A 1000-fold increase is far greater than the risk described for Down syndrome.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Trisomy 21 is specifically identified as an etiologic risk factor for AML, so the risk is clearly increased.

questions.stem: Two inherited conditions associated with an increased risk of acute myeloid leukemia are Fanconi anemia and ataxia-telangiectasia. Which of the following mechanisms do these two syndromes share?

choices.label: D
choices.text: Mutation of a tumor suppressor gene

choices.label: E
choices.text: Prior exposure to an alkylating agent

explanation.summary: Fanconi anemia and ataxia-telangiectasia are DNA repair syndromes, one of the genetic syndrome categories associated with AML.
explanation.whyCorrect: Known genetic syndromes associated with a risk of AML include DNA repair syndromes such as Fanconi anemia and ataxia-telangiectasia, as well as tumor suppressor mutations. Fanconi anemia and ataxia-telangiectasia belong to the DNA repair group.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Balanced translocations such as t(15;17) are acquired somatic events in leukemic cells, not the inherited defect in these syndromes.
whyWrongByChoice.B: An extra chromosome 21 is Down syndrome, which is listed as a constitutional chromosomal abnormality rather than a DNA repair syndrome.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Tumor suppressor mutations describe the other genetic syndrome group, Li-Fraumeni syndrome and neurofibromatosis.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Alkylating agent exposure causes therapy-related AML and is unrelated to these inherited conditions.

questions.stem: A 68-year-old man has a 6-year history of primary myelofibrosis that has been followed without chemotherapy or radiation. He now presents with worsening fatigue and pallor, and a bone marrow biopsy shows 30% myeloblasts. Which of the following best explains his new diagnosis?

choices.label: A
choices.text: A leukemoid reaction to occult infection

choices.label: B
choices.text: Progression to aplastic anemia with marrow failure

choices.label: C
choices.text: Relapse of an unrecognized lymphoid neoplasm

explanation.summary: Both myeloproliferative neoplasms and myelodysplastic syndromes can transform into AML.
explanation.whyCorrect: Previous hematologic disease is a recognized etiology of AML: both myeloproliferative neoplasms and myelodysplastic syndromes can transform to AML. Primary myelofibrosis is a myeloproliferative neoplasm, and the appearance of 30% myeloblasts in the marrow indicates transformation to acute myeloid leukemia.

whyWrongByChoice.A: A leukemoid reaction reflects a reactive increase in mature white cells, not a marrow filled with 30% myeloblasts.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Aplastic anemia produces a hypocellular marrow without an excess of blasts.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Myeloblasts arise from the myeloid lineage; a lymphoid neoplasm would not produce this marrow picture.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Therapy-related AML follows alkylating agents or topoisomerase II inhibitors, and this patient received neither.

questions.stem: A 59-year-old man who worked for decades in a petrochemical plant with chronic benzene exposure and who has smoked cigarettes for 40 years is diagnosed with acute myeloid leukemia. His exposures are best classified under which of the following etiologic categories for AML?

explanation.summary: Benzene and cigarette smoke are the carcinogens named among the identified etiologies of AML.
explanation.whyCorrect: Though there is often no underlying cause for a patient's AML, several etiologies have been identified. These include carcinogens such as benzene and cigarette smoke, ionizing radiation, therapy for previous malignancy, constitutional chromosomal abnormalities, genetic syndromes, and previous hematologic diseases.

whyWrongByChoice.B: Constitutional chromosomal abnormalities refers to inherited conditions such as Down syndrome.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Ionizing radiation is a separate identified etiology; neither benzene nor cigarette smoke is a form of radiation.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Previous hematologic disease refers to myeloproliferative neoplasms and myelodysplastic syndromes transforming to AML.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Therapy for a previous malignancy refers to prior alkylating agents or topoisomerase II inhibitors.

questions.stem: A 61-year-old woman with newly diagnosed acute myeloid leukemia is found on examination to have an enlarged liver and spleen along with lymphadenopathy. Which of the following best explains these findings?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Blood cell synthesis in these organs as marrow hematopoiesis fails

choices.label: B
choices.text: Consumption of clotting factors within hepatic and splenic vessels

choices.label: C
choices.text: Cytokine release triggered by rapid differentiation of blasts

choices.label: D
choices.text: Increased blood viscosity from circulating blasts obstructing hepatic flow

choices.label: E
choices.text: Platelet sequestration within the splenic red pulp cords

explanation.summary: Hepatosplenomegaly and lymphadenopathy in AML reflect blood cell production in these organs because hematopoiesis in the marrow is ineffective.
explanation.whyCorrect: Patients with AML may have adenopathy and hepatosplenomegaly, caused by the synthesis of new blood cells in these organs due to the ineffective hematopoiesis in the bone marrow, whose space is occupied by malignant cells.

whyWrongByChoice.B: Consumption of clotting factors describes disseminated intravascular coagulation, a coagulopathy rather than a cause of organomegaly.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Cytokine release during differentiation of cells describes differentiation syndrome, a toxicity of ATRA and arsenic trioxide therapy.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Increased viscosity from a large blast population produces leukostasis with neurologic and pulmonary symptoms rather than organomegaly.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Splenic sequestration of platelets is a mechanism of thrombocytopenia in hypersplenism, not the cause of organ enlargement here.

questions.stem: A 63-year-old man with acute myeloid leukemia has a markedly elevated white blood cell count consisting largely of circulating blasts, yet he develops recurrent bacterial infections and fever. Which of the following best explains his susceptibility to infection despite the high white cell count?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Autoantibodies are formed against circulating neutrophils

choices.label: B
choices.text: Blasts are rapidly removed from the circulation by the spleen

choices.label: C
choices.text: Blasts lack the functional ability of mature neutrophils

choices.label: D
choices.text: Circulating lymphocytes have been destroyed by chemotherapy

choices.label: E
choices.text: Complement proteins are consumed by the tumor cells

explanation.summary: Circulating blasts are functionally incompetent, so patients with AML are immunocompromised even when the white cell count is high.
explanation.whyCorrect: Patients with AML have frequent infections due to the lack of mature, functioning white blood cells. While there are plenty of circulating immature white cells (blasts), these lack the functional ability of mature neutrophils, leading to immunocompromise. Patients may have fever secondary to infection from neutropenia or from hypermetabolism of the tumor cells.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Antineutrophil autoantibodies are not part of the pathophysiology of AML.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Splenic clearance of blasts is not the described mechanism; the problem is that the blasts present are nonfunctional.
whyWrongByChoice.D: This patient's vulnerability is present at diagnosis and is not attributed to chemotherapy-induced lymphocyte loss.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Complement consumption by tumor cells is not a described mechanism of immunocompromise in AML.

questions.stem: A peripheral blood smear from a patient with acute myeloid leukemia shows numerous abundant myeloblasts alongside a few normal lymphocytes. Compared with the lymphocytes, which of the following sets of features best characterizes the myeloblasts?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Larger size, higher N:C ratio, fine chromatin, prominent nucleoli

choices.label: B
choices.text: Larger size, lower N:C ratio, coarse chromatin, absent nucleoli

choices.label: C
choices.text: Larger size, segmented nuclei, coarse chromatin, pale cytoplasm

choices.label: D
choices.text: Smaller size, higher N:C ratio, coarse chromatin, absent nucleoli

choices.label: E
choices.text: Smaller size, lower N:C ratio, fine chromatin, prominent nucleoli

explanation.summary: Myeloblasts are larger than lymphocytes and have a high nuclear-to-cytoplasmic ratio, fine smooth chromatin, and visible nucleoli.
explanation.whyCorrect: Blasts are the earliest and most immature precursor cells of a lineage. Compared to normal lymphocytes, the myeloblasts in AML are larger, with higher nuclear-to-cytoplasmic ratios (a relatively large nucleus and a small amount of cytoplasm), finer chromatin, and prominent nucleoli.

whyWrongByChoice.B: A low nuclear-to-cytoplasmic ratio with coarse chromatin describes more mature cells, not blasts.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Segmented nuclei characterize mature neutrophils, which are differentiated cells rather than blasts.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Coarse chromatin without nucleoli is a feature of mature cells, and myeloblasts are larger than lymphocytes, not smaller.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Fine chromatin and prominent nucleoli are correct for blasts, but blasts are larger with a high nuclear-to-cytoplasmic ratio.

questions.stem: Acute promyelocytic leukemia is described as a distinctive subtype of acute myeloid leukemia whose genetics and molecular mechanism are the best defined. Approximately what proportion of all AML cases does APL represent?

explanation.summary: APL accounts for 5% to 15% of all AML cases.
explanation.whyCorrect: The genetics are best defined for acute promyelocytic leukemia, a distinctive subtype of AML that accounts for 5% to 15% of all AML cases. A t(15;17) translocation is present in almost every case of APL.

whyWrongByChoice.A: APL is uncommon but represents considerably more than 1% of AML cases.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Twenty to 30% overstates the share of AML cases that are APL.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Forty to 50% would make APL the dominant subtype, which it is not.
whyWrongByChoice.E: About 75% would describe the majority of AML, far more than APL represents.

questions.stem: Under normal conditions, retinoic acid derived from vitamin A circulates and stimulates the retinoic acid receptor-alpha (RARalpha) on the nuclear surface of myeloid cells, leading to normal DNA transcription. Which of the following is the normal consequence of activation of the RARalpha gene?

choices.label: B
choices.text: Arrest of myeloid cells at the promyelocyte stage

choices.label: C
choices.text: Fusion of lysosomes into cytoplasmic rod structures

choices.label: E
choices.text: Maturation of the cell past the promyelocyte stage

explanation.summary: Activation of RARalpha by retinoic acid promotes maturation of the myeloid cell past the promyelocyte stage.
explanation.whyCorrect: Under normal conditions, RARalpha on the nuclear surface of myeloid cells is stimulated by circulating retinoic acid derived from vitamin A, leading to normal DNA transcription and normal cell maturation. Activation of the RARalpha gene promotes maturation of the cell past the promyelocyte stage.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Apoptosis of mature neutrophils is not the described effect of retinoic acid receptor signaling.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Arrest at the promyelocyte stage is what happens when the PML-RARalpha fusion protein makes the genes unresponsive to retinoic acid.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Fused lysosomes, primary granules, and enzymes form Auer rods, which are unrelated to RARalpha signaling.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Increased neoplastic proliferation is an effect of the abnormal PML-RARalpha product, not of normal receptor activation.

questions.stem: Cytogenetic testing on a 44-year-old man with newly diagnosed acute myeloid leukemia shows inv(16). His oncologist explains that this places his leukemia among the 'core binding factor' leukemias, which carry a relatively favorable prognosis. Along with inv(16), which of the following abnormalities defines this group?

explanation.summary: AML with t(8;21) and AML with inv(16) are the core binding factor leukemias and have a relatively favorable prognosis.
explanation.whyCorrect: Among the other mutations and alterations in AML, AML with t(8;21) and AML with inv(16) are known as the core binding factor leukemias and have a relatively favorable prognosis.

whyWrongByChoice.A: FLT3 mutations carry a generally unfavorable prognosis and do not define core binding factor leukemia.
whyWrongByChoice.C: The t(9;22) translocation is the Philadelphia chromosome of chronic myeloid leukemia.
whyWrongByChoice.D: The t(14;18) translocation is associated with follicular lymphoma, a lymphoid neoplasm.
whyWrongByChoice.E: The t(15;17) translocation defines acute promyelocytic leukemia, a separate distinctive subtype.

questions.stem: Molecular testing on a 57-year-old woman with newly diagnosed acute myeloid leukemia identifies an NPM1 mutation, and no other mutations are detected. Which of the following best describes the prognostic significance of this finding?

choices.label: B
choices.text: No prognostic or diagnostic significance in AML

choices.label: C
choices.text: Prognosis comparable to that of therapy-related AML

choices.label: E
choices.text: Unfavorable prognosis, warranting targeted inhibitor therapy

explanation.summary: An isolated NPM1 mutation in AML carries a relatively favorable prognosis.
explanation.whyCorrect: AML with NPM1 mutations has a relatively favorable prognosis in the absence of other mutations. This contrasts with FLT3 mutations, which are common in AML and are associated with a generally unfavorable prognosis.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Acute promyelocytic leukemia is defined by t(15;17), not by an NPM1 mutation.
whyWrongByChoice.B: NPM1 status is specifically noted as prognostically informative in AML.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Therapy-related AML is aggressive with poor survival, unlike isolated NPM1-mutated disease.
whyWrongByChoice.E: An unfavorable prognosis with targeted inhibitor therapy describes FLT3-mutated AML treated with FLT3 inhibitors such as midostaurin.

questions.stem: A 50-year-old man presents with fatigue and easy bruising. A bone marrow biopsy shows 12% blasts, and cytogenetic testing identifies inv(16). He is diagnosed with acute myeloid leukemia. Which of the following best explains why he meets criteria for AML despite a blast count below the usual threshold?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Certain genetic abnormalities classify a case as AML at any blast percentage

choices.label: B
choices.text: Cytopenias with bruising alone are sufficient to diagnose AML

choices.label: C
choices.text: Inversions require only 5% blasts while translocations require 20%

choices.label: D
choices.text: Peripheral blood blasts are added to the marrow blast percentage

choices.label: E
choices.text: The blast threshold falls to 10% whenever Auer rods are absent

explanation.summary: Specific genetic abnormalities, including t(15;17), t(8;21), inv(16), and t(16;16), are classified as AML regardless of blast percentage.
explanation.whyCorrect: For AML to be definitively diagnosed, a blood smear or bone marrow biopsy must show either 20% or more blasts or blast equivalents, OR specific genetic abnormalities including t(15;17), t(8;21), inv(16), and t(16;16). These abnormalities are classified as AML regardless of blast percentage, so this patient's inv(16) establishes the diagnosis at 12% blasts.

whyWrongByChoice.B: Cytopenias and bruising are clinical findings; diagnosis requires pathologic or genetic criteria.
whyWrongByChoice.C: The listed genetic abnormalities all bypass the blast threshold; no separate percentage applies to inversions.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Blast percentages from blood and marrow are not summed; either specimen may show 20% or more blasts.
whyWrongByChoice.E: There is no alternative 10% threshold based on the presence or absence of Auer rods.

questions.stem: A 60-year-old woman with acute myeloid leukemia begins induction chemotherapy. Two days later, laboratory studies show rising uric acid, potassium, and phosphorus levels, and tumor lysis syndrome is diagnosed. Which of the following additional electrolyte abnormalities is most likely in this syndrome?

explanation.summary: Tumor lysis syndrome comprises hyperuricemia, hypocalcemia, hyper- or hypokalemia, and hyperphosphatemia.
explanation.whyCorrect: Patients with AML are at risk of certain electrolyte abnormalities leading to hyperuricemia, hypocalcemia, hyper- or hypokalemia, and hyperphosphatemia; this phenomenon is collectively termed tumor lysis syndrome. Calcium falls rather than rises in this syndrome.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Calcium is low, not high, in tumor lysis syndrome.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Sodium disturbance is not among the electrolyte abnormalities that define tumor lysis syndrome.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Phosphate rises in tumor lysis syndrome, consistent with this patient's elevated phosphorus.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Uric acid increases in tumor lysis syndrome, which is why allopurinol and rasburicase are used.

questions.stem: A 70-year-old man with newly diagnosed acute myeloid leukemia has a complete blood count showing anemia, thrombocytopenia, and a white blood cell count of 3,200/microL with circulating blasts. Which of the following best describes the white blood cell count expected in AML?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Always decreased because of bone marrow failure

choices.label: C
choices.text: Elevated only in acute promyelocytic leukemia

choices.label: D
choices.text: Normal in all patients until blasts exceed 50%

choices.label: E
choices.text: Often elevated, but it may be normal or decreased

explanation.summary: The CBC in AML often shows leukocytosis from circulating blasts, but the white count can also be normal or decreased.
explanation.whyCorrect: The complete blood count will often show leukocytosis due to large numbers of circulating blasts, although the WBC count can be normal or sometimes decreased. Mature RBCs, platelets, and neutrophils are decreased because the marrow is occupied by blast formation.

whyWrongByChoice.A: The white count is frequently elevated by circulating blasts rather than uniformly low.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Only up to 20% of patients with AML have hyperleukocytosis, defined as a WBC count over 100,000/microL.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Leukocytosis from circulating blasts is not restricted to the promyelocytic subtype.
whyWrongByChoice.D: There is no blast percentage below which the white count is necessarily normal.

questions.stem: A 55-year-old man with acute myeloid leukemia has a white blood cell count of 180,000/microL with confusion and dyspnea. Because of severe comorbidities, he cannot promptly receive intensive induction chemotherapy. Which of the following is the most appropriate next step in management?

choices.label: D
choices.text: Transfusion of packed red blood cells

explanation.summary: When a patient with hyperleukocytosis cannot promptly receive intensive induction chemotherapy, leukapheresis plus hydroxyurea is administered.
explanation.whyCorrect: Generally, AML patients with hyperleukocytosis, with or without leukostatic symptoms, should receive prompt cytoreductive chemotherapy. If patients are not able to promptly receive intensive induction chemotherapy, leukapheresis plus hydroxyurea is administered.

whyWrongByChoice.A: All-trans retinoic acid is used for acute promyelocytic leukemia, not as cytoreduction in other forms of AML.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Observation is inappropriate because symptomatic leukostasis requires prompt cytoreduction.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Red cell transfusion adds to blood viscosity and does not reduce the blast burden driving his symptoms.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Platelet transfusion addresses bleeding risk but does nothing to lower the white cell count.

questions.stem: Flow cytometry is performed on the marrow aspirate of a patient with suspected acute leukemia to determine blast lineage. Which of the following markers in the panel indicates cellular immaturity rather than myeloid lineage?

explanation.summary: In the AML flow cytometry panel, CD34 marks immaturity while CD13, CD33, and myeloperoxidase mark myeloid lineage.
explanation.whyCorrect: Flow cytometry is performed to determine blast lineage. Common markers in AML include both markers of immaturity (CD34) and markers of myeloid lineage (CD13, CD33, and myeloperoxidase/MPO).

whyWrongByChoice.A: CD13 is one of the myeloid lineage markers, not a marker of immaturity.
whyWrongByChoice.B: CD19 is not among the markers listed for the AML panel.
whyWrongByChoice.C: CD33 is likewise a myeloid lineage marker in the AML panel.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Myeloperoxidase identifies myeloid lineage rather than the maturation stage of the cell.

questions.stem: A 39-year-old woman with acute promyelocytic leukemia is started on all-trans retinoic acid. Six days later she develops fever, dyspnea, hypoxia, and hypotension. Her oncologist attributes this to a systemic immune response caused by rapid release of cytokines and other inflammatory mediators, one of the drug's boxed warnings. Which of the following is the most likely cause?

explanation.summary: Differentiation syndrome is a boxed-warning toxicity of ATRA caused by rapid cytokine release as cells differentiate.
explanation.whyCorrect: ATRA carries boxed warnings for embryo-fetal toxicity and differentiation syndrome, which is a systemic immune response caused by rapid release of cytokines and other inflammatory mediators during differentiation of cells. Other significant adverse effects of ATRA include hepatotoxicity, leukocytosis, hypercholesterolemia or hypertriglyceridemia, and thrombosis.

whyWrongByChoice.B: DIC is a consumptive coagulopathy of APL itself, marked by bleeding and clotting rather than this inflammatory picture.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Embryo-fetal toxicity is the other ATRA boxed warning but concerns a developing fetus, not this presentation.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Leukostasis results from increased blood viscosity in hyperleukocytosis and is not a boxed warning of ATRA.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Tumor lysis syndrome is a metabolic derangement with hyperuricemia and electrolyte abnormalities, not a cytokine-driven systemic reaction.

questions.stem: A patient with acute promyelocytic leukemia is treated with combination therapy that includes arsenic trioxide along with all-trans retinoic acid. Which of the following best describes how arsenic trioxide acts on APL cells?

choices.label: A
choices.text: It binds nuclear receptors to induce cell differentiation

choices.label: B
choices.text: It blocks uric acid production during cell turnover

choices.label: C
choices.text: It cross-links DNA strands within dividing cells

choices.label: D
choices.text: It induces apoptosis and degrades the PML-RARalpha protein

choices.label: E
choices.text: It inhibits a constitutively active tyrosine kinase

explanation.summary: Arsenic trioxide induces apoptosis in APL cells and damages or degrades the PML-RARalpha fusion protein.
explanation.whyCorrect: Arsenic trioxide, also a vitamin A derivative, induces apoptosis in APL cells via morphological changes and DNA fragmentation. It also damages or degrades the fusion protein promyelocytic leukemia-retinoic acid receptor alpha (PML-RARalpha).

whyWrongByChoice.A: Binding nuclear receptors to decrease proliferation and induce differentiation describes ATRA, the partner drug in this regimen.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Blocking uric acid production is the action of allopurinol, used to prevent tumor lysis syndrome.
whyWrongByChoice.C: DNA cross-linking is the mechanism of alkylating agents, which are a cause of therapy-related AML.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Tyrosine kinase inhibition describes targeted agents such as FLT3 inhibitors, not arsenic trioxide.

questions.stem: A 41-year-old woman with acute myeloid leukemia achieves complete remission after induction chemotherapy. Her oncologist recommends hematopoietic stem cell transplantation and reviews its risks, including severe infections. Which of the following best describes the role of transplantation in AML?

choices.label: A
choices.text: It is given before induction to reduce the blast burden

choices.label: B
choices.text: It is reserved for acute promyelocytic leukemia only

choices.label: C
choices.text: It reduces later relapse and is the only true cure

choices.label: D
choices.text: It removes the risk of severe infection after treatment

choices.label: E
choices.text: It replaces the need for induction chemotherapy

explanation.summary: HSCT is used after remission is achieved with chemotherapy; it lowers relapse rates and is the only way to cure AML entirely.
explanation.whyCorrect: Hematopoietic stem cell transplantation is often used after first achieving disease remission using chemotherapy. HSCT reduces the rate of later relapse but can cause complications such as severe infections; however, it remains the only way to cure the disease entirely.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Transplantation follows induction chemotherapy rather than preceding it.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Transplantation is used in selected patients across forms of AML, not only in the promyelocytic subtype.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Severe infection is one of the recognized complications of transplantation, not something it eliminates.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Remission is first achieved with chemotherapy, so induction is not replaced by transplantation.

questions.stem: A 33-year-old woman with acute promyelocytic leukemia survives the initial period of life-threatening disseminated intravascular coagulation and completes treatment. Her white blood cell count at presentation was 6,000/mm3. Which of the following best describes her expected long-term outcome?

explanation.summary: Once the early complications of APL are survived, long-term prognosis is excellent, with 5-year survival of 70% to 98%.
explanation.whyCorrect: In APL, the initial presentation can cause life-threatening complications, especially DIC, but after this first stage the long-term prognosis with treatment is excellent: 5-year survival ranges from 70% to 98%. Survival is best in younger patients and in those with lower initial WBC counts, below 10,000/mm3, both of which apply to this patient.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Survival below 10% describes AML arising after topoisomerase II inhibitor therapy, not treated APL.
whyWrongByChoice.C: A 20% 5-year survival badly understates the outcome for APL after the initial high-risk period.
whyWrongByChoice.D: About 40% is well below the survival reported for treated APL.
whyWrongByChoice.E: About 60% still understates the excellent long-term prognosis of APL.

questions.stem: A 58-year-old man with multiple myeloma is scheduled for an autologous transplant. To increase the number of stem cells circulating in his blood before apheresis, he is given several days of a granulocyte colony-stimulating factor. On the third day he develops diffuse aching bone pain. Which of the following is the most likely explanation for his symptom?

choices.label: A
choices.text: A side effect of the G-CSF used to mobilize stem cells

choices.label: B
choices.text: Acute graft-versus-host disease from donor T cells

choices.label: C
choices.text: Progressive bone infiltration by myeloma plasma cells

choices.label: D
choices.text: Oral mucositis from the conditioning chemotherapy regimen

choices.label: E
choices.text: Reactivation of a latent viral infection such as CMV

explanation.summary: G-CSF is the most common agent used to mobilize hematopoietic stem cells, and its most common side effect is bone pain.
explanation.whyCorrect: Hematopoietic stem cells are normally present at very low levels in blood, so agents such as G-CSF (most common), IL-3, thrombopoietin, and the CXCR4 antagonist plerixafor are used to mobilize them from the marrow into the circulation. The brick states that mobilization is generally very safe, with the most common side effect being bone pain from G-CSF administration.

whyWrongByChoice.B: GVHD occurs after allogeneic transplant when donor T cells attack the recipient; this patient has not yet received an autologous graft.
whyWrongByChoice.C: The pain is temporally tied to the mobilization drug, not to disease progression; mobilization is being done as part of planned collection.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Mucositis is a toxicity of the conditioning regimen and causes mouth pain and ulcers, not diffuse bone pain, and conditioning has not occurred.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Viral reactivation causes infection during post-transplant immunosuppression, not bone pain during pre-collection mobilization.

questions.stem: A transplant team is collecting stem cells from a donor by apheresis after mobilization. Before deciding whether the collected product is adequate for engraftment, they need an objective measure of stem cell content. Which of the following is most commonly used to assess the adequacy of a peripheral blood stem cell product?

choices.label: A
choices.text: ABO antibody titer measured in the collected product

choices.label: B
choices.text: Absolute reticulocyte count of the donor after mobilization

choices.label: C
choices.text: Number of CD34+ cells per kilogram of recipient body weight

choices.label: D
choices.text: Serum G-CSF concentration measured at the time of collection

choices.label: E
choices.text: Total white blood cell count in the collected product

explanation.summary: Adequacy of a peripheral blood stem cell product is judged by CD34+ cells per kilogram of recipient body weight.
explanation.whyCorrect: CD34 is a marker of hematopoietic stem/progenitor cells. The brick states that adequacy of peripheral blood stem cell products is generally measured through the number of CD34+ cells per kilogram of recipient body weight, with greater than 2 x 10^6 CD34+ cells/kg often considered the minimum acceptable dose, although engraftment can occur with lower doses.

whyWrongByChoice.A: ABO antibody titer relates to blood-group compatibility, not to the stem cell dose in the product.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Reticulocyte count reflects red cell production and is not the standard measure of stem cell product adequacy.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Serum G-CSF level is not used to gauge the number of stem cells actually collected.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Total white cell count reflects mature leukocytes and does not specifically quantify the hematopoietic stem cells needed for engraftment.

questions.stem: A healthy 30-year-old volunteer is scheduled to donate stem cells using the traditional, historical source for transplantation. She is taken to the operating room and placed under general anesthesia. Which of the following best describes how her donation will be obtained?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Apheresis through a peripheral intravenous line

choices.label: B
choices.text: Aspiration through needles in the posterior iliac crest

choices.label: C
choices.text: Collection from placental vessels after delivery

choices.label: D
choices.text: Leukapheresis after several days of plerixafor

explanation.summary: Bone marrow, the traditional HSC source, is procured by aspiration from the posterior iliac crest under general anesthesia.
explanation.whyCorrect: The brick states that bone marrow has historically been the traditional source for HSCs, and the procurement procedure is done under general anesthesia, in which marrow is aspirated through large-bore needles inserted into both sides of the posterior iliac crest. It is generally a very safe procedure.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Apheresis through an IV line describes peripheral blood stem cell collection, which does not require general anesthesia.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Collection from placental vessels describes umbilical cord blood, obtained at the time of delivery, not from a healthy adult volunteer.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Plerixafor-based leukapheresis is a mobilization/apheresis approach for peripheral blood collection, not marrow aspiration under anesthesia.
whyWrongByChoice.E: The spleen is not a source of stem cells for transplantation; marrow is aspirated from the iliac crest.

questions.stem: A 6-year-old child of mixed ethnicity needs an allogeneic transplant but lacks an HLA-identical sibling and has no suitably matched unrelated adult donor in the registry. The team elects to use umbilical cord blood. Which of the following is a major limitation the team must anticipate with this source?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Cord blood cannot cross histocompatibility barriers

choices.label: B
choices.text: Cord blood is contraindicated in children

choices.label: C
choices.text: Inevitable severe bone pain in the recipient

choices.label: D
choices.text: The need for donor general anesthesia and marrow harvest

choices.label: E
choices.text: The small number of stem cells per unit

explanation.summary: Umbilical cord blood units contain relatively few stem cells and carry an increased infection risk from immunologically naive cells.
explanation.whyCorrect: The brick lists the major limitations of cord blood as the relatively small number of HSCs in each unit (cell dose often requires two units for an adult) and an increased risk of infections, particularly viral infections or reactivation, given the naive immunologic nature of the stem cells.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Cord blood cells are immunologically naive and are actually able to cross the usual histocompatibility barriers of conventional transplants, an advantage rather than a limitation.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Cord blood is a valuable option in patients, including children, who lack matched donors; it is not contraindicated in children.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Bone pain is a side effect of G-CSF mobilization in peripheral blood donors, not a limitation of cord blood.
whyWrongByChoice.D: General anesthesia and marrow harvest describe bone marrow donation; cord blood is collected from the placenta at delivery.

questions.stem: A 42-year-old woman with primary myelofibrosis undergoes a transplant using hematopoietic stem cells donated by her HLA-matched brother. Which of the following best classifies this type of transplant?

explanation.summary: Receiving stem cells from another person, related or unrelated, defines an allogeneic transplant.
explanation.whyCorrect: The brick defines allogeneic stem cell transplant as the infusion of stem cells from a related or unrelated donor. Because the cells come from her brother rather than herself, this is an allogeneic transplant, which additionally offers a graft-versus-tumor effect.

whyWrongByChoice.B: Autologous rescue again refers to reinfusing the patient's own cells after high-dose chemotherapy, which is not the case here.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Autologous transplant uses the patient's own stem cells, not a donor's.
whyWrongByChoice.D: A syngeneic autograft is a contradictory term; the cells here are from a sibling donor, making the transplant allogeneic.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Xenogeneic (between species) transplantation is not a category described for HSCT in this brick.

questions.stem: A hematologist explains that one reason to choose an allogeneic transplant over an autologous transplant for a patient with acute myeloid leukemia is that the allogeneic graft provides an additional anti-cancer mechanism beyond conditioning chemotherapy. Which of the following describes this additional mechanism?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Direct cytotoxicity of mobilizing agents on tumor cells

choices.label: B
choices.text: Enhanced red cell production correcting anemia

choices.label: C
choices.text: Neutralization of tumor cells by the patient's own reinfused cells

choices.label: D
choices.text: Replacement of destroyed small bile ducts in the liver

choices.label: E
choices.text: The donor's immune system attacking residual tumor cells

explanation.summary: Allogeneic transplant adds a graft-versus-tumor effect, in which donor immune cells attack residual cancer.
explanation.whyCorrect: The brick states that allogeneic transplant results in two mechanisms for fighting cancer: the cytotoxic effects of the preparative (conditioning) chemotherapy, and the donor's immune system attacking residual cancer cells, known as the graft-versus-tumor effect. HSCT also provides an immunologic graft-versus-tumor effect overall.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Mobilizing agents such as G-CSF move stem cells into blood for collection; they are not described as directly cytotoxic to tumor cells.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Improving anemia through red cell production is a general marrow function, not the distinguishing anti-cancer mechanism of allogeneic grafts.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Reinfusing the patient's own cells describes autologous transplant, which lacks the donor immune graft-versus-tumor effect.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Destruction of small bile ducts is a feature of GVHD injury, not an anti-cancer mechanism.

questions.stem: In the days leading up to Day 0 of a transplant, a patient receives a combination of chemotherapy drugs, in this case together with total body irradiation. Which of the following best states the goals of this conditioning regimen?

choices.label: A
choices.text: To establish the patient's ABO blood group and HLA tissue type

choices.label: B
choices.text: To immunosuppress the recipient and eliminate as much tumor as possible

choices.label: C
choices.text: To provide long-term antimicrobial and antifungal prophylaxis

choices.label: D
choices.text: To stimulate the recipient's own marrow to overproduce and release stem cells

choices.label: E
choices.text: To treat established graft-versus-host disease of the skin and gut

explanation.summary: The pretransplant conditioning regimen aims to immunosuppress the recipient and eliminate as much tumor as possible.
explanation.whyCorrect: The brick explains that in the days prior to transplant the patient receives conditioning chemotherapy (the conditioning regimen), generally a combination of chemotherapy drugs with or without radiation, with the goal to immunosuppress the recipient and eliminate as much tumor as possible.

whyWrongByChoice.A: ABO and HLA typing is part of the pretransplant evaluation done earlier, not the purpose of conditioning chemotherapy.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Antimicrobial prophylaxis addresses infection risk during myelosuppression and is not the goal of the conditioning regimen.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Conditioning is myeloablative (wipes out the marrow); it does not stimulate the recipient marrow to overproduce cells.
whyWrongByChoice.E: GVHD is prevented and treated with immunosuppressive drugs after transplant; conditioning is given before the graft.

questions.stem: Two weeks after an allogeneic transplant, a patient's blood counts begin to recover. The team documents that the absolute neutrophil count has exceeded 0.5 x 10^9/L on the first of three consecutive days. This finding is used to define which of the following?

explanation.summary: Myeloid engraftment is defined as the first of 3 consecutive days with an ANC above 0.5 x 10^9/L.
explanation.whyCorrect: The brick defines myeloid engraftment as the first of 3 consecutive days in which the absolute neutrophil count exceeds 0.5 x 10^9/L, typically occurring within 21 days of the graft infusion, marking that donor cells have begun producing new blood cells.

whyWrongByChoice.A: GVHD is defined by donor T cells attacking recipient tissue, presenting with rash, diarrhea, and organ dysfunction, not by a neutrophil threshold.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Mucositis is a mucosal toxicity of conditioning and is unrelated to the neutrophil count criterion for engraftment.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Primary graft failure is the failure to achieve threshold counts beyond day 28; here counts are recovering, indicating successful engraftment.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Secondary graft failure occurs when a patient who initially engrafted later loses graft function in at least two cell lines; this patient is engrafting, not losing function.

questions.stem: A patient who successfully met threshold blood counts one month after transplant later develops declining function in both the red cell and platelet lines without recovery. Which of the following best describes this complication?

explanation.summary: Loss of graft function in at least two cell lines after initial engraftment defines secondary graft failure.
explanation.whyCorrect: The brick states that secondary (late) graft failure occurs in patients who initially meet threshold counts for engraftment but subsequently lose graft function in at least two cell lines, as seen here with declining red cell and platelet lineages after successful early engraftment.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Oral mucositis is a mouth toxicity of conditioning, not a description of loss of graft function.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Primary (early) graft failure is failure to achieve threshold counts at any point beyond 28 days after HSCT; this patient did initially reach threshold counts.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Pulmonary toxicity is a regimen-related organ complication and does not describe the marrow-lineage failure defined here.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Successful engraftment would show sustained counts, not a subsequent loss of function in multiple cell lines.

questions.stem: About one week after high-intensity conditioning and stem cell infusion, a transplant patient develops a dry, sore mouth with painful ulcers, making eating difficult. This is the most common regimen-related organ toxicity in transplant recipients. Which of the following is the most appropriate description of its management?

choices.label: A
choices.text: High-dose G-CSF to mobilize additional stem cells

choices.label: B
choices.text: Immediate systemic immunosuppression to halt donor T cells

choices.label: C
choices.text: Supportive care with saline and antimicrobial rinses

explanation.summary: Oral mucositis is managed supportively with rinses, cryotherapy, pain control, and parenteral nutrition when needed.
explanation.whyCorrect: The brick notes that oral mucositis, inflammation of the mouth, occurs in a majority of transplant recipients (70-87% in one study) due to the high-intensity conditioning regimen, and that current management is supportive: rinsing with saline solutions and antimicrobials, cryotherapy, pain control, and possible parenteral nutrition.

whyWrongByChoice.A: G-CSF mobilizes stem cells before collection and is not a treatment for oral mucositis.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Immunosuppression is used to prevent and treat GVHD, not the mucosal toxicity caused directly by conditioning chemotherapy.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Mucositis is an expected self-limited toxicity of conditioning and is not an indication for re-transplantation.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Stopping antimicrobial prophylaxis would increase infection risk during immunosuppression and is not part of mucositis care.

questions.stem: Several weeks after an allogeneic transplant, a patient develops a maculopapular skin rash, diarrhea, and an enlarged liver and spleen. The team explains that donor immune cells are recognizing his tissues as foreign. Which of the following complications is most consistent with this presentation?

explanation.summary: Donor T cells attacking recipient tissue after allogeneic transplant, causing rash, diarrhea, and hepatosplenomegaly, is graft-versus-host disease.
explanation.whyCorrect: The brick describes GVHD as a potentially fatal complication that typically occurs after allogeneic transplantation, in which the donor's transplanted T cells attack the recipient's organs. Patients may present with a maculopapular rash (which can desquamate), nausea, diarrhea, vomiting, abdominal pain, and hepatosplenomegaly, often affecting the skin, liver, and gastrointestinal tract.

whyWrongByChoice.A: An ABO reaction is a blood-group compatibility issue, not the donor-T-cell-mediated multiorgan syndrome described here.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Graft failure is defined by lack of donor cell engraftment or loss of counts, and this patient received an allogeneic, not autologous, transplant.
whyWrongByChoice.C: G-CSF bone pain is a mobilization side effect and does not cause rash, diarrhea, or hepatosplenomegaly.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Oral mucositis causes mouth soreness and ulcers, not a multi-organ picture of rash, diarrhea, and organomegaly.

questions.stem: During the post-transplant recovery period, a patient is started on medication specifically intended to reduce the risk of graft failure and graft-versus-host disease. Which of the following classes of medication is being given for this purpose?

explanation.summary: Immunosuppression is given after transplant to reduce the risk of graft failure and graft-versus-host disease.
explanation.whyCorrect: The brick states that during the recovery period immunosuppression is given to reduce the risk of graft failure and graft-versus-host disease, and that immunosuppressive drugs are used to both prevent and treat GVHD.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Antimicrobial prophylaxis is given to reduce the risk of infection during myelosuppression, not to prevent graft failure or GVHD.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Conditioning chemotherapy is given before Day 0 to immunosuppress and eliminate tumor, not as post-transplant GVHD prophylaxis.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Blood transfusions are used to treat low counts (anemia and thrombocytopenia), not to prevent GVHD or graft failure.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Mobilizing agents are used before collection to move stem cells into blood, not during recovery to prevent GVHD.

questions.stem: The first documented human marrow transplantation was performed in 1939, when a patient was infused intravenously with marrow from a brother who had an identical ABO blood type. Which of the following conditions was being treated in that patient?

explanation.summary: The first documented human marrow transplant, in 1939, treated gold-induced marrow aplasia.
explanation.whyCorrect: Marrow transplantation was first documented in 1939 in a patient with gold-induced marrow aplasia, who received intravenous marrow from a brother with an identical ABO blood type. Since then the field has expanded enormously, to the point that more than 100,000 transplants were performed worldwide in 2020.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Acute myeloid leukemia is now a common allogeneic transplant indication, but it was not the condition in the first documented case.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Multiple myeloma is the most common autologous transplant indication currently, but it was not the disease in the original case.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Severe combined immunodeficiency is treated with allogeneic transplant today; it was not the indication in 1939.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Thalassemia major is among the nonmalignant diseases treated with allogeneic transplant now, not the first documented indication.

questions.stem: A student asks why hematopoietic stem cells, rather than mature circulating blood cells, must be infused to re-establish marrow function after myeloablative therapy. Which of the following properties of hematopoietic stem cells best explains their use?

choices.label: A
choices.text: They are produced only in the placenta and umbilical vessels

choices.label: B
choices.text: They are restricted to the lymphoid line of differentiation

choices.label: C
choices.text: They circulate at high levels in normal peripheral blood

choices.label: D
choices.text: They give rise to all of the cellular elements of blood

choices.label: E
choices.text: They lyse residual tumor cells without any immune assistance

explanation.summary: HSCs are used because they give rise to every cellular element of the blood and are the cells required for engraftment.
explanation.whyCorrect: Hematopoietic stem cells sit at the top of both the myeloid and lymphoid series, generating erythrocytes, granulocytes, monocytes, platelets, and lymphocytes. Because they can repopulate all lineages, they are the cells required for successful engraftment in hematopoietic transplantation, whereas mature cells cannot reconstitute marrow function.

whyWrongByChoice.A: HSCs are obtained from marrow and from mobilized peripheral blood as well as from umbilical cord blood.
whyWrongByChoice.B: HSCs are not lineage-restricted; they give rise to the myeloid series as well as the lymphoid series.
whyWrongByChoice.C: HSCs are normally present at very low levels in the blood, which is precisely why mobilizing regimens are needed before apheresis.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Killing of residual tumor is an immunologic graft-versus-tumor effect mediated by donor immune cells, not an intrinsic property of stem cells.

questions.stem: A 60-year-old man with non-Hodgkin lymphoma mobilizes poorly with several days of granulocyte colony-stimulating factor before planned apheresis. The team adds a second agent that blocks the CXCR4 receptor, releasing stem cells from the marrow into the circulation. Which of the following agents was added?

explanation.summary: Plerixafor is the CXCR4 antagonist used to mobilize hematopoietic stem cells into the blood.
explanation.whyCorrect: Typical agents used to mobilize HSCs from marrow into blood include G-CSF (most common), IL-3, thrombopoietin, and the CXCR4 antagonist plerixafor. Only plerixafor works by antagonizing CXCR4, which releases stem cells from their marrow niche so they can be collected by apheresis.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Erythropoietin drives red cell production and is not one of the agents used to mobilize stem cells.
whyWrongByChoice.B: G-CSF is the most common mobilizing agent, but it is the drug that already failed here and does not block CXCR4.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Interleukin-3 is listed among mobilizing agents but is not a CXCR4 antagonist.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Thrombopoietin can be used to mobilize stem cells, yet it acts through the thrombopoietin receptor rather than CXCR4.

questions.stem: An apheresis product collected from a donor is being assessed before infusion, and the laboratory reports the CD34+ cell content per kilogram of recipient body weight. Which of the following doses is often considered the minimum acceptable for a peripheral blood stem cell product?

explanation.summary: A threshold of greater than 2 x 10^6 CD34+ cells/kg is often taken as the minimum acceptable peripheral blood stem cell dose.
explanation.whyCorrect: Adequacy of peripheral blood stem cell products is measured as CD34+ cells per kilogram of recipient body weight, and a threshold of greater than 2 x 10^6 CD34+ cells/kg is often considered the minimum acceptable dose. Successful engraftment can still occur with lower doses, so the threshold is a target rather than an absolute requirement.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Yields of this magnitude are not achievable by apheresis and do not define the minimum acceptable dose.
whyWrongByChoice.B: This dose is several orders of magnitude below the accepted target and would not be used as the threshold.
whyWrongByChoice.C: A dose of 2 x 10^4 CD34+ cells/kg falls far short of the commonly cited minimum.
whyWrongByChoice.E: A dose of 2 x 10^8 CD34+ cells/kg greatly exceeds the stated threshold and is not the accepted minimum.

questions.stem: A transplant program is counseling patients about the likelihood of identifying a suitably HLA-matched unrelated donor through the registry, and explains that this likelihood varies by ethnic background. Patients of which of the following backgrounds have the lowest reported odds of finding a match?

explanation.summary: Odds of finding a registry match are lowest for patients of Black or African American background, at about 29%.
explanation.whyCorrect: Reported odds of finding a match based on ethnic background are 29% for Black or African American patients, 47% for Asian or Pacific Islander, 48% for Hispanic or Latino, 60% for Native American, and 79% for White patients. This underrepresentation in donor registries is a key reason umbilical cord blood has emerged as an alternative-donor option, along with mixed ethnicity and uncommon HLA haplotypes.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Asian or Pacific Islander patients have roughly 47% odds, higher than the lowest group.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Hispanic or Latino patients have roughly 48% odds of finding a match.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Native American patients have roughly 60% odds, well above the lowest group.
whyWrongByChoice.E: White patients have the highest reported odds, about 79%.

questions.stem: A 4-year-old girl of mixed ethnicity receives an umbilical cord blood graft despite a degree of HLA mismatch that would be considered unacceptable for an adult marrow donor. Which of the following properties of cord blood stem cells permits this?

choices.label: A
choices.text: They are collected before the donor's ABO and HLA types are established

choices.label: B
choices.text: They are depleted of all mature leukocytes during collection

choices.label: C
