choices.text: They are immunologically naive and cross histocompatibility barriers

choices.label: D
choices.text: They are mobilized with G-CSF given to the mother prior to delivery

choices.label: E
choices.text: They divide far more slowly than adult bone marrow stem cells

explanation.summary: Cord blood stem cells are immunologically naive, allowing them to cross the usual histocompatibility barriers of conventional transplants.
explanation.whyCorrect: Umbilical cord blood is collected from the umbilical vessels in the placenta at the time of delivery and is a rich source of hematopoietic stem cells. Because these cells are immunologically naive, they are able to cross the usual histocompatibility barriers of conventional transplants, which makes cord blood an option for patients who lack HLA-identical siblings or suitably matched unrelated donors.

whyWrongByChoice.A: ABO typing is part of the standard pretransplant evaluation and is not what allows cord blood to bridge HLA mismatch.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Cord blood units are not leukocyte-depleted; their naive lymphocytes are precisely why they tolerate mismatch.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Mobilization with G-CSF applies to peripheral blood stem cell donors, not to cord blood collection at delivery.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Proliferation rate is not the property that allows cord blood to cross histocompatibility barriers.

questions.stem: A 30-year-old woman without a matched donor receives two umbilical cord blood units after conditioning. Over the following months the team monitors her especially closely for one category of complication that is increased specifically with this stem cell source. Which of the following is it?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Bone pain from the donor's mobilization regimen

choices.label: B
choices.text: Complications of general anesthesia in the donor

choices.label: D
choices.text: Oral mucositis caused by the conditioning regimen

explanation.summary: The immunologic naivety of cord blood stem cells raises the risk of infection, particularly viral infection or reactivation.
explanation.whyCorrect: Major limitations of umbilical cord blood are the relatively small number of HSCs in each unit, which is why an adult typically requires two units, and an increased risk of infections, particularly viral infections or reactivation. This infection risk follows directly from the naive immunologic nature of the stem cells.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Bone pain is a side effect of G-CSF given to a peripheral blood stem cell donor; cord blood requires no donor mobilization.
whyWrongByChoice.B: General anesthesia is required for marrow harvest from a living donor, not for collection of cord blood at delivery.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Cord blood is an allogeneic graft, so the donor-derived graft-versus-tumor effect is retained.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Oral mucositis is a toxicity of the high-intensity conditioning regimen and occurs regardless of the stem cell source.

questions.stem: A 47-year-old woman with myelodysplastic syndrome has just had her HLA type determined as part of her pretransplant evaluation. Which of the following is the next step the transplant team takes to identify a donor?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Beginning conditioning chemotherapy while a donor is sought

choices.label: B
choices.text: Collecting her own stem cells by apheresis for later use

choices.label: C
choices.text: HLA typing of her immediate family members

choices.label: D
choices.text: Immediate infusion of an unmatched cord blood unit

choices.label: E
choices.text: Repeating HLA typing after a course of immunosuppression

explanation.summary: Once the recipient's HLA type is known, family members are typed first, and the NMDP registry is then searched for unrelated donors or cord blood units.
explanation.whyCorrect: After the patient's HLA type is established by blood draw or cheek swab, the transplant team endeavors to find a donor by first performing HLA typing on family members and then searching the NMDP donor registry for potential unrelated donors or cord blood units.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Conditioning is given in the days immediately before Day 0, once a graft is secured, not while a donor is still being sought.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Autologous collection applies to autologous transplant; myelodysplastic syndrome is treated with an allogeneic graft.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Cord blood is reserved for patients who lack an HLA-identical sibling or a suitably matched unrelated donor, and a search has not yet been done.
whyWrongByChoice.E: HLA type is genetically fixed and does not change with immunosuppression, so repeat typing serves no purpose.

questions.stem: A patient being evaluated for allogeneic transplant is told that he and his immediate family members will each need to have their HLA type determined. Which of the following best describes how these samples are obtained?

choices.label: A
choices.text: A blood draw or a cheek swab

choices.label: B
choices.text: Apheresis after several days of G-CSF

choices.label: C
choices.text: Collection from placental vessels at delivery

choices.label: D
choices.text: Lymph node biopsy under local anesthesia

choices.label: E
choices.text: Marrow aspiration from the posterior iliac crest

explanation.summary: HLA typing is accomplished through a simple blood draw or cheek swab.
explanation.whyCorrect: HLA typing is accomplished through a blood draw or cheek swab. This makes typing of family members straightforward, and the patient's HLA type can then be submitted to a national registry to identify potential unrelated donors.

whyWrongByChoice.B: Apheresis after mobilization is a stem cell collection procedure, not a tissue typing method.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Collection from placental vessels describes obtaining a cord blood unit, not typing a prospective donor.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Lymph node biopsy is not used for HLA typing in transplant evaluation.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Marrow aspiration under general anesthesia is how marrow is procured for transplant, not how HLA type is determined.

questions.stem: A hematology clinic reviews the indications for autologous hematopoietic stem cell transplantation. Which of the following is the most common condition treated with autologous transplant?

explanation.summary: Multiple myeloma is the most common condition treated with autologous hematopoietic stem cell transplantation.
explanation.whyCorrect: Diseases commonly treated with autologous HSCT include multiple myeloma, non-Hodgkin lymphoma, Hodgkin lymphoma, certain solid tumors such as neuroblastoma and germ cell tumors, and autoimmune disorders such as scleroderma. Of these, multiple myeloma is the most common indication.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Acute myeloid leukemia is treated with allogeneic transplant, which adds a graft-versus-tumor effect from donor cells.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Aplastic anemia is a marrow failure state requiring a healthy donor graft, so it is treated allogeneically.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Severe combined immunodeficiency requires donor-derived immune reconstitution and is treated allogeneically.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Sickle cell anemia is listed among the nonmalignant diseases treated with allogeneic transplant.

questions.stem: A 55-year-old man with relapsed Hodgkin lymphoma has stem cells collected and stored, then receives high-dose myeloablative chemotherapy followed by reinfusion of those same cells. Which of the following best describes the aim of this approach?

choices.label: A
choices.text: To avoid the need for any conditioning chemotherapy

choices.label: B
choices.text: To correct an inherited defect in the patient's own stem cells

choices.label: C
choices.text: To provide donor T cells that attack residual lymphoma

choices.label: D
choices.text: To rescue the marrow after chemotherapy aimed at resistant cancer

choices.label: E
choices.text: To supply mature neutrophils and platelets immediately after infusion

explanation.summary: Autologous transplant reinfuses the patient's own stem cells to rescue the marrow after high-dose myeloablative chemotherapy directed at chemoresistant residual disease.
explanation.whyCorrect: Autologous stem cell transplant involves the use of the patient's own stem cells to rescue the bone marrow following the administration of high-dose myeloablative chemotherapy. The aim of this type of transplant is to eradicate residual cancer cells that have demonstrated some resistance to standard chemotherapy.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Autologous transplant is performed precisely because myeloablative conditioning chemotherapy is given.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Correcting an inherited stem cell defect requires a donor graft, since the patient's own cells carry the same defect.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Donor T cells and the graft-versus-tumor effect belong to allogeneic transplant; an autologous graft supplies no donor immune cells.
whyWrongByChoice.E: The graft supplies progenitor cells that must engraft over weeks; it does not provide immediate mature neutrophils and platelets.

questions.stem: A pediatric oncology team is reviewing which malignancies are managed with an autologous rather than an allogeneic graft. Which of the following diseases is among those commonly treated with autologous hematopoietic stem cell transplantation?

explanation.summary: Solid tumors such as neuroblastoma and germ cell tumors are among the diseases commonly treated with autologous HSCT.
explanation.whyCorrect: Diseases commonly treated with autologous HSCT include the hematologic malignancies multiple myeloma, non-Hodgkin lymphoma, and Hodgkin lymphoma, plus solid tumors such as neuroblastoma and germ cell tumors, and autoimmune disorders such as scleroderma. Neuroblastoma falls in the solid tumor group.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Chronic myeloid leukemia appears among the hematologic malignancies treated with allogeneic transplant.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Fanconi anemia is listed among the nonmalignant diseases treated with allogeneic transplant.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Paroxysmal nocturnal hemoglobinuria is an allogeneic transplant indication, since the patient's own clone is the problem.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Wiskott-Aldrich syndrome is an inherited disorder treated with an allogeneic graft.

questions.stem: A 14-year-old boy with sickle cell anemia and recurrent vaso-occlusive crises is referred to a transplant center to discuss potentially curative therapy. Which of the following transplant strategies is used for this disease?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Administration of G-CSF alone to raise circulating stem cell counts

choices.label: B
choices.text: Apheresis performed to remove his abnormal red blood cells

choices.label: C
choices.text: Infusion of his own stem cells after myeloablative chemotherapy

choices.label: D
choices.text: Infusion of stem cells from a related or unrelated donor

choices.label: E
choices.text: Marrow aspiration from the posterior iliac crest for staging

explanation.summary: Sickle cell anemia is one of the nonmalignant diseases treated with allogeneic HSCT, using stem cells from a related or unrelated donor.
explanation.whyCorrect: Allogeneic stem cell transplant involves infusion of stem cells from a related or unrelated donor. Sickle cell anemia appears among the nonmalignant diseases commonly treated with allogeneic HSCT, alongside aplastic anemia, paroxysmal nocturnal hemoglobinuria, Fanconi anemia, thalassemia major, severe combined immunodeficiency, Wiskott-Aldrich syndrome, and inborn errors of metabolism.

whyWrongByChoice.A: G-CSF mobilizes stem cells into the blood for collection; by itself it is not a treatment for sickle cell anemia.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Removing abnormal red cells by apheresis does not replace the marrow and is not a curative transplant strategy.
whyWrongByChoice.C: An autologous graft would return the same defective stem cells and could not correct the underlying disorder.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Marrow aspiration for staging is a diagnostic procedure and is not the therapeutic strategy described.

questions.stem: Before transplantation, a recipient undergoes an extensive evaluation. Which of the following is the primary purpose of that pretransplant evaluation?

choices.label: A
choices.text: To calculate the number of CD34+ cells the patient will need

choices.label: B
choices.text: To decide the timing of post-transplant vaccinations

choices.label: C
choices.text: To document the absolute neutrophil count at baseline

choices.label: D
choices.text: To establish the patient's ABO and HLA type

choices.label: E
choices.text: To identify oral lesions before conditioning begins

explanation.summary: Pretransplant evaluation is performed primarily to establish the patient's ABO and HLA type.
explanation.whyCorrect: Prior to transplant, the recipient undergoes extensive evaluation primarily to establish the patient's ABO and HLA type. ABO and HLA matching is critical to the success of transplantation, mitigating the risk of downstream rejection, and the HLA type then drives the search for a donor.

whyWrongByChoice.A: The CD34+ cell dose is calculated from recipient weight when the collected product is assessed, not as the aim of the evaluation.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Vaccination timing belongs to long-term post-transplant follow-up, not to pretransplant typing.
whyWrongByChoice.C: The neutrophil count matters later, when myeloid engraftment is being defined after the graft is infused.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Oral mucositis is a regimen-related toxicity that develops after conditioning; screening for it is not the purpose of evaluation.

questions.stem: While reviewing the transplant timeline with a patient, the team repeatedly refers to events as occurring on "Day -10," "Day -1," or "Day +14" relative to Day 0. Which of the following does Day 0 denote?

choices.label: B
choices.text: The day myeloid engraftment is documented

choices.label: C
choices.text: The day of the stem cell infusion

choices.label: D
choices.text: The day the central venous catheter is placed

choices.label: E
choices.text: The first day of conditioning chemotherapy

explanation.summary: Day 0 is the day of stem cell infusion, and the whole transplant process is described relative to it.
explanation.whyCorrect: Regardless of the type of transplant, patients undergo a similar process centered around the day of stem cell infusion, which is known as Day 0. Conditioning chemotherapy and catheter placement occur on the negative-numbered days before it, and engraftment and other post-transplant events are counted forward from it.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Immunosuppression is tapered at roughly 6 months if there is no GVHD, far beyond Day 0.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Myeloid engraftment typically occurs within 21 days after the graft infusion, so it falls well after Day 0.
whyWrongByChoice.D: The central venous catheter is placed before conditioning begins, ahead of Day 0.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Conditioning chemotherapy is given in the days prior to transplant, on the negative-numbered days.

questions.stem: A patient has just received her graft infusion and is admitted for the post-transplant recovery period. Which of the following best characterizes this period?

choices.label: A
choices.text: 2-4 weeks of myelosuppression as donor cells populate the marrow

choices.label: B
choices.text: A 6-month interval before donor cells reach the marrow

choices.label: C
choices.text: An interval during which conditioning chemotherapy continues

choices.label: D
choices.text: Immediate normalization of blood counts within 48 hours

choices.label: E
choices.text: Profound leukocytosis caused by the infused graft

explanation.summary: The recovery period is 2-4 weeks of myelosuppression from conditioning while donor cells migrate to the marrow and begin producing blood cells.
explanation.whyCorrect: The post-transplant period is known as the recovery period and is associated with 2-4 weeks of myelosuppression from the conditioning regimen, during which the donor cells are migrating to the bone marrow to begin producing new blood cells. Myeloid engraftment typically follows within 21 days of the graft infusion.

whyWrongByChoice.B: Donor cells home to the marrow over days to weeks, not over a 6-month interval.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Conditioning is completed before Day 0; the recovery period follows the infusion.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Counts do not normalize immediately; the patient remains cytopenic until the graft engrafts.
whyWrongByChoice.E: The hallmark of this period is profound cytopenia, not leukocytosis.

questions.stem: Ten days after stem cell infusion, a transplant recipient has a hemoglobin of 6.8 g/dL and a platelet count of 9 x 10^9/L. Which of the following is the expected supportive measure during this phase?

choices.label: B
choices.text: Blood product transfusion until the counts recover

choices.label: D
choices.text: Immediate infusion of a second stem cell graft

choices.label: E
choices.text: Initiation of stem cell mobilization with G-CSF

explanation.summary: Patients require blood transfusions for the low counts of the recovery period, which rise as the marrow engrafts.
explanation.whyCorrect: During the recovery period patients may require blood transfusions because of their initially low blood counts, and those counts will increase as the bone marrow becomes engrafted. Transfusion is used specifically to treat profound anemia and thrombocytopenia while waiting for engraftment.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Conditioning chemotherapy wipes out the marrow and is completed before Day 0; giving more would deepen the cytopenias.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Antimicrobial prophylaxis is needed during myelosuppression, when infection risk is greatest.
whyWrongByChoice.D: A second graft is not given for expected post-transplant cytopenias, which resolve with engraftment.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Mobilization is used before collection in a donor or autologous patient, not to treat cytopenias after infusion.

questions.stem: A transplant recipient asks when he will be most vulnerable to serious complications after his graft. Which of the following periods carries the greatest risk?

choices.label: A
choices.text: The 2 weeks before conditioning chemotherapy begins

choices.label: C
choices.text: The first year after immunosuppression is stopped

choices.label: D
choices.text: The interval between mobilization and apheresis

choices.label: E
choices.text: The period after routine vaccinations are resumed

explanation.summary: The first 100 days after transplantation are the time of greatest risk for transplant recipients.
explanation.whyCorrect: The first 100 days following transplantation are the time of greatest risk for transplant recipients. This window covers the myelosuppressive recovery period, the peak incidence of regimen-related toxicities and infection, and the onset of acute graft-versus-host disease.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Before conditioning the patient still has intact marrow function and immunity, so risk is comparatively low.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Stopping immunosuppression occurs late, after the highest-risk early window has passed.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Mobilization and apheresis are generally very safe, with bone pain as the most common side effect.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Vaccinations are resumed in the later post-transplant period, when immune recovery is well under way.

questions.stem: A program is quoting outcome statistics to a patient considering transplant and is asked how often the graft fails to take. Which of the following best reflects the overall incidence of graft failure after HSCT?

choices.label: A
choices.text: 1-5% after autologous and 5-6% after allogeneic transplant

choices.label: B
choices.text: 10-15% after autologous and 20-25% after allogeneic transplant

choices.label: D
choices.text: Less than 0.1% after either type of transplant

choices.label: E
choices.text: Substantially higher after autologous than after allogeneic transplant

explanation.summary: Graft failure is uncommon, occurring in 1-5% of autologous and 5-6% of allogeneic transplants.
explanation.whyCorrect: Graft failure is defined as the lack of donor hematopoietic cell engraftment following autologous or allogeneic HSCT, and its overall incidence is low: 1-5% for autologous transplant and 5-6% for allogeneic transplant. It is further divided into primary (early) and secondary (late) phases.

whyWrongByChoice.B: These figures substantially overstate the risk, which is in the low single digits.
whyWrongByChoice.C: An incidence near 30% would not be described as low and does not match either transplant type.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Graft failure is uncommon but far more frequent than 0.1%.
whyWrongByChoice.E: The relationship is reversed: allogeneic transplant carries the somewhat higher rate.

questions.stem: A patient who had been recovering after allogeneic transplant loses donor cell engraftment, and the workup indicates the loss is immune-mediated. Which of the following best describes graft rejection in this setting?

choices.label: A
choices.text: A toxicity of conditioning that injures the oral mucosa

choices.label: B
choices.text: An apheresis product containing too few CD34+ cells

choices.label: C
choices.text: Donor immune cells destroying recipient bile ducts and gut mucosa

choices.label: D
choices.text: Recipient immune cells rejecting the donor hematopoietic cells

choices.label: E
choices.text: Relapsed malignancy progressively crowding the marrow

explanation.summary: Graft rejection is a subset of primary or secondary graft failure caused by immune-mediated rejection by recipient immune cells.
explanation.whyCorrect: Graft rejection is a subset of primary or secondary graft failure and is caused by immune-mediated rejection by the recipient's immune cells. It is therefore the mirror image of graft-versus-host disease, in which the direction of immune attack runs from donor cells toward recipient tissue.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Mucosal injury from conditioning is a regimen-related organ toxicity, not an immune rejection of the graft.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Low donor cell yield is a separate listed cause of graft failure and is not immune-mediated.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Donor T cells attacking recipient organs describes graft-versus-host disease, the opposite direction of attack.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Persistent or progressive malignancy is another recognized cause of graft failure, but it is not immune rejection.

questions.stem: A recipient has still not achieved threshold blood counts 35 days after allogeneic transplant, and the team systematically reviews possible explanations. Which of the following is a recognized cause of graft failure?

choices.label: A
choices.text: An unusually high CD34+ cell content of the infused product

choices.label: B
choices.text: Low donor cell yield in the infused product

choices.label: C
choices.text: Mobilization with G-CSF before the collection

choices.label: D
choices.text: Placement of a central venous catheter before conditioning

choices.label: E
choices.text: Use of a cheek swab rather than blood for HLA typing

explanation.summary: Recognized causes of graft failure include graft rejection, persistent or progressive malignancy, low donor cell yield, medication side effects, and GVHD.
explanation.whyCorrect: Graft failure has a myriad of causes, including graft rejection, persistent or progressive malignancy, low donor cell yield, medication side effects, and graft-versus-host disease. A product with too few donor cells cannot reliably reconstitute marrow function, which is why CD34+ dose per kilogram is measured before infusion.

whyWrongByChoice.A: A higher cell dose favors engraftment rather than causing failure; the concern is a dose below threshold.
whyWrongByChoice.C: G-CSF mobilization is the standard step that makes peripheral blood collection possible and does not cause graft failure.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Catheter placement before conditioning is a routine part of the transplant timeline and is unrelated to engraftment.
whyWrongByChoice.E: A cheek swab is an accepted method of HLA typing and yields the same result as a blood draw.

questions.stem: A transplant recipient's absolute neutrophil count has now exceeded 0.5 x 10^9/L on 3 consecutive days, and the team turns to assessing platelet and red cell recovery. Which of the following best describes how those engraftment thresholds are defined?

choices.label: A
choices.text: By a single platelet count above 150 x 10^9/L on any day

choices.label: B
choices.text: By documented donor chimerism on marrow biopsy at day 30

choices.label: C
choices.text: By normalization of the hemoglobin within 21 days of infusion

choices.label: D
choices.text: By numeric cut-offs identical to the neutrophil criterion

choices.label: E
choices.text: By sustaining an appropriate count without transfusion support

explanation.summary: Platelet and hemoglobin engraftment thresholds are variably defined but generally require sustaining an appropriate count without transfusion support.
explanation.whyCorrect: Myeloid engraftment has a precise definition, the first of 3 consecutive days in which the ANC exceeds 0.5 x 10^9/L. The platelet and hemoglobin thresholds are more variably defined but usually involve sustaining an appropriate count without transfusion support, which distinguishes true marrow recovery from transfused counts.

whyWrongByChoice.A: A single value obtained while the patient may still be receiving transfusions does not establish engraftment.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Chimerism testing is not how the platelet and hemoglobin engraftment thresholds are described.
whyWrongByChoice.C: A fixed 21-day deadline describes the typical timing of myeloid engraftment, not the red cell threshold definition.
whyWrongByChoice.D: The neutrophil criterion is specific to myeloid engraftment and is not applied unchanged to platelets and hemoglobin.

questions.stem: Three weeks after an allogeneic transplant, a patient develops jaundice of the skin and mucous membranes together with watery diarrhea and abdominal pain. Which of the following best explains the jaundice in this complication?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Destruction of small bile ducts by donor immune cells

choices.label: B
choices.text: Direct hepatotoxicity of G-CSF given before collection

choices.label: C
choices.text: Hemolysis of transfused ABO-incompatible red blood cells

choices.label: D
choices.text: Mucosal ulceration of the gastrointestinal tract

choices.label: E
choices.text: Obstruction of the common bile duct by a gallstone

explanation.summary: In graft-versus-host disease, jaundice results from destruction of small bile ducts, while the diarrhea comes from mucosal ulceration of the gut.
explanation.whyCorrect: Patients with GVHD may present with a maculopapular rash that can desquamate, jaundice of the skin and mucous membranes caused by destruction of small bile ducts, nausea, vomiting, diarrhea caused by mucosal ulceration of the gut, abdominal pain, and hepatosplenomegaly. The liver, skin, and gastrointestinal tract are the organs characteristically affected.

whyWrongByChoice.B: G-CSF is given to a donor before collection, and its characteristic side effect is bone pain rather than jaundice.
whyWrongByChoice.C: ABO compatibility is addressed during pretransplant evaluation, and hemolysis does not account for the accompanying gut findings.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Mucosal ulceration of the gut explains this patient's diarrhea and abdominal pain, not the jaundice.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Mechanical biliary obstruction is not the described mechanism of jaundice in this post-transplant syndrome.

questions.stem: A transplant recipient develops an infection during the first weeks after the graft, while still profoundly myelosuppressed. Among the organisms listed, which characteristically causes infection earliest in the post-transplant course?

explanation.summary: Herpes simplex virus is the earliest of the characteristic post-transplant viral infections, clustering in the first weeks after the graft.
explanation.whyCorrect: Transplant recipients are at increased risk for bacterial, fungal, and viral infection given the profound immunosuppression. Among the viral pathogens, herpes simplex virus occurs earliest, clustering around the time of the initial neutropenic period, whereas CMV and adenovirus follow later and VZV appears latest.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Aspergillus infection follows the earlier Candida infections and is not the earliest listed organism.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Cytomegalovirus, along with adenovirus, occurs after the herpes simplex period rather than earliest.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Infection with encapsulated bacteria appears late, after the early gram-positive and gram-negative bacterial period.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Varicella-zoster virus occurs latest of the listed viruses, extending well beyond the early post-transplant months.
